blocks.html:
Journal

The journal is an in-game mechanic which catalogs various discoveries throughout the world. There is also a section dedicated to personal notes, which can be useful as a reference. Many people use the personal notes section for remembering names, locations, or keeping KOS/friendly lists.

This spreadsheet is of all currently available journal entries. There are a few of them that are likely currently unobtainable, such as elaiva and Steintroll cave.

guides.title: Adrenaline & Combat Abilities
guides.summary: Learn how adrenaline is generated, lost, and spent, then compare the combat abilities that can turn a close fight.

blocks.html:
Adrenaline / Combat Abilities

Learn how adrenaline is generated, lost, and spent, then compare the combat abilities that can turn a close fight.

Adrenaline

Players have a new resource known as “adrenaline”. This functions similar to the rage mechanic from World of Warcraft - when inflicting or receiving damage, you gain adrenaline pips. This resource also passively generates when out of combat, but only to either 1 or 2 pips, depending on the player's race. Here is the default UI for adrenaline - notice that it has 2 filled pips with an available 10.
blocks.text: Adrenaline / Combat Abilities Learn how adrenaline is generated, lost, and spent, then compare the combat abilities that can turn a close fight. Adrenaline Players have a new resource known as “adrenaline”. This functions similar to the rage mechanic from World of Warcraft - when inflicting or receiving damage, you gain adrenaline pips. This resource also passively generates when out of combat, but only to either 1 or 2 pips, depending on the player's race. Here is the default UI for adrenaline - notice that it has 2 filled pips with an available 10.

blocks.html:
Gaining Adrenaline:

  • 1 pip of adrenaline is gained per 80 damage dealt with normal swings
  • 1 pip of adrenaline is gained per 20 damage received
  • 1 pip of adrenaline is gained naturally per 20 seconds if depleted
  • 5 pips of adrenaline is gained when executing a target in mercy mode
  • Adrenaline is gained on parry

Adrenaline is not gained from using combat abilities themselves; it must be gained via normal attacks or magic. Adrenaline decays over time if not used and the player is out of combat. The default duration of this is 7 seconds- but this may be stalled by doing 1 point of damage to anything.

Armor impacts the quantity of adrenaline gained indirectly, so you will naturally gain less adrenaline versus heavily armored opponents and you gain less adrenaline if you are heavily armored yourself. Important: pets, PvE, and other objects such as training dummies are a very quick way to boost adrenaline gain as these are weak targets that tend not to parry.

Swapping weapons incurs an adrenaline penalty. Quick testing indicates you lose ½ of your total adrenaline when this happens. Swapping between bare fists and fist + shield does not incur this penalty.

blocks.html:
Each clade has a unique interaction with adrenaline, making them better (or worse) for certain applications.

  • Humans do not experience adrenaline decay until 21 seconds instead of 7
  • Alvarin naturally generate a baseline of 2 adrenaline instead of 1
  • Oghmir gain additional adrenaline when receiving damage
  • Thursars have a cap of 11 adrenaline instead of 10, and they gain slightly more adrenaline from dealing damage

Now that the adrenaline resource is explained, what do you actually do with it?

blocks.html:
Combat Abilities

Each weapon class was given a minimum of 3 combat abilities. These are special attacks or attack modifiers that can turn the tide of a fight in your favor. Access combat abilities through the skill menu, which has the default hotkey of L.

Combat ability books can be purchased at Soldier and Hunter taskmasters with their corresponding currencies. Silver Aegis are used to purchase the majority of combat abilities, while Wooden Therons are used to buy dagger and spear abilities.Here is a catalog of all purchasable books:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZeXhejJxaEmGyXPjiuz2HAWdjOTQtoOsu4H0TfWsoJY/edit?gid=1369404009#gid=1369404009

Important: these books cannot be traded, and each has skill level requirements to read. These skill levels roughly correspond with the strength of the ability. Abilities which require more adrenaline to use require higher skills. These abilities books can be used even when reading other books.

blocks.html:
Shared Abilities - These are usable with ALL weapons, including bare fists. These are all instant activation. These are obtainable from ALL soldier taskmasters.

  • Invigorate (3 cost) - Increases stamina regeneration by 100% for 3 seconds
  • Rejuvenate (3 cost) - Restores 2 health per second for 5 seconds
  • Energise (3 cost) - Increases mana regeneration by 100% for 10 seconds
  • Quicken (3 cost) - Increases movement speed by 3% for 8 seconds
  • Amplify (3 cost) - Increases spell power by 10% for 8 seconds
  • Empower (3 cost) - Increases melee damage by 10% for 8 seconds
  • Brace (3 cost) - Increases physical defense by 25% for 8 seconds
  • Poise (3 cost) - Increases knockdown resist by 50% for 8 seconds
  • Ward (3 cost) - Increase magic defense by 25% for 8 seconds

blocks.html:
Weapon Abilities -

Each weapon has 3 combat abilities, with the exception of the bow which has 7. There are two types of weapon abilities - instant and directional. Instant triggers the moment the key is pressed, while directional modifies the next appropriate attack with that weapon as indicated by the combat abilities menu. For example, the 2h sword ability “Flurry” only activates when a left or right attack is done, but not an overhead or thrust.

Notable abilities are marked with a ⭐. (3) = 3 cost. (d) = directional modifier. (##) = skill-level required.

2h Sword - Gaul Kor, Tindrem, Kam, Kwar Migdal

  • Flurry (2)(d)(50) - 2 flowing cuts which inflict bleed
  • Hanging Thrust (2)(100) - Overhead feints into a strong thrust for 20% armor pierce
  • Hilt Strike (1)(25) - Pummels an opponent for reduced damage, with 10% armor pierce. This knocks back opponents and interrupts spellcasting

1h Sword - Kranesh, Tindrem, Beth Jedda

  • Riposte (2)(50) - Auto parries and counter attacks if timed correctly
  • Thwart (2)(d)(25) - Performs 3 swift cuts
  • Counter (3)(100) - Auto parries and thrusts if successful

Dagger - Kranesh, Kam

  • ⭐Precise Strikes (2)(d)(25) - Thrusts dagger from any 4 direction
  • Piercing Strike (3)(50) - Overhead stabs opponents for 30% armor piercing
  • ⭐ Gouge (3)(d)(100) - A strong attack that inflicts 10 seconds of bleed

2h Axe - Fabernum, Gaul Kor, Kam, Pash

  • Cleave (3)(d)(50) - Cleaves through multiple enemies
  • Severance (3)(100) - A strong overhead attack that cannot be parried. 10% armor pierce and inflicts sapped for 6 seconds
  • ⭐Carve (2)(25) - Right feints and does an upward strike

1h Axe - Fabernum, Gaul Kor, Pash

  • ⭐ Hack (3)(d)(50) - Incredibly strong 3 attack combo that hits for 5% armor pierce.
  • Underhew (2)(100) - Feints left into an under attack that depletes 20 stamina from the target, and can hit multiple targets
  • Split (1)(25) - Punches an opponent with the axehead and saps them for 4 seconds

2h Hammer - Hyllspeia, Cave Camp, Aur, Kam

  • ⭐ Fracture (2)(25) - A thrusting attack that deals reduced damage but has 5% armor piercing, dazes the enemy for 5 seconds, knocks them back, AND interrupts spellcasting

These abilities offer many ways to get through blocking, countering turtling opponents, and dealing exceptional damage very quickly. Make sure everyone learns the specific abilities of ALL weapons. Failure to do so could be catastrophic as many abilities throw in unique challenges, such as strong center attacks from 2h hammers.

Which weapon should you use? As it stands 2h hammers, 1h axe, 1h hammer, dagger, and spear are the strongest. The meta around these are still settling. Use what feels right to you. Some interactions remain under investigation, and future balance updates may alter their value.

Expect the balance to evolve and adjust accordingly.

functions similar to the rage mechanic from world of warcraft - when inflicting or receiving damage, you gain adrenaline pips. this resource also passively generates when out of combat, but only to either 1 or 2 pips, depending on the player's race. here is the default ui for adrenaline - notice that it has 2 filled pips with an available 10. gaining adrenaline: 1 pip of adrenaline is gained per 80 damage dealt with normal swings 1 pip of adrenaline is gained per 20 damage received 1 pip of adrenaline is gained naturally per 20 seconds if depleted 5 pips of adrenaline is gained when executing a target in mercy mode adrenaline is gained on parry adrenaline is not gained from using combat abilities themselves; it must be gained via normal attacks or magic. adrenaline decays over time if not used and the player is out of combat. the default duration of this is 7 seconds- but this may be stalled by doing 1 point of damage to anything. armor impacts the quantity of adrenaline gained indirectly, so you will naturally gain less adrenaline versus heavily armored opponents and you gain less adrenaline if you are heavily armored yourself. important: pets, pve, and other objects such guides.title: Attributes & Stats
guides.summary: Understand every core attribute, the difference between flat and raw bonuses, practical caps, and the systems each stat affects.

blocks.html:
Attributes and stats are a character-defining resource. This section covers these stats, their uses, and other data covering them.

Terminology

  • Flat stat - Increases the stat without breaking the cap.
  • Raw stat - Increases the soft cap of the stat and adds one point to it.
blocks.text: Attributes and stats are a character-defining resource. This section covers these stats, their uses, and other data covering them. Terminology Flat stat - Increases the stat without breaking the cap. Raw stat - Increases the soft cap of the stat and adds one point to it.

blocks.html:
Strength

  • Increases the ability to use heavier weapons, adds damage bonus, stamina, carry weight, armor weight, and alters how strong your character appears.
  • The easiest way to get strength is to punch another character repeatedly.
  • Weapons have a strength requirement stat on them. You generally must be at least 1 point ABOVE this requirement to effectively use a weapon without stamina and damage penalties. For instance, a bow with 81.25 strength requirement means you must have at least 82 strength.
  • Bows are unique in the sense that you gain further stamina benefit from higher strength when using them, particularly when mounted. For a meta dense crepite/dense crepite shortbow, you will want around 92 strength to use it while mounted with minimal stamina drain.
  • The highest possible achievable strength is on an age 30 Thursar Kallard or Thursar Sidoian who is stout with two +4 raw strength rings while using the thursar battlecry clade gift for +20 strength and the Well Built clade gift for +2 max strength as well as +4 mastery raw strength. This totals 133 strength normally or 153 strength when claded.
  • The best weight class to maximize strength is stout.
  • Strength determines how far someone is shield bashed, and how fast the player can move siege weaponry.

blocks.html:
Dexterity - Increases movement speed, stamina, jump height, weak spot chance, and the ability to control a mount. Important to note that the movement speed bonus experiences diminishing returns the higher dexterity is.

  • The easiest way to gain dexterity is to parry attacks repeatedly.
  • Dexterity has a unique property in that it does not scale linearly for most stats. For example, between 25 and 50 dexterity, there is absolutely no gain in movement speed. Above 110 dexterity movement speed gains are diminished. Weakspot bonuses seemingly cumulative and possibly accelerate above 120 dex.
  • A common misconception from fantasy game tropes is that bows are heavily influenced by the dexterity stat. The only impacts dex really has with bows is it increases weakspot on headshots and increases stamina and stamina regen slightly.
  • The maximum theoretical dexterity is 148. It is achievable on an aged 31 veela who is skeletal with two +4 raw dexterity rings and +4 raw dex mastery gift. This is an absolutely horrible build, and do not do it.
  • The min-maxed best weight class for dexterity is skeletal, but skeletal is bad. The recommended approach is to if you must focus dex it should be lean, fit, or even stout.

blocks.html:
Constitution – Increases HP, stamina, carry weight, and armor weight.

  • The easiest way to level constitution is by parrying attacks repeatedly.
  • Constitution is a critical stat. The vast majority of characters should have it maximized. In a full loot pvp game, having HP above 0 is pretty important. The two exceptions for builds that do not require high constitution are skeletal mages (griefer builds which aim to not get hit) or Arcane archers (their horse gets focused first).
  • The maximum theoretical constitution is 146. An aged 23 Blainn who is lean/fit/stout with two +4 raw constitution rings and the Hefty clade gift boosts it this high as well as raw con masteries. This should net around 226hp, depending on weight and size. If these rings also have two +11 hp stats on them and the character is max sized, a player could theoretically have mid 240's hp. If overweight this is boosted to the high 240's. If bulging and max size this becomes an impressive 263 hp! It is recommended to go lean/fit/stout, however as movement speed is so important.

blocks.html:
Intelligence – Increases mana, mana regen, Magic spell power, and reading speed. Spell power increases linearly with intelligence level.

  • In Mortal Online 1, intelligence increase defense versus pilfering. players may see this return when thievery is readded to the game.
  • The maximum theoretical intelligence is 147. An aged 62 pure huergar who is obese with two +4 raw int rings and the +1 raw int mastery can achieving this. This gives the theoretical maximum amount of spell damage. The dexterity and constitution penalties of being obese generally force the player build to be mounted. Players can also achieve this intelligence as skeletal, but skeletal oghmir is not viable. Avoid spending time with skeletal oghmir.
  • The majority of melee characters in the game do not need intelligence. It is sometimes advisable to get during the early stages of character development to increase reading speed, but there is little reason to have it afterwards.
  • The quickest method to level intelligence is repeatedly cast magic while riding a horse. You can also spam craft items.

blocks.html:
Psyche - Increases mana, mana regen, and magic magic defense. Spell defense scales linearly with psyche level.

  • Psyche is important for skill point allocation, as most magic skills use psyche, or psy + int as the attribute bonus.
  • The theoretical maximum psyche is 151 with a Sheevra with raw trinkets and mastery. This level of psyche gives exceptionally defense versus magic. Most spells will not only hit for a lower amount of flat damage, but most will be resisted as well.
  • Often considered the red headed step child of attributes, it is often overlooked for its utility versus ecumenical/necromancy spells. Many elementalism spells seem to ignore psyche.
  • The consensus is that each point of psyche adds 0.4% flat magic resistance and a small chance to resist spells. In practice, having >Psyche than the spell level of the spell increases resist chance dramatically.
  • Psyche is excellent as a "dump stat". Any excessive skillpoints that do not fit in a build benefit from putting the remaining points into psyche. Trinkets with +psyche are rather useful as most people do not maximize points in this attribute, meaning builds that utilize +psy rings are often not dependent/bound to their trinkets.
  • The quickest method to level psyche is by casting magic while riding a horse.
  • Psy also impacts your players total Kau in the spiritworld. essential for spiritists.

blocks.html:
Size/Height - Size increases height (2 height per 1 size), weight range (bigger character = bigger weight), health, and damage bonus.

  • The height display is often misunderstood as it relies heavily on rounding. Often times players will have a character in the character creator that says it is 220 size, and they enter game at 219. Eating a small bit of +size food generally solves this.
  • Size altering food will have stats that say Size Growth 0.037 or -0.037. As a result, each single unit of food consumed will decrease size by 0.037 points. Since every 0.5 points of size is 1 height, this means you need to eat 28 units of these food to change height by 1, and 56 to change size by 1.
  • There also exists 0.02 and 0.025 size food which is simpler to calculate with: 50 units per size and 40 units per size respectively.
  • While size increases damage bonus and other stats, there are potentially significant negatives to being a large character size. Size physically increases the size of a character model, making them very easy to hit, and very easy to call out in PvP. If there is a single max sized thurkhall in an enemy group, he is usually the first to get focused- and usually with magic! Size also costs attribute points. There's also the issue of mount weight limitations and penalties if riders are too heavy.
  • When eating to increase size/height, another stat must be set to - to increase size if there are no free attribute points. If decreasing size, extra points should be restored to the attribute pool upon crossing a nodeline or relogging.
  • The biggest char possible is an aged 30 thursar/kallard with all clade gifts and has eaten extra growth food. This comes out to 225cm tall with a size of 113. In imperial measurements this is 7'4". The smallest possible char is a huergar aged 72+ at 150cm (4'11").
  • Food to increase height is generally called "Salutary Salvia Oil Decoction" and shrink food is generally called "Salutary Gamun Oil Decoction".

The height display is often misunderstood as it relies heavily on rounding. Often times players will have a character in the character creator that says it is 220 size, and they enter game at 219. Eating a small bit of +size food generally solves this. Size altering food will have stats that say Size Growth 0.037 or -0.037. As a result, each single unit of food consumed will decrease size by 0.037 points. Since every 0.5 points of size is 1 height, this means you need to eat 28 units of these food to change height by 1, and 56 to change size by 1. Weight - Weight is a stat that indirectly impacts characters but is build-defining. The clearest effect of weight is that characters models will alter based on the weight, i.e. an obese character will appear morbidly obese while a stout character will look physically strong.

Weight is broken down into several classes. This chart highlights what exactly those changes are:
blocks.text: Weight - Weight is a stat that indirectly impacts characters but is build-defining. The clearest effect of weight is that characters models will alter based on the weight, i.e. an obese character will appear morbidly obese while a stout character will look physically strong. Weight is broken down into several classes. This chart highlights what exactly those changes are:

blocks.html:
Skeletal - Useful for mages which go FULL mage and are either parry gods or they understand movement on another level. Characters who have this weight are going to have very little HP and will be very weak to damage. There are no fighter builds for this weight class.

Bony - Like skeletal-lite, but with a bit more HP. Generally a pointless weight class.

Skinny - Has a respectable amount of HP while being fast. Useful for mages and nothing else.

Underweight - Fast, while maintaining a decent amount of speed for mages. Not useful for fighters.

Lean - Certain mage builds benefit from this a lot. Other races, such as thursar khurite fighters, can reach fairly respectable movement speed while using this.

Fit - Nothing particularly good about this weightclass. Generally better for most characters, even mages, to go stout due to the minor dex penalty plus the significant HP gain.

Stout - The bread and butter of builds. Most fighters, hybrids, paladins, etc, should be this weight class.

Overweight - A generally niche weight class which can be used for high hp at minimal loss of speed/damage bonus.

Fat - The dexterity penalties of this class combined with the mediocre int/psy bonuses make this a hard weight class to sell. Certain niche fighter builds run this for maximizing HP while still maintaining a modest movement speed.

Bulging - The sweet spot for most mages. The dexterity penalty is hefty, but the HP/int/psy gain are big boons to it. Bulging sheevra mages can still manage to run about 431 speed with this.

Obese - This is the slowest weight class by a significant margin, but it gives a decent amount of HP to offset the constitution loss. Mounted mages love this weight class. Certain weird foot mage builds could utilize it but that approach is not recommended.

blocks.html: Altering character weight comes from altering a characters health/stamina reserves. Gaining weight comes from hitting the cap of the health/stam reserve and continuing to eat, while losing weight involves minimizing the reserve and continuing to use reserves. A practical recommendation is to never grinding weight loss but rather drinking -weight potions which are generally found on the broker. When you find your ideal weight class, it is best to be on the upper range of the weight of that class just before reaching the next class, as this gives the most HP.

blocks.html:
Attributes are Valuable - A lesson in Mastery and Trinkets

What would you rather have- 1% intellignece, or 1 spellpower? 1 constitution or 1hp? 1 psyche or 1 mana?

The answer to all of these questions is the attributes. Attributes are potent statistics to stack on your character. Most characters benefit a ton from maxing out their attributes, and even by gaining raw stats. Let's take a look at roughly what each point does. Note these are eyeballed/roughly estimated, so don't take these values as gospel.

1 point of Strength

  • ~0.35-0.60% damage bonus
  • ~1.5 stamina
  • ~0.05 free armor weight
  • ~0.25 carry weight
  • Lessened stamina usage on swings/bow draw
  • Access to heavier weapons
  • Skillpoints for strength based skills

1 point of Dexterity

  • Movement speed based on dex value. This has diminishing returns
  • ~1 stamina
  • ~1 jump height
  • Weakspot chance
  • Unquantified amount of manueverability
  • Skillpoints for dex based skills

1 point of Constitution

  • 1hp
  • .25 carry weight
  • 0.02 armor weight
  • ~1.5 stamina
  • Skillpoints for con based skills

1 point of Psyche

  • 1 mana and thus regen as well
  • ~0.4% of magic resist
  • Skillpoints for psyche skills. This is huge for mages since so many of their skills are psyche based!

1 point of Intelligence

  • 1 mana and thus regen as well
  • Spell power
  • Reading speed
  • Thievery defense

As you can see, attributes add many utility. Their problem is they generally aren't focused. One doesn't build constitution to boost armor weight, and one doesn't build dexterity for jump height. These effects are bonuses that have oftentimes intangible benefits to the player. Of the numerical bonuses such as +hp or +mana, these are easy to compare. Pick the statistics that give the greatest benefit for the least investment. Don't rush the stamina portion of the mastery tree if you don't have maxed attributes for instance.

guides.title: Bounty Hunting
guides.summary: Track criminal contracts from taskmaster to turn-in, with rewards, seeker-raven use, target hunting, and extraction basics in one place.

blocks.html:
Bounty Hunting

Track criminal contracts from taskmaster to turn-in, with rewards, seeker-raven use, target hunting, and extraction basics in one place.

Overview

The goal of bounty hunting is to pull bounties and hunt down murderers to neutralize them, and then successfully extract back to the taskmaster. Players that have over 10 murdercounts receive a red name and the risk of being hunted. This system is intended to serve several purposes, including generating conflict, giving risk to the red playstyle, and giving “lawful” players an activity to pursue for rewards.

blocks.html:
The central NPC involved with bounty hunting is the Bounty Hunter Taskmaster. He is located in the inns of all major lawful towns. This NPC is also accompanied by the Coraxi Birdkeeper that sells extra seeker ravens.

Bounty hunting goves rewards per successful contract:

  • 1 Bounty Hunter Renown
  • 40 Might (Prominence)
  • 4 Town Rep
  • 1 Gold Corax Coin
  • 4 Gold coins

From these rewards, 100 Gold Corax coins can be traded to the Taskmaster for the legendary Coraxi Seeker Cape. This cape is extremely rare, and has unique feather ruffles along the shoulder.

blocks.html:
In addition to being a fun activity to do, bounty hunting can also be a worthwhile pursuit. The reputation gained from successful hunts stacks up nicely. Red players also tend to be more experienced and will often run in quality gear.

Preparation

Any blue player can start bounty hunting at any time. However, it is not advised to do so until a respectable level of gear along with combat proficiency is gained. Maxed out clade gifts as well as a high mastery level are recommended as well. Remember that bounty hunters fight reds exclusively. As a baseline, people with high murdercounts will be much more experienced at PvP than the average town player.

While solo bounty hunting is thrilling, it is generally advisable to run in groups of 2+. A coordinated bounty hunting group will see much more success than the individual player who runs headstrong into enemy zergs. Don’t feel bad if you outnumber your targets- this is the life they chose.

It is essential to have a dismount mechanic in your arsenal. In most situations, mounted archery and earthquake are the premiere dismount tools. Lancing can be viable, but is not very good at chasing fleeing targets. Boulder is only useful when on the ground and not for chasing fleeing players.

An AoE effect such as lightning bolt or miasma is highly useful for bounty hunting. Finding AFK targets in houses is not unheard of, and being able to nuke them ends the bounty quickly without needing to wait for them to open the door. While not a satisfying end, killing an AFK is sometimes necessary to complete the bounty.

Gear up in quality gear, with full reagents, weapons, potions, at least 10 seeker ravens, and whatever else is necessary for a long trip where multiple fights are possible. You are now ready to begin the hunt.

blocks.html:
The Hunt

To start a bounty hunt, bring 1 gold to the Bounty Hunter taskmaster and select “Sign Contract”. You may also add a name to the window to sign the contract with another player in your close proximity and get the same target.
blocks.text: The Hunt To start a bounty hunt, bring 1 gold to the Bounty Hunter taskmaster and select “Sign Contract”. You may also add a name to the window to sign the contract with another player in your close proximity and get the same target.

blocks.html: You will then be given 1 seeker raven and the contract. By default your target should be within 5000 meters, which is around the distance from Fabernum to Meduli. If no reds are within this zone, targets further out will be found. If no reds are on the server (such as right on server restart), a simple message will pop up saying no targets are found.
blocks.text: You will then be given 1 seeker raven and the contract. By default your target should be within 5000 meters, which is around the distance from Fabernum to Meduli. If no reds are within this zone, targets further out will be found. If no reds are on the server (such as right on server restart), a simple message will pop up saying no targets are found.

blocks.html:
You will be given some precursory info including the name of your target, the guild they belong to, and the amount of murdercounts they have. Player and guild reputation is extremely important when it comes to bounty hunting. Knowing who your target is, where they play, what they play, who they play with, and other valuable info can help you succeed with a contract.

At this point your goal is to find them. The seeker ravens are an extremely potent tool for this as they give a bearing and distance to your target. For example if the bounty hunter starts in Fabernum and the target is 5000m to the south, the hit is roughly in the Vadda region. Start traveling that way and use more ravens to reach your target and get updated locations.

It is generally recommended to bring 10-20 ravens for each bounty. Targets can move, and having extra ravens will help pinpoint them down.

Once you finally reach your target, it is time to kill them. That part is up to you.

blocks.html:
Complications

Challenge 1: They are in a house.

This is a common challenge, with a few less-than-ideal solutions. If you are a fighter, your solution is simply wait them out. You can dive the house if the door is opened, but be careful. For mages or anyone with necromancy (such as arcane archer builds), AoE magic works to nuke them. Effective options include firewall, lightning bolt, miasma, and even auw surge. many builds which run necromancy but not elementalism can summon a walker and auw surge the target through the walker.

Challenge 2: You dove a house and killed your target, and you are now stuck inside.

A tough problem to have, and sometimes it is simply worth it to suicide and sacrifice the contract. However, there are a few other methods that offer a solution. You can:

  • Simply wait to see if they will open the door again
  • Send the owner a message and offer to trade their gear set for freedom
  • Log out and log back in later to see if the door is opened
  • If the house is guild tagged, see if you have any contacts in their guild that will open the door for you

blocks.html:
Challenge 3: They are in a zerg.

This is a tough one. You either need to isolate, assassinate, or get a bigger army. Sometimes you can convince them to 1v1 for the bounty, but many groups might not honor this, or worse, will gank if their guy starts losing. This scenario can also be resolved by strategically informing enemies of the guild their location and numbers, and tagging along with the other group.

Challenge 3: They are your friend.

Ask them. Usually friends are pretty agreeable to giving bounty contracts. If you are fighting alongside them, you can do a little damage to them in the middle of the fight, and if they die you get the bounty contract finished anyway.

blocks.html:
Misc.

The social aspect of bounty hunting cannot be understated. Many times rapport can make or break a successful bounty contract- whether that be from having a respectful duel for the contract, or a group letting you escape.

Players who bounty hunt compete globally to have the highest number of successful hunts. You can see the leaderboard here: https://steamcommunity.com/stats/1170950/leaderboards/8273620/

Certain players abuse a steam exploit to give themselves steam achievements. Bounty hunting takes a very long time to stack kills, so as of 2026, someone with over 1000 bounties is a fraud. As of January 2026 the highest legitimate bounty hunter has 560 kills (Zero).

guides.title: Mastery System
guides.summary: A practical tour of late-game Mastery progression, point limits, node value, prominence experience, and long-term build planning.

blocks.html:
Mastery System

A practical tour of late-game Mastery progression, point limits, node value, prominence experience, and long-term build planning.
blocks.text: Mastery System A practical tour of late-game Mastery progression, point limits, node value, prominence experience, and long-term build planning.

blocks.html:
Overview

Players must hit level 20 clade to unlock the Mastery system. A new menu on the menu bar unlocks at this point. All future prominence (glory, might, surplus) now contributes to mastery experience. Mastery experience up to around level 50 is relatively quick, with diminishing returns. Each level of mastery gives 1 mastery point, which can be spent on a single node.

At launch, the mastery system has 440 nodes on the celestial mastery map, of which the player can choose 110 of them. Each of these nodes is roughly equivalent to 1/3-1/4th of a clade gift in terms of power, with a few notable powerhouse nodes which will be explained below.

Each of these nodes is roughly equivalent to 1/3-1/4th of a clade gift in terms of power, with a few notable powerhouse nodes which will be explained below.

blocks.html:
The Mastery System is broken down into 6 general “Nebulae” which are based in parts of the cosmic map.

From the center top going clockwise, the nebulae are:

Skill - This gives flat action and profession skill points. The deeper you go into the tree, the more favorable the skill points given are.

Constitution - Focuses on health, damage resistance, and thirst.

Dexterity - Gives bonuses to weakspot, jump heigh and fall damaget, stamina, and bow skills.

Clade Specific - This varies based on the race of the character. This includes mostly attribute bonuses and clade gift bonuses, such as increasing the effectiveness of warcrys.

Strength - Physical damage, carry weight, armor weight, and anti-pet tech.

Intelligence - Gives concentration bonus, spell power, spell cost, and mana regen.

There are a total of 1000 mastery levels available to gain. The first 110 mastery levels grant a mastery point which can be spent in these nebulae. However, there is significant upfront cost to unlocking each nebulae. In the above picture, there are green circles at the first node of each tree. To gain permanent access, one must purchase Elixers of Aptitude from the magic vendor for 500g, which is consumed to then unlock the starting nodes. Further nodes on that tree can be unlocked with mastery points alone.

blocks.html:
Allocation Strategy:

The primary objective of the mastery system is to increase the overall power of the character. It is thus important to allocate mastery points into relevant + strong masteries for the intended purpose of the character. That might sound obvious, but there is a key qualifier there- strong masteries. Many masteries are either inefficient or off-purpose.

Masteries are a game of opportunity cost. Investing 3 points into +2 action points, +4 profession points, and +2 action points isn’t going to have the same impact as +1 dex, +1 dex, and +4 raw dex for alvarin.

blocks.html:
There are a few extremely high value masteries that should be considered by all players, regardless of their build:

https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1109332322848874558/1259212006137921647/image.png?ex=668adc11&is=66898a91&hm=dee888678f6da280967e4df1c89429286318a1e13ebd2dd5261c366c2e6b9a14&

  1. AI Damage Resist - In the constitution tree, it gives 2% damage resist from all AI attacks, including tamed/ritual/non-tamed/dominated. Compared to the measly +1 def vs. [specific pet], this gift is worth approximately 6 mastery points worth of value (+2% vs ritual, +2% versus tamed, etc).
  2. Damage TO AI - In the strength tree. Similar to the damage resist, this is a 6x bonus compared to the normal damage to AI gifts.
  3. +4/2 Raw attributes - These are race specific but offer a HUGE bonus in stats for minimal investment of 3 mastery points. Alvarin get +4 raw dex, oghmir get +4 raw con, thursar get +4 raw strength, and humans get +2 raw everything. These are high impact, low investment masteries.
  4. Free Armor Weight - Whether you’re a mage or a fighter, this is a decent pickup. Fighters are able to break their softcap for armor weight with it by 1kg, and mages are functionally given many skill points that they otherwise would have had to spend to meet their armor weight.
  5. Physical Resist - +0.5% physical resist x 4 = 2% damage reduction versus players AND AI. Pretty significant returns on investment versus other masteries such as +0.375 blunt.
  6. Race shouts/warcries - Certain racial abilities are high impact and fight deciding. Thursar lifesteal gives incredible value. Increasing the duration of the alvarin warcry makes yours outshine un-specialized shouts. If your racial abilities are character defining, make use of them.

blocks.html:
Offsetting attributes and skills points is a viable strategy to maximize usage of the mastery system. For example, there exists +0.2kg free armor weight mastery gifts which total 1kg. For a mage, this is the equivalent of ~20 armor training points. Taking these gifts avoids an 11-point investment in the skill-point nebulae while retaining the prerequisite bonuses of +1 strength and +6 kg carry weight.

Similarly, let’s say your character has maximum intelligence, but you need strength points. Invest in the +intelligence tree anyway, and you can now reallocate those extra attribute points into strength. This effectively turns +intelligence into +strength.

Stacking certain masteries is very desirable. For example, +2% physical resist and +2% AI resist gives a +4% resist to AI damage in total. However, they are likely stacking and multiplicative (although this remains unconfirmed yet). Combine that with trinkets, clade gifts that reduce damage, akh bond, and defensive stance, and you can have a supremely tanky character.

Another example of stacking masteries to compound their effect is +0.5% mana regeneration, -0.5% spell cost, and +mana. All three of these, in effect, allow you to cast more spells. However, all 3 of them together combine their effects and actually give a greater boost than when the effects are isolated. For example, +2.5% mana regeneration on a mana pool of 100 is 2.5% better. Now do +2.5% mana regeneration on a mana pool for 110 - and that mana regen is effectively 10% stronger than otherwise.

That said, it is important to actually put in the effort to max out your tree. Unmastered characters will always be suboptimal compared to a fully built one. Mastery didn’t just augment the power of characters- it forces you to participate or you will be left behind.

Titles

There are a total of 20 unique mastery titles to be earned. While maximum mastery point benefit comes from hitting only level 110 mastery level, the cap on the system is 1000, giving players with too much time on their hands the opportunity to cheese their way to the highest levels for the leaderboards.

Here are the titles and their corresponding mastery level requirement:

The Capable - 10

The Proficient - 20

The Skillful - 30

The Determined - 40

The Accomplished - 50

The Experienced - 60

The Seasoned - 70

The Weathered - 80

The Persistent - 90

The Steadfast - 100

The Resolute - 105

The Enduring - 110

The Relentless - 200

The Unwavering - 300

The Masterful - 400

The Lasting - 500

The Enlightened - 600

The Everlasting - 700

The Transcendent - 800

The Eternal - 1000

to break their softcap for armor weight with it by 1kg, and mages are functionally given many skill points that they otherwise would have had to spend to meet their armor weight. physical resist - +0.5% physical resist x 4 = 2% damage reduction versus players and ai. pretty significant returns on investment versus other masteries such as +0.375 blunt. race shouts/warcries - certain racial abilities are high impact and fight deciding. thursar lifesteal gives incredible value. increasing the duration of the alvarin warcry makes yours outshine un-specialized shouts. if your racial abilities are character defining, make use of them. offsetting attributes and skills points is a viable strategy to maximize usage of the mastery system. for example, there exists +0.2kg free armor weight mastery gifts which total 1kg. for a mage, this is the equivalent of ~20 armor training points. taking these gifts avoids an 11-point investment in the skill-point nebulae while retaining the prerequisite bonuses of +1 strength and +6 kg carry weight. similarly, let’s say your character has maximum intelligence, but you need strength points. invest in the +intelligence tree anyway, and you can now reallocate those extra attribute points into strength. this effectively turns +intelligence into +strength. stacking certain masteries is very desirable. for example, +2% physical resist and +2% ai resist gives a +4% resist to ai damage in total. however, they are likely stacking and multiplicative (although this remains unconfirmed yet). combine that with trinkets, clade gifts that reduce damage, akh bond, and defensive stance, and you can have a supremely tanky character. another example of stacking masteries to compound their effect is +0.5% mana regeneration, -0.5% spell cost, and +mana. all three of these, in effect, allow you to cast more spells. however, all 3 of them together combine their effects and actually give a greater boost than when the effects are isolated. for example, +2.5% mana regeneration on a mana pool of 100 is 2.5% better. now do +2.5% mana regeneration on a mana pool for 110 - and that mana regen is effectively 10% stronger than otherwise. the exact meta behind mastery trees is not fully discovered yet. it may take years to understand what is most optimal. that said, it is important to actually put in the effort to max out your tree. unmastered characters will always be suboptimal compared to a fully built one. mastery didn’t just augment the power of characters- it forces you to participate or you will be left behind. titles there are a total of 20 unique mastery titles to be earned. while maximum mastery point benefit comes from hitting only level 110 mastery level, the cap on the system is 1000, giving players with too much time on their hands the opportunity to cheese their way to the highest levels for the leaderboards. here are the titles and their corresponding mastery level requirement: the capable - 10 the proficient - 20 the skillful - 30 the determined - 40 the accomplished - 50 the experienced - 60 the seasoned - 70 the weathered - 80 the persistent - 90 the steadfast - 100 the resolute - 105 the enduring - 110 the relentless - 200 the unwavering - 300 the masterful - 400 the lasting - 500 the enlightened - 600 the everlasting - 700 the transcendent - 800 the eternal - 1000 an excel sheet of the mastery system: mastery level xp requirement. levels 87+ might be 1 or 2 xp points off due to rounding, which could compound to a bit bigger values at later levels.

blocks.html:
Dagger Veela

EDIT: You can choose to SWAP PSYCHE FOR INT due to akh bond changes

The role of this character is to dive mages, kill fleeing enemies, and to harass/draw attention away from the enemy group. This version is built for meta dungeons - with 100 ritualism so that you can have a risen 125 white bear. Potion utilization is a necessity, as diving often means getting put to low HP without any other support. Round out potion utilization with trinkets. Optionally, you may drop rituals and put necromancy spells to 70 and add ecumenical at 100 for earthquake. In the dungeon version, 30 ecu is used for self purify and corrupt/mindblast. You will also notice a lack of anatomy on this build. That is due to anatomy overall being not amazing. This being an end-game build, you should be using potions, friendly mages, and HoT food to recover. If you really need anatomy, get a good skillpoints neck.

blocks.html:
Spear Veela + Direwolf MA.

  • Uses a direwolf for minimum investment. One of the best MA mounts. Due to you not having room, for controlled aiming, your goal is to hug enemy mounts and poke them this way.
  • Naturally trinkets dramatically increase the power of this build. The recommended approach is to getting FAW to boost leg armor.
  • 20 ecu is for purify and mindblast. Use wisely.
  • Age 31 to near maxed strength, but optimized dex/con. With this build you can use a 119 strength longbow.

Your longbow is a spongewood/dense crepite recurve long at 28%

  • If you get a really baller necklace with high skill points you can consider going into aiming technique/controlled aiming
  • Recognize you are a budget MA without controlled aiming. Play accordingly.

blocks.html:
Sidoian Lance / Mounted Mage. Uses risen clothos maidens. Has good offensive magic. Benefits from % pierce trinkets the most. Doesn't particularly need extra attributes or skill points. Sub out endurance for swimming if you want some weird get-out-of-jail free card, otherwise endurance is great for reducing mercy time in case you get shot on your mount, as well as a nice passive regen boost.

Important - this build is specifically not built with an armor set in mind. Adjust the armor training level to your desired build. The ideal is pansar scale + huskweave khurite splinted imo.

blocks.html:
Thursar Tindremene Fighter + Earthquake.

This build is a fully built thursar foot fighter with the addition of high psyche and earthquake. Earthquake gives strong utility versus mounteds who get surprised when a steel thursar puts them on their ass. The psyche gives rather strong magic defense, especially when combined with properly utilized adamant. Flesh out anatomy with your amulet.

Optionally swap to hammers (and adjust masteries) to fully counter mounteds/heavy armor.

blocks.html:
Thursar Sidoian Lykiator Lancer/Weakspot MA

This is a supreme strong beastmaster MA build which maximizes pierce damage and has very strong sustain.

This hits extremely hard with lances. It also has chase potential versus enemy mounteds with the bow. This is a hunter killer build which can dominate the battlefield. Requires many game sense on when to swap between lance and bow. Watch out for earthquake.

  • Relies on other characters to supply with lykiators
  • This build is currently tuned for platescale/ironfur khurite splinted. Update heavy armor training a little for more blunt defense.
  • Extremely benefits from +22% pierce rings
  • Benefits a lot from +8 raw strength rings to bring the asym strength from 125 to 133.
  • Lykiators + beastmastery relies on 2 main abilities: chase instinct for chasing/fleeing, and active regeneration for strong HP sustainability
  • The lykiator beastmastery abilities generate many hunger. Player carcass is great to feed to counteract this.
  • Benefits pretty nicely from a +28 skillpoint amulet to round out defensive stance. If you get a +78 skillpoint amulet you can alter masteries and drop the skill point tree in favor of thirst/defenses
  • Relies on thursar passive regeneration for healing. Bring a good potion just in case, anyway.
  • Works with Thursar Kallard too.

Veela Spearman + Longbowman.

Maximize usage of runner's high to armor pierce. Tactically choose when to swap between bows and spears. Round out anatomy and endurance with amulet skillpoint bonuses. Requires +22% pierce rings, and ideally at least +1 raw dex.

blocks.html:
Skinny Sheevra Mage

A high skill cap tanky mage which has access to the majority of magic. Stack defense trinkets and use a 9% ecu damage necklace.

Use mental leech to recover mana.

Religiously use brace.

Pansar scale + bloodsilk is the peak armor, but feel free to use platescale + bloodsilk for normal pvp.

Ritualism can be dropped for swimming or spiritism if desired.

blocks.html:
Hammer Veela + Earthquake

Anti-Armor 1h maceman which excels at bopping targets for big damage. One distinct advantage of this build is it can use a kamikaze horse to earthquake a mounted player and then locks him out of remounting with the 1h mace.

Ideally use 1h tindremic messing war clubs for optimal gameplay.

Can wear nearly full steel/ironfur; add a free-armor-weight amulet if you want steel legs too.

blocks.html: Clothos/Ormek Maiden Dominator. Uses high end spiders. Very lethal. Takes many APM/skill/microing to be really good at.
blocks.text: Clothos/Ormek Maiden Dominator. Uses high end spiders. Very lethal. Takes many APM/skill/microing to be really good at.

blocks.html:
Sheevra Longbow Hybrid

Uses 115 strength longbows. Synergizes incredibly well with the armor pierce from Runner's High. Has enough mana for tons of self heals, offensive corrupts, and lightnings. Focus on Pierce > Raw Strength > Raw Dex > HP > Mana > Stamina for rings. Uses ritual pets for force multiplication. Has earthquake to dismount. This is a strong and enjoyable build when played to its strengths.

guides.title: Off Meta Builds
guides.summary: Experimental and specialized character templates for players who prefer unusual combinations, niche roles, and adaptable playstyles.

blocks.html:
Thurkhur Solo PK Lancer. Uses Taur Dogs and spears to dismount prey and then sic the taur dog on them. Uses lifesteal + styg + pots to regenerate HP. Armor weight is calibrated for plate scale / ironfur khurite splinted, offering decent dismount protection.

Age 26 max height is a viable alternative to this. That version has more damage bonus and HP at a slight cost to speed. This variant can also wear full tindremic steel without trinket.

That version has more damage bonus and HP at a slight cost to speed. This variant can also wear full tindremic steel without trinket.

Pure Sarducaan mounted mage. 266 mana without trinkets. Very good mana regen. Semi-foot viable in groups if you know how to block or invest in good gear. Sub balance for blocking if desired. Sub balance for elementalism if desired. Sub rituals for a living pet if desired. Adjust heavy armor training to your desired armor weight.

EDIT: Drop sprinting for 100 ecu.

Mounted MA Hybrid. Horse killer, PvEr, support-type. This build is heavily flexible. The iteration you see here is wheelchair-only. Ground skills can be added if desired.

blocks.html: Bulging Sheevra MM - Foot viable. On paper this vanilla build sucks. With skadite+ trinkets it is fantastic. 426 movement speed so faster than most melee. Highest mana potential of any build (just eat some blood kua to go obese for 420 movement speed). Good HP. "Oh shit" clade gifts. Risen mount that doubles as a combat pet. A little lackluster in the solo realm, but overall doable. Cannot emphasize enough how important trinkets are to increase skills and HP. If you want to focus on foot stuff more but retain MM, go age 50. If you REALLY want to focus on foot, go age 31. You will be wearing light armor so you need to know how to parry.

blocks.html:
Dark Archer Mage Hybrid

This is a very skill based build which is intended for group play. This is a support mage which uses bow as its offensive tool, and as backup if you run out of mana. Archery has an incredible high skill cieling, especially when on foot, so only the best of the best are going to be able to maximize the usage of a build like this.

For combat abilities, The recommended approach is to force shot, rejuvenation, mana regeneration, stamina regeneration, and brace. Since you utilize 3 resource pools (hp/stamina/mana), maximizing them is critical.

This build does NOT have reliable dismounting capabilities. It can act as a super budget mounted archer, but that is not reliable.

This photo is trinketless. You need to get good trinkets. Ideally you get high attribute point, max pierce, max mana, max hp rings. Ideally you also get high ecu damage, and physical defense necklace too, with many skill points. The better the trinkets, the better this build becomes. 20%+ pierce rings are highly recommended.

The current stat setup allows for platescale/huskweave mage armor, which is rather tanky + a greywood round shield for when you are dove by a veela. Tailor your armor training to the gear you are wearing.

For ritualism The recommended approach is to a tanky pet that isn't too low such as a risen white bear. This pet will act as your self-peels, and is a force multiplier in group fights. Do not send it in to die willy nilly. You can also choose to drop ritualism for 100 endurance, or 62 endurance/50 swimming for that extra utility.

Edit: made a mistake with the masteries. Drop 6 from your choice and add that to +effective archery strength

blocks.html:
Jungle Hunter -

A highly specialized ganking build which uses dual hunter lizards to almost immediately backstab and kill any single target while on the ground. The goal is to hyper-focus individual targets so hard that they do not have a chance at counterplay. This is a veela so targets cannot escape. The goal is to dive with both hunter lizards while stabbing away (or holding on them if they are parry-whoring). The most important combo is Sneak Attack + Toxic Bite, which does BIG damage, even through steel. The hunter lizards will require micromanagement to effectively continue DPSing targets.

The logic of using melee is because it is the highest DPS in addition to maximizing hunter lizard focus regeneration, while also keeping hunter lizards from being focused. If they focus hunter lizards, you stab. If they focus you, hunter lizards get free combo hits off.

This build is the closest equivalent to an "assassination rogue". The recommended approach is to using splinted or banded leggings so that you do not have heavy crunchy metal footsteps. This helps maintain the element of surprise and gets the hunter lizard combo off more consistently.

Pierce/HP rings are highly recommended. At least 50 skillpoints on a gold amulet helps a lot in giving you more potion utilization or anatomy (depending on your access to good potions). Use a +49 dominate or taming amulet to gather these.

This build has 2 notable shortcomings:

  1. It has no anti-mounted capability. You will either be forced to rely on teammates or an opponent royally messing up to dismount them.
  2. Healing is limited. There is no player healing, so you will require either a good amulet with skill points, HoT food, good potions, or other players who can heal you. Hunter lizard healing can be done with the Active Regeneration beastmastery ability, however.

utilization or anatomy (depending on your access to good potions). use a +49 dominate or taming amulet to gather these. this build has 2 notable shortcomings: it has no anti-mounted capability. you will either be forced to rely on teammates or an opponent royally messing up to dismount them. healing is limited. there is no player healing, so you will require either a good amulet with skill points, hot food, good potions, or other players who can heal you. hunter lizard healing can be done with the active regeneration beastmastery ability, however. khurite skele mage (post sarducaa patch). wears over 21kg of armor. has 37.5% base mana regen no matter armor weight. very tanky. add +hp and +mana rings with raw dex/int for max effect. swap erudite and probably max psyche clades for "southerner" if it is needed.  double hunter lizard skinny mage uses double hunter lizard with sneak attack + toxic bite. functions as a full ecu mage otherwise. amulet and cutting armor weight will likely be needed for other magic schools. does require 20-30 taming amulet/dom to sustain. conversely you can drop some armor training to get taming. can also do level 110 + 110 hunter lizards alternatively. tindremene paladin build. focused on melee, but has relatively strong magic capabilities. add khurite to the mix for more chase and escape potential. swap endurance and sprinting for necromancy and ritualism if you want to specialize in necro pets. can go sarducaan for more focus on magic and smaller height. human daggermage. has respectable damage bonus and can hold its own in a fight in the right hands. remember that you're a mage first and a dagger user second. this is probably rather off-meta, so tune it to your environment. uses 12kg sets (not bad!). human dominator tank mage. runs stout/fit/lean (you need to have points in strength) to wear steel armor. relatively mobile. uses clothos or ormek maidens as its utility. this is more of a midline mage build that is heavily resistant to being dove by enemies because of the ultra heavy armor. likely off-meta, but excels in certain niches. oghmir railgunner. uses horses + beastmastery to haul your fat ass around. you have 1 mana pool so aim well and strip naked to rest when out-of-mana. pair with free-armor-weight necklaces and ideally +9% spiritism damage, plus +8 raw int rings. definitely off meta but when hitting the right targets (low psyche or enemy pets) it is absolutely devastating. can choose to go skeletal for much more maneuverability at the cost of hp. updated dagger mage. high skill cap build. use at your own risk. this version is fit, but you can go stout for more mana/tankiness at the cost of speed, or lean for speed at the cost of mana. has enough elementalism for ember, conflagration, and shock. can swap endurance and 40 points in other skills for ritualism if desired. hunter lizard jungle ma ganker uses beastmastery + weakspot archery to kill individual targets. micromanage the hunter lizard with sneak attack + toxic bite. this build assumes you have a ~+40 taming trinket. if you don't have a taming neck, sap points from defensive stance and probably vitalism. extra skillpoints from your combat amulet should go into defensive stance. if you get dismounted you are a budget mage or foot archer until the stamina pool runs out. this is a very specialized build. uses guides.summary: Compare the playable clades by physical profile, signature gifts, common roles, advantages, and limitations before committing to a build.

Compare the playable clades by physical profile, signature gifts, common roles, advantages, and limitations before committing to a build.

First, a visual guide to the phenotypes of the different clades:
blocks.text: Compare the playable clades by physical profile, signature gifts, common roles, advantages, and limitations before committing to a build. First, a visual guide to the phenotypes of the different clades:

blocks.html:
Alvarin

The Alvarin consist of the Sheevra and the Veela and are related to the elf archetype. Even the name Alvarin comes from the Scandinavian root word “alv”, which means elf. These enigmatic groups originate on the continent of Lykia/Urmothâr to the southeast of Myrland and they only have a small presence on myrland. Their small stature, affinity for magic, innate stamina bonuses, and nimbleness makes them ideal for magic, light infantry, and rogue-type characters. They also excel as masters of the environment.

  • The Sheevra are dark cave elves. They are more sophisticated than their Veela cousins, with a greater focus on magic and alchemy. Their high intellect and psyche allow them to excel as mages. Sheevra characters are viable even as paladins or deathknights.
  • The Veela are primitive jungle elves. They are rarely seen with more than a loincloth and primal weapons. These are the fastest characters possible.
  • Both the Sheevra and Veela are animistic in nature and worship spirits known as Anam. Sheevra are capable of molding inorganic matter to their will, while Veela can mold organic matter. This does not have notable gameplay uses yet.

Defining PvP Clade Gifts:

blocks.html:
• Aerialist - gives Alvarin a stark advantage against non-Alvarin when it comes to jumping and terrain navigation. This greatly reduces fall damage and can even jump out of most T3 strongholds safely.
  • Alvarin sight - a built-in wallhack that gives unparalleled awareness. Especially useful in dungeons to scout for enemies. Turn 45 degrees away from where you want to see for maximum viewing distance.
  • Alvarin warcry - a powerful speed boost for the character and the group. Useful for both chase and escape.
  • Combat Leap - somewhat of a luxury, but it allows Alvarin to be effective in combat in uneven or hard-to-navigate terrain.
  • Naiad - makes Alvarin undisputed masters of water.
  • Resting pulse - makes Alvarin stamina recovery unmatched.
  • Runner/Sprinter - in conjunction with high dexterity give Alvarins the highest speed possible in game.
  • Runners High - Extra stamina regen and speed on a quick cooldown is highly useful.

Ideal Roles:

Sheevra are fantastic dagger mages, bulging mages, skeletal mages, and even obese mages. The high int/psyche cap combined with the dexterity and environmental clade gifts makes Sheevra mages the most survivable of all mages. Sheevra paladins are viable too, although they tend to need trinkets to round out their stats, and their mana pool isn’t competitive compared to a human.

Veela are the ideal chaser and diver. They are incredibly fast with decent damage bonus and can wear heavy armor. Combined with damage % rings, these characters are an ideal mage killer. Warclubs, daggers, spears, and swords are very competitive on a Veela fighter.

Disadvantages:

Alvarin have a difficult time competing in melee against thursars or oghmir due to the damage and hit point difference. Alvarin tend to be weaker to burst damage than other races due to lower hit point pool as well. The mana regen differences compared to dedicated human mages makes alvarin fall off a bit in larger scale engagements where mana management counts more.

blocks.html:
Human

The humans are comprised of Kallardians, Khurites, Sarducaans, Sidoians, and Tindremenes. This versatile race can wielding powerful magic while maintaining proficiency in other forms of combat. What they lack in straight physical power is made up for in their ability to take on multiple roles. While it is true they are considered a “jack of all trades'', they truly excel in hybridized forms of warfare.

  • Kallardians are fundamental Nords, with a proud martial culture built upon strength.
  • Khurites are broadly based on east and central Asian cultures, and they have a series of nomadic and non-nomadic tribes in a loose confederation.
  • Sarducaans are the Middle Eastern analogs, with a magic focused society based on the continent of Sarducaa to the west of Myrland.
  • Sidoians are former slaves of the Shinarians, and have developed a highly spiritual civilization in the wake of the collapse of Shinaria.
  • Tindremenes, inspired by ancient Romans and Greeks, cling to a decaying empire in the Northwest of Myrland and on an island to the north.

Defining PvP Clade Gifts:

blocks.html:
• Cleric - useful because it gives paladins/deathknights and mages competitive mana regeneration over non-humans.
  • Human Warcry - Used in conjunction with tactician to allow for exceptionally magic AoE damage to pass through a friendly group while nuking enemies.
  • Mental Power - A free cleanse that also mitigates magic damage.
  • Roughrider - Opens up many free skill points for mounted hybrid builds.
  • Shamanistic - A quality of life gift which makes humans never have to eat.
  • Tactician - One of the strongest clade gifts in game- is used to prevent friendly fire. Particularly useful with spells like fireball, lightning bolt, and auw surge.
  • Versatile - Gives a big skill point advantage over non-humans, especially when combined with the Erudite gift.

Ideal Roles:

Sarducaans and Tindremenes excel at paladin/deathknight and mage gameplay. The general idea is to be a fully functional melee character, but also have enough mana to heal, and to do burst damage. This is particularly effective for groups which rely on dumping spells such as auw surge at the beginning of a fight- the human shoots off his heavy AoE and then switches to melee until his mana pool regenerates. Sarducaans are arguably the best character to use for hybrid mounted archer ritualists as they have the skill pool to support it, the smallest size, and respectable magic abilities.

Sidoians have a smaller attribute pool, but due to their high intelligence cap they are excellent mounted obese mages. Excess attributes tend to go towards strength which is irrelevant for a mounted mage.

blocks.html:
Disadvantages:

Humans will not match the speed of the alvarin, the melee prowess of a thursar, or the intelligence of an oghmir. More specialized roles will outcompete humans- alvarin will be able to flee and chase better, thursars will be better in melee, and oghmirs will do more magic damage and be more survivable. This means the strength of a human is best complimented in group gameplay. While a solo human is possible to make work, it is when humans are weakest.

blocks.html:
Oghmir

Blainn and Huergar make up the Oghmir clade. The closest mythological analog for the Oghmir are dwarves. Unlike in other fantasy settings, Oghmir are actually humans that were evolutionarily and magically modified from humanity. A goddess named Oghma is likely responsible for imbuing them with their current form. These beings tend to live underground or far north. Oghmir are stout and intelligent, with great recovery skills. They excel at being small tanky fighters as well as potent mounted mages.

  • The Blainn are a type of frost dwarf. They tend to live in the colder regions of the world and associate with the Kallards. The Blainn have the highest natural constitution and make for excellent foot fighters. While in the lore they are no longer dependent upon ichor, for gameplay reasons they are still able to consume it.
  • The Huergar are a type of magical cave dwarf. They are mostly located around the Tindremic Empire and in a place known as Gal Barag (which is preceded by the Minotaur Dungeon). They have long since sealed the entrance to Gal Barag to protect themselves from external threats. Huergar are the smartest of all clades, and serve extremely well as mages or deathknights due to having extra attribute points over Blainn.

Defining PvP Clade Gifts:

blocks.html:
• Armor Bearer and Armiger give a total of 6kg of armor weight. That enables oghmirs to wear very heavy armor with minimal downside.
  • Beer Belly - Worth 100 points of potion utilization on top of being stackable with potion utilization. Allows for exceptionally recovery with potions.
  • Inhale - Aka “crack pipe” is a potent recovery tool which can be spammed in a fight to recover lots of HP. Combine with high HP food such as blood kua meat for even better results.
  • Stoneskin - Gives a significant inherent defense worth roughly 50 points in defensive stance.
  • Strong Back - Allows hauling of far more loot than any other race.

Ideal Roles:

Oghmir are ideal for two specific melee roles: vanilla fighter and akh bond fighter. Blainn are better for regular fighters because of the more favorable stats (constitution specifically), while Huergar are ideal as akh bond fighters due to having enough extra points in psyche to cast the spell with a small investment into mental training. Both are potent and excel in group combat. It could be argued that vanilla fighters are obsolete and akh bond fighters are better, but that is still up to debate.

Huergar are also some of the best mounted mages as they have the highest intelligence of any clade possible. Their ability to nuke opponents from a horse is unrivaled. Pair with ritual pets and this becomes one of the most oppressive classes to play against.

Disadvantages:

Speed. Speed. Speed. Oghmir are slow due to their low natural dexterity and they do not have many attribute points to spare to specialize in anything else. They are one of the worst solo clades due to their low speed and reliance on ichor pipes which leaves them vulnerable.

blocks.html:
Thursar

The Thursar are a hybrid race between the humans and Risar (orcs). Thursars can come from any flavor of human, but lore-wise human society generally does not accept them. They tend to live in slums, outskirts, or Thursar-specific villages. They usually resort to brigandry or thievery due to their primitive Risar heritage as well as their social status. Thursars have an inherent aversion to magic and are susceptible to harm from it.

Defining PvP Clade Gifts:
blocks.text: Thursar The Thursar are a hybrid race between the humans and Risar (orcs). Thursars can come from any flavor of human, but lore-wise human society generally does not accept them. They tend to live in slums, outskirts, or Thursar-specific villages. They usually resort to brigandry or thievery due to their primitive Risar heritage as well as their social status. Thursars have an inherent aversion to magic and are susceptible to harm from it. Defining PvP Clade Gifts:

blocks.html:
• Adamant - Gives a potent damage reducing passive which can be flipped for magic defense at will.
  • Battlecry - Useful for initial pushes, securing kills, and otherwise boosting group damage.
  • Indefatigable - Makes Thursars use their stamina efficiently when attacking.
  • Life Steal - exceptionally potent when used in 1v1s, against pets, or against weak targets.
  • Styganthrope - The defining clade gift of Thursars. Gives a extremely amount of HP passively but with the drawback of being less healable by teammates. This is a pivotal gift which gives Thursars 1vX potential without needing to heal. Hands down the strongest 1v1 gift in game.

Ideal Roles:

Thursars are fighters. There is little room for hybridization due to low skill points and unfavorable stats. The joke of “Thursar Shaman” is a meme. Players can be a Thursar-Tindremene or Thursar-Sarducaan to have access to akh bond and ritualism as well as some supporting ecumenical, but that is as far as the clade should go. Otherwise it is ideal to go with Thursar-Khurite or Thursar-Kallard for strong melee abilities.

The best use for Thursars is 1v1 combat. Their inherent HP regeneration, high HP, and high damage bonus allows them to dominate in this sphere against all other clades. For group combat, Thursars are best utilized as a 2nd line/mage peeler role due to their size and how easy it is to focus them with magic. It is better that they are in a role where they are not relying on lots of healing and can focus on dealing damage almost strictly.

Disadvantages:

Thursars tend to be very weak to magic due to their inherently low psyche as well as with the adamant debuff. Their large character model size also makes them an easy target to hit with spells. Calling out “focus the giant thursar” is easy and most people can land hits on large characters like this. The system also includes the problem of healing reduction due to styganthrope which makes thursars a little suboptimal for group play.

straight physical power is made up for in their ability to take on multiple roles. while it is true they are considered a “jack of all trades'', they truly excel in hybridized forms of warfare. kallardians are fundamental nords, with a proud martial culture built upon strength. khurites are broadly based on east and central asian cultures, and they have a series of nomadic and non-nomadic tribes in a loose confederation. sarducaans are the middle eastern analogs, with a magic focused society based on the continent of sarducaa to the west of myrland. sidoians are former slaves of the shinarians, and have developed a highly spiritual civilization in the wake of the collapse of shinaria. tindremenes, inspired by ancient romans and greeks, cling to a decaying empire in the northwest of myrland and on an island to the north. defining pvp clade gifts:  cleric - useful because it gives paladins/deathknights and mages competitive mana regeneration over non-humans. human warcry - used in conjunction with tactician to allow for exceptionally magic aoe damage to pass through a friendly group while nuking enemies. mental power - a free cleanse that also mitigates magic damage. roughrider - opens up many free skill points for mounted hybrid builds. shamanistic - a quality of life gift which makes humans never have to eat. tactician - one of the strongest clade gifts in game- is used to prevent friendly fire. particularly useful with spells like fireball, lightning bolt, and auw surge. versatile - gives a big skill point advantage over non-humans, especially when combined with the erudite gift. ideal roles: sarducaans and tindremenes excel at paladin/deathknight and mage gameplay. the general idea is to be a fully functional melee character, but also have enough mana to heal, and to do burst damage. this is particularly effective for groups which rely on dumping spells such as auw surge at the beginning of a fight- the human shoots off his heavy aoe and then switches to melee until his mana pool regenerates. sarducaans are arguably the best character to use for hybrid mounted archer ritualists as they have the skill pool to support it, the smallest size, and respectable magic abilities. sidoians have a smaller attribute pool, but due to their high intelligence cap they are excellent mounted obese mages. excess attributes tend to go towards strength which is irrelevant for a mounted mage. disadvantages: humans will not match the speed of the alvarin, the melee prowess of a thursar, or the intelligence of an oghmir. more specialized roles will outcompete humans- alvarin will be able to flee and chase better, thursars will be better in melee, and oghmirs will do more magic damage and be more survivable. this means the strength of a human is best complimented in group gameplay. while a solo human is possible to make work, it is when humans are weakest. oghmir blainn and huergar make up the oghmir clade. the closest mythological analog for the oghmir are dwarves. unlike in other fantasy settings, oghmir are actually humans that were evolutionarily and magically modified from humanity. a goddess named oghma is likely responsible for imbuing them with their current form. these beings tend to live underground or far north. oghmir are stout and intelligent, with great recovery skills. they excel at being small tanky fighters as well as potent mounted mages. the blainn are a type of frost dwarf. they tend to live in the colder regions of the world and associate with the kallards. the blainn have the highest natural constitution and make for excellent foot fighters. while in the lore they are no longer dependent upon ichor, for gameplay reasons they are still able to consume it. the huergar are a type of magical cave dwarf. they are mostly located around the tindremic empire and in a place known as gal barag (which is preceded by the minotaur dungeon). they have long since sealed the entrance to gal barag to protect themselves from external threats. huergar are the smartest of all clades, and serve extremely well as mages or deathknights due to having extra attribute points over blainn. defining pvp clade gifts:  armor bearer and armiger give a total of 6kg of armor weight. that enables oghmirs to wear very heavy armor with minimal downside. beer belly - worth 100 points of potion utilization on top of being stackable with potion utilization. allows for exceptionally recovery with potions. inhale - aka “crack pipe” is a potent recovery tool which can be spammed in a fight to recover lots of hp. combine with high hp food such as blood kua meat for even better results. stoneskin - gives a significant inherent defense worth roughly 50 points in defensive stance. strong back - allows hauling of far more loot than any other race. ideal roles: oghmir are ideal for two specific melee roles: vanilla fighter and akh bond fighter. blainn are better for regular fighters because of the more favorable stats (constitution specifically), while huergar are ideal as akh bond fighters due to having enough extra points in psyche to cast the spell with a small investment into mental training. both are potent and excel in group combat. it could be argued that vanilla fighters are obsolete and akh bond fighters are better, but that is still up to debate. huergar are also some of the best mounted mages as they have the highest intelligence of any clade possible. their ability to nuke opponents from a horse is unrivaled. pair with ritual pets and this becomes one of the most oppressive classes to play against. disadvantages: speed. speed. speed. oghmir are slow due to their low natural dexterity and they do not have many attribute points to spare to specialize in anything else. they are one of the worst solo clades due to their low speed and reliance on ichor pipes which leaves them vulnerable. thursar the thursar are a hybrid race between the humans and risar (orcs). thursars can come from any flavor of human, but lore-wise human society generally does not accept them. they tend to live in slums, outskirts, or thursar-specific villages. they usually resort to brigandry or thievery due to their primitive risar heritage as well as their social status. thursars have an inherent aversion to magic and are susceptible to harm from it. defining pvp clade gifts:  adamant - gives a potent damage reducing passive which can be flipped for magic defense at will. battlecry - useful for initial pushes, securing kills, and otherwise boosting group damage. indefatigable - makes thursars use their stamina efficiently when attacking. life steal - exceptionally potent when used in 1v1s, against pets, or against weak targets. styganthrope - the defining clade gift of thursars. gives a extremely amount of hp passively but with the drawback of being less healable by teammates. this is a pivotal gift which gives thursars 1vx potential without needing to heal. hands down the strongest 1v1 gift in game. ideal roles: thursars are fighters. there is little room for hybridization due to low skill points and unfavorable stats. the joke of “thursar shaman” is a meme. players can be a thursar-tindremene or thursar-sarducaan to have access to akh bond and ritualism as well as some supporting ecumenical, but that is as far as the clade should go. otherwise it is ideal to go with thursar-khurite or thursar-kallard for strong melee abilities. the best use for thursars is 1v1 combat. their inherent hp regeneration, high hp, and high damage bonus allows them to dominate in this sphere against all other clades. for group combat, thursars are best utilized as a 2nd line/mage peeler role due to their size and how easy it is to focus them with magic. it is better that they are in a role where they are not relying on lots of healing and can focus on dealing damage almost strictly. disadvantages: thursars tend to be very weak to magic due to their inherently low psyche as well as with the adamant debuff. their large character model size also makes them an easy target to hit with spells. calling out “focus the giant thursar” is easy and most people can land hits on large characters like this. the system also includes the problem of healing reduction due to styganthrope which makes thursars a little suboptimal for group play. comparative stats this comparative chart looks at the attribute pool, size difference, general purpose, and ratings of each clade: attribute pool is taken from the absolute maximum, accounting for minimum height and no clade gifts. take into account age for minimum and maximum height (72 for min height, 30 for max). alvarin will also change height with the long life clade. there is usually rounding with height which may display it 1 point higher or lower than the chart. the rating scale is in relation to all other clades/races. with a potentially shifting meta and balance, this chart is liable to change in the future.
