blocks.html:
• You can only do a fatality (execution) on humanoid opponents. This includes walkers.

Players receive partial invulnerability while committing a fatality

  • Sprinting out-of-combat mode does not consume stamina reserves
  • Players receive a healing penalty on bandages when they take damage of 20 or more during the timer. Pets receive a healing penalty when bandaging when they take damage of 10 or more. This effect is cumulative if taking multiple hits.
  • Adding character height also adds to character width. Tall characters can be blocked from entering certain locations because of width and not necessarily height. Take for example many death traps or mage-only entrances in houses!
  • Only the owner or a guildmate can pay the upkeep on houses/strongholds/keeps. Allies CANNOT pay the upkeep.
  • Paladin-style builds can swap to magic and keep adrenaline without losing it by simply sheathing their weapon and casting. Swapping from a weapon to fists incurs the swap penalty, which should be avoided.

Spiritism buffs do NOT persist through death. If you are living and you get a spiritism buff and die, you lose the buffs

  • Every 5 units of hunger equates to 1 food eaten
  • Using the quick swap between fists and a fist + shield does not incur an adrenaline penalty. This is important for mages who are casting with fists out and then need to defend with a shield.
  • You can search by player name or guild name on the broker to bring up all relevent listings
  • You can see the average guild member reputation at town guild stones
  • Guild wars can be ended only by the guild that declared them, or automatically if said guild runs out of funds to maintain the upkeep for it

Dispelling a portal gives a text message that tells you if the portal was opened from the living world, or the etherworld. This can help you pinpoint where the spiritist came from and went to

  • Players can report a maximum of 4 other players for murders. If another player participated but did proportionally too low of damage, they cannot be reported
  • When riding as a passenger of a mount, skills that you normally gain while riding a horse (controlled riding, swift riding, etc) raise normally
  • AI tends to have biases towards attacking certain parts of the player. For example, spiderlings hit legs the majority of the time, and sometimes torso. No observed case has shown them hit heads. You can test which parts creatures hit at what % by recording the damage they do
  • You can tell a non-combatant pet, such as a horse, to attack a target. This will cause the horse to closely follow them without doing damage
  • Using a shield + no weapon automatically applies the unarmed blocking bonus, heavily reducing the need to run the blocking skill. This is mostly applicable to mages who want a survival tool without the skill investment

• The bank in Haven city and the Haven dock are linked

Haven allows you to take up to 6 items from it to the mainland, with a combined gold value of 10g

  • Certain items, such as maalite, are blacklisted from being taken off of Haven
  • You can gain a maximum of 300 taskmaster renown on Haven
  • You can leave Haven after reaching level 5. The limit on clade levels gained is 8
  • Daggers cannot handlehit
  • Pulling a bounty defaults to targets within 5km. If none are found within this range, it is extended to 10km

blocks.html:
• If a living pet is rideable but does NOT have a young form, they can be ridden below the normal level 25. For example, a level 22 Clothos Maiden can be mounted.

Tagmaton campsites (TC building) can be opened with /bank

  • Some skills which are unlocked but at effective level 0 do not work. For example, if taming is 0, you cannot tame a horse. If passive regeneration is 0, you will not gain xp. When unlocking skills like this, be sure to raise them to at least level 1.
  • The "0.1 health regeneration" masteries are measured in ticks of 6 seconds. This maths out to 1hp/minute per node.
  • "+1.25% weakspot chance" masteries do NOT work with bows. 2% marksmanship masteries do. Do not waste extra points when building a weakspot MA.
  • When you have an extra amount of applied skillpoints and the game detects it (for example, if a secondary skill is converted into a primary in a patch), the game will pull the extra points from skills that are already assigned. One observed case received like -100 ritualism.
  • Firewall ticks 20 times. After the 12th tick, you can recast it to keep a constant wall on the ground.

• You can trade a maximum of 16 item "slots" per trade

  • Ember and hailstone do multiple damage ticks per hit. One portion is elemental (fire and cold), and the other is physical (blunt and pierce respectively).
  • Because ember and hailstone tic twice, they also accelerate the essence orb +% magic damage combo effect
  • Dying with an unequipped trinket in your inventory does not consume a charge
  • Certain static spawns can have variable spawns. For example, there are spawns that cycle randomly between urial, molva, and wolf
  • You cannot give murdercounts if you are last hit by an untamed AI

blocks.html:
• Culinariums give the "campfire" resting bonus when resting inside

Extraction materials that are dropped on the ground because the extractor is not in close proximity will generally last 30 minutes (even if the bag is partially looted)

  • Damage that is mitigated by Akh Bond does NOT deplete health reserves of the player
  • Force arrow is reduced by -knockback effects. Retreat is NOT reduced by -knockback effects
  • Oghmir pipes (inhale) health reserve damage slightly scales with the amount of effective health reserves the player has. The less reserves, the less health reserve penalty there is.
  • You can push most AI to cause it them move. Guards and many other town NPCs, however, cannot be pushed.
  • The +buff duration essence orb effect does NOT increase the duration of blood kua heal over time. It does increase the duration of magic reflect potions.

• Blue meteor spawners flash whenever they spawn orbs to pick up

The +glory essence orb effect works for tasks

  • Trolls are considered CREATURES for the purpose of essence orb luck effects
  • The "boss luck" ONLY applies to bosses which are in an arena setting and give the alert that you are fighting them. This does not apply to trolls, invasion waves, broodmother, etc

• You can place bags on your hotbar. Using the hotkey opens or closes the bag.

Bow strength needs to be EXACTLY the strength of the bow for combat abilities to work and to not incur a stam penalty. If you are even 0.01 strength over, the penalty applies

• Buildings which are destroyed offer 2880 minutes (48 hours) of time for the owner to loot

Mana reserve regeneration essence orbs DO work to regenerate kau in the etherworld. It is typically a very slow regen, however

  • Divinium equipment has a glow which imparts environmental lighting. It is somewhat like an equipped torch!

  • Observed cases show polyhedron spawners create a max of 2 waves, 3 waves, and boss. Other observed cases show it spawn without a boss. It does not seem consistent.

blocks.html:
• You can search for different tiers of essence orbs on the broker by filtering for trinket base tier. Cuprum = t1, silver = t2, gold = t3

Server restarts clear out outlaw spawns. It takes 1 hour for them to start spawning

  • There is a small cooldown of 10 minutes between taking UNCLAIMED outposts
  • When you complete the queue to login to the game, your spot is saved for 10 minutes in case you get bumped out for some reason
  • Prominence and gold upkeep + outpost income accumulate when the server is taken offline
  • All tameable pets can be dominated. Dominate-only pets will only give a prompt to dominate. You will not be given the option to tame them
  • Outpost territories give a bonus if they are in the same region as the owners keep, or if the owner zones are adjacent to zones owned by the guild that has a keep in it

blocks.html:
• While outpost bonuses are boosted by having a connected keep, multiple connected keeps under 1 guild does NOT give an extra bonus

You can spurt the Ultumeki lava pools to get rid of them

  • Structures which are building lose defense % when they are damaged. Structures which are fully built are permanently locked into their base defense value
  • Karin Mara (The Glass Furnace) deals about a small amount of damage per tick while you are inside
  • The closer you get to the center of the glass furnace, the faster and harder the ticks hit
  • Resting greybar away with the shaministic clade is NOT impacted by house nor campfire bonuses. It will restore 10 reserves every tick at the same tickrate no matter what
  • The human clade gift "Charismatic" for 5% buy/sell prices has has generous rounding for many things because it applies to both buy AND sell. For example, combat ability books that cost 10 coins will only cost 9 after the bonus

blocks.html:
• /yell allows you to chat up to 25m. /say allows you to chat up to 10m

The terrorbird beastmastery ability "Piercing Shriek" does NOT require you to target the terrorbird nor its target to work

  • You can more easily place a TC structure or house by holding interact (default R) to "place it", then hold left click to move it. This locks it in place and lets you fine tune where it is placed
  • While rotating a TC structure or house deed when placing, you can hold left control to decrease the turn radius. That enables for finer tuning of the placement
  • 40 units of Heal-over-time (HoT) food is optimal for the most health restored per unit of food eaten (thanks @Ebefar for this math)
  • 68 units of HoT food is optimal for the most amount of healing vs. the amount of food eaten (thanks @Ebefar for this math)
  • 104 units of HoT food is the hardcap of when eating more food has diminishing returns to the point of it becoming wasteful due to the time it takes to eat each unit vs. the healing provided. Avoid eating more than 104 HoT food at a time (thanks @Ebefar for this math)

guides.searchText: obscure mechanics general less obvious interactions and edge cases that the game rarely explains, collected for fast reference and practical testing. type /emote squat when riding a mount to enter a special phase where the rider hugs the mount and is less targetable certain spells are impacted by the psyche of the target- even if they are friendly. for example, mental healing works best when targetting a low psyche ally. sacrificial eruption is more effective when hitting a low psyche target as well. contrary to popular belief, longbows can weakspot- they just need to use broadhead arrows instead of longbow arrows type /loot when standing over a bag that is underground. this will take a second to activate, but it looks everything close to you. to get a good idea of your ping to the server, go to windows cmd and type- ping 51.89.234.64 - then hit enter. the strength calculation to use mounted weapons is the weapon weight x30. a 1kg weapon thus requires 30 strength to use, a 2kg requires 60, 3kg 90, etc. dexterity tooltip says it gives weakspot. this does not apply to bows. height works off of decimals - you can eat size food and it will incrementally gain. age does not follow this same pattern, and any potions drunk must be >1 age to work. stamina and mana regeneration are % based. the greater the resource pool, the proportionally faster it regenerates. "reward" capes from the escape menu can be deleted and reclaimed ad infinitum. killing a horse allows for murdercounts if the player dies soon after. this only works if the player is killed by another player, ai, or other natural causes. using the suicide button does not allow for murdercounting. wood structures have a natural 50% damage resistance. stone structures have a natural 80% damage resistance. doors can be broken into by smashing them with weapons. however, their defense is proportional to the hp of the structure. a building with 100% hp has 100% door defence. a building with 50% hp has 50% door defense. aggressive stance does not work with mounted combat. shields cause equipment hits when struck. the equation for how damage is calculated is [shield defensive stats] + [chest armor defensive stats] + [defensive stance bonuses] + [trinket bonuses] + [clade gift bonuses] + [mastery bonuses] + [magic effects such as akh bond]. the most misunderstood aspect of this is that the chest piece is always what stacks, no matter what part of the shield is struck. pet equipment, no matter the size of the animal, is uniform in weight, defense, and material cost. steel heavy campodon armor is the same as steel heavy bear armor in all regards except what it can be equipped on. arrows only consume bow durability when they hit a valid target. missing a shot does not use bow durability. risen pets always use the "medium" sized model of the creature, and never the young nor elder/alpha versions. this means they are smaller at max level than their living counterparts. pets can be flagged as in combat while mounted, gaining the 4x xp bonus. arrow velocity is reduced when it hits water - meaning there is reduced damage the longer it is in water. you can even see it shoot slowly! many spells are not impacted by the -50% mount penalty for not having mounted magery. for example, mindblast always hits for maximum, atrophy always reduces stamina by the full amount, earthquake will always dismount, and corrupt always fulfils its role of preventing healing. weapons have distance "sweet spots". in most situations, weapons do most damage when at maximum range from the target but still making contact. /loot was added as a command a long time ago but documentation for it is non-existent. use this while standing over/near loot that is stuck in collision or underground. horses have a default follow distance when pressing the follow command. double tapping the follow command causes the horse to approach you even closer, to within bag opening distance. resting in a house gives huge regeneration boosts. in a house + with a campfire is even higher. house doors can be broken down. their defense is proportional to the hp of the structure, i.e. at 100% hp, the defense is 100%, and at 50% hp, the defense is 50%. that enables attackers to break into houses while sieging to kill repairers. spur on is a beastmastery ability which increases the stamina regen of a mount, and forces them into 4th speed. this is one of the few mechanics which allows mounted mages to adjust their speed mid cast. all resources in game have an associated rgba color value. this is observable via the color of potions made with an item. emotes can be maintained while running. do the emote, don't move, and then hit your autorun key. this has some rp elements, but also messes with your hitbox a little weapon swapping is faster than manually unsheathing the weapon. that enables for quicker casting swaps. using a potion with a weapon out is slow- swap weapons or sheathe first to speed up the process! capes are mostly aesthetics only. however, certain capes have a large profile and can actual be used to hide animations and trick enemies. proper camera movement is required for this. miasma is a spell that counts as poison damage, and is thus impacted by affects that reduce poison (such as the thursar clade gift) elementalism spells are either pure magic damage, or they have a physical component to them. many water spells are modified by slash damage, some earth spells impacted by blunt, and ice are modified by pierce. the spell tooltip will contain the info needed to know this. some tasks have a "quick completion" bonus that doubles the amount of xp given. soldier tasks lose this bonus upon death, while hunter, foraging, and fishing, do not. bounties are completely lost on death. the alvarin warcry also increases jump height, and likely increases weakspot chance "bleed" effects are removed by using a bandage your strength is taken into account for blocking/parry damage reduction. the lower your strength, the more chip damage occurs shields have an inherent defense bonus versus ai which has unparryable attacks (i.e. mino king, sators) miasma gives mental offense xp per tick. using it to splash on big groups of mobs is fast to level it there is a small microphone icon next to players names when they are in game and have voip enabled. if there is no microphone, it either means their voip is disabled or they are alt tabbed the control undead spell lasts for 15 minutes on player-made walkers. re-casting control undead on them refreshes this timer without the need to summon a new walker. earthquake dismounts when it is self-cast and hits the target, or when it directly hits the target. if it hits the targets mount, it does not dismount. this is likely a bug when parrying with a shield, the defense stats of the shield are added to the defense calculation, resulting in heavily reduced damage every skill with an attribute bonus has a chance of raising that attribute everytime that skill is used. for example, the crusher appliance has +intelligence and +strength, meaning you can gain both when crushing! the lower level an attribute, the easier it is to raise it the thursar battlecry and oghmir rock solid are clade gifts which act as taunts for nearby untamed ai. tactician only works for your pet if you are guilded. unguilded pets do not receive the bonus. every 2 points in the height stat is equal to 1 size, and thus costs 1 attribute point. max engineering and advanced engineering makes a character build 5x faster. structures that are under construction lose a high portion of their defensive bonus. for example, a medium house goes from 80% defense to 62%. the normal defensive values are restored once the structure is completed. shield bashing a target that is jumping gives them a large boost. shield bashing distance is determined by the strength of the basher housing give a significant boost to regeneration when resting inside of them. you can tell if this bonus is active if the logout timer in that spot is 10 seconds. 10 seconds = yes, 120 seconds = no. accepting the gold from a cod >10k gold will actually stack all of the gold into 1 pile. players can have a stack of gold up to at least 99,999 depositing a stack of gold >10k will force the stack to split into 10k + the remaining. for example, if you deposit a stack of 45k, it becomes 10k + 35k. it is possible for ai to fight each other. for example, if you are fighting a creature with an aoe attack such as alchemist bowman and the bowman hits a bear with its explosive shot, the bear will attack the bowman if enough aggro is generated. you can choose which side to dismount on by targeting the left or right side of your pet. living pets change their size at level 26 to become an adult. they change their size again at 100 to become "alpha/elder". pets must be a minimum of level 26 to mount, with a few exceptions like terrorbirds. risen are always the adult (but not elder/alpha) model. mental projectile is one of the few offensive spells that always penetrates magic reflection (without expending it). certain spells will always kill and skip mercy mode - mental projectile, mindblast, and shock are a few. melee can kill and skip mercy mode if the damage is high enough. usually this is only really seen when a 2h maul hits a mage. zoology lores give 20% damage mitigation and 20% damage bonus to living pets under your control. risen does not gain a benefit from zoology. getting hit by physical damage while banadaging lowers the amount healed at the end of the timer. minor bandages take the largest hp loss penalty, while regular and major bandages are supposed to have a reduced penalty. fall damage scales with inventory/equipment weight. the more weight, the more damage. guild ranks are gained by capturing supply towers and spending prominence. they can also be lost by losing a keep, surrendering a wardec, or running out of upkeep in the chancerry. arrows that hit a body of water lose velocity and damage the further they travel in water. in beta there was a good chance at lightning strikes during rainy weather. this could hit players. it has been disabled, but may return in the future. it takes approximately 3 hours for a pet to go from 0 to 1000 hunger. looting a war combatant target (orange) also flags the looter as war combatant and can be killed by guard. this doesn't apply to bystanders who see the bag as blue, although they may flag for looting blue bags. the broker has several backend keywords that aren't readily apparent, particularly with trinkets (which have hidden names). an amulet of tukh indicates it is a mounted archery amulet - try searching tukh on the broker! if there are for some reason multiple banks in your vacinity, /bank will only open the nearest one. when guards do significant damage (possibly any) to an npc such as an outlaw, the loot drop and clade xp from that npc is disabled. houses are bound to your steam/epic account. ownership remains valid even after a character is deleted. concentration (chance to resist spell casting interruption) is only 50% as effective on mount as it is on foot. this caps out at 50% with full concentration skill and all masteries. all mounts regen stamina and the same rate. mount swim speed is 1/4th of the land speed. weapon skills not only increase average damage, they also increase the amount of stamina a successful parry restores. gem effect luck has a greater impact than people realize- with 0% luck an amethyst can only hit 6% [pierce/blunt/slash] -> with max effect luck this raises the cap to 7%. magic xp gained per cast is based on the base cost of the spell, before reductions such as mental focus. typing /? gives a chat response of most chat commands. certain elements of the ui can be pre-patch. for example, there is an old set of pet command icons that are only obtainable by downloading a prepatch ui file! pet bandaging heals for a flat amount based on the total hp of the pet. the more hp, the more healing. zoology lores as a general rule give a damage bonus versus the target. an exception to this are the "simian" lores, which are the lores for the player characters. placeable refining ovens are restricted to keeps only, for some stupid reason. spells have a hidden "alignment" to them. good spells don't turn you grey, while "evil" spells turn you grey on cast. this is a legacy assignment from mo1 that was just hidden for mo2 but still has gameplay impacts. pet equipment weight and defenses are uniform across all creature types. steel campodon armor weighs the same as steel horse armor. pets must be within 30m of the player to gain combat xp. wood from the lightest/least dense to the heaviest/most dense: spongewood -> whitewood -> firmwood -> greywood -> dapplewood -> brownwood -> blackwood -> ironwood -> stonewood*. density impacts stats like weight, durability, etc. the subsisting skill at level 100 cuts the mercy mode timer by 50% and increases the hp regained drastically. you can estimate your location on the in-game map (hotkey m) by looking for nearby named tc structures and control towers. lance damage follows the laws of general relativity. running into a lance does massively increased damage, while running away from it reduces it by a lot. loot is localized. a monster in one location might have drops that one is another location does not. the prime example of this are camp sators compared to temple sators - the temple sators are far more lucrative! left clicking your pets icon opens the pet menu. (thanks @wyndorn) the weekly server restart is generally at 2am est/6am gmt on wednesdays. alvarin move speed clades do not work in water or while mounted a house that is being built progressively gains defense % as it is built, up to 80% defense when fully built. houses walls progressive build every 25% hp that is constructed. achievement progress (and likely statistics) are shared between all characters on your account. unguilded houses can be sieged at any time, while houses with a claiming stone must have a declaration to siege. reputation of 0 is enough to enter a city. -1 is where you become detested. guilds can only be wardec'd if they have at least 2 murderers in them. if a non-war target horse rider has a wardec target passenger, the horse itself can still be targetted by guard towers. war flag takes precedent over red flag. a war target that is red will flag attackers in town as war combatants. this remains unconfirmed, but local grey flag supercedes war combatant status (but does not display). i.e. if someone heals a red friend in town, orange flagged players can then attack the healer. test at your own risk. players killed by a boulder will have all of their weapons and armor completely obliterated. risen pets can be left anywhere in the world and they will passively gain experience as long as you remain logged on daily tasks can be opened on any day and saved/turned in any other day- but the day you turn in it, it counts as "completed" for that specific day! soldier and hunter tasks lose their "quick execution" bonus when you die. the forager task does not lose this bonus. bounty tasks always disappear when you die, even if they are completed. weight gain is usually impacted by health reserves, but players can gain weight by eating over your stamina reserve cap. amulet defense stats are calculated after all other values, meaning they are more effective on light armor than on heavy. durability damage done to weapons is based on what type of material it is hitting. hitting a naked takes basically no dura while hitting plate armor incurs many dura loss. the person who gets the very last hit on an ai sees its bag almost immediately. anyone else sees it approximately a second later. this gives looting priority to the last-hitter. likewise to the last one, loot luck and rare trinket gem luck on proc for the person doing the last hit. if you are grouped and one person is running luck rings, let them get the last hits- especially on bosses! armor and inventory weight update at a delayed rate. this means its possible to pick up absurd amounts of weight and move for a few moments before encumbrance hits. the corrupt spell only cancels out bandages when the bandage finishes. a bandage timer of 10 seconds while corrupted for 9 seconds left will still heal. equerries that are destroyed will still have pets in them when a new one is placed in that same location. multiple equerries that are in close proximity can be on the same "micro node", and share pet stockpiles. the hp/s mastery gift in the top right mastery tree do not gain the extra stygantrope bonus blunt damage masteries and rings work with elementalism boulder, starfall, stone, and other blunt based spells. houses that are freshly built are able to be sieged without a declaration. houses that are over 24 hours old with a guild stone must have a siege declaration to be sieged. steam maintenance is usually done around 6pm est/11pm gmt which results in login disruptions. shields stored on the backup "weapon set" do not impact armor weight. when the weapon set is swapped, the weight penalty kicks in. 1 size = 2 height. "height food" is actually size food. character models physically increase when size increases, not when height itself increases. killing player pets count for task progress. (risen pets don't count). pets gain xp when the pet owner is within 30m of them and an ai dies. the ai that dies can be outside of this 30m radius. the ai could theoretically be infinite distance away from the pet and it would still gain xp. pets automatically teleport to players when they do not have valid pathing to the player. there are two conditions where this is disabled: if the pet is in a house, and if the pet recently took damage. daily tasks can be accepted and saved for another day, but the player cannot accept a new daily task on the cycle that the initial daily task was turned in. holding alt and right clicking multiple items in your inventory queues them all for deletion. this is a great way to mass delete. weapons can left, center, and right block while mounted. you cannot overhead block however. inventory bags can be renamed by control right clicking them when they are in your inventory you can bandage while resting and not interrupt the resting bonus. thrusting (couching) while mounted does heavy durability damage to the weapon. slashing does not do heavy dura damage. reds that are attacked by blues first can freely loot the blue as if the bag was "local grey" flagged. ai which retreats (i.e. alchemist bowman) can be forced to a cliff edge, where it will be forced to stand and fight. the type of pet you are mounted on determines the sway pattern of the weapon you are using. i.e. terrorbird forces a left/right bob while a taur dog is up and down. pets which are abandoned usually disappear after 20-30 minutes. "low quality" ore nodes are ones in locations that are too accessible, such as in a city. these obviously give really poor yields. double yield ore nodes are in high value areas such as granum pass. the gathering rate on these is 2x, but they still give the normal total of ore per spot (~3333 til it starts to deplete). using a clade respec potion from the magic vendor penalizes you 10% of your total clade xp. usually you can respec without losing clade levels, especially if you have a good bit of mastery xp. each pet level linearly increases health, damage, defense, and rider weight. all ai, including bosses, will be between level 0 and 125 and have varying stats because of it. this is why bosses like the nitre queen can be really easy or really difficult! there are outlier cases where ai are above 125, and that is either due to a bug or sv making that happen. manually de-leveling a skill causes it to be at the maximum xp of the previous level going overencumbered while in an otherwise dismounted state (i.e. falling), overrides the rule and forces a dismount if you are ever stuck in a falling state while on a mount and cannot dismount, combine the last two mechanics described. - your armor weight by 1 point, and go overencumbered to force a dismount, then gain 1 xp in armor training to regain it. only works if your set is tailored to your armor training level. ore meteors drop relic fragments. radiant fragments drop proportionally to how much owe is mined (i.e. max mining/lore increases chance per hit). the ore itself refresh slowly over time until they collapse. wave relics are a great choice to chase because they are basically guaranteed orb drops when you kill the boss of the final wave. many client-sided light effects such as casting spells or preparing a placeable interact with the world and can give information. use these as ghetto light sources when in dark places. horse taming is interrupted if another target crosses the targetting crosshair mid-tame. mitigate this by either looking straight up or straight down while taming. when rerolling from a human to another race, be sure to subtract 50 skill points from a skill you wish to lose due to losing the bonus of the "versatile" clade gift. failure to do so will cause it to automatically yoink points from something you probably don't want it to. purple and blue relic meteors last approximately 2 hours and 15 minutes before decaying. water ward does not allow melee, ranged, or direct target magic to penetrate through it. hug a wall and water ward to have a survival tool against most threats. the elementalism spells "shadow" and "mirage" prevent targetting through them. players can "lock" people out of interacting with doors by dropping these spells on them. your guides.title: User Interface
guides.summary: A tour of important interface panels, indicators, menus, and controls that are easy to overlook during normal play.

blocks.html:
A tour of important interface panels, indicators, menus, and controls that are easy to overlook during normal play.

Popups

The very first thing that should be done with UI is setting up text popups. Go to the settings, chat section, and put Skills/Combat/Game/Server on popup by checking those boxes. This will display a message in the center of your screen in addition to the chat box.

Next, adjust the color of COMBAT messages to BRIGHT RED. This is super important because anytime you take damage, receive damage, or anything else related to fighting, you instantly know with absolutely no confusion. This is essential. Adjust the colors of other chat boxes as desired.

The image below shows an example configuration:

blocks.html:
UI Layout

The next element of the UI which is important to modify is the layout of HP bars, compass, and hotbars. The general best practice is to have them centered and near the bottom of the screen. The compass should be easily viewable and clear. A useful option is the round compass. Adjust the size as needed. Keep them from obstructing your view. Additionally, type /fps in the chat box to enable the FPS meter.

The layout below is an example tuned for quick access and clear combat visibility. There is a ton of effort into this UI setup. Everything was considered from hotbar and compass alignments, to positioning of text popups, to debuff spacing between the compass.

blocks.html:
Hotkeys

The next step is to set hotkeys. This is a highly personal design and everyone is going to have different preferences. The most important thing with setting up hotkeys is to have easily accessible and logical keys. Fighters can often get away with just having clade gifts and healing items next to their hotbars with simple 1-6 hotkeys, but mages and hybrids are a different story as they have magnitudes more keys to manage.

For mages the ideal setup is one in which all frequently used commands are clustered around your WASD keys. That enables for the quickest and most accurate execution of magic possible by reducing finger travel. The F1-F8 keys are excellent for using more niche abilities. Several letter keys are occupied by menus and can be changed. Particularly, F R V Y G B H J K can be changed. If any overwritten menu needs to be accessed via hotkey, change them to either [ ]; ‘,. / or number pad keys. They can also be manually accessed by enabling the mouse and selecting them from the bottom-center of the screen.

When setting hotkeys, there are a few core fundamentals to consider:

-Put the most frequently used hotkeys close to the WASD movement keys to reduce finger travel

-Cluster similar abilities together so that your brain associates that section of the keyboard

-Avoid using hotkeys with the control button. These force a walking pace and can cancel other spells.

-F1-F12 are excellent choices for non-critical or slower paced commands

an example hotkey scheme is as follows:

The first hotbar uses keys 1-8 which are dedicated to core magic spells as well as the ultra critical Q and E hotkeys.

blocks.html:
1 - Spurt to break magic reflects and finish targets. It is hotkey 1 because it is used in every single fight.

2 - Corrupt is set to 2 because it is a critical offensive spell that is casted often

3 - Magic reflect is casted frequently and can win mage fights when timed properly

4 - Thunderlash is a single target lightning damage

5 - Shock covers dual-target lightning damage

6 - Lightning bolt is multitarget lightning damage

7 - Atrophy is used to cripple fleeing targets and pets but isn’t used as frequently as 1-5

8 - Boulder is a dismounting spell but cast infrequently enough where it should be decently far from WASD

Q.- Purify is such a critical spell it deserves to be right next to the movement keys

E - Lesser heal is also so critical it needs to be instantly accessed

Recognize how the more frequently a spell is to be casted, and the more useful it is, the closer it is to the WASD movement keys. One question that arises from the selection of Q and E for purify and lesser heal are how self-casting and spell release should be handled? In this example, C is the self-cast key and spell hotkeys are pressed again to release them. There is no reason to have a release spell button when only 1-4 + Q/E are the only spells that use it. Press 3 twice to charge and release Magic Reflect. The spells that release at the end of a charge are set to keys further away from the movement keys because they do not need to be pressed again.

guides.title: Weakspot
guides.summary: How weakspot chance works, which weapons and bonuses affect it, and where the mechanic fits into different combat setups.

blocks.html:
Weakspot

How weakspot chance works, which weapons and bonuses affect it, and where the mechanic fits into different combat setups.

Mechanics

Weakspots occur on stab/pierce attacks or headshots with bows the chance of a weakspot is a hidden percentage that is influenced by several factors. These six variables are combined in a calculation to determine if a weakspot occurs.

  • Equipment Type -

Different weapons, and particularly weapon heads, increase weakspot chance. Mercy daggers have the highest weakspot chance while other weapons such as hammers, and axes cannot weakspot ever. As a rule, crafted spears cannot naturally weakspot either. Swords can weakspot with thrust (center) attacks. Each weakspot chance is unique to the weapon head and is modified by the other variables.

Daggers rely on the weakspot mechanic the most. Of the dagger heads, mercy weakspots the most. Risar and heavy daggers weakspot the least. The other heads have modest weakspot chance. Trading flat damage for weakspot is the design of it, with lighter daggers doing less damage but having a higher penetration chance.

  • Dexterity -

The higher the dexterity, the higher the weakspot chance. This is on a curve however. Testing compared several different points of dexterity with a cronite mercy dagger with an incisium handle. At 132 dex it was weakspotting for ~50% chance. Using a different head will tank the weakspot chance, but at the benefit of increased damage per hit, since mercy daggers have such low inherent pierce. See this chart to get an idea of the results and curve:

blocks.html:
Using a head other-than-mercy will result in a lower overall weakspot chance. The curve will still hold true, however. The downside to this curve is to achieve the higher dex to consistently weakspot, you must be a lower weight class which sacrifices strength to the point of giving up a heavy amount of damage bonus, making the weakspot less effective.

  • Equipment Materials -

Handle/coating materials impact weakspot moderately. The highest weakspot coating materials are pansar scales. The highest weakspot handle materials are likely oghmium > dense crepite > incisium > crepite. However, the weakspot chance with the animal materials are not that great and the durability loss is high. It is likely better to invest into steel/tungsteel for the handle material to boost the durability at a minor cost of weakspot.

  • Clade (Alvarin True Sight) -

This gives a 10% increase to the base weakspot chance. The bonus cannot be valued precisely until the base weakspot chance is known. SV has stated in the past they intend to add a weakspot stat to the character window, but it is not in yet.

  • Marksmanship (Bow) -

Marksmanship gives approximately 0.5-0.6% weakspot chance per point invested in it. This means at level 100 marksmanship you can expect around 60% weakspot chance, without taking dex into account. This ONLY applies to bows, and ONLY applies to headshots. Marksmanship does not interact with anything else.

• Weapon Charge (Melee) -

Weakspot chance scales with how charged the weapon attack is. The more charged an attack is, the greater the weakspot chance. Waiting for a circle flash and then feint attacking (also called a flash attack) maximizes weakspot chance as it removes human timing.

blocks.html:
• Combat Abilities -

Certain combat abilities are capable of weakspot. Notably Heave with a polesword can weakspot, even though it is a slash attack. Dagger abilities CANNOT weakspot, surprisingly.

Weakspot and Archery

Archery has slightly different mechanics than melee. Only headshots can weakspot with bows. The selection of ranged weapons is also much more limited, and the material choices are straightforward. There is no way to build a bow for weakspot chance, and even if there was, the range stat on bows are too important to divert from simply making dense crepite bows.

Bodkin arrows do not seem to have increased weakspot over broad head. Overall, bodkin arrows are simply not worth using for combat.

Contrary to popular belief, longbows can weakspot. The catch is, you must be using bodkin or broadhead arrows. It is the longbow arrows that cannot weakspot!

Weakspot has a few niche PvE applications too, especially with bows. Certain monsters have very high pierce resistance which are countered by weakspot. Snow trolls are a prime example- they take about 1 damage per shot normally, but with a weakspot they take heavy damage. That enables for a marksman MA with good aim to solo trolls with a few hundred arrows.

Other

The myth of heavy armor impacting weakspot - patch 2.0.0.0 brought a change which made “heavier daggers” weakspot much less. This note combined with discussion during a developer livestream about heavier armor impacting weakspot chance led to a misconception among the community that wearing heavier armor currently reduces weakspot chance. This is objectively false in the games current state, and no such change has ever been made. The “heavier dagger” patchnote specifically referred to Risar and Heavy dagger heads.

guides.title: Capes
guides.summary: Browse cape sources, appearances, rarity, and related unlock requirements without hunting through scattered records.

blocks.html:
Capes are soulbound vanity items which offer some utility for PvP. They help identify teammates, obscure your hitbox, potentially act as camoflage in certain environments, and allow for weapon morphs to be concealed with the cloth collision. Overall the utility of a cape indicates that certain ones should be worn (and some avoided).

This section will highlight the capes in game and their location. These are naturally subject to change. Additional options include non-obtainable capes in game, such as the ones Khurite guards wear.

guides.title: Combine Skill
guides.summary: Reference the skills and material relationships used when combining resources, including the requirements that influence results.

blocks.html:
The combine skill is an often underutilized skill that all characters have. The rule of thumb for this skill is if an item can be instered into one of the item slots in the combine window, it can be combined with something. This section will give known recipes for combine.

  1. Campfires - These are used to increase health/mana regeneration when you sit by them. They also act as a heat source for cooking food. The standard recipe for these are 100 stone + 100 wood. Not all woods or stone works for this though. Spongewood, greywood, whitewood, and dapplewood are good. Ironwood and firmwood are not. Granum is good, saburra is not. If the item can fit in the slot, it should work.

blocks.html: 1. Scroll Cases + Seal Keys - Scroll cases are rare pickables or drops that can be opened with seal keys which are purchasable from elemental tables. Regular scroll cases will drop simple scrolls or elementalism books, while ornate ones will drop the more rare and expensive rewards.
blocks.text: Scroll Cases + Seal Keys - Scroll cases are rare pickables or drops that can be opened with seal keys which are purchasable from elemental tables. Regular scroll cases will drop simple scrolls or elementalism books, while ornate ones will drop the more rare and expensive rewards.

blocks.html:
1. Potions / Kegs - Combine allows you to mix and match potions. This is useful for partitioning potions to useful quantities, storing them en masse, or for combining effects. One notable use for this is to combine purify potions and healing ones, allowing you to get rid of corruption and heal a significant amount with one chug.

Important to note that the “main item” is the one that receives the quantity from the secondary. See the flowchart below.

guides.searchText: item catalog items a broad visual index of equipment and notable items, organized to make identification and comparison faster. this section will attempt to catalogue all obtainable items in game and give a brief description of what it is for, and where to go it. this list may not be 100% accurate due to the sheer number of items and how often the game changes. use this as a baseline for discovering items. this list will be difficult to maintain in alphabetical order so use the search function to browse items. format item name: what it's called source: where it's from use: what it's for irl equivalent: what it is (probably) [picture] item name: aabam source: tephra extraction use: necromancy reagent irl: lead item name: aegicite source: imbued calamine in the fabricula use: magic reflect potions irl: unk item name: almine source: tephra extraction use: refining master metals and tindremic messing irl: possibly aluminum item name: amarantum source: granum extraction use: extraction material irl: unk item name: amulet source: world and boss drops use: increases characters defenses, magic abilities, and skill points item name: arcronite source: galbinum and pyroxene extraction use: master metals irl: possibly aluminum item name: argus sponge source: western jungle oceans use: potion multiplier irl: some sort of sea sponge item name: arthropod carapace source: spider/athropod butchery use: cheap armor and shield materials irl: chitin item name: artifacts / artifact piece / abacus bead / obelisk capstone / incensed papyrus / urmath tablet / sargon prism / teuin stele / myrland chronicles source: pois, generally necromancy related, event drops use: augments the stats of ritual pets irl: no specific equivalent item name: bags / small bag / medium bag / spacious bag / large bag / grand bag / capacious bag source: equipment vendor use: increases inventory/bank space item name: cooking vessel / baking stone / turnspit / steam pot / baking pot / smoke box / fermentation jar / cooking pot source: cooking vendor use: alters the stats of food, sometimes negatively. each device specializes in a different stat (hp/stamina/mana, etc) item name: bandage / minor bandage / major bandage source: minor bandages are from the utility vendor. bandages are from bandits/poi boxes, and event drops. major bandages are from event drops. use: heals using the anatomy skill. major bandages allegedly reduce hp loss penalty for being hit while bandaging item name: banner / steel khurite banner / steel white banner / steel red banner source: equipment vendor use: target identification- fits in the tabard slot item name: barley / barley flour source: barley fields - notably southwest of morin khur. use the grinder to make barley flour use: cooking item name: basileus source: basileus spawns in the mediterannean climate near meduli (usually erroneously called sands) use: cooking, possibly alchemy irl: basil item name: beeswax source: bee hives (not yet in game) or certain poi chests use: alchemy item name: biting oil source: utility vendor use: unk irl: sulfuric acid item name: black sea glass source: sator drop use: currency for jungle camp elementalism bench irl: sea glass - weathered glass smoothed by the sea water item name: blackwood source: cutting blackwood trees found in the toxai region use: cooking mana food- not great for other crafting. irl: pear trees due to the trees dropping pirum (pears) item name: bleck source: processing bleckbende use: cheap building metal, also for refining bron (bronze) irl: tin item name: bleckbende source: crushing saburra use: processes into bleck in the furnace irl: tin ore item name: blood ore source: crushing or attracting granum or gaborre use: processes into pig iron for making steel and steel alloys irl: iron ore item name: bloodsilk source: clothos maiden queens use: ultra-light armor with good pierce defense irl: spider silk item name: boiled leather source: not in game yet use: unk item name: bone tissue source: most animals. walkers butcher into a ton of it use: crafting material- useful for leveling item name: book / skill book source: librarians or sometimes world drops. see #book-vendors for rare books. use: levels skills to stated level (usually 50/70/100) item name: bor source: world pickable, usually near water sources use: catalyst for extraction, possibly alchemy irl: the element boron item name: brained leather source: not in game yet use: unk irl: brained leather - leather literally preserved in brain matter item name: bron kelp item name: brownwood source: brownwood trees in the jungle and eastern myrland use: building material irl: some sort of jungle tree, possibly a type of giant palm item name: burning salts pouch guides.title: Trinkets
guides.summary: Understand trinket tiers, gem and effect combinations, charging, repair, appraisal, and the bonuses worth watching for.

blocks.html:
Introduction

Understand trinket tiers, gem and effect combinations, charging, repair, appraisal, and the bonuses worth watching for.

Basics

Trinkets include rings and amulets. Each trinket consists of two parts: the metal and the gem. Each portion determines the range of stats that the trinket can have.

This chart from an MO2 developer stream highlights 5 tiers of both metal and gem:

Each trinket consists of two parts: the metal and the gem. Each portion determines the range of stats that the trinket can have. This chart from an MO2 developer stream highlights 5 tiers of both metal and gem:

blocks.html:
From lowest to highest

Metal: Cuprum -> Silver -> Gold -> Skadite -> Oghmium

Gem: Red Coral -> Amethyst -> Topaz -> Ruber -> Adamant

Each higher tier of metal or gem gives access to another line of stats. For instance, a cuprum amethyst has 1 line of trinket effect, and 2 lines of gem effect. An Oghmium Adamant has 5 lines of each. The most powerful trinket possible consists of Oghmium + Adamant. These are exceedingly rare, however. Many players utilize silver, gold, or skadite trinkets as part of their normal loadout.

Players can have one amulet and two rings equipped at one time. Equipped trinkets do not drop on death, but trinkets in the inventory do. Unidentified trinkets cannot be worn and thus will always drop on death.

Trinkets must be charged with polish to bestow their effects. Each time a trinket is polished it gains 3 charges. 1 charge is lost per death. Charging is done at the enchanter NPC or by using the combine skill with a trinket + polish of the appropriate level. Higher tier polish can be used for lower tier trinkets, i.e. a gold polish can be used on a silver ring.

blocks.html:
Trinkets can be rerolled with an item known as flux. This is a rare drop from spirits in the etherworld (spiritists and friends can acquire it). It is also known to drop from certain events. As with polish, higher tier flux can reroll lower tier metal. The gem tier of the trinket is irrelevant for both polishing and re-rolling a trinket.

Acquisition

Trinkets are drops from monsters, found in chests, from fishing, and can be rewards for certain actions such as picking event bags. Here are the some common places to find trinkets based on metal tier.

Stats

This chart covers the specific trinket effects that are possible on all amulets and rings and the maximum value it can have per line. Cuprum, silver, red coral, and amethyst cannot reach these values.

blocks.html: There is an underlying limit to how many a trinket can have. For example, a topaz ring cannot have +11% blunt, 11% slash, and 11% pierce. Only an adamant ring can achieve those stats. The exact math behind what limits a trinket is complex and outside of the scope of this guide. The important thing to know is higher tier metals and rings allow for greater effect.

blocks.html:
Mechanics Explained

  • Flat Attribute - Adds 1 point to an attribute. Can cause overflow.
  • Raw Attribute - Adds 1 point to an attribute + 1 stat cap.
  • Loot luck - Increases chance of getting good drops from a kill. Functionally is a +% to rolls. Trinket user or his pet must get the last hit on an enemy.
  • Rare Trinket Gem Luck - Increases chance of upgrading the gem on a trinket drop. Trinket user or his pet must get the last hit on an enemy. Works with fishing.
  • Loot amount - Increases quantity of stackable items looted (i.e. carcass). Trinket user or his pet must get the last hit on an enemy. Works with pickables. Unconfirmed if it works with fishing.
  • Damage % - Functionally acts as damage bonus when
  • Trinket Effect Luck - Increases the chance of a good roll for the metal values on a trinket when identifying or rerolling with flux.
  • Gem Effect Luck - Increases the chance of a good roll for the gem value on a trinket when identifying or rerolling with flux.
  • Health/Stamina/Mana - Gives a flat amount to these values.
  • Skill Point - Adds a flat amount to a skill. Can overflow.
  • Mana Reduction % - Reduces the mana spent on a spell of the specific school when cast.
  • Defense % - Reduces damage when received from a specific source. Compounds with other effects.
  • Free Armor Weight % - Increases the amount of armor weight a character can hold when equipped.

blocks.html:
Trinket-Binding

Binding is an informal term to describe when a character becomes non-PvP viable when their trinkets are uncharged. For example, if a fighter character has a necklace which gives +5 armor training and they leave their effective armor training at 95 to compensate (95+5), should their trinkets become uncharged they will lose access to heavy armor training due to the dip in the armor training level. It is critical that characters are either fully geared with trinkets charged, or they are unbound.

Players can be trinket bound for crafting as well, particularly if the trinket gives a crafting skill >30. For example, if a player’s character has a +45 armor crafting trinket and they leave their armor crafting skill at 55, the armor that this character makes when not using that trinket dips below the magical threshold of 70. If emergency armor needs crafted, this character’s crafting will be wildly inefficient compared to one with 70+ effective skill sans trinket. It is thus recommended for skills which are critical to

Mitigating the risk of becoming a dud from losing trinket charges can be done through careful selection of trinkets and their bonuses. Critical skills which are absolutely mandatory for functioning of a character build should be generally avoided. Auxiliary skills and attributes should be focused on. For example, having a +40 endurance or +40 survival value on an amulet is generally OK to lose; a character is not crippled when they lose this. Losing +40 mental training, however, completely ruins a mage. Use prudence when deciding what skills are bound to trinkets.

Raw stats, free armor weight %, mana reduction, defense %, health/stamina/mana, damage %, and (generally) +flat psyche are great values to have on trinkets as these do not normally cripple a build when lost.

For example, having a +40 endurance or +40 survival value on an amulet is generally OK to lose; a character is not crippled when they lose this. Losing +40 mental training, however, completely ruins a mage. Use prudence when deciding what skills are bound to trinkets. Raw stats, free armor weight %, mana reduction, defense %, health/stamina/mana, damage %, and (generally) +flat psyche are great values to have on trinkets as these do not normally cripple a build when lost.

blocks.html:
Ecumenical

Read Ecumenical to desired level. If that level is >70, lock domination and read domination until ecumenical is the desired level.

To level domination to maximum, read Domination II to max, then find a black bear that says “low chance to dominate” and spam try and dominate it until domination is maxed. You might have to use several black bears as your level range changes.

blocks.html:
Elementalism

Elementalism is the most difficult grind to overcome for magery. This is not a cheap nor quick challenge, but it gives great rewards. This process might take a whole play session if you are dedicated.

The most reliable way to level elementalism is through a technique where you lock the parent skill and train sub skills to 100, and then unlock the parent skill and raise it. This technique will be used extensively. You will not see XP gain when leveling a child skill that is higher level than the parent skill. Keep casting and you will periodically gain levels. You will not see level gains like normal leveling with this. Follow these steps EXACTLY as they are written and it will work.

A strong practice is mise en place- i.e. have everything ready before starting. However, that is not always realistic. Make sure you keep track of what step you are on.

blocks.html:
Some notes:

If you are overleveled on elementalism you will simply not gain XP. For example, mirage requires elementalism to be locked at 25. Should your intensification bump up from attribute changes or by being unlocked, you will stop leveling arrangement until it is reduced back down to 25.

The exact number of reagents is variable based on your stat bonuses and clade gifts. The rare reagents needed for this method are sweat salts from GK/MK mage valley, and lodestone powder from grinding lodestones. Flowing Nimbic Spirits are optional but recommended and are bought with lodestones/geodes from the elementalism vendor table.

There is an issue when you gain a level in magic schools where it incorrectly allows leveling of subskills past their effective. Relog if you stop gaining XP. You can also try setting elementalism to -1 and then relevel with a propulsion spell.

After you are done with all steps your intensification level will be overflowed and must be corrected.

Arcana/Polarization are optional, but highly useful for generating rain.

blocks.html:
Necromancy

Method 1 - Spell Grinding

This is best done with a +Necromancy necklace. Skip high cost spells with your necklace by equipping it and casting more favorable spells if needed. Also useful to be in higher level ranges of spells to make casting more successful, i.e. if you are 40 necromancy you can equip a +10 necromancy amulet to reach effective level 45 and cast blind at a much better rate until you hit 56 effective skill, then unequip and keep raise the skill using blind.

Read Necromancer’s Notes

Raise Walker or Cloud of Ashes -> 22

Raise Strong Walker -> 38

Raise Greater Walker -> 40 (or skip with trinket)

Blind -> 56

Death Hand -> 58

Crawling Hands -> 70

Atrophy -> 78

Akh Bond -> 85

Mental Leech -> 100

Method 2 - Tupilak Grinding

Read Necromancer’s Notes

Raise Walker or Cloud of Ashes -> 20

Read Notes of Necromantic Rituals

Ritual summon trash mobs until level 25 Rituals (amount of times varies, usually ~50 depending on your skill bonuses)

Raise a Tupilak and spam it’s level 25 ability on an equerry -> 100 Necromancy/Rituals

guides.title: Mage PvP Guide
guides.summary: Combat fundamentals for mages, covering positioning, spell choice, survival, team play, pressure, and resource management.

blocks.html: Mage PvP Guide
blocks.text: Mage PvP Guide

blocks.html:
Introduction

Combat fundamentals for mages, covering positioning, spell choice, survival, team play, pressure, and resource management.
blocks.text: Introduction Combat fundamentals for mages, covering positioning, spell choice, survival, team play, pressure, and resource management.

blocks.html:
Prerequisites

The very foundation for success is proper game settings and UI/hotkey management. Being a mage in MO2 is a first person shooter style of gameplay, and game performance is critical. Lag or sluggish controls can break an otherwise skilled player, or limit their peak performance. Read #client-performance, #ergo-and-gear, and #user-interface for guides on these elements of gameplay.

The recommended approach is to having a high quality positional audio headset. A set with 7.1 surround sound, even if software based, gives a distinct advantage over standard headsets or earbuds. This is important for several aspects of magery, particularly surviving.

The character to use will be fully leveled. The expectation for this build is a minimum of 62 ecu and 92 necromancy. Ideally the build will have 62 ecumenical, 100 necromancy/rituals, and 80 elementalism/intensification. The armor used should be a minimum of keeled scale/ironwool. If you need an example build to use, check out #meta-builds. Ideally this character will be a bulging Sheevra mage, stout/fit/lean Sheevra dagger mage, or some flavor of non-obese human. Bulging Sidoian or Sarducaan is the standard for large-scale human mages. Fat mages and mounted mages are outside of the scope of this guide.

blocks.html:
Ecumenical Overview

The word “ecumenical” in the context of Mortal Online 2 means broad utility. Ecumenical has a wide range of useful spells and is a “hitscan” spell school, meaning that the spells are a laser that instantly hits the target when aimed. When a spell is charged it remains chambered for up to 20 seconds. It is recommended to be level 62 ecumenical for most mages. Ecumenical hosts powerful spells:

Corrupt - Damage over time spell that denies healing while active

Lesser Heal - A quick casting single target heal with low mana cost

Magic Reflect - Reflects a broad selection of spells at the caster. Remains active for a long period of time

Purify - Cleanses many negative status effects (all necro debuffs, corrupt, fulminate)

Spurt - Medium range low cost single target damage

Thunderlash - Long range single target damage

blocks.html: Other notable spells include earthquake for dismounting and outburst for long range single target damage. Ecumenicals role in PvP is to be quick casting impact spells. Ecumenical is not very mana efficient for offensive magic, but it is highly efficient for healing/defensive use. This school can be used while mounted, and walking is permissible when casting.

Ecumenical is not very mana efficient for offensive magic, but it is highly efficient for healing/defensive use. This school can be used while mounted, and walking is permissible when casting.

blocks.html:
Elementalism Overview

Elementalism uses the combined power of earth, fire, water, and wind to impact the battlefield. In the context of PvP it is used primarily for its AoE abilities and high efficiency damage spells. This school is generally projectile based and must be aimed to hit its targets. Elementalism hosts some of the best AoE in game with the notable spells of:

Fireball - Medium speed AoE projectile that burns targets after impact

Firewall - High damage burn that melts pets and denies chokepoints

Gravity Snare - Long range projectile which collects players it hits and forcefully shoves them

Lightning Bolt - Medium speed AoE that causes

Shock - Fast casting and mana efficient direct damage spell that can arc to nearby targets

Starfall - Area-of-effect with strong zoning capabilities plus it dismounts

Static Charge - High damage potential area of effect wall spell

Elementalism cannot be used while mounted. Spells that are cast are released on spell completion and cannot be chambered. Walking is allowed while casting.

blocks.html:
Necromancy Overview

Necromancy is the power over death. This is one of the most potent magic schools for three reasons: auw surge, walking dead, and ritual pets. Here is a list of notable necromancy spells for PvP:

Akh Bond - Gives an inherent ~17.5% damage reduction while active on a pet

Atrophy - Slows enemy pets and gives a -50% stamina regeneration debuff for its duration

Auw Surge - A cone shaped area-of-effect spell which can be casted while sprinting

Death Hand - High damage single target lifesteal spell with very short range

Miasma - The most potent area of effect spell in game

Raise Greater Walker - Hordes of greater walkers are notoriously hard to kill and they do not run out of stamina

blocks.html:
Spiritism Overview

Spiritism is not often used in (alive) PvP as it more focuses on etherworld (dead) spells. The two spells which are notable for PvP as a dex mage are mental projectile (laser beam) and mental healing for mana regen. Mental projectile is functionally a rail gun that can hit for incredible damage at long range, but it requires many skill and timing because it cannot be chambered and it casts immediately at the end of its charge.

blocks.html:
Spell Selection and Reagents

The majority of spells in game aren't optimal for use in PvP. A practical setup uses 1.5 hotbars (~15 spells) regularly. Auxiliary skills such as raise walkers or the highly situational spells are on Function (F keys) or non-priority keys. Keep all frequently used spells close to the WASD keys. The image below is an example hotbar, with priority spells from 1-8 + Q, E, R, and Y. Everything else is non-priority or too situational to have on those keys.

  1. Spurt - For stripping magic reflects and finishing mercy mode targets
  2. Corrupt - For denying enemy healing
  3. Thunderlash - For single target damage when shock isn't indicated
  4. Shock - For high efficiency spell damage that can do small AoE
  5. Lightning Bolt - For dumping into enemy groups
  6. Static Charge - For killing pets/PvE
  7. Atrophy - For crippling pets and oghmirs/thursars/humans (rare usage)
  8. Magic Reflect - For pre-fight buffs and limiting magic damage on group

Q. Purify - For cleansing negative effects on self and team

E. Lesser Heal - For spamming out healing

R. Death Hand - For high single target damage with lifesteal

Y. Auw Surge - For chasing/opening damage on enemy groups

blocks.html:
This spell list is non-exhaustive, as inevitably these may be changed or more spells may be added. Keep to the principle of having important spells easily accessible with your fingers. This example omits the release hotkey and instead presses the spell key again, though either preference works.

Having enough reagents to win the fight is important. Running out means losing access to the toolkit the character is built around. The specific loadout of the mage is dependent on their spell selection and build. However, a rule of thumb can be established- if you find returning to base and there is an excess of regs, you likely brought too many. Ere on the side of bringing too many, and slowly adjust the loadout to meet the demands of a fight.

an example loadout when adventuring - 128 lesser heals, 32 thunderlashes, 64 lightning bolts/static charges, 32 shocks, 16 magic reflections, 16 corrupts, 8 atrophies, a few clouds of ashes, 4 crawling hands, and 1 starfall. If going to a large scale fight, the number of reagents for big spells should increase. While it is not wise to rely on looting to replenish resources, with this many spells it is likely that an enemy mage will have died before the full reagent supply is exhausted. Ere on the side of having slightly too many regs rather than too little.

On a side note, to keep inventory clutter to a minimum, keep your spellbook in the bottom right slot so that it doesn't intermingle with looted items.

blocks.html:
Defensive Options

There are three philosophies for survival with dex mages: shield, parry, and speed. Which one you decide to use boils down to your effectiveness with them.

Shields - The strategy of using a shield is to have it unequipped. When an enemy dives, equip the shield and position your camera so the shield is facing the opponent. As they swing on you, maneuver

Pros - Allows casting while moving/kiting, reduces damage by a ton with a good shield/chest armor piece. Reduces bleedthrough damage when parrying

Cons - High cost (gold), requires heavy armor training, mana regen is gimped while shield is active, stamina loss when hit

Parry: The skill of using a weapon to block and parry all incoming damage

Pros - Mitigates majority of damage, low cost, regens stamina

Cons - Requires a weapon, chip damage can be significant versus blunt weapons if strength is low, locks you out of casting

Speed: The art of using movement to evade and dodge enemies

Pros - If weaponless, allows for optimal casting, free to use, requires a specialized build

Cons - Hardcountered by some mechanics such as pets, mounteds, or Veelas

Most Sheevra mages will run 431-450ish speed. Humans will run about 420. Humans are indicated to use parry or shields, while alvarin are indicated to use any of the defense styles. The ideal style is shieldplay with 3d positioned audio cues to alter movement. Review 0:51 to 1:08 of this video https://youtu.be/k5iCmLaeE9g and notice how positioning of the camera (and some luck) made 4 of the 5 attacks into equipment hits with greatly reduced damage.

blocks.html:
1v1 Strategy

1v1 is not the strong suit of a mage. However, Players can dominate given certain circumstances. Winning a 1v1 comes down to good mana management, pet usage, terrain negotiation, footwork, and the player's mechanical skills. This subsection will give a broad set of principles when encountering different archetypes:
blocks.text: 1v1 Strategy 1v1 is not the strong suit of a mage. However, Players can dominate given certain circumstances. Winning a 1v1 comes down to good mana management, pet usage, terrain negotiation, footwork, and the player's mechanical skills. This subsection will give a broad set of principles when encountering different archetypes:

blocks.html:
Countering Thur/Ogh Fighters

Non-veela fighters, particularly oghmirs and thursars, are natural prey of a dex mage. That does not mean the kills are free, however. The differential between 419 and 440+ movement speed makes dex mages able to essentially kite indefinitely in most circumstances. With perfect play this means a 1v1 versus a Thur/Ogh fighter should always result in either a draw or a win.

The general strategy will be:

  1. Position yourself for safety. This could mean distance or height advantage.
  2. Open with damage spells. Thunderlash/shock/lightning bolt/fireball. If you have a pet, sic it on them. See how they react.
  3. Follow up with a corrupt or more direct damage. See how they react. If they flee, make chase. If they push, use your movement. If a thursar pops lifesteal, make a judgement call whether to call pet back or to commit to more damage spells while the thursar is corurpted.
  4. If they are unable to kill the pet (you should be managing the pets life/calling back if its going to die), and they unable to kill you (you are kiting them), add more damage to them. Eventually this results in their death assuming you keep corrupt active.

blocks.html:
Do not let fighters get a sticky on you. With proper trinkets, you can die very quickly.Avoid trading/jousting with death hand unless you ABSOLUTELY know what you're doing with footwork and aiming. Death hand is a monster of a spell, but it is a supremely high skill cap ability. See: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5iCmLaeE9g

Corrupt is an important spell when fighting thursars and oghmir. Thursars, with styganthrope, have the potential to heal a ton if left unchecked. It is a race between damage and their innate regeneration, bandaging, and potion usage.

When using pets vs. Thursar specifically, keep extremely mindful of their lifesteal clade. An unarmored pet being hit by a thursar will heal the fighter to full. You must either preemptively corrupt the fighter or pull the pet back to prevent all damage being absorbed and the pet dying freely.

blocks.html:
Countering Paladins

Paladins are generally humans, which have low psyche. This makes them vulnerable to straight magic damage, although they do have clade gifts to use to counter you.

The #1 thing when fighting a paladin is to prevent their healing. They have the potential to outheal your mana bar if left unchecked. Corruption + shock is key to keeping them from recovering. Use thunderlash if you have a pet in melee with them. Keep mindful that a corrupt can be instantly cleansed for free by them, and reapply it.

Similar to fighters, keep distance, kite, and apply pet pressure while doing direct damage until they die. Paladins are more versatile than traditional foot fighters, but if they bleed they can still be killed. The biggest difference is understanding their utility and countering it.

blocks.html:
Countering Mages

Mage 1v1s used to be a stalemate because of high recovery potential. This is no longer the case with shock + ritual pets. A simple well placed shock spam kills any mage. Use positioning, cover, pets, and spell timings to beat your enemy. Even throwing in a surprise magic reflect when you expect direct damage can reflect a good amount of damage and give you the initiative.

Some strategies-

Shock, corrupt, and spurt are the main anti-mage spells. Shock for pure damage, corrupt to interrupt their healing/cancel their casting, and spurt to cancel casting/strip reflect.

Daggers are a natural counter to a mage as they hit quickly and can do a decent amount of damage. Since your speed will likely match theirs, you have the ability to go full melee if you are built for it.

Pets are an absolute monster when it comes to killing mages. Risen lynx, 2x living direwolf, terrorbirds, or anything else that is fast with high DPS dominate mages. The only real counter to these is jumping into water, or atrophy spam. If you do fight a mage with enough sense to atrophy the pet, pre-cast purifies to keep the pet cleansed and at full running speed.

If you are subject to a successful shock spam, it is countered by using distance, potions, and footwork. Get either too close to the enemy for them to cast it (as it arcs to them), or get far enough away where you can recover and regain initiative.

blocks.html:
---Anti-Mounted---

Good mounted players pose a serious threat to mages. Bad mounted players can basically be ignored.

Versus an MC (mounted melee/combat) it boils down to footwork, parrying, and getting a successful earthquake/boulder off. Use terrain to put yourself higher than their swings, or use water to force them into a vulnerable position. Once a dismounting spell is charged, put them on the ground and death hand spam them. They will generally respond to a dismount by panicking and trying to remount. In this timeframe you can lay enough offensive magic to finish them off.

Versus a mounted archer (MA) it's a bit tougher than dismounting an MC because they generally try and keep distance. Against strong mounted opponents, the practical goal is often to force a stalemate rather than chase a clean win. Use terrain, cover, and water to ensure survival. Charge lesser heals and keep high HP. Your goal is survival. Make sure they are stripped of magic reflect and shock their mounts (which arcs to them) to dissuade further aggression by them. Get to a safe area where they cannot pursue. If you CAN get an earthquake or boulder off successfully, finish them off with death hand, shock, or other offensive magic.

Versus a mounted mage (MM) there is no real easy way to win without killing their mount. The best strategy is simply outheal any damage they throw on you (they cast 50% slower than you). If you get a dismount on them the best option is to target THEIR HORSE so they cannot remount. At this point you must use pets, corrupt, daggers, or any other non-ecu/necro spell as their psyche is through the roof. MM's are particularly vulnerable if you lure them into water and kill their mount. Shock spam works great for this.

blocks.html:
---Water Combat---

Mages are the natural apex predator in water due to movement speed (lower armor weight = faster swim speed) and their ranged damage. Underwater combat is a different style of gameplay. It is more strategic, positional based, and less "twitchy" combat. You have to deliberately think about distance and what spells to use.

The rule of thumb for 1v1 underwater is to ZONE your enemy. What this means is to keep them just far enough away where you can cast on them, but they cannot in turn reach you. In a way this is like underwater "footwork". Gauging the distance between you and the enemy is key, and understanding the limits of each specific spell you have is critical to success. Shock is a shining example of this - if you are too far away, it will miss. If you are too close, it will arc back to you. Keeping within that goldilocks zone is how to win.

Here is a video demonstrating (mostly) water combat: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzU0n8T7FoQ

blocks.html:
Group Dynamics

Mages excel best at group play and are masters at several roles:

Healer/Corruptors

Alpha damagers

Finishers

Disruptors

  1. Healers/Corruptors -

Lesser heal and corrupt are the two most important spells in the game. They are mana efficient and high impact. Your ability to heal your group and deny enemy healing is quite brutally the single most impactful thing you can do.

  1. Alpha Damage -

Alpha damage is the act of opening with a damaging spell. This concept simple - A group which receives big damage first is put on the defensive. A group which does big damage first has the initiative. A simple way of winning fights is to kill 1 enemy and reset the fight to neutral. If the enemy loses a player and the fight is reset, they are far less likely to win when the fight re-engages. Alpha damage probes for an opening and gives fighters the ability to pick an enemy.

blocks.html:
1. Finishers -

Enemies who are low HP often focus on parrying to survive. They may also receive attention of enemy mages for priority heals. With this in mind, several spells are excellent finishers which aim to kill the target before they can recover. Thunderlash, shock, mind blast, or any other high damage easily hitable spell is ideal to accomplish this objective. AoE should generally be avoided because your teammates tend to be pushing the target as well.

The most important skill is knowing when to switch from heal/corrupt mode to kill mode. Mages require a high level of situational and battlefield awareness. The most common way to identify a low target is to observe the flow of battle. If everyone is pushing forward, your team likely has momentum and enemy targets which are retreating tend to be low. A simple cursor scan to identify HP pools can see who to focus. Otherwise, audio cues such as "target is low on the west side" can be a good indicator of when to prepare a spell.

  1. Disruptors -

Disruption of enemy groups can be a useful mechanics to sew discord and prevent them from completing certain objectives. The primary disruption mechanics involved sound and visual distortions, particularly with spells like shadow, blinding cloud, and roaring wind. When a group is hit with these spells, it creates confusion and can disrupt their effectiveness in a fight. One example of this in action is casting blinding cloud on an enemy mage line- not only are you limiting their line of sight to prevent their healing, you also cause a damage source which interrupts casting. An enemy group which is being collapsed on also has their mage line disrupted, they are unlikely to recover.
