blocks.html:
Priorities as a group mage:

  1. Listen to leadership commands. They control the flow of the fight and even if they make a "wrong" call, failing to follow it would generally be detrimental. Group cohesion is important.
  2. DO NOT DIE. A dead mage is worthless. You must prioritize survival.
  3. Do not let your teammates die. Heal them. A dead teammate is worthless to you.
  4. Corrupt enemies below 75% hp. This gives an opening for securing them as kills.
  5. Finish enemies with direct damage spells. If your melees cannot secure the kill, it is your job to do so.
  6. Crowd control. Both pets and enemies can be herded or dealt with by AoE spells. This can also include dropping disruption spells like blinding cloud on enemy mage lines, or cutting off their lines of retreat with other niche spells.

blocks.html:
Some Mechanics -

Flick Casting -

This technique is when you target an enemy and immediately rip the mouse away while releasing the spell. This somehow guarantees a hit. The condition with which it works requires you to have a solid target first. It takes a bit of getting used to.

Footwork -

Footwork is a valuable survival tool. It is impossible to accurately teach someone proper footwork via a written guide. It's more of an art. The strategies to utilize footwork to maximum effect generally involve making sharp 90 or 180 turns, kiting through groups, and using barriers (even other players) to break contact with an attacker. Keep conscious of your movement and how it relates to your opponent. Watch videos of successful mages and take notes.

Jump Casting -

Jumping is a powerful tool to reposition while casting. While it is true that you can move while walking and casting, this is not nearly as potent as jumping. To jump cast, sprint the direction you want to move, press space bar, and the moment your feet leave the ground start casting. You can continue to move while the spell finishes charging/releasing.

Self-Heal Chain -

This is the #1 sustain tool that a mage has in their arsenal. Essentially because of the rate of attack melee have, you can time heals inbetween each strike and outheal them while repositioning. Become profecient at using footwork, jump casting, and self-casting a lesser heal chain and you will become much more durable as a mage

blocks.html:
Shield Repositioning -

High quality headphones are needed for this. The idea is you adjust your camera so that your back with the shield on it moves to block anyone attacking you. Use audio cues to slightly lead where your attacker is to maximize the amount of equipment hits.

Spell Animation Hiding

The number one projector of intent with magic is to look directly at a target and give them a full view of what spell you are casting. This is generally not a good thing as they can react to your play. The better option is to position the camera either 90 degrees away from the target, or to have your back completely turned away from them. guides.searchText: mage pvp guide magic combat fundamentals for mages, covering positioning, spell choice, survival, team play, pressure, and resource management. mage pvp guide introduction combat fundamentals for mages, covering positioning, spell choice, survival, team play, pressure, and resource management. prerequisites the very foundation for success is proper game settings and ui/hotkey management. being a mage in mo2 is a first person shooter style of gameplay, and game performance is critical. lag or sluggish controls can break an otherwise skilled player, or limit their peak performance. read #client-performance, #ergo-and-gear, and #user-interface for guides on these elements of gameplay. the recommended approach is to having a high quality positional audio headset. a set with 7.1 surround sound, even if software based, gives a distinct advantage over standard headsets or earbuds. this is important for several aspects of magery, particularly surviving. the character to use will be fully leveled. the expectation for this build is a minimum of 62 ecu and 92 necromancy. ideally the build will have 62 ecumenical, 100 necromancy/rituals, and 80 elementalism/intensification. the armor used should be a minimum of keeled scale/ironwool. if you need an example build to use, check out #meta-builds. ideally this character will be a bulging sheevra mage, stout/fit/lean sheevra dagger mage, or some flavor of non-obese human. bulging sidoian or sarducaan is the standard for large-scale human mages. fat mages and mounted mages are outside of the scope of this guide. ecumenical overview the word “ecumenical” in the context of mortal online 2 means broad utility. ecumenical has a wide range of useful spells and is a “hitscan” spell school, meaning that the spells are a laser that instantly hits the target when aimed. when a spell is charged it remains chambered for up to 20 seconds. it is recommended to be level 62 ecumenical for most mages. ecumenical hosts powerful spells: corrupt - damage over time spell that denies healing while active lesser heal - a quick casting single target heal with low mana cost magic reflect - reflects a broad selection of spells at the caster. remains active for a long period of time purify - cleanses many negative status effects (all necro debuffs, corrupt, fulminate) spurt - medium range low cost single target damage thunderlash - long range single target damage other notable spells include earthquake for dismounting and outburst for long range single target damage. ecumenicals role in pvp is to be quick casting impact spells. ecumenical is not very mana efficient for offensive magic, but it is highly efficient for healing/defensive use. this school can be used while mounted, and walking is permissible when casting. elementalism overview elementalism uses the combined power of earth, fire, water, and wind to impact the battlefield. in the context of pvp it is used primarily for its aoe abilities and high efficiency damage spells. this school is generally projectile based and must be aimed to hit its targets. elementalism hosts some of the best aoe in game with the notable spells of: fireball - medium speed aoe projectile that burns targets after impact firewall - high damage burn that melts pets and denies chokepoints gravity snare - long range projectile which collects players it hits and forcefully shoves them lightning bolt - medium speed aoe that causes shock - fast casting and mana efficient direct damage spell that can arc to nearby targets starfall - area-of-effect with strong zoning capabilities plus it dismounts static charge - high damage potential area of effect wall spell elementalism cannot be used while mounted. spells that are cast are released on spell completion and cannot be chambered. walking is allowed while casting. necromancy overview necromancy is the power over death. this is one of the most potent magic schools for three reasons: auw surge, walking dead, and ritual pets. here is a list of notable necromancy spells for pvp: akh bond - gives an inherent ~17.5% damage reduction while active on a pet atrophy - slows enemy pets and gives a -50% stamina regeneration debuff for its duration auw surge - a cone shaped area-of-effect spell which can be casted while sprinting death hand - high damage single target lifesteal spell with very short range miasma - the most potent area of effect spell in game raise greater walker - hordes of greater walkers are notoriously hard to kill and they do not run out of stamina one unique mechanic with necromancy is that you can sprint while casting these, making them ideal for kiting/dodging. similar to elementalism, however, the spells release at the end of the cast animation and cannot be chambered. spiritism overview spiritism is not often used in (alive) pvp as it more focuses on etherworld (dead) spells. the two spells which are notable for pvp as a dex mage are mental projectile (laser beam) and mental healing for mana regen. mental projectile is functionally a rail gun that can hit for incredible damage at long range, but it requires many skill and timing because it cannot be chambered and it casts immediately at the end of its charge. spell selection and reagents the majority of spells in game aren't optimal for use in pvp. a practical setup uses 1.5 hotbars (~15 spells) regularly. auxiliary skills such as raise walkers or the highly situational spells are on function (f keys) or non-priority keys. keep all frequently used spells close to the wasd keys. the image below is an example hotbar, with priority spells from 1-8 + q, e, r, and y. everything else is non-priority or too situational to have on those keys. spurt - for stripping magic reflects and finishing mercy mode targets corrupt - for denying enemy healing thunderlash - for single target damage when shock isn't indicated shock - for high efficiency spell damage that can do small aoe lightning bolt - for dumping into enemy groups static charge - for killing pets/pve atrophy - for crippling pets and oghmirs/thursars/humans (rare usage) magic reflect - for pre-fight buffs and limiting magic damage on group q. purify - for cleansing negative effects on self and team e. lesser heal - for spamming out healing r. death hand - for high single target damage with lifesteal y. auw surge - for chasing/opening damage on enemy groups this spell list is non-exhaustive, as inevitably these may be changed or more spells may be added. keep to the principle of having important spells easily accessible with your fingers. this example omits the release hotkey and instead presses the spell key again, though either preference works. having enough reagents to win the fight is important. running out means losing access to the toolkit the character is built around. the specific loadout of the mage is dependent on their spell selection and build. however, a rule of thumb can be established- if you find returning to base and there is an excess of regs, you likely brought too many. ere on the side of bringing too many, and slowly adjust the loadout to meet the demands of a fight. an example loadout when adventuring - 128 lesser heals, 32 thunderlashes, 64 lightning bolts/static charges, 32 shocks, 16 magic reflections, 16 corrupts, 8 atrophies, a few clouds of ashes, 4 crawling hands, and 1 starfall. if going to a large scale fight, the number of reagents for big spells should increase. while it is not wise to rely on looting to replenish resources, with this many spells it is likely that an enemy mage will have died before the full reagent supply is exhausted. ere on the side of having slightly too many regs rather than too little. on a side note, to keep inventory clutter to a minimum, keep your spellbook in the bottom right slot so that it doesn't intermingle with looted items. defensive options there are three philosophies for survival with dex mages: shield, parry, and speed. which one you decide to use boils down to your effectiveness with them. shields - the strategy of using a shield is to have it unequipped. when an enemy dives, equip the shield and position your camera so the shield is facing the opponent. as they swing on you, maneuver pros - allows casting while moving/kiting, reduces damage by a ton with a good shield/chest armor piece. reduces bleedthrough damage when parrying cons - high cost (gold), requires heavy armor training, mana regen is gimped while shield is active, stamina loss when hit parry: the skill of using a weapon to block and parry all incoming damage pros - mitigates majority of damage, low cost, regens stamina cons - requires a weapon, chip damage can be significant versus blunt weapons if strength is low, locks you out of casting speed: the art of using movement to evade and dodge enemies pros - if weaponless, allows for optimal casting, free to use, requires a specialized build cons - hardcountered by some mechanics such as pets, mounteds, or veelas most sheevra mages will run 431-450ish speed. humans will run about 420. humans are indicated to use parry or shields, while alvarin are indicated to use any of the defense styles. the ideal style is shieldplay with 3d positioned audio cues to alter movement. review 0:51 to 1:08 of this video https://youtu.be/k5icmlaee9g and notice how positioning of the camera (and some luck) made 4 of the 5 attacks into equipment hits with greatly reduced damage. 1v1 strategy 1v1 is not the strong suit of a mage. however, players can dominate given certain circumstances. winning a 1v1 comes down to good mana management, pet usage, terrain negotiation, footwork, and the player's mechanical skills. this subsection will give a broad set of principles when encountering different archetypes: countering thur/ogh fighters non-veela fighters, particularly oghmirs and thursars, are natural prey of a dex mage. that does not mean the kills are free, however. the differential between 419 and 440+ movement speed makes dex mages able to essentially kite indefinitely in most circumstances. with perfect play this means a 1v1 versus a thur/ogh fighter should always result in either a draw or a win. the general strategy will be: position yourself for safety. this could mean distance or height advantage. open with damage spells. thunderlash/shock/lightning bolt/fireball. if you have a pet, sic it on them. see how they react. follow up with a corrupt or more direct damage. see how they react. if they flee, make chase. if they push, use your movement. if a thursar pops lifesteal, make a judgement call whether to call pet back or to commit to more damage spells while the thursar is corurpted. if they are unable to kill the pet (you should be managing the pets life/calling back if its going to die), and they unable to kill you (you are kiting them), add more damage to them. eventually this results in their death assuming you keep corrupt active. do not let fighters get a sticky on you. with proper trinkets, you can die very quickly.avoid trading/jousting with death hand unless you absolutely know what you're doing with footwork and aiming. death hand is a monster of a spell, but it is a supremely high skill cap ability. see: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k5icmlaee9g corrupt is an important spell when fighting thursars and oghmir. thursars, with styganthrope, have the potential to heal a ton if left unchecked. it is a race between damage and their innate regeneration, bandaging, and potion usage. when using pets vs. thursar specifically, keep extremely mindful of their lifesteal clade. an unarmored pet being hit by a thursar will heal the fighter to full. you must either preemptively corrupt the fighter or pull the pet back to prevent all damage being absorbed and the pet dying freely. countering paladins paladins are generally humans, which have low psyche. this makes them vulnerable to straight magic damage, although they do have clade gifts to use to counter you. the #1 thing when fighting a paladin is to prevent their healing. they have the potential to outheal your mana bar if left unchecked. corruption + shock is key to keeping them from recovering. use thunderlash if you have a pet in melee with them. keep mindful that a corrupt can be instantly cleansed for free by them, and reapply it. similar to fighters, keep distance, kite, and apply pet pressure while doing direct damage until they die. paladins are more versatile than traditional foot fighters, but if they bleed they can still be killed. the biggest difference is understanding their utility and countering it. countering mages mage 1v1s used to be a stalemate because of high recovery potential. this is no longer the case with shock + ritual pets. a simple well placed shock spam kills any mage. use positioning, cover, pets, and spell timings to beat your enemy. even throwing in a surprise magic reflect when you expect direct damage can reflect a good amount of damage and give you the initiative. some strategies- shock, corrupt, and spurt are the main anti-mage spells. shock for pure damage, corrupt to interrupt their healing/cancel their casting, and spurt to cancel casting/strip reflect. daggers are a natural counter to a mage as they hit quickly and can do a decent amount of damage. since your speed will likely match theirs, you have the ability to go full melee if you are built for it. pets are an absolute monster when it comes to killing mages. risen lynx, 2x living direwolf, terrorbirds, or anything else that is fast with high dps dominate mages. the only real counter to these is jumping into water, or atrophy spam. if you do fight a mage with enough sense to atrophy the pet, pre-cast purifies to keep the pet cleansed and at full running speed. if you are subject to a successful shock spam, it is countered by using distance, potions, and footwork. get either too close to the enemy for them to cast it (as it arcs to them), or get far enough away where you can recover and regain initiative. ---anti-mounted--- good mounted players pose a serious threat to mages. bad mounted players can basically be ignored. versus an mc (mounted melee/combat) it boils down to footwork, parrying, and getting a successful earthquake/boulder off. use terrain to put yourself higher than their swings, or use water to force them into a vulnerable position. once a dismounting spell is charged, put them on the ground and death hand spam them. they will generally respond to a dismount by panicking and trying to remount. in this timeframe you can lay enough offensive magic to finish them off. versus a mounted archer (ma) it's a bit tougher than dismounting an mc because they generally try and keep distance. against strong mounted opponents, the practical goal is often to force a stalemate rather than chase a clean win. use terrain, cover, and water to ensure survival. charge lesser heals and keep high hp. your goal is survival. make sure they are stripped of magic reflect and shock their mounts (which arcs to them) to dissuade further aggression by them. get to a safe area where they cannot pursue. if you can get an earthquake or boulder off successfully, finish them off with death hand, shock, or other offensive magic. versus a mounted mage (mm) there is no real easy way to win without killing their mount. the best strategy is simply outheal any damage they throw on you (they cast 50% slower than you). if you get a dismount on them the best option is to target their horse so they cannot remount. at this point you must use pets, corrupt, daggers, or any other non-ecu/necro spell as their psyche is through the roof. mm's are particularly vulnerable if you lure them into water and kill their mount. shock spam works great for this. ---water combat--- mages are the natural apex predator in water due to movement speed (lower armor weight = faster swim speed) and their ranged damage. underwater combat is a different style of gameplay. it is more strategic, positional based, and less "twitchy" combat. you have to deliberately think about distance and what spells to use. the rule of thumb for 1v1 underwater is to zone your enemy. what this means is to keep them just far enough away where you can cast on them, but they cannot in turn reach you. in a way this is like underwater "footwork". gauging the distance between you and the enemy is key, and understanding the limits of each specific spell you have is critical to success. shock is a shining example of this - if you are too far away, it will miss. if you are too close, it will arc back to you. keeping within that goldilocks zone is how to win. here is a video demonstrating (mostly) water combat: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzu0n8t7foq group dynamics mages excel best at group play and are masters at several roles: healer/corruptors alpha damagers finishers disruptors healers/corruptors - lesser heal and corrupt are the two most important spells in the game. they are mana efficient and high impact. your ability to heal your group and deny enemy healing is quite brutally the single most impactful thing you can do. alpha damage - alpha damage is the act of opening with a damaging spell. this concept simple - a group which receives big damage first is put on the defensive. a group which does big damage first has the initiative. a simple way of winning fights is to kill 1 enemy and reset the fight to neutral. if the enemy loses a player and the fight is reset, they are far less likely to win when the fight re-engages. alpha damage probes for an opening and gives fighters the ability to pick an enemy. finishers - enemies who are low hp often focus on parrying to survive. they may also receive attention of enemy mages for priority heals. with this in mind, several spells are excellent finishers which aim to kill the target before they can recover. thunderlash, shock, mind blast, or any other high damage easily hitable spell is ideal to accomplish this objective. aoe should generally be avoided because your teammates tend to be pushing the target as well. the most important skill is knowing when to switch from heal/corrupt mode to kill mode. mages require a high level of situational and battlefield awareness. the most common way to identify a low target is to observe the flow of battle. if everyone is pushing forward, your team likely has momentum and enemy targets which are retreating tend to be low. a simple cursor scan to identify hp pools can see who to focus. otherwise, audio cues such as "target is low on the west side" can be a good indicator of when to prepare a spell. disruptors - disruption of enemy groups can be a useful mechanics to sew discord and prevent them from completing certain objectives. the primary disruption mechanics involved sound and visual distortions, particularly with spells like shadow, blinding cloud, and roaring wind. when a group is hit with these spells, it creates confusion and can disrupt their effectiveness in a fight. one example of this in action is casting blinding cloud on an enemy mage line- not only are you limiting their line of sight to prevent their healing, you also cause a damage source which interrupts casting. an enemy group which is being collapsed on also has their mage line disrupted, they are unlikely to recover. priorities as a group mage: listen to leadership commands. they control the flow of the fight and even if they make a "wrong" call, failing to follow it would generally be detrimental. group cohesion is important. do not die. a dead mage is worthless. you must prioritize survival. do not let your teammates die. heal them. a dead teammate is worthless to you. corrupt enemies below 75% hp. this gives an opening for securing them as kills. finish enemies with direct damage spells. if your melees cannot secure the kill, it is your job to do so. crowd control. both pets and enemies can be herded or dealt with by aoe spells. this can also include dropping disruption spells like blinding cloud on enemy mage lines, or cutting off their lines of retreat with other niche spells. some mechanics - flick casting - this technique is when you target an enemy and immediately rip the mouse away while releasing the spell. this somehow guarantees a hit. the condition with which it works requires you to have a solid target first. it takes a bit of getting used to. footwork - footwork is a valuable survival tool. it is impossible to accurately teach someone proper footwork via a written guide. it's more of an art. the strategies to utilize footwork to maximum effect generally involve making sharp 90 or 180 turns, kiting through groups, and using barriers (even other players) to break contact with an attacker. keep conscious of your movement and how it relates to your opponent. watch videos of successful mages and take notes. jump casting - jumping is a powerful tool to reposition while casting. while it is true that you can move while walking and casting, this is not nearly as potent as jumping. to jump cast, sprint the direction you want to move, press space bar, and the moment your feet leave the ground start casting. you can continue to move while the spell finishes charging/releasing. self-heal chain - this is the #1 sustain tool that a mage has in their arsenal. essentially because of the rate of attack melee have, you can time heals inbetween each strike and outheal them while repositioning. become profecient at using footwork, jump casting, and self-casting a lesser heal chain and you will become much more durable as a mage shield repositioning - high quality headphones are needed for this. the idea is you adjust your camera so that your back with the shield on it moves to block anyone attacking you. use audio cues to slightly lead where your attacker is to maximize the amount of equipment hits. spell animation hiding the number one projector of intent with magic is to look directly at a target and give them a full view of what spell you are casting. this is generally not a good thing as they can react to your play. the better option is to position the camera either 90 degrees away from the target, or to have your back completely turned away from them. this is particularly important with spells like earthquake where projecting its casting can cause an enemy mounted to change their behavior. demonstration of flick + jump casting guides.title: Mana Regen
guides.summary: Compare mana regeneration behavior, armor penalties, resting, food, attributes, and other modifiers that affect recovery.

blocks.html:
Mana and Stamina Regeneration

Compare mana regeneration behavior, armor penalties, resting, food, attributes, and other modifiers that affect recovery.
blocks.text: Mana and Stamina Regeneration Compare mana regeneration behavior, armor penalties, resting, food, attributes, and other modifiers that affect recovery.

blocks.html:
Mana Regeneration Mechanics

Mana regeneration occurs in “ticks”, or set intervals. Normal passive mana regeneration hits once every 3 seconds. Resting ticks are 2 seconds in length, and are a separate timer from the passive mana regeneration. Natural mana regeneration with no modifiers is a simple calculation of 1% of mana pool per 3 seconds, or full regeneration after 300 seconds passively. The vitalism/mana regeneration skill doubles this to 2% per 3 seconds, or full regeneration after 150 seconds. This indicates that every 150 mana is a passive 1 mana per second regen. Resting ticks once every 2 seconds. Resting scales slightly with mana pool.

This chart highlights the regeneration rate of each action/skill level a player with 211 mana has, and what the effective mana per second is for various conditions. Remember that this is irrespective of the mana pool that the player has, so the greater the mana pool, the greater the effective mana-per-second regeneration. This chart assumes 100% vitalism/mana regeneration skill.

Characters with lower mana will rest slightly faster to regen due to resting skill scaling, and characters with higher mana will be slightly slower due to the same.

Armor has an inherent penalty to mana regeneration. This modifier is displayed as a % on the character statistics screen, and it ranges from 10%-100%, but can be temporarily raised with other effects (explained further down). This value is what all regeneration is multiplied by, so the effective time-to-full-mana based on different conditions will be modified by this value. blocks.html:
The next big question mages ask is “what is the ideal armor weight”? This question is asked frequently. There is no specific weight that is universally ideal. For skeletal sheevras, 2kg will be a standard to maximize regeneration. For human siege mages in a dungeon, 13kg+ is not uncommon. The rule of thumb for mage armor weight vs mana regen is:

If you die before you run out of mana, add armor.

If you run out of mana before you die, remove armor.

This balancing act is not perfect, and personal playstyle combined with group composition can influence armor needs.

blocks.html:
Increasing Mana Regeneration

The mana regeneration skill is a vital part of recovering magic. It cuts the time of regenerating the mana pool in half at level 100. This skill is, however, not linear. At lower levels it is proportionately less powerful than when maxed. This indicates that players should either maximize vitalism, or leave it at 0 and view their mana pool as a single use resource.

The meditation skill is a modifier for resting. At 50 meditations, regeneration is increased by 12.5%. At 100 meditations, regeneration is increased by 25%. This might seem potent, but consider that this is an investment of 100 points for what amounts to a conditional <0.4 mana per second that is impacted by armor weight. This is one of the single worst skills in the game in its current form.

Food and potions are a complicated but potential source of mana restoration. Mana potions and mana regeneration potions exist, but they are incredibly expensive for anemic impact. Mana food likewise exists, with food such as glimmercap and moonsponge providing a meager mana amount per unit consumed.

blocks.html:
Campfires also add a portion of mana regen, likely around 40%.

Magic Mana Regeneration

There are two sources of mana regeneration from magic:

Mental Healing (Spiritism): Adds a % based mana regeneration bonus that is impacted by mana regeneration penalties. The target it is cast on acts as a turret and anything nearby receives the bonus. The effect of this is heavily influenced by the psyche of the target, i.e. high psyche characters will give the recipients LESS mana regeneration. A good strategy is to target walkers as a battery since they inherently have low psyche.

Mental Leech (Necromancy): Drains mana from the target. Can be purified. From testing a 10 psyche character loses about 3.6 mana per second. A 100 psyche character loses about 3 mana per second. Can be resisted for about a 50% reduction in impact. This seems to be impacted by intelligence and necro damage effects.

blocks.html:
Endurance adds both 20 flat stamina and 1% stamina regeneration at level 100. At first glance this might seem like a trivial amount of stats. However, on a character with 300 stamina that increases the effective stamina to 320, giving a bonus of 6.67% regen from the stamina + 1% flat, giving a total of 7.67% stamina regen. This is not a trivial amount in the slightest.

Rings are also included in the stamina equation. Certain rings add strength, constitution, dexterity, or flat stamina. For every point of stamina that these stats add, the stamina pool increases, and thus regeneration increases.

Alvarins are notably the best at stamina due to their clade gifts. “Resting pulse” is a massive boost to stamina, offering 3 stamina per second while standing still. The other gift “Runner’s High” is an activated ability that increases stamina regeneration by 15% for 20 seconds. Both offer a significant boost to stamina recovery that outrivals any other clade.

Equipment has the potential of hampering stamina regeneration. Every piece of armor impacts stamina regen negatively. You can see what this modifier is in the statistics screen of the character screen. If the value is 100%, there is no difference. If it is 90%, all regen is 90% as effective.

Weapons, particularly, have indirect stamina implications based on the weapons strength requirement vs the characters strength level. Being under the required strength level of a weapon offers severe penalties to stamina usage. Bows notably also require having strength-greater-than-the-gear. Having strength 10, 20, or even 30 points above the requirement further reduces stamina usage with diminishing effect.
blocks.text: Endurance adds both 20 flat stamina and 1% stamina regeneration at level 100. At first glance this might seem like a trivial amount of stats. However, on a character with 300 stamina that increases the effective stamina to 320, giving a bonus of 6.67% regen from the stamina + 1% flat, giving a total of 7.67% stamina regen. This is not a trivial amount in the slightest. Rings are also included in the stamina equation. Certain rings add strength, constitution, dexterity, or flat stamina. For every point of stamina that these stats add, the stamina pool increases, and thus regeneration increases. Alvarins are notably the best at stamina due to their clade gifts. “Resting pulse” is a massive boost to stamina, offering 3 stamina per second while standing still. The other gift “Runner’s High” is an activated ability that increases stamina regeneration by 15% for 20 seconds. Both offer a significant boost to stamina recovery that outrivals any other clade. Equipment has the potential of hampering stamina regeneration. Every piece of armor impacts stamina regen negatively. You can see what this modifier is in the statistics screen of the character screen. If the value is 100%, there is no difference. If it is 90%, all regen is 90% as effective. Weapons, particularly, have indirect stamina implications based on the weapons strength requirement vs the characters strength level. Being under the required strength level of a weapon offers severe penalties to stamina usage. Bows notably also require having strength-greater-than-the-gear. Having strength 10, 20, or even 30 points above the requirement further reduces stamina usage with diminishing effect.

blocks.html:
Testing also established a theoretical maximum-mana setup. An age 70-72 sheevra has a the highest natural peak with 270 mana. With +8 raw int and + 8 raw psyche rings each with +11 mana (+22 mana total), this comes out to a max potential of 308 mana.

With 308 mana it regenerates 2.05 mana per second, or 6.15 mana per tick. Pretty incredible stuff!

guides.title: Necromancy Walkers
guides.summary: Reference the creation, control, strengths, limitations, and material needs of necromantic walkers.

blocks.html: Necromancy: Walkers
blocks.text: Necromancy: Walkers

blocks.html:
Overview

Reference the creation, control, strengths, limitations, and material needs of necromantic walkers.

There are three types of walker: Regular, Strong, and Greater. Each have particular use cases.

  • Regular Walker are equivalent to graveyard walkers in terms of power. These are the weakest to summon, but also require less upfront mana cost. If many bodies are needed, these are the go-to.
  • Strong Walkers wear ranger armor, and have more HP, are faster, and hit harder than regular walkers. These are better for chasing, but are still squishy.
  • Greater Walkers are by far the most durable of the walkers. They have a high armor rating and do respectable damage. These are the “go-to” walkers as they are not easily peeled and they are sticky.

As Walkers are heavily dependent on mana, and specifically mana regeneration, they are more suited for mage characters to use. Paladins/Death Knights can hold walkers, but they are limited by their stunted regeneration. The higher effective mana regen a character has, the more walkers they can theoretically hold. All Walker types have an upkeep of 0.125 mana per second with 100 walker knowledge lore. This indicates using greaters is generally the better idea.

blocks.html:
Acquisition

Acquiring the ability to summon walkers is simple. First you need a spellbook, then acquire Raise Walker, Raise Strong Walker, Raise Greater Walker, Command Undead, and Control Undead scrolls. All scrolls except for Raise Greater Walker are easily obtainable by farming Necromancers at the various necromancer spawns around the map. Raise Greater Walker is a bit more difficult as it is a rare drop from the Tower of Descensus (Necro Dungeon). It is generally better to buy this scroll if you are incapable of farming it. After acquiring these spells, raise necromancy to the appropriate level. This can be done with raising walkers alone. See #spell-masterlist for more information.

Acquiring the Walker Knowledge book (Tome of the Walking Dead) is a key component of successful walker usage. This dramatically lowers the mana cost of maintaining walkers under your control. It is purchasable from the Piskan Augaur at the Tower of Descensus (Necro Dung) for 2.5g in dungeon currency or you can buy it from other players. Extensive testing covered the mana cost but the footage got corrupted. The current estimate is that, it reduces cost of holding walkers by about 80%. It is a secondary under zoology, so there is no reason NOT to have this skill.

Leveling Walker Knowledge is simple - summon a horde of regular walkers and keep them under your control. Recast control undead every ~14 minutes or so. With about 9 walkers Players can grind to this 100 in approximately 3 hours.

You may also optionally acquire the Sacrificial Eruption and Sacrificial Heal spells, but these are highly situational and not mandatory for normal walker usage. Akh Bond is another potent spell that works decently well with walkers.

blocks.html:
How to Use

Walkers require 3 reagents each - bone tissue, spirits (1, 2, or 3), and an appropriate bone for each. Regular walkers require Emalj, Strong require Molarium, and Greaters require Incisium. You will also need ritual blood + spirits to control and command these summons. The learn how to acquire these reagents, visit the #reagents channel.

blocks.html:
Using walkers is a clunky process, but the payoff is immense. Here is the order of operation:

  1. Cast Raise [Walker Type] as many times as you want. They will spawn on the ground in front of you after a brief delay
  2. Aim at the walkers and cast Control Undead. The walkers are now under your control and will follow you.
  3. Aim at a hostile target and cast Command Undead on them. The walkers will attack that target until it is dead, their aggro is taken by something else, or until you cast command undead on something else.
  4. Cast Command Undead on self to have them re-follow you.
  5. Walkers have a timed life of 900 seconds (15 minutes). This can be refreshed by casting control undead on them again without needing to raise more.

The general strategy of using walkers is to amass an appropriate amount for the task at hand, and sic them on targets you want dead. For example, if you are doing bosses such as Bandit leaders, about 6 greater walkers is sufficient. If you are fighting harder enemies, you can amass even more and use that. Walkers also have "defensive stance" enabled by default, meaning if they are attacked by something they will attack back.

For PvP, having foresight and amassing walkers early and regening mana is preferred. A group of walkers can permanently lockdown players who do not know how to counter them. Being mounted and having a horde of walkers is a viable strategy as well. When combined with ritual pets, the necromancer has access to an absurd amount of raw HP/damage at his disposal. Combining Walkers with a Ritual summon such as a risen taur dog is potent because the pet will clump up with the horde and do significant damage while being body blocked by the undead.

Walkers sometimes get bugged into a slow walking state. To fix this, self cast command undead to get them back following at full speed again.

blocks.html: Determining how many walkers one can use is an art, not a science. As Walkers are heavily dependent on mana, and specifically mana regeneration, they are more suited for mage characters to use. Paladins/Death Knights can hold walkers, but they are limited by their stunted regeneration. The higher effective mana regen a character has, the more walkers they can theoretically hold. In most situations, 4-8 greater walkers is what mages use in PvP. That enables for some mana regen while also maintaining enough power in walkers for them to be effective.

blocks.html:
Sacrificial Eruption + Heal

Sacrificial Eruption is a spell which explodes all of the walkers that are under the control of the necromancer. This spell can be thrown on anything, and as long as it hits, the walkers will explode. This explosion has a slight delay and players should account for desync when using it. This spell has huge damage potential, but also risks wasting many mana on a whiff.

The damage calculation for sacrificial eruption is very misunderstood. The common perception is that greater walkers = little damage, while regular walkers = big damage. This is a half truth. Sacrificial eruption’s effectiveness is based on the psyche of the target. Greater Walkers have higher psyche than normal Walkers. Ergo, when people clump up Greater Walkers and erupt them, the damage seems low. However, if the caster has a group of greater walkers + 1 normal walker and they target the normal walker, all of the greater walkers will explode for big numbers.

SACRIFICIAL ERUPTION DOES NOT DAMAGE THE CASTER

SACRIFICIAL ERUPTION DOES DAMAGE FRIENDLIES, INCLUDING PETS. Tactician does NOT apply to eruption unless it is specifically cast on a friendly.

Here is a demonstration by @Dremlock of doing some eruption in PvP to 1 shot people:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xWwMwqa5tTQ

Sacrificial Heal is absolute dog crap. Literally one of the worst spells in game. Do not use it. It heals for ~35 health for 8 mana AND requires to to target a Walker AND it kills the summon. Just lesser heal for ~30 for 4 mana instead.

blocks.html:
Countering

Countering Walkers is a good skill to have, even as a necromancer. Getting a big horde of undead on you can lock you out of playing. There are several strategies to counter walkers:

  1. Terrain - Walkers are afraid of heights and water. Jump up on stuff and get away from them.
  2. Elementalism - A static shock, fireball, firewall, or any other number of AoE spells are good at handling walkers. Miasma is OK too. These spell are especially good when paired with terrain or wates.
  3. Kill the necromancer - Once a necro is dead, his Walkers no longer have mana to sustain and they become worthless.
  4. Housing - Get inside and close a door. They are 2 stoopid to turn the knob.
  5. Control Undead - Necromancers with higher necromancy levels than the enemy can cast control undead on the walkers and steal them. It is difficult to know if your necromancy level is higher, so just cast control undead and see if it works. Now, if both necromancers are level 100 necromancy, there is some unknown variable no one has been able to discover which allows one necro to steal from the other, but not vice versa. Testing has covered ritual level, psyche, int, and a ton of other potential answers, but the only thing that makes sense so far is character creation date/time.

to eruption unless it is specifically cast on a friendly. here is a demonstration by @dremlock of doing some eruption in pvp to 1 shot people: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xwwmwqa5ttq sacrificial heal is absolute dog crap. literally one of the worst spells in game. do not use it. it heals for ~35 health for 8 mana and requires to to target a walker and it kills the summon. just lesser heal for ~30 for 4 mana instead. countering countering walkers is a good skill to have, even as a necromancer. getting a big horde of undead on you can lock you out of playing. there are several strategies to counter walkers: terrain - walkers are afraid of heights and water. jump up on stuff and get away from them. elementalism - a static shock, fireball, firewall, or any other number of aoe spells are good at handling walkers. miasma is ok too. these spell are especially good when paired with terrain or wates. kill the necromancer - once a necro is dead, his walkers no longer have mana to sustain and they become worthless. housing - get inside and close a door. they are 2 stoopid to turn the knob. control undead - necromancers with higher necromancy levels than the enemy can cast control undead on the walkers and steal them. it is difficult to know if your necromancy level is higher, so just cast control undead and see if it works. now, if both necromancers are level 100 necromancy, there is some unknown variable no one has been able to discover which allows one necro to steal from the other, but not vice versa. testing has covered ritual level, psyche, int, and a ton of other potential answers, but the only thing that makes sense so far is character creation date/time.

guides.title: Ritualism
guides.summary: Follow the ritualism process from preparation to result, with circles, artifacts, materials, outcomes, and common failure points.

blocks.html:
Necromantic Rituals

Introduction

Follow the ritualism process from preparation to result, with circles, artifacts, materials, outcomes, and common failure points.

It is important to understand why ritualism is a commanding skill. Afterall, a summoned creature is sometimes less powerful than its living equivalent. Here are some perspectives which should be considered before adopting ritualism:

  • Compared to all other active skills, Necromantic Rituals is the most potent point for point
  • Highly optimized builds can fit ritualism easily, while living pets will not fit
  • Carcass can be stored en masse for consistent access to summons

It gives access to unique and powerful creatures that cannot be obtained otherwise

  • No creature control, herding, or beast mastery skill needed to use summons.

Here are some perspectives which should be considered before adopting ritualism: Compared to all other active skills, Necromantic Rituals is the most potent point for point Highly optimized builds can fit ritualism easily, while living pets will not fit Carcass can be stored en masse for consistent access to summons It gives access to unique and powerful creatures that cannot be obtained otherwise No creature control, herding, or beast mastery skill needed to use summons.

blocks.html:
With immense power comes heavy cost, however. There are many downsides to necromantic rituals that must be considered before committing to this dark art. Coping with these consequences are mandatory to become successful:

  • Summons tend to lose the defensive stats of their living equivalents
  • One cannot go into towns with summons
  • Although they are stronger, risen horses can’t carry as much as their living counterparts
  • Startup cost is very high and maintaining a cache of undead is time consuming
  • Summoning temporarily impacts players psyche

If the advantages of rituals entice and the negatives do not dissuade, you are destined to become powerful. With proper preparation any threat becomes trivial. Death is not the end.

blocks.html:
Obtaining Necromantic Rituals

There are two ways of acquiring the Necromantic Rituals skill: buying Notes of Necromantic Rituals or obtaining Mortal Nexus of Necromantic Rituals. The notes only level rituals to level 1, while Mortal Nexus raises it to level 70 base skill. Ritual notes are a much cheaper and efficient method of getting maxed rituals, while reading Mortal Nexus is more convenient and thus less of a grind.

Ritual notes are sold in the basement of Fabernum tower at the cost of 50 carved bones. Carved bones drop from necromancers at specific points of interest on the map. The notes are also often found on the trade broker for 300-600g. A trick that can save many money is buying bones directly and purchasing the notes in the basement of the tower.

Mortal Nexus of Necromantic Rituals is significantly more difficult to acquire as it is a rare drop from the boss at the Tower of Descensus. The cost of these far outweigh their benefits. However, they do get rid of the early grind required for notes.

This map below shows the three main vendors for Necromancy:

blocks.html:
Location #1 is where to buy Necromancer’s Notes to learn Necromancy, as well as to buy ritual circles and ritual candles.

Location #2 is the Fabernum tower, which has a vendor in the basement behind a hidden wall which sells Notes of Necromantic Rituals. Near the end of the dungeon there is a lever which opens a backroom. Go into this backroom and you must find the hidden path to find the vendor.

Location #3 is the Tower of Descensus, which houses a powerful Tupilak circle, has drops for the vast majority of necromancy related items, and has a special vendor which you can buy Tupilak ritual circles from.

blocks.html:
Leveling

There currently exists a very cheap method to level necromantic rituals from level 25-100 utilizing a Tupilak and its abilities. This technique requires minimal grinding, and is magnitudes cheaper than the previous method of leveling the necromantic rituals skill. It is possible that there will be a patch to nullify this method in the future.

  1. Get Necromancy to at least level 20.
  2. Acquire and read ritual notes. These typically go for 200g. You can get 50 ritual bones and trade for them in the fab tower basement if needed.
  3. Acquire ritual circles and candles. These are purchasable from the vendor marked at location #1 on the map above. For mages most mages this will require 50 summoning sets due to their attribute bonuses boosting necromantic rituals skill. It will take 105 circles with 10 int and 10 psyche. It is recommended to max your intelligence and psyche while doing this process for maximum attribute bonus.
  4. Gather or buy 5000 chicken carcasses and spam summon them. You will need more than this if you do not have a high psyche and intelligence. Players can also spam kill pigs at their spawn and resurrect them quickly. The goal is to raise rituals/necromancy to 25. Each summoning requires you to place a circle, put in carcass, and put in a candle.
  5. Once rituals are 25, relog. You now need a Tupilak. Tupilak circles are obtainable from the broker for a hefty price, or from the vendor on the hill at the Descensus Tower in exchange for dungeon drops. The recipe for a vanilla tupilak is 4000 mino, 4000 coralis crab, and 4000 troll, 4000 troll, and another 4000 troll carcass. Use your tupilak circle and a ritual candle to make one.

blocks.html: 1. Tupilaks can technically be raised at level 1 rituals, but the trick comes from the interaction it now has with active skills. Tupilaks are not intended to use the beast mastery to use their abilities but rather it scales with ritualism level. At level 25 you unlock the first ability on a tupilak. Spamming this ability raises necromancy AND ritualism. Spam it on an equerry in a stronghold until you hit 100 rituals and 100 necromancy, and you are done! Welcome to the dark side. Having beastmastery at 100 greatly improves focus generation of the Tupilak and thus increases leveling speed.

blocks.html:
Summoning Explained

Ritualism at its base requires three components: a ritual circle, a ritual candle, and a carcass. These three components are always required and they go in the ritual circle in a specific order. Below is an example of a ritual circle, with explanations for each slot:
blocks.text: Summoning Explained Ritualism at its base requires three components: a ritual circle, a ritual candle, and a carcass. These three components are always required and they go in the ritual circle in a specific order. Below is an example of a ritual circle, with explanations for each slot:

blocks.html:
Slot #1 is for the primary carcass of what you are summoning. Whatever carcass you place in this slot is what will spawn. The amount of carcass required is listed in a chart in the next section. You will need to have the total amount of carcass listed in your inventory- for example, a risen desert horse will require you to have 40,000 desert horse carcasses in your inventory.

Slot #2 is for gems. This optional slot augments the attack power of the summon. The greater the gold cost of the item, the greater the effect. There is diminishing returns on this, however.

The best possible gem to put in a ritual summon is the Red Thunderegg, which drops from the Ultimeki / Greater Kimuru boss in the north center portion of the map. This item is sold to vendors for 500g and sells for much more to players. The next best gem is an adamant (diamond), which costs 12g. Unless you are building the ultimate summon, it is generally better to stick with lower gems as the reward is not linear.

Slot #3 is for artifacts. These currently only add HP to the ritual summon, but these are extremely rare and not well tested. In most situations, the effect of the artifact scales with its vendor gold cost. It is likely the effects of an artifact will change in the future.

Slot #4 is for secondary carcass. These resources boost the HP of the summon, with higher quality carcasses giving a greater result. The best known secondary carcass is Snow Troll.

Slot #5 is for ritual candles, which is a required item to complete the summoning.

blocks.html:
Correction - Belbus is 6000 carcass

Water Lizard is probably C or B tier now

Recipes

A common question is “which summons should be used?” and “how should a summon be built?”. The most direct answer to both of these questions is: use the best summon for the job you intend and build it with what is sustainable to you. Use the charts in the above subsections to determine what primary and secondary carcasses you have access to, and what gems you can consistently use. There are no hidden combinations that yield exponentially more powerful creatures. It all comes down to the quality of what is used in the summoning.

When it comes to the purpose of the summon, plan on how exactly the summon will be used in a typical encounter. If you are a mounted archer or mage, it would be ideal to use something like a lynx or panther since they are capable of keeping up with mounts and even hitting enemy mounts in 3rd gear. If you are based in the north, a lynx is going to be your primary summon. If you are in the jungle, use a panther.

At this time, the ideal gem that should be used is the best that you have consistent access to. If you can farm snow trolls, you will have a ton of rubers which are great for increasing your summon’s damage. You will also have access to snow troll carcass, which is the best possible secondary carcass right now. If you regularly farm sewers, the sewer gems are what you will best use.

A go-to inexpensive recipe for a strong general purpose ritual summon is 5,650 celaino primary carcass with 15k lowland molva secondary carcass, plus a topaz. Artifacts are far too uncommon right now to add to non-siege summons.

blocks.html:
Future Tech, Tips and Tricks

Many new creatures are bound to come to the world of Nave. Myrland is only one part of the world of Mortal Online 2, and there are many new planned continents. There were also several unique summons in Mortal Online 1 which have not yet made it, but appear to be planned.

The entire continent of Sarduccaa, a desert land to the west of Myrland, will be full of unique and powerful arthropods and other terrifying animals to slaughter and raise. These bugs offer powerful stats and are quite scary to encounter.

An often hated summon in Mortal Online 1 was the Death Knight. This terrifying creature is the corpse of a powerful human warrior clad in armor. It possessed strong combat abilities as well as the ability to use ranged attacks.

One promised feature is placeable and permanent ritual tables for housing. This will presumably be obtainable from the Tower of Descensus (Necro Dungeon) within the relatively near future. The benefit to this is immense as it is both convenient and saves the need to place expensive ritual tables everytime a summoning ritual is done.

Allegedly, a Tupilak summoned in the Tower of Descensus is more powerful than one summoned with a ritual circle. There is a question as to whether or not this is true at this time.

Summoning or unstabling two ritual mounts at the same time kills one. Summoning or unstabling two ritual combat summons at the same time kills one. Be sure to avoid doing this or you will lose many effort.

It is beneficial to name ritual horses something unique so that you remember not to blindly ride it into town. It may take you a few times of losing your horse and going criminal, but eventually you will remember that ritual summons + town = death.

These bugs offer powerful stats and are quite scary to encounter. An often hated summon in Mortal Online 1 was the Death Knight. This terrifying creature is the corpse of a powerful human warrior clad in armor. It possessed strong combat abilities as well as the ability to use ranged attacks. One promised feature is placeable and permanent ritual tables for housing. This will presumably be obtainable from the Tower of Descensus (Necro Dungeon) within the relatively near future. The benefit to this is immense as it is both convenient and saves the need to place expensive ritual tables everytime a summoning ritual is done. Allegedly, a Tupilak summoned in the Tower of Descensus is more powerful than one summoned with a ritual circle. There is a question as to whether or not this is true at this time. Summoning or unstabling two ritual mounts at the same time kills one. Summoning or unstabling two ritual combat summons at the same time kills one. Be sure to avoid doing this or you will lose many effort. It is beneficial to name ritual horses something unique so that you remember not to blindly ride it into town. It may take you a few times of losing your horse and going criminal, but eventually you will remember that ritual summons + town = death.

follow the ritualism process from preparation to result, with circles, artifacts, materials, outcomes, and common failure points. it is important to understand why ritualism is a commanding skill. afterall, a summoned creature is sometimes less powerful than its living equivalent. here are some perspectives which should be considered before adopting ritualism: compared to all other active skills, necromantic rituals is the most potent point for point highly optimized builds can fit ritualism easily, while living pets will not fit carcass can be stored en masse for consistent access to summons it gives access to unique and powerful creatures that cannot be obtained otherwise no creature control, herding, or beast mastery skill needed to use summons. with immense power comes heavy cost, however. there are many downsides to necromantic rituals that must be considered before committing to this dark art. coping with these consequences are mandatory to become successful: summons tend to lose the defensive stats of their living equivalents one cannot go into towns with summons although they are stronger, risen horses can’t carry as much as their living counterparts startup cost is very high and maintaining a cache of undead is time consuming summoning temporarily impacts players psyche if the advantages of rituals entice and the negatives do not dissuade, you are destined to become powerful. with proper preparation any threat becomes trivial. death is not the end. obtaining necromantic rituals there are two ways of acquiring the necromantic rituals skill: buying notes of necromantic rituals or obtaining mortal nexus of necromantic rituals. the notes only level rituals to level 1, while mortal nexus raises it to level 70 base skill. ritual notes are a much cheaper and efficient method of getting maxed rituals, while reading mortal nexus is more convenient and thus less of a grind. ritual notes are sold in the basement of fabernum tower at the cost of 50 carved bones. carved bones drop from necromancers at specific points of interest on the map. the notes are also often found on the trade broker for 300-600g. a trick that can save many money is buying bones directly and purchasing the notes in the basement of the tower. mortal nexus of necromantic rituals is significantly more difficult to acquire as it is a rare drop from the boss at the tower of descensus. the cost of these far outweigh their benefits. however, they do get rid of the early grind required for notes. this map below shows the three main vendors for necromancy: location #1 is where to buy necromancer’s notes to learn necromancy, as well as to buy ritual circles and ritual candles. location #2 is the fabernum tower, which has a vendor in the basement behind a hidden wall which sells notes of necromantic rituals. near the end of the dungeon there is a lever which opens a backroom. go into this backroom and you must find the hidden path to find the vendor. location #3 is the tower of descensus, which houses a powerful tupilak circle, has drops for the vast majority of necromancy related items, and has a special vendor which you can buy tupilak ritual circles from. leveling there currently exists a very cheap method to level necromantic rituals from level 25-100 utilizing a tupilak and its abilities. this technique requires minimal grinding, and is magnitudes cheaper than the previous method of leveling the necromantic rituals skill. it is possible that there will be a patch to nullify this method in the future. get necromancy to at least level 20. acquire and read ritual notes. these typically go for 200g. you can get 50 ritual bones and trade for them in the fab tower basement if needed. acquire ritual circles and candles. these are purchasable from the vendor marked at location #1 on the map above. for mages most mages this will require 50 summoning sets due to their attribute bonuses boosting necromantic rituals skill. it will take 105 circles with 10 int and 10 psyche. it is recommended to max your intelligence and psyche while doing this process for maximum attribute bonus. gather or buy 5000 chicken carcasses and spam summon them. you will need more than this if you do not have a high psyche and intelligence. players can also spam kill pigs at their spawn and resurrect them quickly. the goal is to raise rituals/necromancy to 25. each summoning requires you to place a circle, put in carcass, and put in a candle. once rituals are 25, relog. you now need a tupilak. tupilak circles are obtainable from the broker for a hefty price, or from the vendor on the hill at the descensus tower in exchange for dungeon drops. the recipe for a vanilla tupilak is 4000 mino, 4000 coralis crab, and 4000 troll, 4000 troll, and another 4000 troll carcass. use your tupilak circle and a ritual candle to make one. tupilaks can technically be raised at level 1 rituals, but the trick comes from the interaction it now has with active skills. tupilaks are not intended to use the beast mastery to use their abilities but rather it scales with ritualism level. at level 25 you unlock the first ability on a tupilak. spamming this ability raises necromancy and ritualism. spam it on an equerry in a stronghold until you hit 100 rituals and 100 necromancy, and you are done! welcome to the dark side. having beastmastery at 100 greatly improves focus generation of the tupilak and thus increases leveling speed. summoning explained ritualism at its base requires three components: a ritual circle, a ritual candle, and a carcass. these three components are always required and they go in the ritual circle in a specific order. below is an example of a ritual circle, with explanations for each slot: slot #1 is for the primary carcass of what you are summoning. whatever carcass you place in this slot is what will spawn. the amount of carcass required is listed in a chart in the next section. you will need to have the total amount of carcass listed in your inventory- for example, a risen desert horse will require you to have 40,000 desert horse carcasses in your inventory. slot #2 is for gems. this optional slot augments the attack power of the summon. the greater the gold cost of the item, the greater the effect. there is diminishing returns on this, however. the best possible gem to put in a ritual summon is the red thunderegg, which drops from the ultimeki / greater kimuru boss in the north center portion of the map. this item is sold to vendors for 500g and sells for much more to players. the next best gem is an adamant (diamond), which costs 12g. unless you are building the ultimate summon, it is generally better to stick with lower gems as the reward is not linear. slot #3 is for artifacts. these currently only add hp to the ritual summon, but these are extremely rare and not well tested. in most situations, the effect of the artifact scales with its vendor gold cost. it is likely the effects of an artifact will change in the future. slot #4 is for secondary carcass. these resources boost the hp of the summon, with higher quality carcasses giving a greater result. the best known secondary carcass is snow troll. slot #5 is for ritual candles, which is a required item to complete the summoning. carcass reference: correction - belbus is 6000 carcass water lizard is probably c or b tier now recipes a common question is “which summons should be used?” and “how should a summon be built?”. the most direct answer to both of these questions is: use the best summon guides.title: Scribing
guides.summary: Learn the scribing workflow, required skills and tools, copy limits, material costs, and factors that affect success.

blocks.html:
Scribing is the skill which is used to apply scrolls into spellbooks, which permanently unlocks the spell for the player as long as the soulbound spellbook is in their inventory. The scribing book is obtained via the Illusionist boss in the Tindrem Sewers, the Sewer King boss in the Fab Sewers, or one of the bosses in the MK sewers. This book will level scribing skill to 70.

To level from 70 to 100, use fulminate, mental projectile, and greater healing scrolls.

To level from 76 - 100, use ressurect scrolls. Scribing is a weird skill in that you need above the minimum skill required for it to give a chance at success.

The equation for scribing success is 100/level range of a scroll. For example, a ressurect scroll is between 75-100. The level range for this is 25 (100-75). Each level within that range thus 1/25th success rate (4%). At level 76, you have a 4% success rate, at 77 you have an 8% success rate, 78 = 12% success rate, etc.

Spell Masterlist

All spells in this section have stats for 105 intelligence on foot. If you have anything other than 105, the values will differ. Being mounted also alters certain values. All spells are in alphabetical order within their schools.

Key

Damage: How much damage it does with 100 mental offense. This can be flat damage or per tick.

Mana: How much this spell costs with 100 mental focus.

Range: How far the spell will throw (1000 units = 10 meters)

Cast Time: How many seconds it takes to charge

Skill Range: Required spell levels to cast. At max skill range it is 100%.

Reagents: What it costs to cast this spell.

There are also certain conditions where these rules have exceptions. For example, if you have a magic reflect and your target has a magic reflect, ecumencial and necromancy spells will reflect off of the initial target, but NOT proc the casters reflect and instead penetrate it without using it up. In this same scenario with an elementalism spell that is reflectable, it will bounce off the initial target and penetrate and proc the magic reflect of the shooter.

Another unique scenario is when hitting a with reflectable spells and it hits multiple targets. For example, ignition from the elementalism propulsion school procs reflect. When hitting multiple targets, it procs the reflect on all of them, but only reflects back one source of damage.

guides.title: Spell Tier List
guides.summary: A practical comparison of spells by usefulness and role, with context for why each option performs where it does.

blocks.html:
This section goes over all current spells and ranks them according to their usefulness and effectivness in PvP.

S Tier - Exceptional spells

A Tier - Great spells which might have some situational usage

B Tier - Either average power or they require specific conditions which are not always present

C Tier - Mediocre spells which have limited use

D Tier - Bad spells

Utility - Spells which are either reliant on other effects or not directly useful for PvP. These will not be explained.

blocks.html:
S Tier

Lesser Heal - The most useful mage spell. Its efficiency is unmatched and it drives the flow of a fight. The low mana cost, quick cast, and impact it has is unparalleled. Certainly the best healing spell in the game.

Magic Reflect - There is no reason other than laziness not to have magic reflects on before every single fight. This is almost a strictly beneficial spell that increases the resiliency of your group and can easily counter alpha damage in a fight.

Corrupt - The fight winner. A single corrupt has the potential to prevent an infinite amount of healing, while also doing damage. Targets which are below 75% should be corrupted.

A single corrupt has the potential to prevent an infinite amount of healing, while also doing damage. Targets which are below 75% should be corrupted.

blocks.html:
A Tier

Akh Bond - This is basically a free 17.5% damage reduction as long as you are within range of your pet. The only reason not to have it on at all times during PvP is if you do not have necromancy, or your pet is dead for some reason. Even having it on a spare horse is useful.

Thunderlash - One of the best single target spells. Useful for finishing targets, or when shock is not indicated. Stick with shock unless you have a teammate fighting an enemy, in which case switch to this. The downside? Mana intensive and can be resisted rather harshly.

Spurt - There are 3 uses for spurt - stripping magic reflect, executing mercy mode targets, and interrupting casts of enemy mages. The very cheap cost, high range, quick cast time, and utility this spell offers make it a fantastic addition to your arsenal.

Purify - The cure-all. Gets rid of corrupt, fulmination, and most necro effects for a whopping 6 mana.

Mental Projectile - The “railgun” of the magic world. It is high direct target damage that has a 45m range and ignores magic reflect. The downsides are it blinds you when casting and it casts on completion, so it cannot be chambered.

Raise Greater Walker - A horde of greater walkers is a cheap way to multiply a fighting force. Sending them on any character renders that character useless until they deal with the horde. Requires significant prep time and continually costs mana.

Death Hand - The “battlemage” spell which does high damage and heals the caster at a quick cast speed. Will make you out-of-mana quickly, and it is easy to be interrupted since you must be close to the target. Its ability to trade in melee range with this is unmatched.

Shock - One of the most mana efficient offensive spells, it is an ele propulsion spell that acts as a fast casting hitscan, minus the heavy mana cost. The downsides are that it is very skill based, as at close range you get hit with the arc. When an enemy is in the sweet spot of distance, they melt quickly.

blocks.html:
Lightning Bolt - Similar to fireball but easier to hit, it also lacks the burn damage over time. Instead this synergizes more with shock due to adding the shocked status effect. It’s also a heavier investment, so choose between this and just using fireball.

Static Charge - A fantastic area denial spell which can seal chokepoints, get sneaky opening ganks, and it is even good for PvE. Cast it on doors to prevent people from fleeing or entering. Use it against pets to melt them quickly. Only costs a cuprum, too.

Miasma - A strong damage over time spell, but it is easily avoided. Best used to flush out houses, deny pushes, to hit the enemy midline with.

Mental Leech - Drains the enemy mana pool to recover your own. For about 5 mana you can recover approximately 50. Very potent spell which keeps your mana pool full with proper management.

Hailstone - A fast casting direct damage spell that casts very quickly. Very potent versus pets or in mage vs. mage fights.

Ember - Also fast casting direct damage spell. Slightly better than hailstone because it is part blunt damage and can cause a burn effect.

Earthquake - Great for dismounts, but has a hefty mana cost and the self-damage isn’t great. Super short cast range. This is the ultimate anti-mounted tech.

Lightning - A cheap spammable direct damage spell, but is often resisted vs. high psyche characters. Has the potential to melt players if they are low psyche.

blocks.html:
B Tier

Outburst - Damage isn’t great and it is resisted a lot, even if it has incredible range and low skill point requirement.

Flamestrike - Not mana efficient, although it is fantastic burst damage.

Great Heal - Chunky mana cost and is outclassed by lesser heal over time. Great for saving people in the nick of time, but generally lesser heal is better indicated.

Mindblast - Niche use against mages and no one else. Outclassed by most other damage spells except against high psyche targets.

Ether Barrier - Strong in the ether but it is easy enough to survive as a ghost regardless.

Raise Strong Walker - Faster than greater walker, but also much squishier. Generally just better to run greaters.

blocks.html:
Atrophy - The high cost and low duration makes this ineffective versus players. At best it buys 15 seconds versus enemy pets.

Cloud of Ashes - Great as an escape tool or to disrupt enemies, but also requires a target to cast and does self damage. If this did not do self-damage it would be A-tier since it currently disrupts casting!

Firewall - Fantastic versus pets. However, the high skill point cost combined with the need to carry 4 pitch per cast make it outclassed by static shock.

Sand Barrier - A sleeper spell that disrupts enemy mage lines rather well. Pulling it off is somewhat difficult, however. Why not just fireball instead?

Gale - The high mana cost for what is essentially a small push makes this a hard sell to use frequently. Useful mostly when enemies are in vulnerable positions. Otherwise, pass on it.

Auw Surge - This area-of-effect cone damage spell ignores magic reflect and can be casted while sprinting, making it one of the best skirmish damage spells. Great for alpha damage when enemies are clumped. Mana intensive. Can be combo’d with the human war cries and tactician to nuke through friendly lines.

Fireball - A general purpose ranged AOE nuke which causes burning damage and is very annoying to be hit by. Great as an opener or when an enemy group is clumped.

blocks.html:
Tarball - Uniquely effective in Zerg vs. Zerg fights, this bouncy spell can disrupt enemy lines - if it hits.

Boulder - A bouncy spell skill shot which requires good aiming and a bit of luck, this spell is a decent option at countering mounts. It has a high mana cost for a spell that isn’t guaranteed to hit, however.

Sandspout - This is like a budget Auw Surge - it penetrates through enemies and does decent damage for roughly the same mana cost, but it also cannot be casted while sprinting. Combine that with requiring 10 granum powder per cast, and it makes it difficult to kit with.

Tar Pit - Similar to tarball, this is best when lobbing into large clusters of players. The application is zerg versus zerg fights.

Water Spiral - Called the “Water shotgun” since it does incredibly damage to single targets in very close range, this has potential for burst damage. However, a 5 second cast time makes it difficult to properly time landing all 3 projectiles at once, and even more difficult to successfully cast without interruption.

Gravity Snare - Similar to gale, this spell’s application is environment specific. The 125 mana cost of it makes it a really hard sell unless it is critically successful and pushes enemies off of a cliff or something. Can be magic reflected.

blocks.html:
Starfall - A strong visual effect and a great area denial tool and dismounter. However, the high cast time combined with people being able to walk out of it make it ineffective in most situations. Great for holding chokes or preventing people fleeing. Also useful as an opener if the enemy group is unaware of you.

Scaling Fumes - A high damage rocket salvo that is probably going to miss most of its shots. Great at opening ganks, however. The high cast time and scattered impact of the projectiles makes it ineffective most of the time.

Consuming Void - An area of effect blind with niche applications at disrupting mages or paladins. Useful for making a great escape or disrupting a fight, but otherwise a high cost for a spell that might amount to nothing or even be harmful.

Ice barrier - A constant slew of nerfs makes this an increasingly difficult spell to pull off. While its impact is strong, it has a very long cast time, a small bubble, and the duration is not that great. When used properly can split groups. Also useful for some parkour applications.

Shadow - Basically a blinding cloud without the damage. exceptionally high mana cost with a high cast time makes it unappealing.

Conflagration - A neat AoE hellfire-esque spell, it simply does not have a very strong impact.

Crystal Formation - Infinite potential with stacking bleeds, this spell might be a sleeper. Use against people clumped in houses to great effect.

blocks.html:
C Tier

Fulmination - A slightly stronger thunderlash with a delayed effect and it can be purified. Just use thunderlash.

Kau Regeneration - This is not useful for living PvP, and etherworld PvP isn’t decided by this spell.

Mental Healing - Potentially restores a ton of mana to your team, but also requires many coordination for a mediocre effect.

Raise Walker - Synergizes best with sacrificial eruption and heal, but those are also mediocre spells. Regular walkers are simply too squishy to be impactful against anyone but a pure mage or pets.

Blind - The high mana cost combined with the short duration of this effect make it mediocre in all regards. Just shoot damage spells at the enemy.

Stone - An ultra-mana efficient spell that requires good aiming and for desync to cooperate. Not great versus moving targets, but can good effect if the shooter is skilled enough.

Starshower - The high cast time combined with low hit probability makes this an average spell at best, however it does have niche uses. Several mages spamming this on a house make it a somewhat decent way of countering house hugging.

Sacrificial Eruption - A meme spell. Could potentially have big impact if properly controlled, but desync and the inconsistency of walker usage make it janky. You’re also investing a huge amount into walkers just to use them for 1 burst spell that is probably not going to work properly.

Sludge - Not with the mana cost, cast time, or synergy with fire spells. Should probably go in

blocks.html:
Torrent - Not impactful enough. Low damage and does not push back well enough.

Dust Burst - Not impactful enough. The bleeding/blind effect do not work against targets that aren’t intentionally standing in the effect.

Mending Vapors - Does less healing than a lesser heal, and at a slower rate. Might have niche use at removing ignited but, just use lesser heal.

Ignition - The concept is promising, but the hit detection is just too poor. Combine it with a relatively high mana cost compared to other propulsion spells for not-much-more damage makes this not impactful enough. Might have niche applications versus stacked pets, but why not just use static shock?

Geyser Wall - Not enough impact. Requires a nimbic spirit to cast.

Stilling Mist - Similar with mending vapors, it is not worth the cast time. Just use lesser heal. Could use a buff.

Comet - A worse fireball that doesn’t do burn damage. Synergizes with pierce rings but just use fireball.
