blocks.html:
Scouring Stream - High mana cost for low damage. It’s a budget auw surge replacement at best.

Fuming Bubble - A worse fireball that uses poison instead. Just cast fireball.

Whirlwind - A slightly stronger gale. 3 second cast time makes it tough to use.

Lava Ball - Great when it hits, but slow projectiles combined with high cost make this mediocre.

Hailstorm - High cost, high reagent cost, and requires snow to use. Just use fireball.

Roaring Wind - Has big impact on enemy groups when they are clustered. Sews many confusion due to its blinding and deafening effect. However, has high cast time, high mana cost, and in most environments it isn’t all that useful.

Firestorm - 12 second cast time? Requires both dry AND windy weather? 5 Pyropite? Pass on this. Just cast fireball.

blocks.html:
Lightning Ball - In theory this should be a good spell. Can be moved after casting, and has a decent shocking effect. In practice it’s better just to throw fireballs.

Water Ward - Has a niche effect of making the caster basically invincible versus melee/arrows, but the low duration combined with the inconsistency of the barrier effect make this basically useless. Eventually you run out of mana or reagents to keep casting it.

Stone Wall - Buggy, and not impactful in most circumstances. It might be a better spell when they tweak it more.

Mirage - Has an effect where people cannot interact with doors or chests, so can interrupt house fighting. Otherwise it’s not that impactful. The sweat salt requirement is heavy, too.

blocks.html:
D Tier

Ether Momentum - A speed spell. Useful for traveling between cities. Not practical to cast in etherworld PvP.

Benumb Mind - Atrocious impact for a 22 mana cost spell. Can be purified. The only application for this was cheesing PvE, and even that is fixed now.

Sacrificial Heal - Sacrifice your undead for a glorified lesser heal that costs twice as much mana and has a longer cast time? Absolutely abysmal impact and high cost. Just use lesser heal.

a fantastic area denial spell which can seal chokepoints, get sneaky opening ganks, and it is even good for pve. cast it on doors to prevent people from fleeing or entering. use it against pets to melt them quickly. only costs a cuprum, too. miasma - a strong damage over time spell, but it is easily avoided. best used to flush out houses, deny pushes, to hit the enemy midline with. mental leech - drains the enemy mana pool to recover your own. for about 5 mana you can recover approximately 50. very potent spell which keeps your mana pool full with proper management. hailstone - a fast casting direct damage spell that casts very quickly. very potent versus pets or in mage vs. mage fights. ember - also fast casting direct damage spell. slightly better than hailstone because it is part blunt damage and can cause a burn effect. earthquake - great for dismounts, but has a hefty mana cost and the self-damage isn’t great. super short cast range. this is the ultimate anti-mounted tech. lightning - a cheap spammable direct damage spell, but is often resisted vs. high psyche characters. has the potential to melt players if they are low psyche. b tier outburst - damage isn’t great and it is resisted a lot, even if it has incredible range and low skill point requirement. flamestrike - not mana efficient, although it is fantastic burst damage. great heal - chunky mana cost and is outclassed by lesser heal over time. great for saving people in the nick of time, but generally lesser heal is better indicated. mindblast - niche use against mages and no one else. outclassed by most other damage spells except against high psyche targets. ether barrier - strong in the ether but it is easy enough to survive as a ghost regardless. raise strong walker - faster than greater walker, but also much squishier. generally just better to run greaters. atrophy - the high cost and low duration makes this ineffective versus players. at best it buys 15 seconds versus enemy pets. cloud of ashes - great as an escape tool or to disrupt enemies, but also requires a target to cast and does self damage. if this did not do self-damage it would be a-tier since it currently disrupts casting! firewall - fantastic versus pets. however, the high skill point cost combined with the need to carry 4 pitch per cast make it outclassed by static shock. sand barrier - a sleeper spell that disrupts enemy mage lines rather well. pulling it off is somewhat difficult, however. why not just fireball instead? gale - the high mana cost for what is essentially a small push makes this a hard sell to use frequently. useful mostly when enemies are in vulnerable positions. otherwise, pass on it. auw surge - this area-of-effect cone damage spell ignores magic reflect and can be casted while sprinting, making it one of the best skirmish damage spells. great for alpha damage when enemies are clumped. mana intensive. can be combo’d with the human war cries and tactician to nuke through friendly lines. fireball - a general purpose ranged aoe nuke which causes burning damage and is very annoying to be hit by. great as an opener or when an enemy group is clumped. tarball - uniquely effective in zerg vs. zerg fights, this bouncy spell can disrupt enemy lines - if it hits. boulder - a bouncy spell skill shot which requires good aiming and a bit of luck, this spell is a decent option at countering mounts. it has a high mana cost for a spell that isn’t guaranteed to hit, however. sandspout - this is like a budget auw surge - it penetrates through enemies and does decent damage for roughly the same mana cost, but it also cannot be casted while sprinting. combine that with requiring 10 granum powder per cast, and it makes it difficult to kit with. tar pit - similar to tarball, this is best when lobbing into large clusters of players. the application is zerg versus zerg fights. water spiral - called the “water shotgun” since it does incredibly damage to single targets in very close range, this has potential for burst damage. however, a 5 second cast time makes it difficult to properly time landing all 3 projectiles at once, and even more difficult to successfully cast without interruption. gravity snare - similar to gale, this spell’s application is environment specific. the 125 mana cost of it makes it a really hard sell unless it is critically successful and pushes enemies off of a cliff or something. can be magic reflected. starfall - a strong visual effect and a great area denial tool and dismounter. however, the high cast time combined with people being able to walk out of it make it ineffective in most situations. great for holding chokes or preventing people fleeing. also useful as an opener if the enemy group is unaware of you. scaling fumes - a high damage rocket salvo that is probably going to miss most of its shots. great at opening ganks, however. the high cast time and scattered impact of the projectiles makes it ineffective most of the time. consuming void - an area of effect blind with niche applications at disrupting mages or paladins. useful for making a great escape or disrupting a fight, but otherwise a high cost for a spell that might amount to nothing or even be harmful. ice barrier - a constant slew of nerfs makes this an increasingly difficult spell to pull off. while its impact is strong, it has a very long cast time, a small bubble, and the duration is not that great. when used properly can split groups. also useful for some parkour applications. shadow - basically a blinding cloud without the damage. exceptionally high mana cost with a high cast time makes it unappealing. conflagration - a neat aoe hellfire-esque spell, it simply does not have a very strong impact. crystal formation - infinite potential with stacking bleeds, this spell might be a sleeper. use against people clumped in houses to great effect. c tier fulmination - a slightly stronger thunderlash with a delayed effect and it can be purified. just use thunderlash. kau regeneration - this is not useful for living pvp, and etherworld pvp isn’t decided by this spell. mental healing - potentially restores a ton of mana to your team, but also requires many coordination for a mediocre effect. raise walker - synergizes best with sacrificial eruption and heal, but those are also mediocre spells. regular walkers are simply too squishy to be impactful against anyone but a pure mage or pets. blind - the high mana cost combined with the short duration of this effect make it mediocre in all regards. just shoot damage spells at the enemy. stone - an ultra-mana efficient spell that requires good aiming and for desync to cooperate. not great versus moving targets, but can good effect if the shooter is skilled enough. starshower - the high cast time combined with low hit probability makes this an average spell at best, however it does have niche uses. several mages spamming this on a house make it a somewhat decent way of countering house hugging. sacrificial eruption - a meme spell. could potentially have big impact if properly controlled, but desync and the inconsistency of walker usage make it janky. you’re also investing a huge amount into walkers just to use them for 1 burst spell that is probably not going to work properly. sludge - not with the mana cost, cast time, or synergy with fire spells. should probably go in torrent - not impactful enough. low damage and does not push back well enough. dust burst - not impactful enough. the bleeding/blind effect do not work against targets that aren’t intentionally standing in the effect. mending vapors - does less healing than a lesser heal, and at a slower rate. might have niche use at removing ignited but, just use lesser heal. ignition - the concept is promising, but the hit detection is just too poor. combine it with a relatively high mana cost compared to other propulsion spells for not-much-more damage makes this not impactful enough. might have niche applications versus stacked pets, but why not just use static shock? geyser wall - not enough impact. requires a nimbic spirit to cast. stilling mist - similar with mending vapors, it is not worth the cast time. just use lesser heal. could use a buff. comet - a worse fireball that doesn’t do burn damage. synergizes with pierce rings but just use fireball. scouring stream - high mana cost for low damage. it’s a budget auw surge replacement at best. fuming bubble - a worse fireball that uses poison instead. just cast fireball. whirlwind - a slightly stronger gale. 3 second cast time makes it tough to use. lava ball - great when it hits, but slow projectiles combined with high cost make this mediocre. hailstorm - high cost, high reagent cost, and requires snow to use. just use fireball. roaring wind - has big impact on enemy groups when they are clustered. sews many confusion due to its blinding and deafening effect. however, has high cast time, high mana cost, and in most environments it isn’t all that useful. firestorm - 12 second cast time? requires both dry and windy weather? 5 pyropite? pass on this. just cast fireball. lightning ball - in theory this should be a good spell. can be moved after casting, and has a decent shocking effect. in practice it’s better just to throw fireballs. water ward - has a niche effect of making the caster basically invincible versus melee/arrows, but the low duration combined with the inconsistency of the barrier effect make this basically useless. eventually you run out of mana or reagents to keep casting it. stone wall - buggy, and not impactful in most circumstances. it might be a better spell when they tweak it more. mirage - has an effect where people cannot interact with doors or chests, so can interrupt house fighting. otherwise it’s not that impactful. the sweat salt requirement is heavy, too. d tier ether momentum - a speed spell. useful for traveling between cities. not practical to cast in etherworld pvp. benumb mind - atrocious impact for a 22 mana cost spell. can be purified. the only application for this was cheesing pve, and even that is fixed now. sacrificial heal - sacrifice your undead for a glorified lesser heal that costs twice as much mana and has a longer cast time? absolutely abysmal impact and high cost. just use lesser heal.

guides.title: Spiritism
guides.summary: Core spiritism systems explained, including ether travel, portals, spirit boxes, spell use, and progression requirements.

blocks.html:
Spiritism

Core spiritism systems explained, including ether travel, portals, spirit boxes, spell use, and progression requirements.

  1. Spiritism - The magic school and a primary skill, and is required to cast all spiritism spells. This is a book from the normal magic librarian in all cities for 2.5g.
  2. Multiverse Lore - Parent but secondary skill required to learn the portal skills. Kill the Minotaur King in the Mouth of Gal Barag (Mino Dungeon) for a chance at a scroll which is then turned in for the lore book at the Spiritism vendors in all major towns.
  3. Ether Lore - Primary skill. Child of multiverse lore, parent of Ether Portals. No known function. Purchasable from the normal magic librarian in all cities for 1.5g. Do not confuse this with Ether Portals.
  4. Ether Portals - The skill required to enter portals. Minimum of level 60 is required to enter portals at all. The higher the skill, the less spirits are lost from spirit boxes when entering/leaving a portal. At skill level 100 there is no loss.

Spiritism traders are Shinar Kipouri (Sidoian) merchants that sell related scrolls and books for this school. These NPCs are found in all major cities. The 3 things they sell are:

  • Multi Universe Lore - Bought with the Multi Universe Knowledge scroll from Mino Dungeon.
  • Ether Portal Knowledge - Trade the Portal Dimensions Knowledge scroll from the Shinarian Temple (Sator Dungeon)
  • The Etherworld Portal scroll - Purchasable with a Forest Troll head.

blocks.html:
Spiritism is very expensive to get into for most players due to monopoly and difficulty of obtaining the currency. Particularly, the multiverse knowledge scroll is a relatively low drop chance from the minotaur dungeon and requires a large group to contest.

Many players run 90 spiritism/portal lore. This saves 20 skillpoints and still gives full access to the spell suite at the cost of resurrection/portal spell success chance as well as a small penalty to spirits in boxes when coming out of a portal. Otherwise this is a great way to add the school to a build without full investment.

blocks.html: Spells
blocks.text: Spells

blocks.html:
Dispel Portal - Gets rid of a portal. This is either to counter enemy spiritists, or to “hide” your own portal if you don’t want people to see the glowing red.

Ether Barrier - Provides a 60 second shield that reduces kau damage received. Only effective in ghost mode.

Ether Momentum - Increases ghost form move speed by 200 units for 5 minutes. Can be casted while moving so good for when traveling long distance. Only effective in ghost mode.

Etherworld Portal - Opens a portal. These last for 1 minute and can be used by anyone with Ether Portals skill - meaning it can act as a “resurrect” for anyone with the skill.

Expel Spirit - Self cast this to allow banishment of spirits. This is required for spirit farming. Also required for banishing spirits when alive. Can be casted on other ghosts- even those who do not have portal or spiritism lore.

Kau Regeneration - Boosts your natural Kau regen rate - which is both your life and mana. Can only be casted in ghost mode. Only effective in ghost mode.

Mental Healing - Grants a % boost to passive mana regen for targets it hits. Is negatively impacted by the psyche of the target that it hits. The caster can never receive this benefit.

Mental Projectile - Also known as the “Rail Gun”. It is a very long range single target beam that does good damage, particularly versus pets or mounts. Can be used while both living or dead. If it targets a ghost player, it does Kau damage and can banish. This spell also ignores magic reflection!

Resurrect - Brings a ghost to life if they accept the spell. Must be paired with the Transcendental Awareness spell.

Transcendental Awareness - Used to see the dead. While living, cast this to see ghosts so that you can resurrect or banish them. While dead, it allows seeing NPCs/AI/Horses and other non-players.

blocks.html:
Transcendental Seance - This is used to draw spirits out. Different locations have different numbers and power of spirits generally based on the HP of creatures in that location. Unique in that it is the only spell that doesn’t require a reagent.

Most spiritism scrolls are obtainable from killing sators in the sator dungeon (jungle beach), killing the gravekeeper (Fabernum tower), and sometimes from bandits. Many of the entry level scrolls are found on the magic vendor. Ether momentum also drops in the Minotaur dungeon. Check the broker, too.

blocks.html:
Why Become a Spiritist?

There are a few notable use-cases for this playstyle. Spiritists can act as a priest, it has access to a unique form of PvE to gather spirits and flux, and there are a few niche but potent spells in its arsenal. Here are there various use-cases for spiritism:

PvE Application

Farming spirits - The most common use of Spiritism is to spirit farm. This involves going into the Etherworld, drawing out spirits, and doing a mini-game to expel them and harvest their power. The guide for this is further down below.

Spawn ‘n’ Scribe - A uniquely potent usage of spiritism is to portal into dungeons, loot scrolls, scribe them, and portal out. Since spellbooks are bound to your character, they are not lost when entering or exiting a portal. This is notably potent in the Tower of Descensus (Necro Dungeon) because many high value necro scrolls spawn in the coffers that can be scribed.

Railgun - The Mental Projectile spell is a very long range beam that does good damage to AI. This can be abused while mounted or even on foot to kill various creatures.

Priest - Accidents happen and people die in dungeons. Having a spiritist with resurrection can help recover from a partial wipe and keep a group going. If one guy dies during a boss, for example, you can breathe life back into him and regear him while you exit the dungeon. highly useful, especially for groups with noobs prone to dying.

blocks.html:
PvP Application

Ghost Scouting - In the past, Spiritists could simply see the living. This has since been removed but there are still ways to use a ghost to figure out enemy activity. With the “Transcendental Awareness” spell AI and pets will be visible - so if the Spiritists see several creatures in a dungeon fighting, it means someone is there! Spiritist ghosts may then cast “mental healing” as a self cast to see nearby players in their combat log to get an idea of who and how many targets there are. Players can also hear many things as a ghost- such as siege weapons, woodcutting, or mining.

Ninja Assassin - A niche but skill based application; a spiritist opens a portal in a place they are not expected to be and then they use either the deathhand spell (necromancy) or they use mental projectile. Since these spells only require a spirit box, you already have it. Mostly useful versus AFK players.

Mounted Railgun - One very potent application of the “Mental Projectile” spell is that it chews through pets. In the context of mounted gameplay, As a result, a mounted spiritist which effectively uses the mental projectile spell will be a potent dismounter. This is particularly useful when an enemy is trying to flee, as the spiritist can repeatedly chunk the mount for 100+ damage from a very far range.

Priest - People die in large scale fights. The side with the spiritist on resurrection duty acts as a force multiplier that has, on more than one occasion, turned the tide of a fight. This is both applicable to siege fights, but also to dungeon fights when the numbers are high enough.

Mana Battery - The spell “Mental Healing” can give a sizeable mana regen to nearby targets. It is casted on a single target, but does an AoE that gives all close-by targets this boost. One caveat is it NEVER hits the caster so they do not gain the effect. This effect likely compounds with other mana regen boosts.

blocks.html: Banishing - A spiritist using “expel spirit” can drain other ghost mode players with their left click beam, or by using mental projectile. This forces enemies to nearest non-TC priest and can disrupt their desired resurrection. It is also useful for punishing groups that lose people in dungeons. Banishing is difficult if not near impossible when the target is zig zagging. Target low kau players with mental projectile to instantly banish them.

blocks.html:
Spirit / Flux Farming

Spirit Farming is the a common use for spiritism. It provides a steady source of income, and is a decent mini-game to conquer. Here are the steps to do it:

Step 1. Enter the Etherworld through a portal. Bring as many spirit boxes as you desire.

Step 2. Go to a location with the target spirits you want. Spirits with 1 orb are found in random places while higher “value” locations like dungeons or boss rooms have stronger ones.

Step 3. Self cast Expel Spirit and then Transcendental Seance. The seance will force spirits to answer your call and summon them.

Step 4. The jellyfish spirits will start to shoot a beam with orbs. Target the beams by holding left click and aiming at them. Once the floating orbs are all dead, focus the jellyfish until it is expelled.

Spirits with 1 orb are found in random places while higher “value” locations like dungeons or boss rooms have stronger ones. Step 3. Self cast Expel Spirit and then Transcendental Seance. The seance will force spirits to answer your call and summon them. Step 4. The jellyfish spirits will start to shoot a beam with orbs. Target the beams by holding left click and aiming at them. Once the floating orbs are all dead, focus the jellyfish until it is expelled.

blocks.html:
Step 5. Once spirit boxes are filled or enough flux is obtained, resurrect (either with portal or at a priest) and enjoy the rewards.

Notes:

  • If spirits with multiple orbs are too difficult, bring help. This is not strictly a solo activity. In most situations, stick to 4 orbs and below as a solo.
  • Gold flux is the highest publicly known yield from spirits. Skadite and oghmium flux are obtainable by killing the boss of the Undercroft dungeon.
  • Spiritists tend to be very territorial of their spirit farm. Do not be surprised if they banish you for encroaching.
  • Buffs such as momentum and barrier are highly recommended when farming.

blocks.html:
Other Mechanics

Kau is the spirit energy a player has. It is similar to mana, and in-fact uses the same mana bar, but it has different mechanics to raise it. +Mana does NOT increase Kau, but +Psyche does. Kau regenerates a lot faster than mana. Spiritism levels itself also increases Kau.

Many spiritism spells are intended to be self casted. However, they by default cast outwards. You can start casting and hit the self-cast button while it is charging to change target to self. Alternatively you can start the cast, cancel it, then hit your self cast button.

The left click beam that ghosts have does not count as a spell. It is not impacted by masteries or trinkets. For example +9% spiritism damage on a necklace does not work with this.

The Kau Beam (official name) can be strengthened with an essence orb effect.

Getting banished as a spirit forces a drop of all spirit boxes. You could theoretically banish other spiritists farming and steal their rewards. Home priesting also drops all spirit boxes.

Spirit boxes dropped by a banished ghost player can be picked up by another ghost. Flux is not dropped upon banishment. Players will still resurrect with their flux.

A portal opened by someone with level 60 portals lore has a 10% tax on spirits in ALL spirit boxes in inventory. A medium spirit box with 150 spirits in it will drop 10% (-15) to 135/150 spirits at this level. If the portal is opened by someone with 100 lore, the tax is nullified.

blocks.html:
Transcendental Seance can sometimes be used in conjunction with abandoned pets to spawn, or even walkers. This is not totally consistent, but it has been known to work.

Mental projectiles range is equivalent to the “name-tag” distance. If you can see their name-tag, you can tag them with it.

Jellyfish Spirits can be temporarily disabled if they are hit with a moment of kau beam (left click).

Resurrecting at a priest instead of coming through a portal with spirit boxes incurs a 50% spirit penalty to spirit boxes. Portals are the only viable way to resurrect and maintain spirits.

Transcendental Seance is useful if you’re trying to banish another player as you can basically force jellyfish to help fight them.

Trinket charges are NOT lost when entering portals.

Mental projectiles range is equivalent to the “name-tag” distance. If you can see their name-tag, you can tag them with it. blocks.html:
Conclusion

Spiritism is a niche magic school. Most people don’t run it- and many people don’t want to run it. The high cost for starting combined with the niche spells that have limited utility mean people pass up spiritism for other more direct schools. That said, spiritism is more of a strategic magic school rather than a tactical one, with many benefits for guilds which choose to run them. Even though spiritism is not super powerful, it fits right in with the sandbox RPG design of Mortal.

including ether travel, portals, spirit boxes, spell use, and progression requirements. spiritism - the magic school and a primary skill, and is required to cast all spiritism spells. this is a book from the normal magic librarian in all cities for 2.5g. multiverse lore - parent but secondary skill required to learn the portal skills. kill the minotaur king in the mouth of gal barag (mino dungeon) for a chance at a scroll which is then turned in for the lore book at the spiritism vendors in all major towns. ether lore - primary skill. child of multiverse lore, parent of ether portals. no known function. purchasable from the normal magic librarian in all cities for 1.5g. do not confuse this with ether portals. ether portals - the skill required to enter portals. minimum of level 60 is required to enter portals at all. the higher the skill, the less spirits are lost from spirit boxes when entering/leaving a portal. at skill level 100 there is no loss. spiritism traders are shinar kipouri (sidoian) merchants that sell related scrolls and books for this school. these npcs are found in all major cities. the 3 things they sell are: multi universe lore - bought with the multi universe knowledge scroll from mino dungeon. ether portal knowledge - trade the portal dimensions knowledge scroll from the shinarian temple (sator dungeon) the etherworld portal scroll - purchasable with a forest troll head. spiritism is very expensive to get into for most players due to monopoly and difficulty of obtaining the currency. particularly, the multiverse knowledge scroll is a relatively low drop chance from the minotaur dungeon and requires a large group to contest. many players run 90 spiritism/portal lore. this saves 20 skillpoints and still gives full access to the spell suite at the cost of resurrection/portal spell success chance as well as a small penalty to spirits in boxes when coming out of a portal. otherwise this is a great way to add the school to a build without full investment. spells dispel portal - gets rid of a portal. this is either to counter enemy spiritists, or to “hide” your own portal if you don’t want people to see the glowing red. ether barrier - provides a 60 second shield that reduces kau damage received. only effective in ghost mode. ether momentum - increases ghost form move speed by 200 units for 5 minutes. can be casted while moving so good for when traveling long distance. only effective in ghost mode. etherworld portal - opens a portal. these last for 1 minute and can be used by anyone with ether portals skill - meaning it can act as a “resurrect” for anyone with the skill. expel spirit - self cast this to allow banishment of spirits. this is required for spirit farming. also required for banishing spirits when alive. can be casted on other ghosts- even those who do not have portal or spiritism lore. kau regeneration - boosts your natural kau regen rate - which is both your life and mana. can only be casted in ghost mode. only effective in ghost mode. mental healing - grants a % boost to passive mana regen for targets it hits. is negatively impacted by the psyche of the target that it hits. the caster can never receive this benefit. mental projectile - also known as the “rail gun”. it is a very long range single target beam that does good damage, particularly versus pets or mounts. can be used while both living or dead. if it targets a ghost player, it does kau damage and can banish. this spell also ignores magic reflection! resurrect - brings a ghost to life if they accept the spell. must be paired with the transcendental awareness spell. transcendental awareness - used to see the dead. while living, cast this to see ghosts so that you can resurrect or banish them. while dead, it allows seeing npcs/ai/horses and other non-players. transcendental seance - this is used to draw spirits out. different locations have different numbers and power of spirits generally based on the hp of creatures in that location. unique in that it is the only spell that doesn’t require a reagent. most spiritism scrolls are obtainable from killing sators in the sator dungeon (jungle beach), killing the gravekeeper (fabernum tower), and sometimes from bandits. many of the entry level scrolls are found on the magic vendor. ether momentum also drops in the minotaur dungeon. check the broker, too. why become a spiritist? there are a few notable use-cases for this playstyle. spiritists can act as a priest, it has access to a unique form of pve to gather spirits and flux, and there are a few niche but potent spells in its arsenal. here are there various use-cases for spiritism: pve application farming spirits - the most common use of spiritism is to spirit farm. this involves going into the etherworld, drawing out spirits, and doing a mini-game to expel them and harvest their power. the guide for this is further down below. spawn ‘n’ scribe - a uniquely potent usage of spiritism is to portal into dungeons, loot scrolls, scribe them, and portal out. since spellbooks are bound to your character, they are not lost when entering or exiting a portal. this is notably potent in the tower of descensus (necro dungeon) because many high value necro scrolls spawn in the coffers that can be scribed. railgun - the mental projectile spell is a very long range beam that does good damage to ai. this can be abused while mounted or even on foot to kill various creatures. priest - accidents happen and people die in dungeons. having a spiritist with resurrection can help recover from a partial wipe and keep a group going. if one guy dies during a boss, for example, you can breathe life back into him and regear him while you exit the dungeon. highly useful, especially for groups with noobs prone to dying. pvp application ghost scouting - in the past, spiritists could simply see the living. this has since been removed but there are still ways to use a ghost to figure out enemy activity. with the “transcendental awareness” spell ai and pets will be visible - so if the spiritists see several creatures in a dungeon fighting, it means someone is there! spiritist ghosts may then cast “mental healing” as a self cast to see nearby players in their combat log to get an idea of who and how many targets there are. players can also hear many things as a ghost- such as siege weapons, woodcutting, or mining. ninja assassin - a niche but skill based application; a spiritist opens a portal in a place they are not expected to be and then they use either the deathhand spell (necromancy) or they use mental projectile. since these spells only require a spirit box, you already have it. mostly useful versus afk players. mounted railgun - one very potent application of the “mental projectile” spell is that it chews through pets. in the context of mounted gameplay, as a result, a mounted spiritist which effectively uses the mental projectile spell will be a potent dismounter. this is particularly useful when an enemy is trying to flee, as the spiritist can repeatedly chunk the mount for 100+ damage from a very far range. priest - people die in large scale fights. the side with the spiritist on resurrection duty acts as a force multiplier that has, on more than one occasion, turned the tide of a fight. this is both applicable to siege fights, but also to dungeon fights when the numbers are high enough. mana battery - the spell “mental healing” can give a sizeable mana regen to nearby targets. it is casted on a single target, but does an aoe that gives all close-by targets this boost. one caveat is it never hits the caster so they do not gain the effect. this effect likely compounds with other mana regen boosts. banishing - a spiritist using “expel spirit” can drain other ghost mode players with their left click beam, or by using mental projectile. this forces enemies to nearest non-tc priest and can disrupt their desired resurrection. it is also useful for punishing groups that lose people in dungeons. banishing is difficult if not near impossible when the target is zig zagging. target low kau players with mental projectile to instantly banish them. spirit / flux farming spirit farming is the a common use for spiritism. it provides a steady source of income, and is a decent mini-game to conquer. here are the steps to do it: step 1. enter the etherworld through a portal. bring as many spirit boxes as you desire. step 2. go to a location with the target spirits you want. spirits with 1 orb are found in random places while higher “value” locations like dungeons or boss rooms have stronger ones. step 3. self cast expel spirit and then transcendental seance. the seance will force spirits to answer your call and summon them. step 4. the jellyfish spirits will start to shoot a beam with orbs. target the beams by holding left click and aiming at them. once the floating orbs are all dead, focus the jellyfish until it is expelled. step 5. once spirit boxes are filled or enough flux is obtained, resurrect (either with portal or at a priest) and enjoy the rewards. notes: if spirits with multiple orbs are too difficult, bring help. this is not strictly a solo activity. in most situations, stick to 4 orbs and below as a solo. gold flux is the highest publicly known yield from spirits. skadite and oghmium flux are obtainable by killing the boss of the undercroft dungeon. spiritists tend to be very territorial of their spirit farm. do not be surprised if they banish you for encroaching. buffs such as momentum and barrier are highly recommended when farming. other mechanics kau is the spirit energy a player has. it is similar to mana, and in-fact uses the same mana bar, but it has different mechanics to raise it. +mana does not increase kau, but +psyche does. kau regenerates a lot faster than mana. spiritism levels itself also increases kau. many spiritism spells are intended to be self casted. however, they by default cast outwards. you can start casting and hit the self-cast button while it is charging to change target to self. alternatively you can start the cast, cancel it, then hit your self cast button. the left click beam that ghosts have does not count as a spell. it is not impacted by masteries or trinkets. for example +9% spiritism damage on a necklace other spiritists farming and steal their rewards. home priesting also drops all spirit boxes. spirit boxes dropped by a banished ghost player can be picked up by another ghost. flux is not dropped upon banishment. players will still resurrect with their flux. a portal opened by someone with level 60 portals lore has a 10% tax on spirits in all spirit boxes in inventory. a medium spirit box with blocks.html:
Alchemy

Build an alchemy foundation with ingredient properties, potion structure, lore requirements, testing methods, and useful combinations.
blocks.text: Alchemy Build an alchemy foundation with ingredient properties, potion structure, lore requirements, testing methods, and useful combinations.

blocks.html:
Purpose of Alchemy

Why alchemy? Alchemy provides several unique benefits and can become highly profitable when its materials and recipes are managed carefully. Its products cover several recurring guild needs. Common alchemical products include:

  • Rare Material Extraction
  • Direct Health/Health Regen Potions
  • Direct Mana/Mana Regen Potions
  • Age Alteration
  • Weight Alteration
  • Magic Reflect
  • Magic Defense
  • Purification
  • Money

Set realistic expectations: this profession is time consuming and data intensive. New research requires meticulous record keeping, charting, and spreadsheets. Alterations of recipes can be costly wastes of time It is, however, possible to be an alchemist and follow pre-established recipes (and that’s OK).

Skills

The following skills affect alchemy and potion production. If doing potion making it is functionally mandatory to have potion and advanced potion making maxed out for the best results.

Main/Mandatory Skills:

  • Alchemy
  • Potion/Advanced Potion Making

blocks.html:
Auxiliary Skills:

  • Animal Materials - For all animal materials; broad use
  • Arthropoda - For spider queen carcass. Good for heal-over-time pots, but bad for direct healing.
  • Alchemical Dissolvents - For using dissolvents, mostly salt
  • Alchemical Minerology - For extracting glimmering essence and for creating mana regen, purify, magic defense, and magic reflect potions
  • Botany - For using plants; broad use
  • Petrology - For using rocks/ores
  • Metallurgy - For using metals
  • Pisces - For using fish such as Calxfish
  • Holozoa - For using Red bulbtip and Argus Sponge. Good for heal-over-time pots but bad for direct healing.
  • Milling/Ore Extraction Appliances - Extracting Flours/Powders with grinder
  • Herbalism - Extracting Plants
  • Alchemy Contraptions - Extracting with Fabricula
  • Botany Appliances - Extracting with Herbologeum/Press

Specializing in material lores is usually beneficial to the stats of potions with a few exceptions. Zoology lores and metallurgy are generally bad skills to have if using spider queen carcass, argus sponge, or skadite as a multiplier for direct healing potions, for example. Generally, however, if you are using a material in a potion you want the material lore.

blocks.html:
Material Extraction

Alchemy ingredients are often extracted materials. While not exclusively for alchemy, This section covers alchemy (fabricula), milling, press, and herbologeum extraction. For other types of extraction such as ore extraction, use the related extraction references.

The fabricula is used to obtain alchemical materials as well as materials to make Tindremic messing. The herbologeum is meant to extract seeds, carpels, and essences which are useful in various applications. The press is used for getting oils from specific items. The mill is to obtain grains and powders.

blocks.html:
Alchemy Materials and Potion Making

Potion structure begins with a straightforward rule, even though the resulting combinations can become complex: start with a base material -> add multipliers/volumizers until the desired effect is achieved.

Different multipliers will have varying degrees of effectiveness based on the base ingredient. A multiplier which works for the base of direct healing will not likely work for mana regeneration, and vice versa. Negative multipliers exist so be careful what you select. Altering the ratios of base material and multiplier impacts the end product for better or worse.

blocks.html:
Combine Skill and Interpreting Potions

Different potions can be combined using the “Combine” command. Combining two potions produces a potion that mixes the properties of the two source potions. The formula for determining the properties of the resulting potion can be expressed as

([Property of Potion 1] x [Quantity of Potion 1] + [Property of Potion 2] x [Quantity of Potion 2])/([Quantity of Potion 1] +[Quantity of Potion 2]).

As an example, suppose you plan to combine 100 units of a potion with 4.5 DH and 200 units of a potion with 7 DH. To calculate the resulting DH of the new potion you would calculate as follows:

([4.5 DH] x [100 Units of Potion] + [7 DH] x [200 Units of Potion])/([100 Units of Potion]+[200 Units of Potion]) = 6.16 DH

Remember that all the properties of the combined potions carry into the new potion, so it is important to run this same calculation for all the important properties of the combined potions.

Also remember that the amount of combined potion will be limited by the capacity of destination container. When viewing the Combine window in the game, the container placed in the left box is the destination container. If the destination container has less capacity than the amount of potion on the right side of the Combine, then the combine will only mix the amount of potion that will fit into the remaining capacity of the destination container.

Guide to Buying Potions

Suppose you’re already making money doing something else, and you’d rather pay someone to make your potions. Here are some things you should know when shopping for and assessing the utility/value of a potion.

---Quantity---

Potions come in containers (either vials or kegs). The amount of potion contained within the container is listed on the tooltip when mousing over the potion. When shopping, pay careful attention to how much potion is in the container.

blocks.html:
---Counteracting Effects---

It is possible for a potion to have 2 effects that counteract one another. For example, direct healing and direct poison will effectively neutralize one another when the potion is consumed. So a potion that has 6.400 direct heal and 0.1700 direct poison will result in a net healing effect of 6.23 when the potion is consumed. A similar effect occurs between heal-over-time and poison-over-time, though remember that duration is also a factor with these two effects. When shopping, pay careful attention to offsetting effects.

---Combination Potions---

Some alchemists like to mix two or more potions with different effects to create a one-sip solution to common field challenges. For example, you’ve been ambushed by a mage who has corrupted you and blasted you to half health. An alchemist can make a potion that can simultaneously purify corruption, restore health, and put up a spell reflect in a single chug. If you know a good alchemist, talk to them about tailoring potions for your specific needs.

blocks.html:
Guide to Using Potions

You have either created or purchased potions of some kind. How do they work?

⦁ Sip or Chug

You can (and usually should) control how much potion you drink. The amount you drink will determine how strong of an effect the potion has, or whether the potion has any effect at all.

One fast click-release to drink one unit. Click-release X times in rapid succession to drink X units. Click and hold to drink as much as your belly will hold.

⦁ Thirst

Thirst is how much potion you are able to drink at the present moment. Without any skill modifiers or clade gifts, a character’s maximum thirst is 10, which means that the character may consume 10 units of potion at once. After consuming a quantity of potion, a character’s thirst will be reduced by the amount of potion consumed (each 1 unit of potion consumed removes 1 thirst). Thirst regenerates at a rate of roughly 1 unit of thirst per 14 seconds.

A character may increase their maximum thirst in the following ways:

⦁ Potion Utilization (Skill): adds up to 10 additional units of thirst at skill level 100

⦁ Beer Belly (Oghmir Clade Gift): adds 10 additional units of thirst

blocks.html:
---Direct Heal and Direct Poison Consumption---

Each unit of Direct Heal/Poison potion consumed will restore/deduct health equal to the values listed on the potion. So a potion with 6.3 direct healing and 0.1 direct poison will heal the user 6.3 health and simultaneously poison the user for 0.1 health for each unit consumed. Consume more to multiply the effects.

---Purify Consumption---

The effect can be characterized as “all-or-nothing” in the sense that if a character consumes a potion with Purify, the character must consume enough of the potion to reach 100% of the effect, or nothing will happen. The number of units consumed multiplied by the percentage value listed on the potion must be greater than or equal to 100%.

Furthermore, consuming so much potion that the Purify effect exceeds 100% will trigger the effect, but the excess potion consumed will do nothing.

For example, when using a potion that has 100% purify, the character need only drink a single unit (one fast click-release) to purify their corruption. However, when using a potion that has 10% purify, the character must drink 10 units or more (10*10%=100%) To activate the effect.

blocks.html:
--Consuming All “Over Time” Effects (Heal Over Time, Magic Defense, Mana Regeneration, Magic Reflect, Poison Over Time)---

These potion categories are probably the most difficult to understand due to the less intuitive calculations that are used to calculate the magnitude of their effects. The way to calculate any of the effects of consuming one of these potions is as follows:

√[Amount Consumed]*[Listed Value of the Effect]

Potency and Length:

For all “Over Time” potions, the outcome for length is in seconds. For Heal Over Time and Poison Over Time, the outcome for potency is per second (HP gained per second or HP lost per second). For static effects like (Magic Defense, Mana Regen, Magic Reflect), the outcome for potency is the fixed increase in percentage of the effect (% of Mana Regen increased for the duration of the potion effect).

So let’s look at a potion that has 0.316 Heal Over Time and 67 Heal Over Time Length. Consuming 10 units will result in the following effects:

√10x0.317 Heal Over Time = 1.002 HP (per second)

√10x67 Heal Over Time Length = 211.87 seconds

This potion will provide roughly 1hp per second for 211 seconds.

Side note- the magic defense stat seems to disproportionately impact elementalism damage!

blocks.html:
---Age Potion Consumption---

Age is fortunately quite simple. It is the amount of age increase or decrease listed on the potion multiplied by the amount consumed. Current testing indicates any resulting value is rounded down to the nearest whole number, so drinking 10 units of an age potion with.099 age increase will not do anything. Likewise, drinking 10 units of an age potion with 1.99 age increase will only increase age by 1 year. Age is stored as a whole number (not a decimal) so drinking incremental amounts does nothing.

blocks.html:
---Weight Gain/Loss---

Due to the difficulty with precisely measuring both changes in weight and the magnitude of weight changing potions, there is no perfect consensus on the exact calculation for potions effecting weight. The closest way to predict the effect of a weight changing potion is: 50kg * [amount consumed] * [listed weight gain/loss value]. Remember: unseen decimals in the listed potion potency (e.g. 0.003xx weight increase) as well as unseen decimals in a character’s weight (e.g. 56.xx kg) can make the outcome prediction less precise.

blocks.html:
Future Research

With everything learned above, what more is there to discover with alchemy? Combining different potions with the “combine” skill can yield potent results. For example, a direct healing potion combined with a purification potion can yield a get-out-of-death-free result. A potion which purifies AND heals you to full? Other unique combinations may exist and await discovery.

Potion making is often about optimization of recipes. It doesn’t take a rocket surgeon to dump a ton of salvia oil into a keg and get crazy good healing properties, but it is not economical. Striking a balance between cost, efficiency, and output is not easy and highly desired. Searching for low-cost, high impact potions is always a goal of a researching alchemist.

Finally, there is the chance at unknown effects or yields. It remains possible that brained leather is already in game and just awaiting to be made with alchemy. There might be new ways of creating old materials, or finding ways to give utility.

Want to advance your alchemy research? Hop over to the Chosn Alchemy discord for a more advanced look at this subject: https://discord.com/invite/55dQE34g5w

They have an alchemy calculator over there, too.

Age Potions

Age potions utilize Cleansed Drakon (Age+). or Cleansed Nymph Herb (Age-). Simply gather these resources and put them in the herbologeum to cleanse. Cleanse in multiples of 20 to take advantage of the Alvarin "Plantshaper II" gift.

For a simple age potion put 6:5 cleansed herb:purified water. This ratio can be modified at higher quantities to reduce waste.

be combined using the “combine” command. combining two potions produces a potion that mixes the properties of the two source potions. the formula for determining the properties of the resulting potion can be expressed as ([property of potion 1] x [quantity of potion 1] + [property of potion 2] x [quantity of potion 2])/([quantity of potion 1] +[quantity of potion 2]). as an example, suppose you plan to combine 100 units of a potion with 4.5 dh and 200 units of a potion with 7 dh. to calculate the resulting dh of the new potion you would calculate as follows: ([4.5 dh] x [100 units of potion] + [7 dh] x [200 units of potion])/([100 units of potion]+[200 units of potion]) = 6.16 dh remember that all the properties of the combined potions carry into the new potion, so it is important to run this same calculation for all the important properties of the combined potions. also remember that the amount of combined potion will be limited by the capacity of destination container. when viewing the combine window in the game, the container placed in the left box is the destination container. if the destination container has less capacity than the amount of potion on the right side of the combine, then the combine will only mix the amount of potion that will fit into the remaining capacity of the destination container. guide to buying potions suppose you’re already making money doing something else, and you’d rather pay someone to make your potions. here are some things you should know when shopping for and assessing the utility/value of a potion. ---quantity--- potions come in containers (either vials or kegs). the amount of potion contained within the container is listed on the tooltip when mousing over the potion. when shopping, pay careful attention to how much potion is in the container. ---counteracting effects--- it is possible for a potion to have 2 effects that counteract one another. for example, direct healing and direct poison will effectively neutralize one another when the potion is consumed. so a potion that has 6.400 direct heal and 0.1700 direct poison will result in a net healing effect of 6.23 when the potion is consumed. a similar effect occurs between heal-over-time and poison-over-time, though remember that duration is also a factor with these two effects. when shopping, pay careful attention to offsetting effects. ---combination potions--- some alchemists like to mix two or more potions with different effects to create a one-sip solution to common field challenges. for example, you’ve been ambushed by a mage who has corrupted you and blasted you to half health. an alchemist can make a potion that can simultaneously purify corruption, restore health, and put up a spell reflect in a single chug. if you know a good alchemist, talk to them about tailoring potions for your specific needs. guide to using potions you have either created or purchased potions of some kind. how do they work? ⦁ sip or chug you can (and usually should) control how much potion you drink. the amount you drink will determine how strong of an effect the potion has, or whether the potion has any effect at all. one fast click-release to drink one unit. click-release x times in rapid succession to drink x units. click and hold to drink as much as your belly will hold. ⦁ thirst thirst is how much potion you are able to drink at the present moment. without any skill modifiers or clade gifts, a character’s maximum thirst is 10, which means that the character may consume 10 units of potion at once. after consuming a quantity of potion, a character’s thirst will be reduced by the amount of potion consumed (each 1 unit of potion consumed removes 1 thirst). thirst regenerates at a rate of roughly 1 unit of thirst per 14 seconds. a character may increase their maximum thirst in the following ways: ⦁ potion utilization (skill): adds up to 10 additional units of thirst at skill level 100 ⦁ beer belly (oghmir clade gift): adds 10 additional units of thirst ---direct heal and direct poison consumption--- each unit of direct heal/poison potion consumed will restore/deduct health equal to the values listed on the potion. so a potion with 6.3 direct healing and 0.1 direct poison will heal the user 6.3 health and simultaneously poison the user for 0.1 health for each unit consumed. consume more to multiply the effects. ---purify consumption--- the effect can be characterized as “all-or-nothing” in the sense that if a character consumes a potion with purify, the character must consume enough of the potion to reach 100% of the effect, or nothing will happen. the number of units consumed multiplied by the percentage value listed on the potion must be greater than or equal to 100%. furthermore, consuming so much potion that the purify effect exceeds 100% will trigger the effect, but the excess potion consumed will do nothing. for example, when using a potion that has 100% purify, the character need only drink a single unit (one fast click-release) to purify their corruption. however, when using a potion that has 10% purify, the character must drink 10 units or more (10*10%=100%) to activate the effect. --consuming all “over time” effects (heal over time, magic defense, mana regeneration, magic reflect, poison over time)--- these potion categories are probably the most difficult to understand due to the less intuitive calculations that are used to calculate the magnitude of their effects. the way to calculate any of the effects of consuming one of these potions is as follows: √[amount consumed]*[listed value of the effect] potency and length: for all “over time” potions, the outcome for length is in seconds. for heal over time and poison over time, the outcome for potency is per second (hp gained per second or hp lost per second). for static effects like (magic defense, mana regen, magic reflect), the outcome for potency is the fixed increase in percentage of the effect (% of mana regen increased for the duration of the potion effect). so let’s look at a potion that has 0.316 heal over time and 67 heal over time length. consuming 10 units will result in the following effects: √10x0.317 heal over time = 1.002 hp (per second) √10x67 heal over time length = 211.87 seconds this potion will provide roughly 1hp per second for 211 seconds. side note- the magic defense stat seems to disproportionately impact elementalism damage! ---age potion consumption--- age is fortunately quite simple. it is the amount of age increase or decrease listed on the potion multiplied by the amount consumed. current testing indicates any resulting value is rounded down to the nearest whole number, so drinking 10 units of an age potion with.099 age increase will not do anything. likewise, drinking 10 units of an age potion with 1.99 age increase will only increase age by 1 year. age is stored as a whole number (not a decimal) so drinking incremental amounts does nothing. ---weight gain/loss--- due to the difficulty with precisely measuring both changes in weight and the magnitude of weight changing potions, there is no perfect consensus on the exact calculation for potions effecting weight. the closest way to predict the effect of a weight changing potion is: 50kg * [amount consumed] * [listed weight gain/loss value]. remember: unseen decimals in the listed potion potency (e.g. 0.003xx weight increase) as well as unseen decimals in a character’s weight (e.g. 56.xx kg) can make the outcome prediction less precise. future research with everything learned above, what more is there to discover with alchemy? combining different potions with the “combine” skill can yield potent results. for example, a direct healing potion combined with a purification potion can yield a get-out-of-death-free result. a potion which purifies and heals you to full? other unique combinations may exist and await discovery. potion making is often about optimization of recipes. it doesn’t take a rocket surgeon to dump a ton of salvia oil into a keg and get crazy good healing properties, but it is not economical. striking a balance between cost, efficiency, and output is not easy and highly desired. searching for low-cost, high impact potions is always a goal of a researching alchemist. finally, there is the chance at unknown effects or yields. it remains possible that brained leather is already in game and just awaiting to be made with alchemy. there might be new ways of creating old materials, or finding ways to give utility. want to advance your alchemy research? hop over to the chosn alchemy discord for a more advanced look at this subject: https://discord.com/invite/55dqe34g5w they have an alchemy calculator over there, too. age potions age potions utilize cleansed drakon (age+). or cleansed nymph herb (age-). simply gather these resources and put them in the herbologeum to cleanse. cleanse in multiples of 20 to take advantage of the alvarin "plantshaper ii" gift. for a simple age potion put 6:5 cleansed herb:purified water. this ratio can be modified at higher quantities to reduce waste.

guides.summary: Plan armor crafts by style, material, weight, protection, durability, and the skills needed for reliable results.

blocks.html:
Armor Crafting

Plan armor crafts by style, material, weight, protection, durability, and the skills needed for reliable results.

Armor Types

There are 4 (four) armor types in game: cloth, soft, laminated, and plate armors. Each has distinct characteristics and appropriate use-cases.

  • Cloth Armor - Comprised of Rugged Garments and Tindremic Attire
  • Soft Armor - Tindremic Guard, Kallardian Padded, Ranger Armor, Risar Berserker
  • Laminated Armor - Khurite Splinted, Kallardian Banded
  • Plate Armor - Mercenary Plate, Risar Berserker, Tindremic Knight, Draconigena Armatus

Cloth armor is ideal for ultra-greedy mages who want maximum mana regeneration. Soft armor is the standard for mage armor as well as light hybrids. Laminated is for heavy hybrids, siege mages, or fighters which want to save on the stamina penalty. Plate armor is the standard for fighters.

Armor Explained

The distinction between armor types (cloth/soft/laminated/plate) has no direct impact on the effectiveness of the armor. Plate armor can be poorly made and offer less protection than a soft armor set. The biggest difference between the armor types are the profession skill requirements and the types of materials they can be made out of. Each individual armor set has somewhat of a unique niche.

  • The cloth armors (rugged garments and Tindremic attire) are ideal for max mana regeneration due to light weight.
  • The soft armors (Kallardian padded, ranger, berserker, and guard) are ideal for solid defense while maintaining light weight. Guard is admittedly pretty mediocre, however. Berserker boasts great blunt defense, while kallardian is the most efficient for weight and has good pierce defense.
  • Khurite splinted has the highest possible blunt defense and offers pretty efficient defense. It is ideal for human hybrids and mounted archers, as well as siege mages.
  • Draconigena offers superior pierce defense while being lightweight.
  • Tindremic Knight has really good slash/blunt modifiers, but lacks a little in pierce.
  • Mercenary has great pierce modifiers while also having solid blunt/slash.
  • Risar Soldier is a high efficiency plate set, but lacks of raw defenses.

blocks.html:
Mana/Stamina Efficiency

The two primary considerations when armor crafting are weight and defense. Heavier armor weight costs extra skill points in the form of armor training, it impacts stamina regeneration, and it affects mana regeneration. It is thus important to minimize weight while maximizing defense, although this may be disregarded for fighters who want absolute maximum defense.

The weight efficiency is most important for mages and hybrids, as mana regen is heavily penalized the higher up in armor weight. The current mana curve is listed in these charts:

blocks.html:
The most reliable way to calculate the overall efficiency of an armor style is to use a consistent crafting design, then take an average of the defenses it offers, and then divide that by the weight. So for example, let’s compare kallardian norse, tindremic guard, and ranger armor. All three will be keeled scale/ironfur. The average defense for the kallardian is 39.36. The average defense for the guard is 41.92. The average for the ranger is 40.21.

Using kallardian as the base (x), As a result, ranger is ~2.1% better defensive values. Tindremic guard is 6.5% better defense! However, consider the weight - this kallardian set weighs 6.4, the ranger 7.08, and the guard is 8.44. As a result, for that extra 6.5% defense over kallardian, the guard armor is 31.8% heavier, which is absolutely not efficient and thus not worth it for mages. The goal is to minimize weight while maximizing defense, so by-in-large kallardian padded is more efficient.

Another consideration is what specific threats you will face. Ranger might have better overall values than kallardian, but kallardian is better against pierce but is weak to slash.

An even more niche consideration for efficiency is individual armor pieces. Certain armor pieces are more weight efficient within the exact same set. For example, ranger armor sleeves are proportionally extra heavy while the helmet is extra light.

blocks.html:
The next consideration is the efficiency of the materials when it comes to weight. Proportional more defense comes from using certain materials. For example, scales are more efficient in this order: ganoid -> keeled -> horned -> plate -> pansar. While pansar offers the most raw stats, it is not weight efficient, while ganoid offers the highest defense to weight ratio! Other materials such as cronite are ultra weight efficient, while tungsteel is very poor.

What does all this boil down to? Not much for fighters unless they are trying to meet a specific armor weight due to their build. For mages and hybrids, it indicates that wearing high efficiency, lightweight armor is possible with proper optimization. Ganoid/keeled scales with ironwool, ironfur, or guard fur is idea for mages, preferably with a lightweight set like kallardian or ranger. For hybrids it might be better to wear plate or pansar scales in a laminated set to eek out that extra bit of flat defense while still maintaining modest mana regeneration.

blocks.html:
Crafting Process - Extra Material / Sliders

The primary mechanic behind armor crafting is applying a core material, then a padding material. Both have big impact on the quality of the armor. There is then an “Extra material” slider that can be adjusted. The rule of thumb is to always set the material sliders to 100% for gear that is being worn. You lose weight/armor efficiency when you lower this slider, even though you save on materials.

Example Sets

The armor crafting process does not produce necessarily complicated results.

Highest overall defense - Oghmium + Ironfur mercenary plate

PvP standard for fighter - Steel + ironfur mercenary plate

Best for dex mages - Platescale + Bloodsilk or Huskweave tindremic guard

Best for mana efficiency/defense - Ganoid + bloodsilk kallardian padded

Best for blunt defense (mounted) - Pansar scale + ironfur khurite splinted

Best for max mana regen - Rugged garments or tindremic attire - Ironfur + ironwool

blocks.html:
Economics of Armor Crafting

Requisition of materials is an often overlooked aspect of this profession. While it would be ideal to craft oghmium/ironfur armor for every single set, that is just not realistic. Use what resources are local, available, acquirable, and cheap - and apply them to sets which are used for appropriate functions.

An example of good armor crafting economics is for a jungle-living guild to kill turtles and jungle trolls. They then have access to reptile carapace + ironfur for producing cheap but effective sets en masse for PvE or casual PvP. Due to their ease of access to ironfur, these guilds can also produce steel / ironfur sets for when PvP matters. A guild in Morin Khur could do the same with heavy carapace + ironsilk from the Nitre queen.

The bottom line - use what is available, cheap, and won’t enslave you to gathering. Don’t waste steel and above on PvE. Save the expensive materials for the fights that matter.

blocks.html:
Pet Equipment Crafting

Technically pet equipment crafting is a form of armor crafting as it gives progress towards the grandmaster armorer title. The same general principles apply to pet equipment crafting as they do armor crafting. The difference with pet crafting is that weight only matters if riding the pet. There is no penalty to wearing as heavy armor as possible for combat pets, such as bears and taur dogs.

blocks.html:
Shield + Armor Interaction

The shield mechanic overlaps with armor, specifically the chest armor piece. As a result, any equipment hits has a cumulative effect with the chest armor, adding both the shield defense and the chest piece defense together. This also applies for parrying. The application of this is primarily for mages, but any playstyle can use it- any build which relies on equipment hits from shields should use above average defenses on the chest, while being able to skimp on the legs/arms/helmet. For example, a mage is able to use platescale chestpiece + a shield and keeled scale accessory pieces.

blocks.html:
Adamant Tipped Engravers

The "Adamant Tipped Engraver" is a rare drop from many bosses. It is a tool which allows you to craft legendary quality gear which offers 25% extra durability and a unique inscription on the item.

The requirement for crafting a legendary item is to have the adamant tipped engraver, 100 in all armor crafting skills the item requires and 100 in all of the material lores being used.

In most situations, the durability boost is nice, but not game changing. The entire purpose of legendary items is swag. Wearing them should be reserved for fancy sets to show off wealth, or for sieges, perhaps.

blocks.html:
Wood

Mortal has a rather in-depth system for trees and their products compared to other games. Why even acquire wood? This material fills small niches, but it is essential to have it to compete. So let’s take a look at what this gathering niche has to offer.

Dendrology is the skill which governs trees and wood. This skill increases the yield when gathering as well as the crafting quality of items made with wood. 70 skill minimum is needed to craft with the best stats, and any higher skill is extra durability.

There are currently 8 woods in the game, with an extra 2 planned to be added for Sarducaa. The chart below highlights many properties of the woods, and their specific uses. In general, the order in which they are listed is from weakest to strongest.

This skill increases the yield when gathering as well as the crafting quality of items made with wood. 70 skill minimum is needed to craft with the best stats, and any higher skill is extra durability. In general, the order in which they are listed is from weakest to strongest.

blocks.html:
What specific uses does wood have?

  1. Building / Territory Control - With few exceptions, just about every structure that is build requires a heavy amount of wood. Some structures require several stacks of wood to be fully built. Reference #territory-control to see the chart outlining the requirements.
  2. Longbow and Asymmetrical Bowery - Spongewood and Whitewood offer the best weight to strength to range ratio there are. These woods are essential to making competitive bows in this category.
  3. Shieldcrafting - Wood is a requirement to craft the core of shields. In most situations, greywood and ironwood are the viable woods in this category.
  4. Mana Nourishment - Blackwood can be cooked in a fermentation jar to make some rather potent mana nourishment food. However, molarium and incisium also fill this niche so this utility is now largely obsolete.
  5. Tapii - Tapii is a magical wood which offers weakspot bonuses in dagger hilts. This material is made by gathering globs from a “Toghair” tree on Sarducaa. This is then combined with other woods (ideally stonewood) to create mystical Tapii wood.
  6. Cooking - Different woods have properties that can be useful in cooking. For example, the “smoke box” requires 10% of the ingredients to be wood to work. This is a largely unexplored aspect of cooking. Let the community know if you find any unique recipes.
  7. Fishing - Each wood has unique properties when used as fishing bait. Due to the extreme amount of variables, you will have to discover for yourself what works best where and against what fish!

blocks.html:
In Mortal Online 1 there was much more utility behind woods in the sense of construction. Each wood had a “density” that determined how much HP it gave buildings, and how fast that building was constructed. Essentially you would get big bonuses for using heavier woods such as stonewood, and you were penalized for using light woods such as spongewood. This mechanic is NOT in Mortal Online 2 however. If it ever returns, expect the value of more dense woods such as ironwood to rise.

Keeping roughly 100,000 wood available provides a useful reserve. You never know when you need it, and it's easy to stack.

Instead, they opted to combine several trees that are similar enough that they share the same wood type and properties. Other observed cases show willow trees in game that function as whitewood! So to put it simply, take the real world equivalent with a grain of salt.

grain of salt. the system also includes a hidden unique wood not normally accessible called “trainingwood”. this material is only obtainable on haven as part of the tutorial. it can be brought to the mainland. there is no known extra utility of this.

guides.title: Bow Crafting
guides.summary: Compare bow types, components, materials, strength requirements, range, and damage when planning a craft.

blocks.html:
Compare bow types, components, materials, strength requirements, range, and damage when planning a craft.

Bow Types
blocks.text: Compare bow types, components, materials, strength requirements, range, and damage when planning a craft. Bow Types

blocks.html:
Bows have 2 shapes: recurve and decurve.

Recurve maximizes the damage of the bow at the cost of durability. Decurve maximizes the durability of the bow at the cost of damage. In general, bows are so cheap that recurve is simply the standard. Decurve is theoretically better for PvE if the goal is to save on material costs of hunting. Bows are cheap and the dura is high enough where decurve should not be used.

Bows have 3 styles: Short -> Long -> Asymmetrical

Shortbows are ideal for low strength characters and can be used on mount.

Longbows are the highest damage bows possible but can only be used on foot. They gain extra benefit from longbow arrows which do more flat damage at the cost of weakspot chance.

Asymmetrical bows have an oblong shape which enables their usage on horseback. They are slower than shortbows, but they do more damage per hit. Pound for pound they are weaker than longbows, and they do not benefit from longbow arrows.

Bows have 2 composition designs: Self and Composite

Self bows are made of a single material, while composite are made of multiple. Self bows have no known utility over composite. The rule of thumb is always make composite bows, even if using the same crafting material as the base and secondary material.

blocks.html:
Skills

Bowyery skills should be tailored to the types of bows that will be made. A full bowcrafter will have 6 skills:

  • Animal Materials - for crepite and dense crepite lore. Basically mandatory.
  • Asymmetrical Bow Crafting - For Asym bows. Drop if only making shortbows or longbows.
  • Botany - for wood lores. Drop if only making shortbows.
  • Bowyery - The main skill. Mandatory.
  • Long Bow Crafting - Drop if only making shortbows.
  • Recurve Bow Mechanics - Basically mandatory.
  • Short Bow Crafting - Mandatory.

Auxiliary skills that compliment bow crafting are woodcutting/botany and butchery to acquire the materials, but they are not required. Crepite is plentiful and cheap enough where stacks of it can be purchased for very cheap from other players. Woodcutting is a secondary and can be done without botany inefficiently, but wood costs are low so this is not a huge issue- just a time sink.

Crafting skills may be locked at level 70 to receive full max range stat, but will take a significant penalty to durability. The recommended approach is to maxing all skills to 100 or at the very least have a trinket that adds to bowyery to use when crafting. Bow durability on recurve bows is important enough to justify the skill point investment.

blocks.html: Bow Stats
blocks.text: Bow Stats

blocks.html:
There are four primary stats on a bow: weight, durability, max range, and strength requirement. Weakspot chance is also likely a hidden stat, but it is not worth chasing.

Weight of bows is always 1kg, no matter the style or materials used.

Durability is how many shots the bow gets. Every shot landed costs 0.10 durability. At 20% durability, bow damage drops dramatically. As a result, a bow with 85.00 durability has an effective 68 durability, which is 680 shots. A bow with 100 durability has 800 effective shots to it.

Max range is for both damage and distance the bow shoots. You always want the highest max range possible.

Strength requirement is the minimum strength that a character using the bow should have. A bow with 81.25 strength should thus have a minimum of 82 strength. Higher strengths receive stamina reduction benefits. Mounted players should also have an additional 5-10 strength higher than the base strength requirement to offset mounted penalties.

blocks.html:
Crafting Process

The entire bow crafting process involves balancing strength requirement to max range. The goal is to minimize strength requirements and maximize the range. Composite bows use a material balance mechanic which determines how much base material versus secondary material is used. Using the sliding mechanic, you change the rigidity of the bow, and thus the strength and range. Design the bows around the strength of the character wielding it.

Composite bows use a material balance mechanic which determines how much base material versus secondary material is used. Using the sliding mechanic, you change the rigidity of the bow, and thus the strength and range. Design the bows around the strength of the character wielding it.

blocks.html:
As a general rule, the further towards the stronger material the slider is, the higher strength and less efficient it is. The inverse is true: the further towards the weaker material, the less strength but higher efficiency it is. For all bow types, recurve composite bows are the best for strength efficiency. No exceptions. The only crafting materials that really matter for bowcrafting are Dense Crepite (best), Spongewood (best), incisium, whitewood, and crepite. The latter 3 materials are for budget bows. Tapii wood is the actual best material for bowcrafting, but it is not in game yet.

Shortbow crafting is easy: Simply find the strongest material you have available and craft at 5% material balance. Crepite is so cheap and plentiful that this material should be used. Horn is a super budget but mediocre choice as well.

Longbows and asymmetrical are a bit more nuanced. Use this chart as a frame of reference for what is being crafted:

blocks.html:
Should you make a long or asymmetrical bow that is too high of a strength requirement, alter the material balance to a different percentage. For example, if you want to craft a 97 strength bow instead of a 99, raise the % of spongewood/dense crepite recurve longbow to 48% from 46%. The majority of characters fall within these strengths above. Once you have discovered a recipe that works for you, create a template in the crafting window or simply write down the recipe and it can be reproduced easily.

The most common mistake when crafting bows is having the base and secondary materials mixed up. Should you craft bows that have funky stats, you probably put dense crepite/crepite as the primary material instead of the wood by accident. Bows are cheap and the materials are easy to get. When in doubt, spam out a few and you can get the right results with trial by error.

guides.title: Cooking
guides.summary: Work through cooking tools, ingredient behavior, nourishment, effects, lores, and repeatable recipe testing.

blocks.html:
Cooking Guide

Work through cooking tools, ingredient behavior, nourishment, effects, lores, and repeatable recipe testing.

There are five reasons to cook:

Zoology/lore XP

Reserve nourishment/Weight

Size food

Healing-over-Time Food

Research - Mana food? Age food? Magic defense food?

Admittedly many of the benefits of cooking are outclassed by other mechanics. For example, zoology lore is a one-time skill raise that can be done with skinning/butchery. You also don’t need to actually have cooking to gain the xp benefit from skinning. Healing-over-time food is great and all, but eating uncooked blood kua has a similar potent effect. For nourishment, pig pie from the vendor does a sufficient job at maxing reserves- while humans don’t even need to eat!

Advanced Cooking Tools - Includes fermentation jar, baking pot, smoke box, and steam pot.

Material Lores

Fishing - Useful for acquiring blood kua and ventriosus

⭐Herbalism - Needed to process certain materials such as Drakon and Nymph Herb

Milling - Refines grains into flours, which are more potent.

⭐Botany Appliances - Allows use of the herbologeum and press to process many resources.

Gathering / Woodcutting / Dendrology / Advanced Dendrology - Useful for blackwood for mana nourishment.

Zoology / Pisces - Good for preparing certain ingredients such as Ventriosus
