blocks.html:
Overview

Cooking is just as complex as alchemy, but does not yield the same benefits. Most of the utility comes from reserve nourishment, but there are a few useful products such as health-over-time food, height food, and weight loss food. While these effects overlap a little with alchemy, they use a different resource pool (hunger) instead of thirst. This means a player can stack these effects with potions for rather profound results.

The underlying system for cooking is the same as alchemy, but with more variables. The general premise is using a primary ingredient and modifying its stats. This can be spelt, gamun oil, salvia oil, or any other number of ingredients. This ingredient has a base set of stats (some of them unique), which are then modified by every other ingredient that is added to the cooking window. In the case of weight loss food, for example, brown shorekelp oil contains the weight loss stat. This stat is then “boosted” by adding karoton juice to it, making a much improved weight loss food over using the simple base of brown shorekelp oil. Cooking tools also have an impact on the quality and potency of the end product. Choosing the right cooking tool can be the difference between a potent food, and an inert one. While most useful recipes have likely been discovered, there are still an abyss of untested combinations- but these admittedly are likely fruitless.

blocks.html:
Cooking Tools

Each cooking tool specializes in a different cooking niche. These offer small boosts to the effectiveness of food in differing capacities. These are also mandatory for specific unique recipes.

Baking Pot - Good stam and good health. Makes pies with 80% flour and 20% meat.

Baking Stone - Used for making breads. Stamina nourishment, but not great. Use at least 40% flour and 20% liquid.

Cooking Pot - General purpose cooking tool. Used to make the majority of useful recipes.

can deep fry by using oils.

Fermentation Jar - Mana nourishment food. Does not require a fire. Over 30% of it must be liquid.

Smoke Box - Overall nourishment for all stats. Requires over 10% of the recipe to be wood. Avoid using liquids.

Spit - Stamina nourishment food.

Steam Pot - Great overall stats (but not the best at any). Requires a good portion of the recipe to be liquid- approx 30%.

In addition to “useful recipes”, there are unique recipes that result in various end products (which offer no additional utility). These are based on various cooking tool + ingredient combinations. They are fun to explore, but don’t offer an apparent benefit other than novelty.

Avoid using liquids. Spit - Stamina nourishment food. Steam Pot - Great overall stats (but not the best at any). Requires a good portion of the recipe to be liquid- approx 30%. In addition to “useful recipes”, there are unique recipes that result in various end products (which offer no additional utility). These are based on various cooking tool + ingredient combinations. They are fun to explore, but don’t offer an apparent benefit other than novelty.

Major undiscovered effects are unlikely, though they cannot be ruled out.

blocks.html:
Ingredients

Just about any gatherable and extractable can be used as an ingredient. You’ll notice in the chart immediately above that there are liquids, oils, fuels, flours, and “fillers”. Use good judgment compared to real life to determine what-is-what! For example, tallow is animal fat, and thus works as an oil. Steppe rush is burnable, and is thus a fuel. All grinded grains count as flours. “Fillers” in this context are anything that doesn’t logically fall into another category.

Certain ingredients can be placed in the cooking menu, but “fail” cooking and get booted out. A good example of this is the troll head. This implies that there is a very specific use case for this ingredient, but the improper “ratio” or tool is being used. Calx powder can also be added to the window, but likewise fails. Perhaps there is a unique combination of tool and extra ingredients that make this particular filler into something useful.

Extraction

Many recipes call for extracted materials. These will typically be from botany appliances- the press and herbologeum. The guide for extracting is found in the #botany-extraction channel. Quickly leveling these skills is found in #leveling-professions

Sophistication:

Sophistication was a stat in MO1 which was gained by eating certain fancily prepared foods. This unlocked access to certain high society content in Tindrem. This added new dialogue options to certain Tindrem NPCs which revealed more in-depth game lore. Sophistication will possibly return to MO2. To prepare for this, stockpile the various “creft” (lobster), roe, and kelp dragon.

blocks.html:
Eating Mechanics

Eating food has its own unique functions. Reserve nourishment is a simple addition- if you eat 1 unit of, you will restore the amount of nourishment listed on the food up to your maximum reserves. Height food also works like this- although the values are decimals and not exactly hidden. You can lose -0.5 height, for example, but it will not display on your character since height is displayed as whole numbers only.

For foods that have “over-time” effects such as health restoration food, the value restored is actually the square root of the total value. The easiest way to calculate this is to use @EmertiQ’s calculator found here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17d2IxYwcsy_LXvWFPZCjLVvVDuPz77EPSCYvqhL9Vqs/edit?gid=0#gid=0

Food poisoning is a result of eating food with too much of a food poisoning stat. When food poisoned, the healing a player receives from food is stopped. There is supposed to be a throwing up animation which stuns the player, as well, but that is not in game yet.

blocks.html:
Niche Mechanics:

The food poisoning stat is mysterious and not fully explored yet. However, if enough food poisoning is incurred, it prevents further healing. A 100hp heal-over-time food with high food poisoning might actually be useless!

Passive regen reduces food poisoning. The cause is unclear, but the effect is reproducible. This will mitigate the potential of the food poisoning penalty, but not remove it.

2 Height = 1 Size. Eating size food increases size directly, and height indirectly. Size is not a whole number and operates on decimals, so it will gain incrementally.

Character height maximums on the character creation window are not always accurate, and players can “break” the cap by eating additional +height food after character creation. There is no easy way to measure how much extra height can be gained, so simply consuming an extra +1 extra size food (usually 28 units of 0.37) after reaching your supposed cap will remove all doubt.

Alcohol content of recipes currently does not seem to do a single thing in MO2.

Certain ingredients get unique names when prepared. For example flakestone becomes flakestone shale, bor and nitre become salts.

Thursars have the “Controlled Metabolism” clade gift which doubles the stamina nourishment they receive from food.

blocks.html:
Future Research

It is possible there are tons of unique effects in cooking that are unlearned or well kept secrets. For example, would it be possible to make mana-over-time food? A food with an effect such as purify? This remains unknown. There are a brazilian different combinations of foods, and there might be ultra niche combinations that yield potent results. There is an exceptionally amount of complexity to cooking, and some interactions may still be undiscovered. I’m not going to be the one to research these, but you can!

If you want to join a community of excel-spreadsheet-users dedicated to perfecting the art of cooking and alchemy, The recommended approach is to joining the Chosn Alchemy Discord server found at: https://discord.gg/3mwB59AvQs

Here's making steel for beginners:

Mine Calx -> Crusher the calx into coal + calx powder -> Furnace 10k coal with 535 coal cataslyst in furnace for Coke.

Mine granum -> Crusher granum into blood ore -> Furnace 10k blood ore + 385 coke into pig iron

Mine saburra -> Grinder 10k saburra + 1k water for saburra powder

Refine 10k pig iron + 5k calx powder + 5k coke into grain steel

Refine 10k grainsteel + 5k coal + 5k saburra powder into steel

Skills needed

Primaries:

Basic Ore Extraction

Intermediate Ore Extraction

Metallurgy

Ore Extraction Applainces

Petrology

Secondaries:

Gathering

Mining

Basic Metals

Pig Iron Lore

Iron-Based Alloys

Grain Steel Lore

Steel Lore

Communitors (ore extraction appliances)

Crusher Operation

Grinder Operation (you can actually use crusher if desired)

Thermal Appliances

Refining Expertise

Igneous Rock

Granum Lore

Sedimentary Rock

Saburra Lore

Coal Lore

Calx Lore

Coke Lore

Blood Ore Lore

There are more advanced methods of going straight to steel, but those require even more specialization + risk because of the appliances they use. For example, blast furnace gives 25% more blood ore and thus 25% more steel overall, but it's not safe to use it.

blocks.html:
Refining is a straight forward profession. You combine two types of metals to create an alloy while using the refining oven. The quantity of product created scales with refining level, as well as with the individual material lores. Every recipe is a simple 2:1:1 ratio. So for example, to create steel, use 2 grainsteel per 1 unit of coal per 1 unit of saburra powder. 10k of the base metal will yield 7k end product without any clade gifts.

blocks.html:
Tips, Tricks, and Misc. Info

-Certain species of fish are very specific to certain pools of water. Kelp dragon can be found in all of the oceans, but it also can be found in the rivers of Canteri. It is not found in other rivers!

-Try weird bait when experimenting. For example, leptoid scales are really bad at catching fish, but it removes so many from the possibilities that it makes catching trinkets easier.

-Focus on reproducible fishing setups when targeting specific catch. Stand in an exact location, use an exact depth and hook size, and aim at specific markers to ensure your cast is the same every single time.

-Butchered fish always sell for more than raw. Increase profits even more with the Alvarin butchering clade (Faunist).

-Loot luck does NOT impact trinket rates with fishing.

-Majority of fish fall under the Perciformes, Teleostei, or Osteichthyes zoology skills.

-Celaeno cave has unique fish such as dark catfish, but these don’t really have a use right now.

-In most situations, hook size can be altered. Size 50 and 100 hooks are almost interchangeable and sizes 1-10 can be used for most things.

-There are many notable fishing spots. Sausage lake, celaeno cave, Toxai bridge, cave camp cave are marked on the map below.

-Consider using blue sorex for trinkets since it cuts out Canna from the drop table.

blocks.html:
Future of Fishing

  • There is a character statistic known as "sophistication" which is gained from consuming exquisite items such as exotic animals and well prepared dishes. Fishing will offer many avenues for raising this statistic and reaping the rewards of high society.
  • Future updates will bring a boss known as a Tamigula which drops rare and powerful cosmoid scales and carapaces for crafting. It also drops meat which is potent in healing potions This was historically caught with a white rabbit foot as bait in the jungle of Myrland.
  • Many fish will be used to create dyes for when the dyeing system is in place. Bronze creft, red squilla, blue sorex, and many others will be usable as pigment to create unique colors to dye armor parts.
  • Fishing will offer many resources for creating poisons.

blocks.html:
Swimming

Swimming as a unique and powerful skill for both exploration and combat. Those with swimming have significant advantages against those who can't. This section covers the mechanics of swimming.

Speed

Movement speed while swimming is determined by many variables:

  • Base swim speed is 110
  • Each point of dexterity adds 0.5 swimming speed
  • Swimming skill increases speed by up to 20%
  • Crawling skill increases speed by up to 40%
  • "Sprinting" (using shift key) increases both speed and stamina usage by 25%
  • Being out of stamina incurs a 75% movement speed penalty
  • Every kg of armor weight penalizes speed and stamina by 1%
  • Every kg of inventory penalizes speed and stamina by 0.5%
  • Resistance swimming reduces the armor/inventory penalties by up to 25%
  • Mounts each have unique speed stats that are modified by equipment weight + rider weight

Buoyancy

Buoyancy is a hidden stat that determines how quickly (if at all) a character can float. A character with negative buoyancy will always sink and must slide along terrain to gain height. Buoyancy is impacted mostly by the resistance swimming skill and the character's equipment/inventory weight. While swimming, if you can raise along the Z axis by holding the space bar, you have buoyancy. The greater the buoyancy stat the more control you have over this.

Breath

Characters have a finite amount of oxygen before they take drowning. This timer is modified by the swimming skill, diving skill, constitution, as well as the alvarin "Naiad" clade gift (+10 seconds flat). Once a player runs out of breath they start to take drowning damage, which does about 12 damage per tick.

Oxygen is recovered at a rate of 10% per second. This means you must surface for 10 seconds to fully recover the air meter. This scales with other variables, so it will always be 10 seconds. Stamina regeneration is impacted by oxygen. You have 100% stamina regeneration at 100% oxygen meter and 50% while at 0% oxygen.

blocks.html:
Some notes:

It should be noted that swimming favors mage gameplay. The low armor weight combined with ranged damage and vertical movement means that mages generally have the advantage against fighters. That said, it is possible for fighters to specialize into swimming heavily. If a Veela decideds to disrobe and jump in the water, it makes mages cry.

A common question with regards to swimming is: "Is 50 skill enough?".

The answer is, it depends. Think of it like a game of rock/paper/scissors. 100 swimming > 50 swimming > 0 swimming > 100 swimming (on land). A player with 50 swimming is going to blow unskilled characters out of the water, but they also get fairly countered by those with 100 swimming. As a tool to "Get out of jail free", 50 swimming is sufficient as a low-cost investment.

blocks.html:
Gathering / Foraging / Pickables

Find and identify harvestable resources while understanding gathering skills, tool choices, yields, and regional availability.

Gathering

Gathering explicitly refers to mining and woodcutting and requires the use of an equipped tool to harvest. Rocks, trees, and mining meteors are all gathering-based.

Here are a chart of all gathering base yields:

Gathering Gathering explicitly refers to mining and woodcutting and requires the use of an equipped tool to harvest. Rocks, trees, and mining meteors are all gathering-based. Here are a chart of all gathering base yields:

blocks.html:
There are several effects used to increase gathering yield. These are all compounding, and the rule of thumb is they also increase the amount of available yield from the target node. For example, a granum node which gives 4000 units with a +10% mining buff will give 4400 units before depleting.

Here is a list of all mining yield bonus effects:

  • Stoneshaper II (Alvarin Clade) - Increases mining yield by an additional 10%
  • Outpost 10% mining bonus from owning an applicable territory
  • Keep bonus - 5% (when combined with outpost bonus)
  • Double yield nodes in select locations, i.e. Granum pass
  • Essence orb Double Chance - Generally around 28-30% chance per tick
  • Essence orb - flat mining % chance. Available evidence suggests the cap is 20% with a t3 orb
  • Double nodes - certain locations give 2x the base yield, such as granum pass and tephra crater
  • Relic of prospecting - ~10% mining yield (global). This can scale with the number of players in a guild.

Combining these effects can be VERY potent:

blocks.html:
Mining also has a chance at “rare materials”. This really boils down to extra gems, radiant fragments from meteors.

  • Stoneseer (Alvarin Clade) - Increases chance at acquiring rare materials when mining by 10%
  • Geologist (Oghmir Clade) - Increases chance at acquiring rare materials when mining by 10%
  • Essence orb - Increases rare chance at acquiring rare material. Generally around 5-10%

Rare materials that are extracted are node-dependent. Tephra can drop full adamants, while calx generally drops rubers. Granum can drop rough adamants, but will typically drop rough grossulars.

Here are a list of all woodcutting effects:

  • Double gathering orb - ~30% chance of 2x
  • Woodcutting essence orb - 10-20%
  • Outpost bonus - 25%
  • Keep bonus - 5% when combined with outpost
  • Dendrologist (Alvarin Clade) - 10% increased chance to acquire rare materials when lumberjacking

Rare materials for woods are typically in the form of ambers, which are simply vendor trash for extra gold.

blocks.html:
Foraging/Pickables

Foraging refers to the harvesting of pickable resources, including books. Foraging has many application when it comes to alchemy, cooking, magic, and rare items. Anything that can be “gathered” but isn’t a stone nor wood node is a forage/pickable.

blocks.html:
Here are some highlight examples of foraging:

  • Argus Sponge - For alchemy. Found in jungle waters.
  • Bor Chunk - For extraction. Found near some beaches.
  • Calamine Shale - Reagent. Found in wooded rocky areas.
  • Coal - Reagent and catalyst. Found in mountainous areas.
  • Corn - Creates stamina food and weight gain potions.
  • Drakon - Used for age + potions. Found near specific lakes.
  • Essence Orb (Pickable) - Can spawn many valuables including up to T3 essence orbs. Comes from blue meteors.
  • Gamun - Used for size- food. Found in desert plains.
  • Nahuat - Duuuude weed lol
  • Naturists Satchel - Used for beastmastery books
  • Nymph Herb - Used for age- potions
  • Raffle Bags - Has rare goodies. Spawns during the Krampos event every Christmas
  • Salvia - Used for health potions and height+ food. Found on cliffsides.
  • Sea Dew - Used for health potions. Found in select sea locations.

There are over 100 different pickables around the world, so every single one will not be listed. If you need to know where one is, try finding a task for it and a map marker will show it. If you can’t find it, ask around. Worst case scenario, go explore!

Here are all of the effects that impact foraging/pickables:

  • Loot amount rings / masteries increases the yield of the pick, if possible
  • Loot luck rings / masteries - Increases the chance at a good item being picked
  • Essence orb Foraging Yield - Increases the yield of the pick, if possible

—-

guides.title: Leveling Actions
guides.summary: Efficient training actions for the skills that improve through repeated use, grouped for quick progression planning.

blocks.html:
This section goes over every single skill in game and gives leveling strategies for each of them. The goal is to have the cheapest, most convenient, and the most effective leveling for each skill. Skills are broken down into broad sections.

Gathering Skills

Gathering - Only really gained by mass gathering.

Mining - AFK mine rocks. It is preferable to do this close to a bank, or use a horse. Each rock "node" yields approximately 3333 rock before running out of resources.

Woodcutting - AFK cut trees. Start with spongewood trees so that you gain botany lore as well at the same time.

Movement

Athletics / Runspeed / Sprinting / Breathing Technique - Sprint around.

Riding / Swift Riding / Controlled Riding - These skills are easily gained by running in a circle on a horse. The problem is getting the books, which are bought in Khurite towns and Tindrem.

Jumping - Spam the space bar. Better to train in conjunction with landing technique.

Landing Technique - Read the book to max and then find a pair of stairs you can climb and drop down from to take only 0 fall damage. The roofs of strongholds generally work well for this.

Survival / Swimming / Resistance Swimming / Diving / Crawling - These skills are really easy to level up. Read all the books so that you know the skill, cancel them. Find a shallow water source where your character still wades without drowning and afk.

blocks.html:
Combat Skills

Armor Training / Heavy Armor Training - Run around in combat mode with armor that is HEAVIER than you can wear. For instance if your cap is 8.99/8.99 armor weight, you need to run around with 9 weight or more for this to raise.

Balance / Knockdown Resistance / Knockback Resistance - Read the books. Untested* - sit on a mount and get hit with blunt weapons for 25+ damage

Blocking / Blocking Endurance / Defensive Stance / Unarmed Blocking - Have a friend spam attacks at you while you are blocking. The system also includes a large cluster of spiderlings in the bottom of the haven rat cave. Aggro all 10+ of them and block with a shield. Heal up as needed.

Combat Maneuvering / Momentum / Combat Movement - Move around in combat mode.

Feint - Move in combat mode with a weapon drawn. Let this skill level passively during normal play; there is no efficient way to train it through a macro.

Combat Balance - Read the book. Certain pet abilities cause knockback which give xp for this but it isn't consistent.

Combat Techniques - Will raise passively as Defensive Stance and Aggressive Stance raise. This skill doesn't do anything except act as a parent for Def/Agg stance.

Melee Combat / Brawling / Unarmed Technique / Aggressive Stance - Find a friend and punch him repeatedly.

blocks.html:
Mounted Combat / Mounted Charge - Get on a horse and stand still while hitting an AFK friend with wooden weapons.

Ranged Combat / Archery / Aiming Technique / Controlled Aiming / Marksmanship / Mounted Archery- Get controlled riding to 35 and archery to 60. Read Aiming technique to 60. Read and drop controlled aiming, marksmanship. Read mounted archery and keep it reading. Once you have all of these skills, get on a horse and repeatedly shoot a guilded friendly horse in the head using bodkin arrows with the weakest bow you can make from horseback.

Weapon Skills - Axes / Clubs / Spears / Daggers / Poleaxes / Poleswords / Swords / Lances / Unarmed Tech - Have a friend go AFK, beat him repeatedly for about an hour and a half with the weapon of your choice.

blocks.html:
Survival / Domestication / Misc. Skills

Active Regeneration/Resting - Lose HP and rest.

Anatomy / Damage assessment - Read anatomy to max and then spam out bandages.

Beastmastery - Attack with living pets and have them use abilities.

Beastmastery Influences/Masteries - Use abilities for each respective species. Once you hit 75 read the mastery book and use the mastery skills til max. Doable on equerries/priests.

Creature Control / Advanced Creature Control / Herding / Veterinary Care / Animal Care - Read the books, or have a pet out over a period of time. Levels passively with a pet out. Herding requires more than 1 pet out. Easiest way to do this is have 4+ horses and tell them to attack an NPC. Horses do not do damage so this can be done in town.

Endurance - Sprint around.

Passive Regen - Read the book. If your health reserves are a little low, it will give you XP every minute. This is a very very long term skill to raise.

Potion Utilization - Read the book, and drink water potions.

Subsisting - This one takes forever. Repeatedly get put into mercy mode a quadrillion times.

Taming - Read book to max. Find a black bear that is "low chance at taming". Each 1/4th of the circle that is successful gives 9xp. Attempt to fill the taming circle to 3/4ths each time and then stop taming. Repeat until you need to find a higher level bear, or until level 100.

blocks.html:
Magic Skills

Animism - Currently not available to learn.

Concentration - You can only read these books up.

Domination - Read the books to 70. Use the same strategy as taming (see above).

Ecumenical Spells - It's best to read this book to 62. If you wish to raise it higher, read it to 70 and then read the domination book to max it out.

Meditation - Best to raise when macroing up your other magic skills. When you have an empty mana bar, simply lay down to rest and this will raise. This will also raise Vitalism. Wear 15kg+ heavy armor to get regen to 10% to extend the resting time.

Magic Schools - You must read the book, or read the book to a certain point, and then raise Ecumenical Spells or Spiritism.

Mental Offence / Mental Focus / Mental Training / Mana Regeneration / Mounted Magery - This is a fun one. Cast spurt or lesser heal several thousand times. Do it on a mount with 25 controlled riding if you want to level mounted magery concurrently.

Multiverse / Ether Lore / Portal Lore - Read books to max. Self cast portals.

Necromancy/Ritualism - Get necromancy to 25 and ritualism to 25. Raise a tupilak and spam the noxious gas ability on an equerry til 100 in both skills.

Necromancy alone can be trained cheaply by raise walker to 23 -> raise strong walker to 38 -> use a necromancy necklace to boost to 40 -> blind to 56 -> take necklace off -> blind to 56 again -> necklace back on and crawling hands to 70 -> benumb mind to 78 -> atrophy to 88 -> mental leech to 100.

Spiritism - Read book to max. Cast transcendental awareness to 86. Cast ether portal to 100.

Vitalism - Read the book to 35, and then get the mana regeneration skill. It will level passively whenever your mana regens.

guides.title: Leveling Professions
guides.summary: Progress crafting and profession skills with practical material choices, training routes, and ways to control waste.

blocks.html:
Crafting Skills

Cooking / Advanced Cooking - Go to a source of water, and collect 50k water or so. Cook it on the spot. Advanced cooking will take more than this.

Cooking Tools - Like with cooking, get as much water as possible and utilize the tools. Some tools require flour, or wood, so use the minimum amount of those ingredients.

Potion Making/Adv Potion Making - Make a few kegs of water potions.

Refining - The most reliable way to get this skill up is to mass produce Messing or Bron from Saburra. This skill takes quite a long time to raise.

Extraction - Crushing Saburra or Granum en masse is The most reliable way to raise this.

Herbalism - Gather herbs from around the world and extract them in the Herbologium. Nahuat in the jungle is the fast mode to leveling this. Salvia and Seadew are a great source of herbalism skill, and the oil is used in high end health potions.

Milling - Gather craploads of any type of grain, such as Rye, and extract it in a crusher to get rye flour. Can be used on other applainces. You can also press fruits and vegetables for their juices.

Butchery skills - The most reliable way to raise butchery is to simply butcher carcasses en masse. After getting butchery workbench to 35, you can start to use the butchery table. Your best option is to buy carcasses from other players and then butcher the carcass and sell the mats to the utility vendor. You will take a loss at first, but in the long run you will profit many hundreds of gold.

blocks.html:
Basic / Intermediate / Advanced Ore Extraction - There is no real easy way to get these up, except by continuing to extract rocks as normal. Reading the books are always a good option.

Glassblowing / Pottery - Neither are in game yet.

Bowcrafting Skills - Using only spongewood or whitewood at minimum density, mass produce the specific type of bow you want to level.

Shield Crafting - Using only spongewood or whitewood at minimum density, mass produce small round shields.

House / Workshop construction - Not in game yet.

Weapon Crafting - Simply mass produce spongewood, whitewood, or bone tissue weapons of each handle / weapon head type you want.

Armor Crafting / Armor Type Lores - For the soft armors, simply make sleeves or gloves out of cotton or leather. For everything higher, create gloves out of keeled scale and cotton, on lowest density.

Fletchery - Currently not in game.

Engineering / Advanced Engineering - Read the books high, and then build houses.

Dyeing / Tailoring - Not in game yet.

Alchemy - Make kegs of potions out of water.

Papyrology / Paprus Lore / Sarduccan Papyrus lore - Not obtainable in game yet.

Reading / Skimming - many people laugh when they hear that there is a book about reading, but honestly, read the damn thing. Pop skimming at 100 reading and drop it if you need to read something else.

Various Meat Lores - Simply acquire it en masse by butchery (which will raise the lore), and then cook it.

guides.title: Lockpicking
guides.summary: Prepare for lockpicking with the required tools, skills, difficulty ranges, chest behavior, and route considerations.

blocks.html:
Lockpicking

Lockpicking is a profession skill and a mini-game which allows you to unlock chests in the world for loot. Most bandit camps, many dungeons, and some open world spots host chests which can be picked. The most notable use-cases for lockpicking are gathering gems and gold from places like Melissar’s Vault, or looting Golden Hammers from Sarducaan chests to trade for the Dezirh Plate Armor book. Lockpicking does NOT work on player house doors nor player owned chests.

Basics

  • Lockpicking is learned via action only, and can be grinded to max on novice chests alone
  • Lockpicks come in 3 tiers - Novice, Adept, and Master
  • Novice lockpicks are found in barrels around the world
  • Novice picks are used for chests with up to 4 pins and are found in barrels around the world
  • Adept picks are used for chests up to 6 pins and are found in novice chests. These require 50 skill to use
  • Master lockpicks are used for chests up to 8 pins and are found in adept chests. These require 100 skill to use
  • Each time a chest is picked, 1 durability is used from the lockpick
  • There is NO penalty for failure
  • There is NO benefit to exceeding to skill level requirement for your target chest
  • Chests spawn items in ticks of approximately 30 minutes
  • Chests have specific loot, and a % chance of spawning what is assigned to each slot every tick
  • There is no set time for a chest to fill as it is luck based
  • Novice chests are typically found around the world. Adept are usually found in more dangerous areas. Master are found in dungeons and as select world chests
  • Boss chests CANNOT be lockpicked
  • When your character is lockpicking, it stands in a crouched state to alert other players of your action. Keep aware of your surroundings

blocks.html:
There are several components of lockpicking that need to be explained to understand lockpicking:

  • Lockpick - This device is used to lift pins
  • Tension Wrench - A tool that applies turning pressure to the lock, allowing pins to be locked in place on the sheer line
  • Driver Pins - These are forced down by springs. When the lock is in a locked state, these prevent the lock from turning
  • Key Pins - These are pins that rest within the lock and are forced up when a key is inserted, pushing the driver pins upward as well
  • Sheer Line - The line inside of a lock where pins rest into place when the device is unlocked
  • Spring - These apply downward pressure to the pins force the lock to rest in a locked state

When the lock is in a locked state, these prevent the lock from turning Key Pins - These are pins that rest within the lock and are forced up when a key is inserted, pushing the driver pins upward as well Sheer Line - The line inside of a lock where pins rest into place when the device is unlocked Spring - These apply downward pressure to the pins force the lock to rest in a locked state

blocks.html:
Controls

A - moves the lockpick to the left

D - moves the lockpick to the right

W - moves the lockpick upward into the pins

Hold Right Click - Adjust the tension wrench

Mouse Drag Left - Increase force on the tension wrench

Mouse Drag Right - Decrease force on the tension wrench
blocks.text: Controls A - moves the lockpick to the left D - moves the lockpick to the right W - moves the lockpick upward into the pins Hold Right Click - Adjust the tension wrench Mouse Drag Left - Increase force on the tension wrench Mouse Drag Right - Decrease force on the tension wrench

blocks.html:
Technique

The mini-game of lockpicking is confusing at first, but very straightforward once you understand the basics.

  1. Get a lockpick and find a chest. Interact with it (Default E)
  2. Hold left click to apply pressure to the tension wrench (for the entire duration of the mini-game)
  3. Move your mouse left and right to adjust the tension. You will generally be applying pressure LEFT
  4. Start applying pressure to pins with the W key. Adjust between pins with the A and D keys
  5. If the pin jumps up freely, there is not enough tension. If the pin does not move up, there is too much tension. Adjust tension by moving the mouse left and right
  6. Find which pin has the most resistance to being picked with the least amount of tension. This will be your first target
  7. Adjust tension until it barely rises, but still rises
  8. Force the pin upwards with the W key until it reaches the sheer line. Once it is snugly stuck in the sheer line, it will jiggle
  9. At this point you should not be moving the mouse to the right to release tension.
  10. Increase tension slightly by moving the mouse left and probe other pins to find the next one that has the most resistance
  11. Continue forcing pins and locking them into the sheer line until they are all completed and the lock opens
  12. If you find yourself in a position where you have too much tension and release tension drops pins, you did the pins in the wrong order. Change the order you do the pins so that the ones with most resistance to being probed are done first

guides.title: Shieldcrafting
guides.summary: Compare shield styles and materials by weight, durability, coverage, and crafting requirements.

blocks.html:
Compare shield styles and materials by weight, durability, coverage, and crafting requirements.

The primary pvp use of a shield is to force equipment hits. An equipment hit occurs when the collision of a weapon hits the collision of a shield. When this occurs, the defensive stats of the shield are added into the damage calculation, potentially reducing damage by a significant amount. The general calculation for character damage on a strike involves lots of variables; wearing a shield and forcing equipment hits simply adds the defensive bonuses of the shield to that calculation. With other effects such as defensive stance, trinkets, and clade gifts, this can result in a severe reduction in damage received. Important: this calculation for equipment hits always stacks with the chest armor piece, no matter what part of the body is under the shield. It is thus important to wear a strong shield and strong chestpiece to maximize the impact that a shield has.

The primary PvE use of a shield is to increase the blocked damage amount, particularly against creatures that cannot be parried. The most notable of these is the minotaur king. To use this mechanic simply block like normal and the passive damage reduction will occur.

Now that the purpose of shields is explained, next will be how to properly craft them.

blocks.html:
All shields consist of 3 parts: the core, the frame, and the coat.

The core is always made of wood. The only two materials worth using for this slot are greywood and ironwood. Greywood is ideal for lightweight shields with acceptable durability, and ironwood is best for maximum protection with incredible durability. Other woods either have abysmal durability, or they are wildly inefficient for defensive purposes.

The coat is the second most important element of a shield's material choices. This material will also have the most impact on the aesthetics of the shield. Animal materials (caparace/leathers/scales/teeth), woods, certain rocks (maalite/jadeite/nyx, etc), textiles, and metals can be used for this slot. Ideally, steel, pansar carapace, tungsteel, or other high defensive value materials will be used. A tungsteel coat will generally give 81.X pierce defense on an ironwood frame, while steel gives ~76.X. The greywood equivalents to these are 69.X and 64.X respectively. Generally aim for the best material with the highest values you can, as these will offer the most protection.

The frame material is the least most important part of a shield, but it does have stat-impacting effects. Certain animal materials (teeth/bones/horns/etc), metals, and certain rocks can be used for the frame. The single most efficient material for weight to defense ratio for a frame is bone tissue. Other fantastic trim materials are flakestone, incisium, or molarium. Metals should probably not be used as this drastically increases the cost of a shield while also increasing weight while not increasing defenses enough.

To make this simple: an optimal material choice for shields is ironwood(core)/steel(coat)/flakestone(trim). Substitute greywood if you need lighter weight, and use tungsteel if you want better protection.

blocks.html:
The next element of crafting viable shields is the choice of shield type, shield size, and shield frame. The right choice of shield design is paramount in making it work for your character.

The shield type (round/tower, kite) is important because this directly determines how much surface area it covers. Round shields are generally inefficient *for weight to surface area, so their only niche uses would be to save weight or for PvE usage. Kite shields are currently not in game. Thus for most circumstances, towershields are the optimal choice.

The shield size is the next most important thing. As the primary users of shields are alvarin/human mages and oghmir fighters, the optimal shield size will be small. Anything bigger offers heavy diminishing returns on how much surface area is protected while dramatically increasing weight. The order of smallest hitbox to greatest in shields is:

Small

Standard

Medium

Large

Heavy

As shields become larger, they get significantly heavier. For context, a small greywood/steel/flakestone tower shield weighs 7.36kg, while a heavy shield of the same make weighs 10.02kg! Thus it is important to tailor your shield size to your characters height. Using *too big of a shield will have extra build requirements over smaller shields (in the form of increased need for armor training), as well as stamina/mana penalties. If a shield is too small, it may not provide adequate equipment hit coverage.

The image below demonstrates the size difference a shield has in coverage on a typical Sheevra mage character.
blocks.text: The next element of crafting viable shields is the choice of shield type, shield size, and shield frame. The right choice of shield design is paramount in making it work for your character. The shield type (round/tower, kite) is important because this directly determines how much surface area it covers. Round shields are generally inefficient *for weight to surface area, so their only niche uses would be to save weight or for PvE usage. Kite shields are currently not in game. Thus for most circumstances, towershields are the optimal choice. The shield size is the next most important thing. As the primary users of shields are alvarin/human mages and oghmir fighters, the optimal shield size will be small. Anything bigger offers heavy diminishing returns on how much surface area is protected while dramatically increasing weight. blocks.html:
Frame style choice is a consideration to have. While this is mostly aesthetic, there are functional differences between the types. Durability, weight, and hitbox size are all impacted by the frame style. Cross frames will offer the lightest weight, but they also lose a bit of the trim. Brute frame have the heaviest weight and highest durability, but they have bulkiness that may force extra handle hits. A useful option is full boss frames as a happy medium, while retaining a balanced visual design. Choose what fits your needs best.

blocks.html:
Taming or Domination

Which to pick? In general, taming is the better option. It does not have the primary requirement of ecumenical spells, and the pets are tradable. That said, domination has two unique aspects that give it value:

Coralis crabs - the tankiest PvE option in game. Very strong in PvP as well.

Web pull/snare - Clothos maidens and flingers have the ability to yoink enemies into your line at the cost of most of their focus, and they have the only activated slow ability in game with their snare. Are they worth it...? That's for you to decide.

When in doubt, go with taming.

blocks.html:
Stable Mechanics -

The equerry is the place to store pets. Here are the basic mechanics of it.

Equerry slots:

  • Base of 5 slots
  • +1 slot per 20 points in management (for a max of +5)
  • +2 slots per stable slot mastery (for a max of +6)
  • The maximum combined stable slots are 16 total with all upgrades.

Equerries work on a micro-node system. Equerries that are within a micro-node share their pool of creatures. These micro-nodes are approximately 75m x 75m large.

Stabling a pet requires it to be unequipped of all gear. Pets generally need to be within 15m of the stablemaster to be stabled. Barriers between the pet and the equerry are ignored when stabling (you can stable a pet from outside of a house to a stablemaster inside).

If an equerry is destroyed, stabled pets remain on the micro-node. Rebuilding or replacing the equerry NPC will make them accessible again.

Pets that are stabled maintain their loyalty, HP, and hunger levels. Pets which are unstabled have approximately a 1 minute grace period where they cannot lose loyalty due to not having enough pet points. Pets always spawn with maximum stamina when unstabled. This means you can burn stamina fully and then stable and unstable to refresh the stamina pool to full.

Equerries can be accessed from a short distance with the /equerry or /stable chat commands.

guides.title: Weaponcrafting
guides.summary: Build melee weapons by comparing heads, handles, materials, damage profiles, durability, weight, and strength requirements.

blocks.html:
Weaponcrafting

Build melee weapons by comparing heads, handles, materials, damage profiles, durability, weight, and strength requirements.

Here is an overview of weapon types and their niche:

Axe - High slash and blunt weapon with generally shorter range. Not meta.

Dagger - Low strength piercing weapon that can weakspot (armor penetration). Only useful for mages.

Hammer - Anti-armor weapon with generally shorter reach. Meta.

Lance - Mounted only weapon that is either pierce or blunt focused. Can guarantee dismounts. Situationally useful.

Poleaxe - Long weapon with strong blunt/slash and decent pierce. Too heavy for practical use.

Polesword - General purpose long reach weapon that uses slashes. Too heavy for practical use.

Spear - Thrusting weapon that benefits from pierce. Great at morphing/animation abuse. Meta.

Swords - General purpose weapon, easy to use. Weak vs. heavy armor. Meta if facing underequipped enemies or mages, otherwise subpar compared to hammers.

blocks.html:
Required Skills

Weaponcrafting has two branches of skills required - the weaponcrafting/hilt skills themselves, and the material lores. Choose specifically what you want to craft (i.e. steel swords) and you will pick and choose which skills are needed.

Weaponcrafting Skills:

Weaponcrafting - Mandatory overarching skill

Basic Blade Crafting - For swords, spears, axes, and daggers

1h Blade Hilt Crafting - For swords and daggers

Blunt Weapon Crafting - For maces, axes, poleaxes, and lances

1h Shaft and Club Crafting - For Lances, axes, maces, poleaxes, and poleswords

Material Lores -

Animal Materials - Mostly for dental lore to use incisium for poles, and for scales

Master Alloys - For cronite and oghmium weapons (best in slot)

Metallurgy - For steel, tungsteel, messing/tindremic messing, and master alloys

Petrology - For maalite (daggers/spears), flakestone (cheap weapons + poleaxes), nyx (cheap blunt weapons)

Scales - High durability weapon coating + weakspot scales. Pansar scales are the best weakspot material and they offer many extra durability on hilted (not pole) weapons.

blocks.html:
Most weaponcrafters specialize in one specific weapon branch. Either they do blade crafting for swords/daggers/spears, or blunt crafting and do maces. Poleaxes, axes, and lances are niche products that not many people use, but you can do those if you’re feeling like a special snowflake.

As for materials choice selection, most people can get away with just using animal materials (incisium/ironfur/guard fur) and metallurgy for steel or messing weapons. Scales specialize and improve specific weapons like daggers and swords, but it is not mandatory.

70 Skills - Weapons made with 100 crafting and material lore skills have maximum durability. You can lower the skills/material lores down to 70 to maintain the same effectiveness of the weapon (i.e. the same slash/pierce/blunt stat) but at the cost of durability. This is only recommended if you offset the lowered skill with a trinket that bridges that gap. Weapon durability is simply too important to cut corners.

Weapons lose effectiveness at 20% durability. If a weapon has 100 durability, it maintains usefulness from 100 durability down to 20. After it reaches the threshold of 20%, it loses a significant amount of damage. It is important to have 100 skill and 100 material lore.

Adamant Tipped Engravers are rare drops which allow for a “legendary” quality item to be crafted with 100 weaponcrafting skills and 100 material lore skills. This state adds a unique weapon engraving as well as a small boost to durability. From an economics standpoint this is wasteful. Save these for flex or siege fights.

Crafting Process

  1. Choose a weapon type and handle.
  2. Choose weapon head.
  3. Add Core material - Bones, metals, certain minerals, wood
  4. Add Grip material - Cloth, fur, scales
  5. Add Head material - Bones, metals, certain minerals

Core materials are what the hilt/shaft is made of. This has a modest impact on strength requirement and weight and minimal impact on damage.

Grip material mostly impacts durability with a minor effect on weight/str requirement. Can impact weakspot.

Head material has significant impacts to damage, strength requirement, and weight. Choose wisely.

On the left is an adorned shaft. On the right is a gripped shaft. The gripped shaft has significantly more range than the adorned, making it better suited for fighting. Unless you plan on hugging enemies with a fast character, avoid adorned. Someone could use an adorned shaft and mistakenly think this weapon type are bad because of the reach- but it is in fact the shaft limiting the weapon.

Play around in the mortaldata calculator to see specific and precise weapon stats: https://mortaldata.com/workbench/

blocks.html:
Rules of thumb with weaponcrafting:

  • Keep weapon weight low if it can be helped. High weapon weight and strength requirement = increased stamina usage.
  • Avoid 1h swords. They do not have enough dura to be viable.
  • The strength requirement of the weapon should be under the strength of the character with few exceptions. If a weapon requires 99.4 strength, the character using it should have 100.
  • Metals are fine to use in hilts to increase durability. They are extremely costly and heavy on shaft/pole weapons- use incisium for pole weapons instead.
  • Avoid hilts which have bulky hitboxes as these can force handle hits on otherwise good strikes.
  • Pansar scales and then placoid scales are ideal as a grip material for weakspots. Pansar scales also have the highest durability. They are ideal for use on hilts, but not shafts.

blocks.html:
Handle hits are one of the most important considerations for crafting a weapon. All weapons have a hitbox that collides with enemy hitboxes. If a weapon design tends to hit a target and does handle hit damage instead of hitting properly, even on seemingly perfect hits, the head might have a bad hitbox.

Take maces for example - a war club has slightly more blunt damage than a warhammer. It also costs way more strength to use. This would indicate perhaps a low strength warhammer would be viable for PvP for low strength characters like hybrids or mages. However, warhammers have an atrocious hitbox that make landing hits difficult. This precludes it from being a viable weapon for any strength level. That said, don’t confuse aiming skill issue with a genuinely bad weapon hitbox. Test thoroughly on training dummies.

However, warhammers have an atrocious hitbox that make landing hits difficult. This precludes it from being a viable weapon for any strength level. That said, don’t confuse aiming skill issue with a genuinely bad weapon hitbox. Test thoroughly on training dummies.

blocks.html:
Meta Weapons

PvP meta weapons are simple. Use the best materials available with optimal head and shaft/hilt.

Mace - 1h war club with gripped handle. Tindremic messing head. Plate scale grip. Incisium core.

Sword - 2h heavy great blade with khurite hilt. Oghmium/Cronite head. Pansar scale grip. Tungsteel core.

Spear - Risar spear with simple handle. Oghmium/Cronite/Maalite head. Plate scale grip. flakestone core.

Dagger - Risar dagger with risar hilt. Oghmium/Tungsteel head. Pansar scales grip. Tungsteel core.

PvE weapons are a different beast. Rather than focusing on good damage, they should be acceptable damage plus higher durability, or they should focus on being ultra cheap and disposable. Typically players will use what materials they have on hand. Flakestone is a common choice as it hits quickly and is cheap to produce.

blocks.html:
Weakspot

Weakspot is a % chance to give armor penetration. Weakspot adds no damage to an unarmored opponent. Swords and daggers are the primary weapons that can weakspot. In general, a metal head + placoid/pansar scale + incisium is going to give a high weakspot chance.

See #weakspot for more information on this.

In general, a metal head + placoid/pansar scale + incisium is going to give a high weakspot chance. See #weakspot for more information on this.

blocks.html:
The Damage Calculation

The math for exactly how damage is calculated isn’t fully known. Even if it was known, there isn’t much benefit in actually knowing it. Here is a rough understanding of how damage is determined:

[weapon stats] + [clade gift] + [aggressive stance] + [trinket bonuses] + [weapon sweetspot calculation] + [charge %] + [feint/counterattack modifiers] + [weakspot modifiers] + [natural damage spread] + [weapon skill level]

vs.

[defense stats] + [clade gifts] + [defensive stance] + [trinket bonuses] + [akh bond bonuses] + [counter-reduction]

Weapons are a critical part of this equation, but they are not the only portion. Remember that when building characters. A crafted weapon can elevate a character, but it in of itself is not the only factor in being effective in combat.

melee weapons by comparing heads, handles, materials, damage profiles, durability, weight, and strength requirements. here is an overview of weapon types and their niche: axe - high slash and blunt weapon with generally shorter range. not meta. dagger - low strength piercing weapon that can weakspot (armor penetration). only useful for mages. hammer - anti-armor weapon with generally shorter reach. meta. lance - mounted only weapon that is either pierce or blunt focused. can guarantee dismounts. situationally useful. poleaxe - long weapon with strong blunt/slash and decent pierce. too heavy for practical use. polesword - general purpose long reach weapon that uses slashes. too heavy for practical use. spear - thrusting weapon that benefits from pierce. great at morphing/animation abuse. meta. swords - general purpose weapon, easy to use. weak vs. heavy armor. meta if facing underequipped enemies or mages, otherwise subpar compared to hammers. required skills weaponcrafting has two branches of skills required - the weaponcrafting/hilt skills themselves, and the material lores. choose specifically what you want to craft (i.e. steel swords) and you will pick and choose which skills are needed. weaponcrafting skills: weaponcrafting - mandatory overarching skill basic blade crafting - for swords, spears, axes, and daggers 1h blade hilt crafting - for swords and daggers blunt weapon crafting - for maces, axes, poleaxes, and lances 1h shaft and club crafting - for lances, axes, maces, poleaxes, and poleswords material lores - animal materials - mostly for dental lore to use incisium for poles, and for scales master alloys - for cronite and oghmium weapons (best in slot) metallurgy - for steel, tungsteel, messing/tindremic messing, and master alloys petrology - for maalite (daggers/spears), flakestone (cheap weapons + poleaxes), nyx (cheap blunt weapons) scales - high durability weapon coating + weakspot scales. pansar scales are the best weakspot material and they offer many extra durability on hilted (not pole) weapons. most weaponcrafters specialize in one specific weapon branch. either they do blade crafting for swords/daggers/spears, or blunt crafting and do maces. poleaxes, axes, and lances are niche products that not many people use, but you can do those if you’re feeling like a special snowflake. as for materials choice selection, most people can get away with just using animal materials (incisium/ironfur/guard fur) and metallurgy for steel or messing weapons. scales specialize and improve specific weapons like daggers and swords, but it is not mandatory. 70 skills - weapons made with 100 crafting and material lore skills have maximum durability. you can lower the skills/material lores down to 70 to maintain the same effectiveness of the weapon (i.e. the same slash/pierce/blunt stat) but at the cost of durability. this is only recommended if you offset the lowered skill with a trinket that bridges that gap. weapon durability is simply too important to cut corners. weapons lose effectiveness at 20% durability. if a weapon has 100 durability, it maintains usefulness from 100 durability down to 20. after it reaches the threshold of 20%, it loses a significant amount of damage. it is important to have 100 skill and 100 material lore. adamant tipped engravers are rare drops which allow for a “legendary” quality item to be crafted with 100 weaponcrafting skills and 100 material lore skills. this state adds a unique weapon engraving as well as a small boost to durability. from an economics standpoint this is wasteful. save these for flex or siege fights. here is a general list of weaponcrafting materials, their general uses, and a generalized rating. this is subject to change with balance patches and choose weapon head. add core material - bones, metals, certain minerals, wood add grip material - cloth, fur, scales add head material - bones, metals, certain minerals core materials are what the hilt/shaft is made of. this has a modest impact on strength requirement and weight and minimal impact on damage. grip material mostly impacts durability with a minor effect on weight/str requirement. can impact weakspot. head material has significant impacts to damage, strength requirement, and weight. choose wisely. choosing the head and handle type is a key defining feature of a weapon. blocks.html:
Naturist Satchels are world pickables which are (generally) inside of, or adjacent to locations relevant to a creature. Oftentimes they are within the spawn. These drop beastmastery books that are specific to the spawn. This section is not all inclusive, meaning you can possibly find specific books in locations other than what is listed here.

Satchels more-often-than-not drop "ruined books". These are vendor trash and serve no purpose other than being a failed roll. The chance at getting an actual mastery book is relatively low. Other times these satchels will contain animal zoology lore books, which will give an idea of what mastery book might be inside. For example, the Mountain Spider mastery book is obtained from a satchel that also drops Arachnid lore.

guides.title: Bosses
guides.summary: Prepare for major encounters with locations, group-size guidance, important mechanics, notable drops, and common risks.

blocks.html:
Bosses are challenges which offer unique rewards. Often contested, these are one of the primary drivers of activity within the game. This section will go over bosses, their locations, general strategies to fight them, and the unique rewards they offer.

Alchemist Bowman - Found in camps around the world. Drops alchemy mats and lesser healing potions on death. This is a simple DPS race. Uses a ranged attack, so be careful not to get pulled into extra enemies. Can be solo'd.

Bandit Leader - Found in sewers and certain world camps. This boss is a super bandit, but has no unique mechanics. Has a chance of dropping black or kallard capes, depending on the spawn. Can be solo'd.

Clothos Maiden Queen - Found in clothos caves. There are 2 on the continent of myrland, both in the north. Drops carcass which is useful for alchemy. Butchers into blood silk. Small chance at dropping oghmium trinkets. Spawns red and green eggs - green eggs MUST die or they spawn spiderlings. Red eggs must be avoided or they do lots of damage when they explode. Bring 6+ people. This is basically a DPS race with the chance at having spiderlings spawn and snowball.

Descensus High Priest - Found in the Tower of Descensus (commonly referred to as Necro dungeon). This is one of the most contested, but also most profitable bosses in game. Guaranteed to drop necromancy scrolls. Has a decent chance at dropping oghmium trinkets in the chest. Bring 2+ people if you are familiar with the fight, or 7+ if you are not used to it. This boss instantly kills one target and can turn them into a tupilak. Otherwise it is a DPS race fight where he occaisionally goes into stasis and you must kill undead to prevent him from healing.

Drug Den Leader - Found in the upper portion of Morin Khur sewers. Has a chance at dropping rare vials. Simple DPS race. Can be solo'd.

blocks.html:
Elder Sator - Found in the Sator Temple. Drops rare gems as well as skadite trinkets. Can be solo'd, but The recommended approach is to 2 plus because you cannot parry it.

Gravekeeper - Found in the bottom of the Fabernum tower. Drops lexicons of death, which are a unique cosmetic spellbook which may have utility in the future. Cycles between an AOE attack, summon zombies, and corrupt. Can easily be done with a pet and healing, or by kiting it with ranged attacks. This is easiest solo due to the AOE attacks.

Illusionist - Found in the base of the Tindrem sewers. Has a unique mirror image spell, but is an easy kill with proper parrying. Drops the scribing book. Can be solo'd.

Nitre Queen - Found in Nitre caves. Drops an egg which is traded for the Ranger Armor crafting book. Also gives ironsilk, heavy carapace, and a good chance at dropping oghmium trinkets. Spawns spiderlings occaisionally, otherwise this is a DPS race. Bring 8+ until your group is comfortable fighting it.

Minotaur King - Found at the end of the Minotaur dungeon. Has 2 stages, an enrage phase where it heals when it takes damage, and a stun phase. DPS must ONLY be done on the stun phase. Otherwise it is a DPS race. Recommend bringing shields and blocking up whenever it is in the enrage phase. Bring 15+ until you are familiar with the mechanics. Drops the minotaur king axe which trades for the Draconigenica armor book at Tindrem. Also potentially drops rare spiritism scrolls for portals.

Risar Chieftan - Found at the base of the Risar Dungeon in Gual Kor. Has a very small chance to drop a Draconigenica cape, which is the widest and best cape for animation hiding. This is a dps race. Can be solo'd by expert players, but generally 4+ is more managable.

blocks.html:
Sator Vessel - Found at the end of the Sator Temple. Spawns orbs which must be avoided but can be killed with magic. If you take too long to kill the boss, the floor fills with poison and you have to jump on the braziers. Drops rare spiritism scrolls needed for portals.

Slum Gang Leader - Found in the slums of the Morin Khur sewers. Drops the skimming book rarely. This is a simple DPS race.

Sewer King - Found in the base of the fabernum sewers. Can drop the scribing book. This is a DPS race which also spawns small landmines that you must avoid.

Troll (Forest/Jungle/Snow) - Found in various spawns around the world. Butchers into ironfur, and has a chance at gold trinkets. Forest trolls have a ranged boulder AOE attack. Jungle have an AOE poison attack which must be purified. Snow have an AOE frost breath attack which is magic damage. Best done with a pet such as a living snapping turtle or risen celaeno with 2+ healers. Obese mages can solo with perfect play. Position your pet between you and the troll so that it can maintain aggro. Can be done with 3 people with a strong melee hitting it and 2 healers- recommend good armor and health food!

Tribe Rat Chieftan - Found in the rat city within the Morin Khur sewers. Can drop the ranger cape, which is forest green. The carcass is useful for ressurecting risen tribe rat chieftans. This fight is a DPS race but you must parry earlier than you expect or his attacks will get through.

Ultimeki - Found in the Ultimeki/Greater Kimuru cave in the north center part of the map. Drops the rare Red Thunderegg which is used to get the Oghmium lore book. This is also the most powerful ritual gem. Also drops Kimurite, which extracts into a ton of great materials. Spawns rock monsters. Bring blunt damage and lots of healing as this is a long fight.

found in camps around the world. drops alchemy mats and lesser healing potions on death. this is a simple dps race. uses a ranged attack, so be careful not to get pulled into extra enemies. can be solo'd. bandit leader - found in sewers and certain world camps. this boss is a super bandit, but has no unique mechanics. has a chance of dropping black or kallard capes, depending on the spawn. can be solo'd. clothos maiden queen - found in clothos caves. there are 2 on the continent of myrland, both in the north. drops carcass which is useful for alchemy. butchers into blood silk. small chance at dropping oghmium trinkets. spawns red and green eggs - green eggs must die or they spawn spiderlings. red eggs must be avoided or they do lots of damage when they explode. bring 6+ people. this is basically a dps race with the chance at having spiderlings spawn and snowball. descensus high priest - found in the tower of descensus (commonly referred to as necro dungeon). this is one of the most contested, but also most profitable bosses in game. guaranteed to drop necromancy scrolls. has a decent chance at dropping oghmium trinkets in the chest. bring 2+ people if you are familiar with the fight, or 7+ if you are not used to it. this boss instantly kills one target and can turn them into a tupilak. otherwise it is a dps race fight where he occaisionally goes into stasis and you must kill undead to prevent him from healing. drug den leader - guides.summary: Understand house types, tiers, construction, upkeep, access, storage, workbenches, defenses, and upgrade planning.

blocks.html:
Introduction to Housing

Understand house types, tiers, construction, upkeep, access, storage, workbenches, defenses, and upgrade planning.

House Types and Sizes

There are currently 3 types of houses and 1 type of keep. Each house type and even the keep can be upgraded from between Tier 1 to tier 3, with increasing costs associated with upgrading. These are all in a “Tindremic” style of architecture. Starvault has stated that they do intend to release further types of housing that are relevant to different clades. This photo shows the different tiers and styles of house:

Each house type and even the keep can be upgraded from between Tier 1 to tier 3, with increasing costs associated with upgrading. These are all in a “Tindremic” style of architecture. blocks.html:
The reason for upgrading a house is straightforward: bigger houses have more internal space, can house more items, and they are more resistant to sieges. The downside is they cost more and take up more space. In most situations, it’s best to simply upgrade all housing to T3. Keeps, while technically a type of house, have extra mechanics tacked on.

blocks.html:
Legacy equerries can be placed in ALL houses. Legacy priests can only be added to strongholds and keeps.

Please note that the T2 keep information is projected and possibly inaccurate. Most keeps are established already and there are no current T2 keeps in game to verify the data against. The T3 keep information is accurate and the resource amount is a total. Tier 2 keep details remain provisional until the owner tab, upkeep tab, equerry, and priest options can be verified.

To estimate how many boulders it takes to destroy a building, you must know its defenses. Manganons have 74 shots before breaking and do 15k damage per shot to a house with 80% base defense + 0% extra defense. Take the current HP of the structure and divide by 15,000. So a T1 house with 3m HP takes 200 boulders to destroy, or 3 manganons total. A T3 keep with 0% defense takes 1667 boulders, or 23 manganons. Adding extra defenses can drastically increase the boulder count needed, so it is recommended to strip enemies of storehouses and supply towers before sieging.

blocks.html:
Mechanics

Placing a house is simple but requires some finesse. Go to a House Vendor found in major AI towns and purchase a deed. Right click the deed to enter building mode. You will see a house outline that is red/green. Find the spot you want and spin, raise, lower, and pray to whatever god you worship that it turns green. Once placed, add some taxes to the house via the owner placard at the front door, and add building materials. Use pickaxes to then build the structure. The engineering and advanced engineering skills increase the build rate. Once the building is fully built it is fully usable and decorations can be placed.

Keeps can only be purchased from the Keep Vendor in Tindrem or Morin Khur. They can also only be placed on 16 different predetermined locations around Myrland. They also have different mechanics which are related to TC which are out of the scope of this guide.

All stone structures come with an inherent 80% defense. Boulders which do 50k damage flat, only hit for 15k on all stone buildings before other reductions. Adding a claiming stone to a house plus having supply towers capture further increases the defense of the house. Building near a storehouse also increases the defense by an additional 15%. Players can go over 100% defense to make buildings invulnerable.

Housing doors are destroyable. Their defense is proportional to the HP of the structure, i.e. if a building has 50% HP, the doors defenses are reduced to 50%. That enables siegers to break in to kill builders.

Deconstructing a house to clear the land can be done through the ownership placard. This is not an immediate effect and can be canceled. No materials or deeds are refunded for this. It is NOT possible to upgrade from a Small to a Medium house. This requires either demolishing or trading away the house and placing a new Medium in a location where it fits.

blocks.html:
Decorations and Workbenches

There are many items which increase the utility of housing. These can give storage options, act as barriers, or they can be used for crafting. It is common to see houses with a maze of walls and obstacles to thwart or even trap intruders. Some even use skinny walls to make it so only Alvarin-sized characters can enter- effectively totally preventing Thursars or other large characters from entering. The layout of a house and how it interacts with gameplay is up to your imagination and creativity. Note that many decorations stack in interesting ways. Take for example this cluster which has every available crafting workbench in it:

blocks.html:
Engineering and Housing

Engineering is a skill which modifies the build rate of housing. The base rate of building is 350hp per tick with zero engineering. Each point of engineering and advanced engineering adds 2% extra, or 7hp per tick. As a result, with 100 engineering + 100 advanced engineering, you're looking at a total of 1,750 per tick. Note that repairing does not gain this benefit, only building new.

One good strategy for ALL characters is to simply have engineering unlocked, but no skill points added. With +10 attribute bonus, this comes out to and extra 70hp per tick, for a total of 420hp per tick. Another good threshold is 50 engineering with advanced engineering simply unlocked. This doubles the building rate plus adds a little extra depending on the bonus of the advanced engineering skill.

blocks.html: Take this image for example. The example has ample stone and maximum metal, but only 662.37/1200.00kg of wood. Divide the amount of resources by the total, and the result shows that 55% of the required wood is present. This being the lowest amount means the house can be built to only 55% - or ~3,850,000hp. At 100% wood, stone would become the limiting material.

guides.title: Invasions
guides.summary: Follow invasion events from scouting and spread to objectives, enemies, camps, trophies, rewards, and regional consequences.

blocks.html:
# Introduction

Follow invasion events from scouting and spread to objectives, enemies, camps, trophies, rewards, and regional consequences.

The current invasion system is centered around “Tagmatons”, which are an insectoid race which causes widespread devastation by consuming everything in their path. Historically, they caused the last major die-off of humans! You can read more about the last global massacre called the “Irruption” here: https://www.mortalonline2.com/a-new-dawn/. This event killed off the majority of surface dwelling life. Eventually the Tagmatons went dormant… until recently. Whether their return will result in another apocalypse is yet to be seen.

Invasions as a system are not explicitly tied to tagmatons. Indeed there have been forms of invasions in the history of Mortal Online as a franchise. Notably, Risars used to establish base camps around Myrland in Mortal Online 1. Consider the overarching invasion system as a foundation that can be expanded upon in the future with other types of foes. For now, this guide will strictly cover this system from the perspective of tagmatons only.

blocks.html:
# General Mechanics

Tagmatons have nested in the jungle in giant subterranean hives. These underground burrows are the source of all of the swarm. These bastions send out drones to various parts of the world. When the drone finds a suitable location to infest, it calls forth a “disgorger” to begin spewing out its insect brethren. Drones are the primary scouting unit which causes invasions to happen in other parts of the map. These invasions can spread far, and the patrols from them can even attack cities.

Hivebreakers are the Humanoid NPC faction which seeks to destroy the tagmaton threat. These groups (lore-wise) attack and kill tagmatons and break up their infestation. In-game, they are a series of vendors where tagmaton trophies can be exchanged for special rewards. The hivebreakers congregate in camps around the world.

Here is a map of all hives as well as all hivebreaker camps:

# Tagmaton Types

There are 11 different tagmaton variants. Each serves a role within their brood- and each poses a different threat to their prey. This section will describe each, and gives strategies for combatting them.
blocks.text: # Tagmaton Types There are 11 different tagmaton variants. Each serves a role within their brood- and each poses a different threat to their prey. This section will describe each, and gives strategies for combatting them.

blocks.html:
Borer

The borer is a burrowing assassin that uses a ranged acid spit to kill its foes. Be careful as several of these can drop a player very quickly. They go underground to hide more often than they are surfaced. The strategy for killing them is to allow them to unburrow, hit them in the head with arrows or a melee weapon, and heal up while it is preparing for its next attack. Avoid fighting multiple of these at the same time. Miasma also works to damage them while they are burrowed.

Broodmother

The broodmother is the strongest of the swarm. It has 3 distinct attacks - a ranged acid spray that deals heavy damage, a very long-ranged webpull which forces a dismount, and an instant kill melee attack that occurs at the end of the webpull if the target is within range. When the broodmother drops to low HP, it summons a massive gorger to spray acid over a very large area. The general strategy for most broodmother fights is to use a weakspot mounted archer and keep it at max distance. Go for headshots and remount anytime it webpulls you. Keep your distance and you just need time to win it.

Mages cannot effectively fight these, and must remain in a support role.

Patrons have access to the broodmother soloing video guide found here: https://discordapp.com/channels/1108799705284096040/1192430123656429568/1403901382934921359

blocks.html:
Bulwark

The bulwark is an indirect artillery bug, and one of the strongest opponents in the game. It is slow moving, and charges up with bioluminescence when it is prepared to strike. The artillery strike can one-shotting entire groups without any chance at survival.

The primary counter to bulwarks is using a weakspot mounted archer at a very long distance. Many times the bulwark will get stuck on a wall, tree, or building, and its artillery strike fails to launch. At this point in time it can be shot freely until death. When it dies, it does MASSIVE aoe damage in a huge radius, so run away while it is dying. The damage output is exceptionally high.

The “legit” way to do these is a thursar with anti-magic adamant and the “Ward” combat ability to tank the damage. This is incredibly risky and time consuming. It is much easier to just bow it from a distance.

Mages do very little magic damage for this and are thus relegated to a support role when fighting these.

Burster

Banelings. These are suicide bombers with two variants - one which is an acid attack, and the other which is explosive. Both do a ton of damage in a very large radius. Kill these at a range with arrows, or kill them up close and be sure to RUN before they explode. Ember/hailstone is viable versus these.

Disgorger

The “Disgorger” is a type of living tagmaton vessel- similar to a Nydus Worm from the Starcraft series. It burrows through the ground and acts as a tunneling drop ship which can deposit swarms of tagmatons. Functionally the act as passive spawners on the ground. To kill them, wait for them to spawn a burster npc. Then kill the burster while lining the burster up with the disgorger. This causes the burster to enter the disgorger and explode, dealing damage. With enough bursters, the disgorger dies and the tagmaton invasion is culled.

Bursters are only found at the hives/disgorgers.

blocks.html:
Drone

Drones are a quasi-caster type which have a disgorger-summoning attack. These are mostly harmless unless they are given space to cast. The strategy to kill these is rush them and chop them down. They are only a threat when they free cast.

Mage scan solo these by using ember.

Harbinger

The harbinger can be seen as a mini-broodmother. It has a web-pull attack and strong melee capabilities. It is also rather tanky. These are extremely dangerous when in a big group of tagmatons as they can chain stun single targets. The most reliable way to approach these is to use a weakspot mounted archer after isolating them from the group. When the webpull ability hits, simply remount and continue shooting. Repeat this process until they are dead.

Mages are not particularly good at fighting these unless as a support role in a group.

Lancer

The lancer is a dashing skirmish unit. It is a high threat for several reasons- it actively avoids melee, it does high burst damage, and its attack is an AOE. Multiple of these can shred small groups very quickly. They are even decently strong versus mounted players if the mounted player fails to dodge. Like with most tagmatons, a weakspot mounted archer is the correct tool to use against these. The strategy when fighting these is to wait for it to rear up, and then move left/right perpendicular against it. It can then be attacked or shot.

Mages can solo these. It is best to use ember/hailstone after dodging the attack. Firewall is not effective versus these.

Scrambler

Scramblers are weak flying units that attack in large swarms. They die instantly to a single point of damage, but they can easily overwhelm players if they bunch up in swarms of 10+. The most reliable way to fight these is snipe them one by one. Spurts, arrows, and other aoe kills them very quickly en masse.

Scramblers are only found at hives/disgorgers.

blocks.html:
Slayer

The slayer is the foot soldier of the tagmaton armies. These have high armor, good HP, and can be very fast. They also have an acid spit attack when they cannot reach their target quickly enough. These are best killed by a weakspot mounted archer, but they can be killed in many other ways. Melee will struggle but it is doable with a thursar. Mage is doable with long range ember/hailstone.

Wriggler

The wriggler is not a world spawn, but they rather hatch from tagmaton eggs that players place. These start at level 1, and must be leveled to level 100. When they hit level 100 they evolve into another tagmaton variant, seemingly at random. Developers have indicated that there is a way to help influence what exactly these evolve into, but this is undiscovered at this time.

blocks.html:
# Rewards

Tagmaton invasions give many different unique rewards. Some of these are extremely powerful and potentially gamebreaking. This section will list the various rewards, and how to obtain them.

Huskbreaker Rewards

The Huskbreakers are a faction of anti-tagmaton hunters which seek to eradicate the insect menace. Kill tagmatons and bringing their trophies to these vendors to exchange for unique rewards ranging from new capes, house decorations, as well as TC structures.

There are 2 unique huskbreaker vendors - the Wardaki Researcher, and the Hivebreaker Artisan. These trophies can be exchanged for hivebreaker marks, or traded directly to the Wardaki Researcher. Note the researcher does NOT accept marks.

SEE IMAGES AT BOTTOM OF GUIDE

blocks.html:
Tagmaton Eggs and the Fallowborn

Tagmaton queens drop a “Tagmaton Brood Egg” on death. This item can be placed on the ground to hatch a “tagmaton wriggler”. This wriggler is a small defenseless pet which behaves like all other non-combat pets. Once the wriggler is leveled to level 100, it will evolve into a random grown “fallowborn” tagmaton. The pool of tagmatons these can grow to is every single one with the exception of the disgorger. Developers have hinted at some influencing factor to guide what the egg evolves into, but that is not publicly discovered yet.
