blocks.html:
There are 3 very powerful tagmaton pets of note -

The Borer. While it loses its ability to burrow, it makes up for that with becoming a rideable mount with a max movement speed of 1192, which makes it on-par with the other interceptor mounts like terror birds and panthers. It also has exceptionally turn radius, and built-in armor.

The Bulwark. Acts as an artillery piece and looks to be extremely potent for siege and outpost fights. Has the potential to one shot entire sections of enemies. Its ranged attack has a fast cooldown, too. Beware if you see an enemy group with one.

The Broodmother. This pet retains all of its abilities. While it lacks strong combat potency, the utility in this pet lies within its ability to stun enemies for several seconds while dragging them in from a range. Should an enemy be dragged in at close range, the instant-mercy ability triggers. This will kill any player in the game, no matter what they are wearing. It should be noted that while the broodmother retains the ranged stun ability, the harbinger variant does not.

blocks.html:
Huskweave

Tagmatons can be butchered for a unique new material known as huskweave. This potent resource is used in armorcrafting and weaponcrafting. It is very similar in ironfur stats (slightly less blunt for more pierce), with the exception that it is lighter! It is equivalent to guard fur in weight. This is considered best-in-slot for fighters and paladins.

blocks.html:
# Conclusion

This dynamic world event has undoubtedly added a rewarding challenge for players, which gives access to many new powerful tools. From new pets to better weapon schematics to upgraded armor backing, the tagmaton invasions are a fruitful addition to the game. Learning to conquer it gives an advantage over others.

Best of luck fighting the swarm.

Mini-Invasions / Incursions

These waves come in 3 quantities - solos, small groups, and large groups. Large groups are announced via server message and have 2x the amount of NPCs as small groups. These invasions will typically spawn near POIs, but this is not a hard rule.

retains the ranged stun ability, the harbinger variant does not. huskweave tagmatons can be butchered for a unique new material known as huskweave. this potent resource is used in armorcrafting and weaponcrafting. it is very similar in ironfur stats (slightly less blunt for more pierce), with the exception that it is lighter! it is equivalent to guard fur in weight. this is considered best-in-slot for fighters and paladins. huskweave lore is a book-only skill. players must obtain 10s worth of tagmaton trophies and buy the lore from the huskbreaker camps before they can extract this resource. in addition to huskweave, most tagmaton variants will drop crepite, dense crepite, and pansar carapace. here is a butchery chart of all tagmatons: # conclusion this dynamic world event has undoubtedly added a rewarding challenge for players, which gives access to many new powerful tools. from new pets to better weapon schematics to upgraded armor backing, the tagmaton invasions are a fruitful addition to the game. learning to conquer it gives an advantage over others. best of luck fighting the swarm. mini-invasions / incursions all humanoid invasions have a high chance of dropping trinkets, radiant fragments, and the bosses of the waves will generally drop essence orbs. these waves come in 3 quantities - solos, small groups, and large groups. large groups are announced via server message and have 2x the amount of npcs as small groups. these invasions will typically spawn near pois, but this is not a hard rule. here are a list of each invasion and their rewards: updated Location: Fabernum west bank on the wall.

Title: Seeking Mercenaries to Kill Rats!

Text: I cannot offer coin, as my pockets are tied up in other, more important matters.

But what I can offer you is whatever you may loot from the ruins these rats have taken up residence in. I tried to live with them, I promise on my mother's grave that I did. I gave them their space, I sought no quarrel with them. And yet, they have begun to raid my storage shed!

I realize I hadn't accounted for the fact that they have thumbs, so I did what anyone reasonably would do and hired a locksmith to seal the food shed.

So what did they do? Why, they dug right beneath the shed!

My requirement is that you are gifted in a martial art or offensive magics. I will not pay anyone to collect your body if you're foolish enough to fight them without proper training and equipment!

They can be found in the lesser used mountain road to the west of Fabernum, in the destroyed fort overlooking the tower below.

Location: Outside Pathfinder Shinarian Labrynth Boss Room:

Title: None

Text: The ruins are even more magnificent than I had anticipated. Every step deeper into these ancient hallways reveals more about our history. Their craftsmanship is unparalleled; the stonework, the inscriptions, and the very air seem to hum with latent power.

My followers and I have uncovered numerous artifacts, each more intriguing than the last. There is a resonance here, a sense of purpose that permeates these walls. I can feel it in my bones. The Shinarians were more than just builders-- they were visionaries, and their secrets lie just beyond our grasp.

The door sealed behind us, and I take that as a sign that we are on the right path. This place has been untouched for centuries, waiting for someone with the will and wisdom to unlock its mysteries.

I am here now.

A few of the others have been restless, but I assure them that our perserverance will be rewarded. The usual promises of filled pockets once we return home are satisfying them at least for now.

There is much to study, and time is a luxury we must afford ourselves. I only hope those on the surface can remain patient and keep their focus on the mission at hand.

These ruins speak to me. They tell of a civilization that harnessed power beyond our understanding. I must learn their secrets. It is my duty, my destiny, to uncover the truth and to wield the knowledge they left behind.

Location: Recreant mini boss topside of labs dungeon, bottom key part

Title: none

Text: The situation has spiraled out of control.

The pathfinder led the rest below, leaving us to fend for ourselves out here. If you ask me, the conflict was unavoidable.

Now, the key is broken, and so is our group

I hold one of the pieces, a burden i never asked for. The other two both seek to restore the key but i think for vastly different reasons. One wants to free our leader, blinded by loyalty. The other loud one just seeks power for themself even if they deny it

Me? I just want to survive. I fear what lies below and i fear what our leader might do if they are freed once they see what happened.

The Pathfinder's wrath is not something I wish to face. I've seen what they are capable of, and its enough to make any sane person hesitate.

The others view me as a coward, but they dont understand the weight of my decision. I refuse to be dragged into their power struggle. I will hide my piece of the key and avoid their conflict. Let them tear each other part if they must

All i want is to escape this cursed ruin and return home. But for now, i must bide my time and stay out of their way

The key remains divided and so does our fate.

Location: Sidonian loyalist, middle key part

Title: none

Text: The situation here grows more dire by the hour. The fight that erupted after the pathfinder descended below has left us in a pitiful state. The key, our only means of reopening the door, now lies broken into three pieces, each held by a fool who thinks their way is best

Its infuriating to see grown warriors acting like children, squabbling over pieces of metal while our leader remains trappe below. Their cowardice and ambition alike have blinded them to our true purpose

I remain steadfast in my loyalty to the pathfinder. We must reunite the key and free our leader. The knowledge and treasures they must have uncovered below are too valuable to be lost to petty infighting.

I will continue to watch and wait for an opportunity to reclaim the pieces and restore our mission. The others may have forgotten their purpose but i have not. Our leader needs us and i will see this through, no matter the cost

Title: Dawa,

Text:

Togtuun has given me enough trouble to last three lifetimes, so this will be the last time I trade my family’s pillows and fabrics.

I’ve sworn it many times, but I am serious about this one. I’m not going back in there again.

I can’t help but feel the way I do, my father died in that place. His body was never even brought to us to be given to the sky.

Every time he sees me, Togtuun pesters me. Calls me "little girl" when I am older than he is! I try to measure the disrespect he is willing to place on my name, and yet it grows.

He disrespects my father and calls him an addict. My father was no addict, he was merely in unimaginable pain.

I pray Togtuun finds himself laying on one of those mats one day.

You may tell him I said that.

– Saikhan

Location: Morin Khur (MK) Sewers, inside the Alchemy/Necromancy lab

Title: Observations, Week Two

Text:

Many who are curious about the vast darkness that exists below us know of the lichen-like growths that grow from the walls of many caverns. To our people, it is known as “Tark’s Breath”, as it seems highly averse to the sun’s light, and yet where the growths are found the air remains sweet and breathable.

Most kinds are indistinguishable from plain gray and brown granum, but I have heard from a Sheevra that occasionally they are different colors.

It would seem deep fungi grow best in areas of particularly thick growths of Tark’s Breath. It is not exactly a common thing to find on the surface, and as such, I have had much difficulty growing full caps from the spores that have recently been brought to me.

The glowing worms of the deep seem to match the glow of the mushrooms presented to them. I do not know if this is because they eat it, or if they can identify the correct color to hide from predators.

Several have spun cocoons, which I did not expect. I wonder what they will become with time?

Title: None

Text:

Like many of the bodies I receive, these two are gravely thin.

I have yet to perfect these particular rituals. Ana’dil is not a tongue familiar to me, and I have neither Sarducaans nor Bediai to help me translate.

If I am performing the rituals correctly, key parts of it remain incomplete.

I have heard legends of Kebechet cultists roaming the sands of Sarducaa, existing as impossible-to-track mobile husks who have truly bested death and even kept some semblance of their wits about them.

If I were to find an immortal, surely it would be a Sarducaan.

I wonder often what state of a being that is. Absolutely no depiction of immortality attained through necromancy is ever described as painless or graceful.

Surely there is some truth to that, and if they truly do exist and hide so thoroughly… perhaps it is for a reason?

The fight that followed was inevitable. In the chaos, the damn key shattered into three pieces, each claimed by those who see a different path going forward. That blind loyalist clings to the past, while the other coward hides

I will gather those who share my vision. We will restoer the key not to free the pathfinder but to face them and make them see the error of their ways.

If they refuse we will do what must be done

Location: Book found along the northwest wall of the first chamber in the Ignis Cavern.

Title: The Crystal Cave By Elie Amatas

Text: Talusain legend tells of a cavern in the mountains where beings were born from clusters of rock and crystal, living simple existences separate from the complex lives of Humans and Oghmir.

Even plants took easily to the place, witnessed in bundles of ferns and grass on the floors and walls among the glittering gems and oddly-patterned stones.

One summer day smoke billowed from the cave, creating a gloom in the skies for weeks that made bears slumber as if it was winter and nightsnatchers crawl from their dens during the day.

It is said the first one to brave the cave and set foot inside only shortly after it settled was a Huergar concerned about the elementals within.

Her grandmother had told her of a time when the place only sang with the songs of crystal, a chime that never seemed to cease so much as shift its pitch up and down—but never having a beginning or reaching an end.

She told her of impossibly sharp Crystal Things that looked like glass, that knew not the fragility of beings made of skin and blood. Whether through maliciousness, ignorant playfulness, or immoral curiosity—they would shred any being made of flesh into ribbons. The cavern wasn't safe then, but the thunder eggs were plentiful, and so many were lost trying to retrieve them.

Through her, she had heard other tales.

Her grandmother personally attested to the existence of a pleasant Dirt-Clod Thing that ambled about inoffensively and without danger. She described to her how it would gather mounds of dirt like a child pulling a pile of sand or snow onto themselves when trying to cover their torso, but doing so made itself larger and larger over the years it was observed.

She even spoke of a Thing that had come from an underground pond of water. It glistened magnificently in the combination of torchlight and crystal before it sank back in, completely disappearing from sight when fully submerged.

The crystal cave painted to her by her grandmother in tales was a place of wonder, danger, and mystery; but she grandmother had not mentioned the Thing of rock and fire that half-slithered from a pool of magma, melting the half-submerged body of the Kimurus she had come to cherish.

There was now heat in the crystal cave.

title: CITIZENS OF MORIN KHUR

Text: For several weeks there has been an increase in the activity of tribe rats.

Although the guard has dealt with the ones we have found we advise caution in the future in areas that are dark and unfrequented, such as:

Long-abandoned homes in the wilderness or on abandoned streets that border the mountains

Unfrequented caves and mines, both natural and man-made

If you sight a tribe rat, do not attempt to fight it alone. Where the is one, there will likely be many more.

Instead, report your findings to a guard.

As always, please share and spread this information. Those who cannot read must also be informed of this threat.

You speak half as much like them and share every drop of their lust to stamp your feet for fathomed slights.

Location: Top of the Western Lighthouse villa on "Wolf Island" along the coast southwest of Tindrem.

Title: N/A

Text: It looks as if I must be my own rescue.

I cannot imagine what possessed the pirates to use their catapults to attack our lighthouse. What desperation may have driven them to such a strange attack, so close to the city?

By the will of the gods, lightning struck their vessel, catching their sails alight and smiting several on board immediately. The mast shivered, striking some of them with debris as well. They retreated further down the coast, surely to survey and return later.

Most of the population from the village further up the road fled. Only a few remained, last I was there. They want to stay and fight. I think it foolish, but I am the one hiding in the ruined lighthouse, perhaps I know little of bravery. I find myself huddled next to a chest of my things that I dragged up the broken staircase.

I know I will have to leave it behind, I just hope those bastards don't find it first.

Title: N/A

Text: The more time I spend here, the more I believe this was the right choice.

It is a small village, and not much happens here. Things are logical, predictable, regular, and boring. That is a blessing in times like these, and I am thankful for it every day.

At one point in my life I had believed it better to perhaps search for an isolated settlement of my people.

I wished to chase the exciting notion that both sides of the Oghmir clade could reclaim some of the ruins in the mountains and make them into a proper settlement. A true home, where we can live true to our customs without being pestered about our ways of life.

But there is comfort in familiarity and, with risk of sounding stereotypical, I simply do not enjoy change.

I may be an Oghmir, but I am also a Fabernumite, and the humans who share this place with us are kind enough. This is far away enough from the noise of the city, and it will do for now.

Title: N/A

Text: How I yearn for the company of scholars and intellectuals.

Instead, I am trapped here, in this town where few understand my desires and interests. Father would rather have me work my fingers to the bone in a mine shaft as he does, and his father did, and his father's father's father did.

Does he not see that I have no interest in these affairs? I do not wish to be a miner, or a woodcutter, or a huntsman, or a smith. I want to be an alchemist! A scholar! A man of knowledge!

Mother has discussed with him about sending me to Tindrem for a year to stay with my uncle Faustus, but I know that I am doomed to stay here.

Text: Dear Tupor,

The first time I saw you fight in the arena, you immediately caught my eye. I leaned over to my friend who asked me who the tall and handsome one is, and she said you were brought from the outskirts of Meduli as a bandit... Is that correct?

Well, I can tell, even from afar, that you are simply misunderstood, likely pushed into the circumstances you found yourself in without much choice.

I have many suitors, my mother says it is because of my looks, but they do not see who I truly am. But I know in my heart that you and I are kindred spirits, and that you would understand me and cherish me as I want to be cherished. During your next match, I will be wearing a bright red stola parted down to my waist, and I will be waving a red fan of the same color.

Look for me Tupor, I will be there!

Title: The Nameless Statues of Tindrem By Tectio da Levita

Text (Pt. 1): One who spends any amount of time int he marvelous city of Tindrem cannot escape the brilliance of figures made of marble. Tragically, some of these figures lack plaques to denote who or what they are meant to commemorate. As one would expect of such inventive and passionate people, the citizens of Tindrem have given each a story.

Some are well-regarded enough to boast multiple!

The Sage

The statue commonly known as The Sage is rumored to be the statue of a great thinker of the Clerus Magica, an academy that sank into the sea only a few short generations ago.

While few Tindremenes are alive today to have experienced the academy in its glory, the organization itself and its great thinkers and inventors glitter brightly among the many stars that light the sky of Tindrem's past.

Another rumor surrounding The Sage is that he was a great scholar and philosopher, who brought knowledge to the people of Tindrem from far-away lands. Perhaps an ancient Provinciale, bringing his most valuable information to the capital?

Could he have been from the ruined city of Gabaria, now known as Gaul'kor?

Some around Tindrem believe so!

The tantalizing promise of knowledge from lands far and wide have long captured imaginations of our people, proof of our adoration for knowledge, exploration, and ambition.

Title: The Nameless Statues of Tindrem By Tectio da Levita

Text (Pt. 2):

The Grieving Woman

Despite lacking a name on her statues, what is known about her would suggest that she was born in Fabernum. It is uncertain how her life took her to the fortified island between Myrland and Sarducaa, but most are certain that her story took her there.

In the most common retelling, an unprecedentedly large group of Nordeveldian pirates attacked the island, abandoning crudely made rats and allowing them to be whisked below Tecton's Fault. Tragically, her mother and father were slain in their bedchambers, and then the woman and her husband were brought before the pirates' leader.

Despite her pleas, her husband was beheaded, and his head was given to her after she begged the Kallard to give him back to her. It is believed that she sat with his head in a prison cell in the dungeon of the fortress for weeks before the island was retaken by the Empire.

Another entirely different story claims that she was the sister of a decapitated member of the Tricapita, cradling her brother's head in her arms one last time. Was this perhaps the result of a plot for power all along and she merely kissed her brother's forehead to sway those into believing her innocent, or was she truly grieving?

Some even go so far as to say she was the mistress of a decapitated emperor, which would make her perhaps the most famous, although nameless, mistress in all of Tindremic history.

All versions of the story are explicit about one thing, however: The woman believed that so long as she kept the man's head, she could hear his spirit talking to her.

Was this madness, or proof that love transcends even death?

Title: A Guide to Visiting Tindrem By Byronos Corii

Text (Pt. 1): This is the first installment of my series of books: "A Guide to Visiting Tindrem: For Provincales and Others".

If you are reading this book then you wish to be prepared to participate in the bountiful glories and opportunities that the capital of Tindremic society can offer to an outsider.

It is true what you have heard: Tindrem and her people are complex and multi-facted, as is to be expected of any highly advanced society. An outsider may feel shocked and overwhelmed, unsure how to proceed or who to trust for a helping hand. It is for these unfortunate souls I have written this book, so that it may serve as a guiding hand in an uncertain place.

Chapter 1: First Steps

It is imperative during your first few months in Tindrem to be keenly aware of your surroundings. The risk comes not from pickpockets or other petty thieves but instead may approach you in the form of liars, vagrants, and opportunists who would exploit you for all you're worth.

You may be approached by a strikingly beautiful woman with hair the color of nyx falling in perfect coils around her face dressed like a beggar in need, or you may see a pitiable old man who seems to be ignored as he lays on the side of the road in what surely are his last breaths. Both are the descriptions of individuals who have been arrested for crimes against newcomers to this grand city.

Although the city guard do what they can to round up these individuals, the greatest grandeur draws in the low lives like moths to a flame.

Title: A Guide to Visiting Tindrem By Byronos Corii

Text (Pt. 2):

To protect yourself, you should appear confident as if you know where you are going. Do not wander aimlessly staring at things the average citizen would not think to notice. Approach your destination with intent, and any who observe you will assume you have been here before. Although tempting, speaking with the guards stationed near the gate is another way to be quickly identified and tracked.

If marked by one of such individuals, they may follow you for quite some time—particularly if you seem rather wealthy or well-connected. If you are unsure if you are being followed or not, you should make nonsensical paths, such as walking in a circle around several buildings.

If the individual in question is still behind you when you complete this circle, you can assume you are being followed.

I must add that this plan is not foolproof by any means. Many pickpockets operate in small packs that may communicate your description with other members.

The most common pickpocket group tactic is where one will get in your way so you're forced to suddenly stop, and another from behind will bump into you as if it was your fault. When you check your pockets after, however, you may very well find your coin purse missing.

Be mindful of obvious distractions such as someone shouting or asking you to read a map or letter for them.

Title: The Colors of Blood by Irius Albius + Erythroheme - Red Blood

Text: In any field documenting the natural world itself, categorization is of both the utmost concern of the research to better understand the properties and behaviors of a subject and is simultaneously the vexation of any scholar who studies their subject thoroughly.

It is a simple truth that things not artificially created to be perfectly organized will never align as well as many would like to think, with perhaps the exception of mathematics.

As a sanguinist, I have seen and attempted to interpret different kinds of blood for much of my lifetime. The blood of a bovine and the blood of a human are certainly different, yet when merely observed in a glass bottle they are impossible to distinguish.

This is not the case for many creatures in the world, and I postulate that there is value in first noting the visual appeance of blood types, which often share common qualities and components based on said appearence. From there, one can then define their specific qualities and origins.

Using this method, I would propose we can categorize blood by its color; Red, Blue, Green, Purple, Clear, Yellow, and perhaps even the color Amber.

As all individuals who may read this book are almost certainly red blooded, it would be naive to assume that red blood, which is to say our own blood, would be described as anything other than "blood".

Even so, for categorical purposes, I believe it important to have a technical name, even if it is one purely used by scholars and practicioners who require discernment between different kinds of blood.

The properties of erythroheme are perhaps the best understood of all blood colors, as it is the most often encountered by us in large quantities. All creatures with a backbone, with the exception of a small number of fish, have red blood. This includes birds, reptiles, mammals, amphibians, and most fish; as well as some species of worm and leech.

Red blood has been used for millenia in medicine, cooking, ritual, and as an alchemical and spell casting reagent.

It either seems to propagate, or propagate from, the bones and other similar structures of creatures with backbones. It is observed as uniquely in some way tied to the very concept of a skeleton, though not exclusively.

While it has been postulated that red blood creates a skeleton in the creature it flows in, the existence of worms and leeches with red blood would imply that instead perhaps the skeleton which makes red blood, or makes blood red.

Location: Oghmium Lore Cave

Title: N/A

Text: I told that half-wit that there was nothing of worth down along that shore, but he will do what he wants to do. I've never shifted his mind on these things.

It looks like I was right, once again. I've found a wrecked Huergar underway by following hearsay after hearsay across the Talus. Many of the things folk told me were somewhat untrue, if not wholly wrong.

Amongst the things I've looked through here, there have been several books about "Oghmium".

Any wisdom on how to craft it is hard to find. The Huergar and Tindremenes both hide anything and everything having to do with it, so it should be able to fetch a lot of coin.

But what would make me more coin are "thunder eggs". A Tind wrote to me, hearing of my many treks across the peaks and through the grottos of the Talus as of late. He said if I can gather him many of these rocks, he will be able to make me rich.

Now all I must do is find some, or one who knows where to get some.

Location: Pillaged Dire Wolf Village POI southwest of "Wolf Island"

Title: N/A

Text: Day 28

We hear the howling of wolves every night. The attacks are becoming more frequent.

I've told the men to travel in groups of two or larger when leaving the camps.

Day 29

We finally killed one of the things, Gorm managed to catch it in the neck with a pickaxe.

He pointed out that it had a closed stitch on its leg. Is it a pack of loose wolves someone was trying to tame doing this?

Day 30

Most of the others have already left, we're considering abandoning this place and doing the same.

I would rather face the wrath of an upset nobilita than whoever may be lurking in those trees and their attack dogs.

Location: Morin Khur north broker building, bookshelf on the north side.

Title: The Stone Wall of Herabalter by Surentai of Morin Khur

Text (Pt. 1): This book has been approved by the Tindremic Literary Council of Morin Khur.

For as long as our people have spoken of Herabalter, the wall built by the Risar bordering the ashen land was a wooden palisade. It was a great wall made of logs, with wooden spikes at its base where the dead bodies of those slain by the Risar could be found.

Over the last century it has become a stone wall. This seems to have happened after the swarm of the terrible insects that dug through the earth and flew through the skies. Before then, any who neared this palisade would meet their death at the hands of the Risar.

It was reported some decades ago that there was a strange development in this place between Myrland and Herabalter: A stone wall was being created.

At first it was assumed this wall would be cobblestone, an extension of the rocks that surrounded the base of the wooden palisade. Over time, however, the rumors of this wall became more clear. It was an impressive structure made of great stone blocks and stone spikes that stretched towards the sky like the fangs of a serpent.

The Risar had developed the practice of building towers while none were watching. This was, and is, a great concern.

Too many think them to be simple, aggressive creatures incapable of intelligent thought and advanced planning. They are seen as bloodthirsty monsters who only wish to hunt, kill, ravage, and cause torment. A species of raiders and bandits, and little more.

This is a false belief.

We would do well to remember that the Risar are capable of speech. They have cultural practices, some not entirely like those of Humans. Their women will abandon their Thursar children in our villages and khurens while we are fast asleep, knowing they will have a better life among us than the hard life of the Risar.

Location: Morin Khur north broker building, bookshelf on the north side.

Title: The Stone Wall of Herabalter by Surentai of Morin Khur

Text (Pt. 2): It would be wise of us to consider the possibility that more is happening beyond the wall than we have historically witnessed from the Risar.

They may have built cities out of the land where volcanic pools bubble and ashes partially block the sun, turning the atmosphere a dreary shade of green.

They may have Risar kings and Risar queens who command the other Risar, instructing them to fortify the the wall to Myrland and punish those who do not fall in line.

Some would say that I am foolish and that it is only a wall and nothing more. I ask any who contain any doubt within themselves to look upon the sketches made of the structure. It is the work of sophisticated minds and it is built with undisclosed but clear intention and purpose.

We must keep a close eye on our neighbors.

Location: Morin Khur, Spiritism trader building, north bookshelf

Title: Tribes of the East by Bemius Amaterna

Text (Pt. 1): This book has been approved by the Tindremic Literary Council of Morin Khur.

Morin Khur has existed for quite some time as something of an anomaly among the Khurite people. While the tribes of the forests and steppes wander Myrland mixing their cultures and intermingling with one another, the tribes of Morin Khur and Toxai are rather stationary.

It is little wonder that both became places where nomadic tribes will also occasionally gather, considering the reliability of their presence. With settlement comes the need for farming, such as rice in Morin Khur and seaweed in Toxai. With farming, if done properly, comes excess and the ability to better store more food in case of drought, famine, or some other such disaster.

The tribes of the two cities reflect this change in culture quite naturally, reflecting those seen in many other settled societies. The people themselves still highly prize physical skills such as horse riding and swimming, but there is also value placed on adherence to laws and social order that is less "free" than those found in Khurens.

While exile remains a common punishment, imprisonment, enslavement, and fines are also popular. Executions are unique in that the Khurs are severely hesitant to spill blood on the ground.

Their methods of disposing criminals are thus rather inventive, such as rolling one up in a carpet and then having him be trampled by horses, tying one up and throwing them in a river, or locking them in a box and leaving them to be subjected to the elements.

Wrestling matches are another form of execution, where an executioner will engage in a fight with the offender. The executioner is invariably a large man, sometimes a Thursar, who is strong enough to break someone's back over their knee.

Title: Tribes of the East by Bemius Amaterna

Text (Pt. 2): Typically multiple steps are taken to ensure the executioner will win, including giving them armor while the offender fights in rags. Often the offender is purposefully paralyzed and left for dead so that a natural sky burial may take place.

This same practice is often not extended to those who are not Khurs.

But the people of Morin Khur are not only their executions, and despite their infamy they make up a rather small portion of their culture.

Angaqs here are typically not solitary members of their tribes as they often are when found riding the steppes. Though especially small tribes may have only one angaq, most have multiple who may even live in certain homes together. The unique cultural expectations of the city have even allowed for temples, where their shamans may learn, worship, and perform their rites among other like minded individuals.

It is not uncommon for a resident of Morin Khur in need of spiritual or magical assistance to visit a temple in the city.

Location: Fabernum tavern, 2nd floor, north table

Title: The Stone Folk of Fabernum by Sirio Miserenna

Text: The Stone Folk have long been a part of Fabernum's history. Before they retreated beneath the mountain, Huergar are said to have frequented the town.

It was the Huergar that the people here learned the specific methods of refining and smelting that Fabernum is now famous for.

After the Conflux, several families of Huergar decided to stay on Fabernum instead of joining their brethren in retreating to the world below.

Although outsiders who know little of the Huergar would paint them as a monolith, there are many divisions of thought and mannerisms among them even when considering the Huergar found in Fabernum in comparison to those found in Tindrem.

The Huergar in Fabernum, although they hold their own values and reside in their own community, tend to be less involved in social climbing than those in Tindrem. Many are quite content to live as the Fabernumites do, focusing on their crafts and what they can offer to the Provinces and the communities around them.

Historically, there was also a small trickle of Blainn from their settlement of Old Hyllspeia up in the Talus Mountains. Although their influence was small, it can be felt in the small injection of Nordveldian names specifically inspired by the Blainn tongue of Lisan Ki. Most, however, follow the principles of Lisan Abnu, the Huergar dialect.

Location: Vadda library, book on the northwest table

Title: N/A

Text: I was taken seven years ago by the Tindremenes as a slave.

For those seven years I worked in Meduli under a nobilita named Petrios.

He was blind.

I learned to read and write for him. I felt pity for the old man. I could have left easily. I did not.

I escaped across the plains when he died of his old age. When I returned to Vadda my tribe had long left.

I will wait here for a time.

Word of my tribe will reach Vadda soon enough. I will help the people here until then.

There is much knowledge to be found in these books.

Location: Forum Tindrem, first building south of the Arena district gate, 2nd floor

Title: Autumnal Celebrations In Tindrem

Text (Pt. 1): Autumn is a time of harvests, and we would be fools to not partake in the many gifts from the gods! Join me, Camulocus di Somniati, on a journey through the many festivals and activities you may choose to participate in during this season!

Wine Festival of Red Leaves

The Wine Festival of Red Leaves is held nearly every year, and has no specific day it is held. Instead, the people wait patiently for the leaves of the trees planted around certain vineyards to redden and become vibrant.

Tents and tables are quickly brought to the villas surrounding the vineyards, where the winemaking families traditionally host a great feast in honor of the leaves changing color. And what would a feast at a winemaker's villa be without wine?

To receive an invitation to the festivities, to be sure either extent your interest (if you happen to be a nobilita), or perhaps offer your services as an attendant of the feast if you are not. The families have plenty of slaves between them who are more than capable of handling the more arduous tasks, leaving you the lighter and more social work.

I have spoken to many who have found work at the feasts there, from courtesans, to musicians, to servers of food and pourers of wine. They are always given generous amounts of time to participate as well, so reliably that it has become tradition.

Location: Forum Tindrem, first building south of the Arena district gate, 2nd floor

Title: Autumnal Celebrations In Tindrem

Text (Pt. 2):

The Haunting of the Fields

This particular game happens at night, and can be quite thrilling!

The story behind this celebration is ancient, originating from a small farming village out in the heartlands of Tindrem. It is said that a powerful venefica from the surrounding woodlands was executed in an especially brutal manner after poisoning a well-loved man of the village. It was only after her death that it was revealed that he had rightfully earned his demise.

It is said that after her death, her spirit still roams the fields, seeking to subject any she may encounter to the same tortures she endured.

The game itself involves a woman, deemed the "venefica" of the night, who is given two chances to win.

First, she must flee those chosen to represent "villagers", who will chase her through a field with lanterns. Her goal is technically to remain hidden for as long as possible, though it is rare the venefica won't allow herself to be found.

This is because once she is caught, a small ceremony will be held where everyone will dine on malus fruit and various desserts, drinks, and sweets made from the fruit.

Once they are full and have let their meals settle, the villagers are then sent out into the fields, where the "venefica" will chase after them. If every last villager is caught before an hourglass settles and a horn is blown, another ceremony is held where the villagers ask her for their forgiveness.

Title: Autumnal Celebrations In Tindrem

Text (Pt. 3): The choice to forgive them is, of course, up to the mood of the venefica of the night. There are three accepted speeches:

One where she accepts their plea, allowing everyone to go home as they were.

The second is where she denies their plea, and the revelers who lost have the "I" of an Interfector painted on their foreheads with a pigment meant to dye their skin for several days.

The third choice is for her to choose for them to be her walking dead servants, who must not speak and obey every order she gives.

Title: Autumnal Celebrations In Tindrem

Text (Pt. 4):

The Feast of Carpo

The Feast of Carpo is a famous celebration that is traditionally held in the Gardens of Tindrem, where the products of the labor of the farms in the Provinces make their way to the city and onto the plates of expectant citizens.

The feast itself lasts for ten days, with an evening meal served every night. Each centered around various fruits and seeds.

Musicians and dancers from across the Provinces travel to attend and give life to the festivities, and many competitions are held in honor of the goddess.

One of the most stunning aspects of this celebration dedicated to the goddess of autumn and harvest is the way that the gardens are masterfully decorated. Oranges, reds, and yellows feature prominently, with clusters of autumnal flowers and branches covering arches.

Text: M,

I am convinced based on what I have observed about tonight's fight in the arena that many bets are going to the gladiator from Meduli. Despite D's assurances, it would seem she is either mistaken or has lied about the outcome. We must be aware of this if we are to bet as much money as we intend to. She has the ear of a certain Consul. Remember that he fancies her even above his personal courtesans. I am going to a dinner where his sister will be attending, and I will see if I cannot find anything more about D or anyone else involved in this.

Be safe and be smart, we have a lot of coin invested in this,

J

M is making a bet on the other combatant. Not the Fabernumite, but the one grabbed from the outskirts of Meduli!

He asked me not to tell you this, but I had to say something as it concerns me greatly. Our families are in good standing, so perhaps that is why he told me? I know his father has hinted to my father's brother about the idea of M and I marrying.

I thought it only right to tell you that last week I saw him handing out handfuls of coins to none other than the sticky-fingered darlings you look after. What moves is he making? Everyone knows he is two-faced, especially after what he said about you at the celebration in the gardens last year.

He is careless, his plan may only work because of his father's deep pockets. We will have to be smart about this or he will be exceptionally hard to beat if all of his resources are going into the Medulian.

Let me know what you plan,

D

She stricked me, tricked both of us, into spending all of that money.

I was too trusting, and I paid the price. I cannot believe that after all I have done for her, all I have done for the city, and all I have done for the Provinces that being unable to pay my taxes was worthy of them attempting to arrest me.

blocks.html:
Location: Next to the tree north of the Fabernum Wayshrine

Title: Musings on these Structures

Text:

The rest of the writing on this page has been scribbled out hastily, and is no longer legible.

... one the Khurs are so fraught about, was it Tjaka Baarve in Urag?

But why then the archway?

It seems pertinent to assume it was not chosen by accident or on a whim of the creators, and so thereby we can conclude it to be purposeful. Wohever constructed these sites were clearly very driven, not to mention capable.

Archways are commonly used to denote passages, is that why they have been employed here? Are these great stone arches symbolic for some purpose, can they be used to pass from one place to another?

What came first, the mesmerizing activity envoloping them in the etherworld or the stonework itself? Are these markers for sites of this kind of phenomena, or is something about them drawing near and concentrating it?

Gah, more questions not answerable by anyone but myself after I have solved these mysteries no doubt.

I fear I have exhausted the knowledge simple observation will afford me, I must begin testing... more intimate exposures.

I have been ruminating on this for some time, and I find myself staring blankly for hours attempting to come up with a detracting or opposing argument toward myself.

Despite the albeit understandable fears that grip me, I must press past them and forward. I must answer the call that pulls on my very being toward this thing, this great current of thriving energy.

I will leave my body tonight, and the unknown will be laid bare before me.

Text:

Orien,

You have a family that you too are responsible for. Or did you forget that when courting you spoke of how you wanted exactly seven children? Well, now you have all seven. Five sons and two daughters.

Evano is sixteen years old. He needs his father here to teach him how to be a proper Tindremene of our family’s status. Every day that you are away he drifts more and more towards that group of plebian boys we so desperately try to keep him from.

I punish him, but it is of no use. He does not respect me the way he respects you.

You cannot keep reveling in the joys of a warm southerly seaside town. Return to us.

Your wife,

Lyssa

blocks.html:
Location: Meduli Tavern, on a table

Title: Meduli's Warm Embraces by Teucerios Condos

Text:

The city of Meduli has long been known as a place of many delights, and though the seaside harbor town has yet to fully recover from the travesties of the Irruption, it is still known to this day for its bordellos and courtesans.

Whether you are a new face to Meduli or are quite familiar with what the city has to offer, if you are seeking companionship for the night then there are several establishments that may be worthy of your attention.

My first word of advice, before I begin my list, is to avoid the docks outright. I have known several who have visited the courtesans there, only to walk away with an itch or a rash.

As one would expect, among the courtesans of Meduli you will find a large majority Tindremenes, with a small amount of Sarducaans and Kallards. Others are especially rare to find.

Domina Orrine’s Domus Voluptas

The Domus Voluptas exists as a rather refined institution, directly sanctioned by the Provinces. She offers the services of both female and male courtesans and masterfully avoids the “themes” of some other bordellos that some find distasteful, while still establishing a distinct, dark atmosphere that smells rich with spices. As an officially sanctioned bordello, you need not worry about diseases or unwanted pregnancies.

The courtesans here are well-educated in the arts, each having an instrument he or she plays. Among my favorites were Tassa and Lander, who will sing and play the lute together when both are available. Their coordination and collaboration are masterful in all of their services.

Anthos Apothymion

The Anthos Apothymion, sometimes simply referred to as “the Anthos” is a bordello with chiefly female courtesans, with a fitting theme of flowers. The women here each take on the name of a flower and said flower can often be found in their hair or pinned to their clothing.

The atmosphere inside is bright, with many windows lining its walls that let in ample sunlight.

Of my favorite practices of the Anthos, it is the ritual of the courtesans giving the patrons of the bordello a flower as they leave that I find the most charming. When I return to my lodging, I need only reach over to my bedside table and inhale deeply to be reminded of the comforting, perfumed embraces of Hyacinth, Rosa, or Paeonia.

blocks.html:
Location: Fabernum Inn, posted outside on its western fence.

Title: Hark!

Text:

You who have found my warning, I beg you do not stay a single night at this inn if you can help it.

When I woke this morning and went for my boots, I was shocked by an ugly rat jumping from them and running over my feet! I barefoot chased the thing downstairs and almost crashed straight into the innkeeper, but before I could blurt out the problem at hand I watched as the rat scurried up their leg and into their pocket, only for it to poke its head out, smugly sneering at me with its awful face!

I at once demanded an explanation, and it turns out the disgusting vermin is their pet! Can you believe it? They just let it run around the inn, who knows where its filthy grubby little appendages have been, other than inside my boots of course. No doubt all the plates and tables are contaminated.

If I wanted to be accosted by an animal, I would seek out that deranged Sheevra who has been going around asking people if he can inhale their bodily odours most inappropriately. I understanding it is common for Alvarin to become intimately fixated on or obsessed with obscure things, but surely this is not something the people should tolerate?

I simply cannot stay at such an establishment, and if you have any sense about you, you won't either.

Fabernum is a strange town.

blocks.html:
Location: Fabernum Inn, on a table next to the Essence Artificer.

Title: Today's Lament

Text:

My best and most promising apprentice, lost to their own hubris...

When I accept eager and spirited scholars under my tutelage and stewardship, it is with the expectation that they enter into this agreement with at minimum the most meager of requisites.

Firstly, do not waste my time. Attend each experiment with a mind open and receptive to learning.

Second, follow my instructions exactly at all times. I do not offer my valuable time to herd disruptive infants.

Third, do not touch or move anything on my desk. Ever.

Fourth, do not mishandle an empty Essence receptacle, categorically failing to perform a basic extraction and instead end up transposing the empty space within the glass orb with your own liver!

Sucus, as I sit now in the inn writing this, I have chosen to keep your orb on my desk as a constant and disappointing reminder of the folly of youth. At least the other apprentices will see your curdled blood stuck inside this glass ball and hopefully think twice about being so careless.

Fret not Sucus, you might still be useful yet.

blocks.html:
Location: Fab Sewer (turn left at the beginning into the dead end)

Title: Strabo

Text:

By the end of this note, you’ll be squinting extra hard.

There was some madman who started calling himself “King of the Sewers”. He’s probably heard the old story, same as all of us, but we all thought it was funny.

Until it wasn’t anymore.

Normally someone like him wouldn’t be a problem, nothing a knife to the throat wouldn’t fix, right? Took care of him myself.

And then someone else decided they’re the new king!

It’s gotten entirely out of hand, they’ve all fallen to the same madness. Everyone wants to be king of the sewers, and they don’t last long before someone else kills them and takes their place.

Oh, and they’re forcing me to write everything for them.

You know that old ruin down here, the one you thought might have been Huergar stonework that was built over?

They’ve decided that’s the ‘castle’. Avoid it.

blocks.html:
Location: Bakti Library

Title: Studies of Nature: The Celaeno

Text:

Page 1/5

This book has been written, edited, and commissioned to

be printed by the Societas Natura Myrland, whose

headquarters may be found in Tindrem.

Other auxiliary branches include those found in:

Meduli, headed by Marios Nearos

Fabernum, headed by Roburo Castellina

Hyllspeia, led by Karan Obelsyn

Basilia Amata, Naturalist and Author

Oyuun, Tracker

---

Page 2/5

BY SOCIETAS NATURA MYRLAND

Few creatures strike more immediate fear when speaking

their name than that of the celaeno. Despite their infamy,

however, seldom little is known about these gargantuan

creatures of the night. With a great deal of anxiety about

my endeavor, I took it upon myself to set out and find

this elusive creature.

Celaenos are nocturnal creatures, and based on

information gathered from autopsy, they share similar

internal structures to bats. In this sense, the celaeno is to

the common bat what the terror bird is to the songbird. A

giant, vicious, flightless form.

The intelligence of such creatures is of question and great

debate. As with any creature that might inspire such

fearsome tales, there are stories that would imply them

to be highly intelligent beings capable of planning and

malice.

You may rest easy as it would seem they are nothing of

the sort.

Celaenos are solitary, nocturnal creatures that may be

found in caves or other enclosed, dark spaces during the

day. It has been observed that they are often near what

we naturalists may call a "cauldron" of bats, which is to

say a large group of them.

It has been observed that they are often near what we naturalists may call a "cauldron" of bats, which is to say a large group of them.

blocks.html:
---

Page 3/5

These cauldrons benefit greatly from the presence of even

just one celaeno, though exceptionally large groups of bats

may see multiple within the same space. "What role does

the celaeno play?" You may wonder. The answer is

dragging meat back into the cave for the other bats to eat.

While this benefit is surely not one-sided, as the celaeno

seem to seek out cauldrons to live amongst, we have yet

to uncover the exact benefit. Some have some rather

outlandish and grotesque theories based on the levels of

guano in caves with celaenos in comparison to those

without celaenos.

The creatures are exceptionally light, likely owing this

trait to their shared ancestry with flying creatures. This

trait allows them to be talented climbers and to

sometimes seem as if they are gliding through the air as if

propelled by some unseen force when leaping and

lunging.

Perfectly built for hunting prey in a forest, mountain, or

even an open field.

---

Page 4/5

Another phenomenon that may be observed in connection

with the celaeno is their participation in the often short-

lived 'great cauldrons'. Such congregations of many, many

chiropterans are not only the stuff of legend: they have

also been observed directly. The formation of one

requires a very specific set of conditions to take place,

including a very large space for the creatures to inhabit,

ample food nearby, and insufficient competition to

prevent them from starving.

These 'great cauldrons' typically break apart once there is

a shift in their dynamics, such as an overpopulation of

nonreciprocal species that benefit from such colonies.

blocks.html:
---

Page 5/5

Though they can be found most anywhere, my own studies

centered in the abandoned mines ofthe area south of Meduli.

With me was Oyuun, a Gakti Khurite tracker and huntsman,

who assured me that he had located a nest.

Oyuun's methods were atypical in comparison to the

Tindremic hunters I have become so very used to. There is a

certain connection to the land that his people have from

years ofwanderingthe wilds ofwestern and southern

Myrland that few can deny.

When we reached the area, he instructed me to carefully

follow in his footsteps and not make a sound. I must admit

that in the dying light of dusk it was quite hard to ascertain

where he had stepped.

Laying down at the very edge of a cliffside, he instructed me

to lay my torso on the ground as he did. All we had to do then

was be silent, and watch. The scent of some pouch he had

opened was offensive to my nose and distracted me a great

deal, but he assured me that it was to cover our scent from

the creature.

Long after the sun fell, I saw the silhouettes of both large and

small bats flying from the opening to the mineshaft in the

moonlight. I could not tell if they were adults and juveniles of

the same species or different kinds of bats, but

something about the sight sent shivers down my back

knowing what would likely emerge soon.

Title: N/A

Text:

Page 1/2

A snake appeared in the village today, it was seen

slithering behind the house of the old woman, Ekh

Nogutani.

I have done the warding rituals as she requested, as she

believes one may have placed a curse on her to call the

creatures so they may strike at her in her sleep.

I do wish to believe her, for my former master and I

cleansed many such curses, but she has made many such

claims over the years.

She is haunted by her past.

She was one of the only survivors of her khuren being

attacked in her youth, she will not speak of this often. The

village knows, but we pretend we do not, for her. We all

have silently agreed to allow her to pretend to have been

from the city above.

Like her, I found myself here after a lifetime of wandering.

But it is my assumption that my life, despite the horrors

that I have witnessed, may have been less hard on me thaw

poor Nogutani.

---

Page 2/2

She has a kind soul.

Animals and children take easily to her, even horses that

startle at the slighted of movements find calm through

Nogutani's gentle touch and faint whispers.

Perhaps there is even something for me to learn from her.

Location: Morin Khur Ravine - Village House

Title: ULAGEI

Text:

ULAGEI,

When I rest and listen to the sound of the waters being

carried to the eastern sea, I hear them whisper to me of a

son.

A son, Ulagei!

I know that he will not have a name until he is of age, but

the words of his potential future bubble from the water as

it splashes against the rocks. I know he is a boy, because

they speak to me names that end in "Ge!" and "Dai!" and

"Der!"

I do not hear "Gei!" I take this to mean that it is simply not

to be. He is not meant to have the ending of his father's

name.

Were he a girl, the water would have surely called name-

endings such as "Jin!" or "Tani!" or perhaps even "Lun!"

But, I am certain that it did not.

Usunge

Chiygeder

Qoldai

Are these names not beautiful?

Location: Tindrem Arena District, Bank Second Floor

Title: N/A

Text:

D, I think we're in trouble.

J seems to be aware something is amiss. I warned you

about his little rats that feed him information about the

matches! What we intend will not be easy. Please assure

me you were not so foolish to involve the Consul's sister.

You may have him at least partially blinded by you,

especially in that red garment you like to wear, but you

surely know the way she looks at you from afar at

every event you attend and sit next to him? She will betray

you to J, and likely betray your lover himself, if it means

advancing herself. This loss will be grievous for all both of

us if J finds out, he alone carries what will be more than a

quarter of our profits.

We had a plan to bet on the Medulian and have M bet on

the Fabernumite, and I trust you're honoring it. Neither of

us stand to benefit from the other's failure, our families are

in good standing.

M.

Location: Toxai Library

Title: N/A

Text:

Page 1/2

When the Tindremenes took over Morin Khur, we initially

tried to adapt to the situation. They brought with them

plans for devices to print books.

They claimed to wish to spread the knowledge of reading

and writing to the people of Morin Khur. Some took

offense to this, particularly my fellow scribes, as we have

our own method of writing and we train many young

apprentices to read and write.

Seeing our offense, they invited us to work with them.

We compared our own method of printing, blocks of wood

pressed to paper instead, and made improvements to our

techniques based on them. We also began printing books

in the style and method the Tindremenes use. There were

many arguments about the proper Tindremic characters to

represent our sounds.

Of the many disagreements, perhaps the largest was the

choice of two characters, KH, to represent a sound the

Tindremic language lacks. As it stands, there is no

standard of how to do this, only an author's preference.

---

Page 2/2

We quickly began producing books to preserve our

stories, history, and tales. The distribution of them

brought the attention of a Tindremene by the name of

Didacus. He took particular offense to our texts concerning

dragons and Geeredh and burnt many of them.

Three of our number were jailed for things they had

written.

Fearing further action, many fled. Some fled westward

toward the young forests, while several others and I fled

through the valley to Toxai. All of us carried our books

with us.

Of those who fled to Toxai, some have returned to Morin

Khur. Others, including myself, remain here.

Although quite some time has passed since this event, I

was approached by a young woman who wishes to learn

to write and make scrolls. She reminds me of myself when

I was a young man. Such a passion for the idea of reading.

Soon Toxai will have another scribe, and she will offer the

perspective of one who was born and raised here without

the oppressive control of Tindrem.

Location: Fab Tower, secret bone turn-in room

Title: Silvena

Text:

We've studied your notes from your stay in the east carefully.

I again remind you that I believe giving them to the others was a mistake. Some of them have begun dabbling in the very same divinatory methods that you explicitly wrote were what seems to have driven the priests mad!

I have tried to convince them to stop, but they are not us. They are but lowly common necromancers tantalized by the draw of power. They know no self restraint, and their playthings stink up the entire structure.

I will be keeping the wall closed as often as possible!

Location: Undercroft, in a jail cell

Title: Nari's Journal

Text:

Hello mother, I’m sorry it’s been so long since we last spoke.

I’m doing much better now, I have a new family that took me in and cares for me. I would like to say I can’t even remember the last time I slept outside with an empty stomach, but I promised I wouldn’t lie to you.

They found me in the stables one night, instead of ignoring me like most, they talked to me and asked me why I was out there and not inside the village. I know I said I wouldn’t speak of it anymore mother, but they were talking to me like I was a person and not an animal, and it just came out. I told them everything.

I told them about our home — Yes, I still remember it. I told them about you and how you taught me to read and write when none of the other children could. How you would take me foraging in the woods outside Vadda, and we would always come back with a fuller basket than the others because you knew where the best bushes grew.

… I told them about the day you left.

How my life has never been the same, how I spend every night hoping to wake up from this nightmare and into the bed you made for me in our old home, with the sound of you weaving outside my window like you used to.

Mother, every day I feel the rage that has been building inside me ever since those cowardly Tindremene’s calling themselves soldiers took you from this world … from me.

He said his name was Kham, and he told me I didn’t have to be afraid anymore, that I didn’t have to be cold, or hungry ever again.

They told me they belong to a group of other Khurites who will stand up to the Tindremenes, to fight them, to hurt them for what they have done. They told me I’m not the only one who tells this story, and that each of them tells a similar one, that I would come to know them in time, as they will come to know mine.

Location: Morin Khur Sewers

"Blue entrance", first large storage room, on top of the rafters

Note: I fixed some typos present in my transcription; reported as well

Title: N/A

The lengths I must go to hide the records of my private

thoughts...

The guards of this city are allowing the sewers and tunnels

to fall to anarchy. Despite their promises that the scum that

teem in these sewers like rats would be ousted, they still

thrive and make our work more dangerous.

The elders of my tribe once shared that aside from the

slaves, even the lowliest of people once existed with some

meager dignity. They mentioned a small village of tents

where the slums sit now, where all one had to do was

merely provide for themselves.

Those times are long behind the city of the mountain now.

The taxes are unpredictable and one cannot predict what

strange fines may arrive at one's doorstep.

Those who decide such things have learned from the

Tindremenes well.

Regardless of the past, we must work.

One of the few organizations accepting people of all levels

of skill is the urland that maintains the sewers below, the

Ugiyan Urland.

It is an urland full of those with no where else to go.

Criminals, misfits, outcasts—All banished below for

hours every day to maintain the sewers.

As one with skills in reading and writing, I do not belong

here. They see little worth in my skills beyond my ability

to read aloud the notes left by the overseers.

Location: Cave Camp East Keep - Northeast against the mountains

Title: Aegos

AEGOS,

When I first tried to trade for a Kallardian helm, imagine

my surprise when I got something quite unlike what you

described.

A conical metal helmet with a half-mask descending to

over the nose and chainmail hanging from all sides, and a

long plume coming off the top had been placed before me. I

immediately rejected their offer, telling them that this is no

Kallardian helm.

They assured me it was, and that it was made in the Great

Forest of Nordveld. When I described what you had

actually wished for to them, they laughed at me and told

me that I spoke of the Kallards of the far north of Nordveld

that live among the tundras and fjords.

Conveniently, those particular ice-eyes are said to have far

less contact with the outside world. An authentic helm of

such a style would be much more expensive.

Naturally.

I offer this to you with a much lighter coinpurse than I had

wished for. I trust that this is enough to convince you to

protect me during my stay in Gaul'kor.

Location: East of Tindrem; Tribe rat den; inside mine

Title: N/A

Why did it have to be the bloodthirsty kind of tribe rat?

Why not the tribe mice I've heard about?

Even a steintroll would've been better. At least you can

try to figure out a steintroll and get on its good side. I've

heard stories of people being brought right in, treated like

a king or a queen by the little shits.

But how do you even begin to try to understand a rat on

two legs that bludgeoned someone to death with a big

rock? Someone else was hiding up here with me, he slid

down and tried to talk to them and they just-Well, they

just killed him.

I think I may just need to run for the exit.

Location: Sylvan Sanctum, outer rooms on a table.

Title: N/A

Text:

I have found a most unusual gemstone.

It is unlike any I have yet studied, of a pale red and much heavier than it looks. Its surface is smoother than one would expect, however most intriguing of all, it is, well, singing.

I didn't notice it at first when I pulled it out of that drawer, but when I hold it close to my head I can hear a most pleasant and pure tone. I can't explain why, but it calms me effortlessly, and I have been carrying it with me everywhere.

The shape of it is also rather odd, it's as if it has been cut to fit perfectly in the palm of my hand.

Location: Sylvan Sanctum

Title: N/A

Text:

We has just expanded into a new region of the structure, taking note of our surroundings and listing our findings and usual.

Nyra, ever the inquisitive one, had only just reached out her hand to examine what appeared to be a simple stone outcropping. The instant she touched it, the seemingly inert rock sprang to life, breaking away from the wall and began lumbering after us! I've not run so fast in quite some time.

What a luxury it would be to study them with my own eyes, what a rare opportunity to encounter a stable entity such as that. All I could make out when I looked back was the glint of something metallic that appeared to be stuck in its chest.

After we made some distance and could no longer hear the thumping behind us, we stopped and caught our breath. It's almost as if it was protecting something, but what?

Location: Fab west bank

Title: Cavete

Text:

As all know, the cliffside village outside of our fair city has fallen into disrepair over the decades.

It would seem that as of late dangerous outlaws, such as exiled Eeta, have taken up residence in the ruins. With the loss of the settlement, the few who tended the ruined altar above have gone silent.

These individuals are well-trained and dangerous, and approaching them in an attempt to negotiate is not encouraged. Inexperienced fighters are encouraged to let other, better trained individuals handle these matters.

Location: Library in the Necro Dungeon

Title: The Imperial Campaigns: A Time of Dragons

Author: Kaia Chloros

The Imperial Campaigns are remembered by the descendents of the Empire as a time of many things. It was a time of grand battles, conquests, and conquering. It was also a time of abundnance and glory, where goods both domestic and foreign flooded the markets of Tindrem allowing her people to partake in Nave's many bounties and curioisities.

It was also a time of architectural and infrastructural ingenuity; to the eastern settlement of Gabaria; to the southerly settlements of Canteri, Chloros, and Amodia; to even the western continents of Sarducaa and Nordveld. The success and refined cultures of the settlements of Beth Jedda and Varborg clearly owe their successes to the Empire's guidance.

From a more poetric perspective, the Imperial Campaigns are also known as a time of dragons and heroes.

As a scholar of magical history, you may find it surprising that I would cover a topic such as dragons. Or perhaps, if you are more informed, you are surprised I didn't write about the topic sooner. Do not be misinformed dear reader: There is much magic to be found in dragons.

As magnifacent, gargantuan creatures of fable and legend, it is little wonder that precious little can actually be confirmed about them. Those who may know hide themselves away in the Specula Summa, and as such we must draw from the wealth of information uttered from all sources, including the Khurs who despise t he dragons so.

The dragons are tied heavily in many legends to the mountains, particularly the Talus Mountains in Tindremic folklore and history. Some say that they are intelligent beings who could fully communicate with mankind if they so chose, while others claim they are nothing but simple beasts, circling the skies and burning cattle.

blocks.html:
Others still haveb speculated that they may have something to do with the lizard-men found in the Stairs of Echidna, which would indeed make them the largest, most powerful, and most influential of the Cold Broods.

As for what they have left behind, there is a rumor that some isolated communities in the Talus Mountains revere them as gods, gathering the bones of dragons and treating them as sacred objects, praying that one day the dragons will return to them.

The Khurites gather their bones for different reasons entirely, as evidence of the "Defeat of the dragon" by their legendary bird-man "Geeredh". It is said that a statue of this creature can even be found in the city of Morin Khur, curiously permitted to stand even after the city was taken by Emperor Livi Avitus.

It is said that these bones, as well as the other parts of a dragon, hold unique magical properties unseen elsewhere. There are also tales of mages and shamans who can harness the lingering power of these magnificent creatures, though evidence of what said magic or ritual would look like is quite lacking.

Instead, we must look to legend and myth to perhaps slightly understand what this could be. The Tindremic Provinces claim that the Empire used dragons during the Imperial Campaigns, a fact rather well attested to by the skeletons said to be found in the south and the Khurites' tales of defeating a dragon that is synonymous with the Empire.

How then were these dragons used?

Were they allies, as some would have us believe? Or trained animals as others would have us believe?

Is the power found throughout their remains merely a coincidence? Or were they themselves capable of casting great magics?

Is it true that they still exist in the caves beneath the Talus Mountains? Or are they long-dead beings, driven to extinction by exploitation and war?

There is much to wonder about dragons, and a great wealth of information to sort through.

As for what they have left behind, there is a rumor that some isolated communities in the Talus Mountains revere them as gods, gathering the bones of dragons and treating them as sacred objects, praying that one day the dragons will return to them. The Khurites gather their bones for different reasons entirely, as evidence of the "Defeat of the dragon" by their legendary bird-man "Geeredh". It is said that a statue of this creature can even be found in the city of Morin Khur, curiously permitted to stand even after the city was taken by Emperor Livi Avitus. It is said that these bones, as well as the other parts of a dragon, hold unique magical properties unseen elsewhere. There are also tales of mages and shamans who can harness the lingering power of these magnificent creatures, though evidence of what said magic or ritual would look like is quite lacking. Instead, we must look to legend and myth to perhaps slightly understand what this could be. The Tindremic Provinces claim that the Empire used dragons during the Imperial Campaigns, a fact rather well attested to by the skeletons said to be found in the south and the Khurites' tales of defeating a dragon that is synonymous with the Empire. How then were these dragons used? Were they allies, as some would have us believe? Or trained animals as others would have us believe? Is the power found throughout their remains merely a coincidence? Or were they themselves capable of casting great magics? Is it true that they still exist in the caves beneath the Talus Mountains? Or are they long-dead beings, driven to extinction by exploitation and war? There is much to wonder about dragons, and a great wealth of information to sort through.

Title: N/A

Author: N/A

Unlike Velius, who would rather prattle about predictions and that failed ruin rightfully designated Lavra Impios, my attention is on what is before us: A structure that stretches deep into the earth.

Based on the opening that yawns out to the Irminian Sea, I believe it's possible part of the original structure may have been lost to the water, though perhaps it was built around it?

Even so, I sense something is amiss. The twists, turns, and tunnels would indicate that the architects followed a pre-designated path. A cave system. I cannot deny the silent presence of the Oghmir emanating from these walls either. I see the evidence of their craftsmanship.

Why, then, was this place abandoned? It would seem that time and time again others have tried to settle this place throughout history, and it always ends in failure.

blocks.html:
Location: Morin Khur Sewers, Rat King Part (I think...)

Title: N/A

Text:

I am lost and tired.

I feel as if I am going insane, so I must write.

This places has so many damned twists and turns, it is like a nightmare induced by the strongest concoction imaginable.

I had thought I escaped and yet here I am once again. Back in the same place.

The city of the rats is real, and I am lost in it.

It is true what the rumors say about the place, the rats make little of their own. It would seem that every structure has been haphazardly mashed together with things they have pilfered to make some twisted interpretation of a settlement.

At times I hear something particularly large lumber through the place, testing the supports of the rickety structures.

It seems to mostly stay across some bridge above.

I can only hope it stays there.

Title: N/A

Text:

The other's can't understand the concern of the Khurites, if most here even understand their tongue at all. They neglect the skill's usefulness, but I have studied their language ever since I was assigned to the east.

It was my immediately apparent fluency that surely earned me the attention of the Procurator.

I listen to the Khurite laborers from time to time. Sometimes they share their nightmares. One said he dreamt of a great, terrible sea bird circling above him in the sea, and he claimed that any time he attempted to reach shore it would dive down and begin to drown him.

Everyone was silent after that.

Title: N/A

Text:

"The Stride of the Murnahas."

That is what I believe he told me he wanted, and so it was on me to provide the body of such a thing. All reported sightings I had ever heard of centered around the Talus Mountains, and it is there that I learned of my quarry: A rumor of a horned monster lurking in a tunnel carved many centuries ago by the hands of the Stone Folk.

When I arrived, the locals were delighted to hear that a man of magical talent had arrived to rid them of their problem. I waited until I was alone at night to cast my spells and confront the beast. I had to worry little about decomposition, the biting air left no room for it. Instead, my new followers and I began a slow march back towards the east with the body of the creature quite literally in tow.

The villagers likely did not even notice the empty graves until the morning.

Credit: @Sigvald

Location: Next to the third set of enemies in the Tower of Descensus.

Title: The Trbe-Forming Rats By Rastius Amateu

Text:

A visual archive of readable world lore, organized by location and title so discovered texts can be found again quickly.

The aggressive sort which dwells just out of sight and attacks when approached is but one of many species scattered throughout the known world, but they are the most well-known due to their aforementioned aggression and proximity to civilization.

They are an extremely territorial species that typically avoid direct contact when left alone. However, they are not unintelligent. Like many other tribe rats, they have been observed rearing the pups of nightsnatchers, and they unanimously form semi-structured societies that intermingle two species of Tribe Rat.

They prove themselves to be cunning time and time again and will present an even greater danger to any who might think these bipedal rodents have the minds of simple beasts incapable of planning or forethought.

The next sort are rather difficult to encounter to those who do not know their locations, and I dare not reveal the ones most familiar to me, lest others who wish them ill will find their way to them.

The rodents I speak of are rather shy of human society and live in mountains and forests. Their fur is typically gray or brown in color, resembling common mice much more than their rat-like counterparts. They build their simple, tiny homes out of grass, clay, and branches—some crafting huts while others seem content with small burrows.

Several groups I've found are even open to trade, though they typically value practical goods they can make use of over curiousities and trinkets.

The third sort I have only encountered second-hand; told to me by a Sarducaan friend of mine. He described desert tribe rats with large ears and long legs that raise bats in the mountain caves, an element I have also seen in the tribe rats I'm familiar with.

Just like the tribe rats of forests that can be found in Myrland, these tribe rats are said to only be found far away from human civilization. When I asked my good friend his theory on why that often seems the case for more peaceful creatures, he simply suggested looking no further than the swords, spells, and bows of man.

A grim but likely theory.

A fourth kind of tribe rat, which I have only managed to find evidence of in writings, are the small-eyed and large-toothed ones with uncharacteristically small ears found exclusively underground that walk on all fours, though little else is written of them beyond their peculiar, highly specialized forms.
