over morin khur, we initially tried to adapt to the situation. they brought with them plans for devices to print books. they claimed to wish to spread the knowledge of reading and writing to the people of morin khur. some took offense to this, particularly my fellow scribes, as we have our own method of writing and we train many young apprentices to read and write. seeing our offense, they invited us to work with them. we compared our own method of printing, blocks of wood pressed to paper instead, and made improvements to our techniques based on them. we also began printing books in the style and method the tindremenes use. there were many arguments about the proper tindremic characters to represent our sounds. of the many disagreements, perhaps the largest was the choice of two characters, kh, to represent a sound the tindremic language lacks. as it stands, there is no standard of how to do this, only an author's preference. --- page 2/2 we quickly began producing books to preserve our stories, history, and tales. the distribution of them brought the attention of a tindremene by the name of didacus. he took particular offense to our texts concerning dragons and geeredh and burnt many of them. three of our number were jailed for things they had written. fearing further action, many fled. some fled westward toward the young forests, while several others and i fled through the valley to toxai. all of us carried our books with us. of those who fled to toxai, some have returned to morin khur. others, including myself, remain here. although quite some time has passed since this event, i was approached by a young woman who wishes to learn to write and make scrolls. she reminds me of myself when i was a young man. such a passion for the idea of reading. soon toxai will have another scribe, and she will offer the perspective of one who was born and raised here without the oppressive control of tindrem. location: fab tower, secret bone turn-in room title: silvena text: we've studied your notes from your stay in the east carefully. i again remind you that i believe giving them to the others was a mistake. some of them have begun dabbling in the very same divinatory methods that you explicitly wrote were what seems to have driven the priests mad! i have tried to convince them to stop, but they are not us. they are but lowly common necromancers tantalized by the draw of power. they know no self restraint, and their playthings stink up the entire structure. i will be keeping the wall closed as often as possible! note: just noticed as i posted that i missed the fact that there is more in the journal. will go back and get the rest and update this post sometime soon. location: undercroft, in a jail cell title: nari's journal text: hello mother, i’m sorry it’s been so long since we last spoke. i’m doing much better now, i have a new family that took me in and cares for me. i would like to say i can’t even remember the last time i slept outside with an empty stomach, but i promised i wouldn’t lie to you. they found me in the stables one night, instead of ignoring me like most, they talked to me and asked me why i was out there and not inside the village. i know i said i wouldn’t speak of it anymore mother, but they were talking to me like i was a person and not an animal, and it just came out. i told them everything. i told them about our home — yes, i still remember it. i told them about you and how you taught me to read and write when none of the other children could. how you would take me foraging in the woods outside vadda, and we would always come back with a fuller basket than the others because you knew where the best bushes grew. … i told them about the day you left. how my life has never been the same, how i spend every night hoping to wake up from this nightmare and into the bed you made for me in our old home, with the sound of you weaving outside my window like you used to. mother, every day i feel the rage that has been building inside me ever since those cowardly tindremene’s calling themselves soldiers took you from this world … from me. he said his name was kham, and he told me i didn’t have to be afraid anymore, that i didn’t have to be cold, or hungry ever again. they told me they belong to a group of other khurites who will stand up to the tindremenes, to fight them, to hurt them for what they have done. they told me i’m not the only one who tells this story, and that each of them tells a similar one, that i would come to know them in time, as they will come to know mine. location: morin khur sewers "blue entrance", first large storage room, on top of the rafters note: i fixed some typos present in my transcription; reported as well title: n/a the lengths i must go to hide the records of my private thoughts... the guards of this city are allowing the sewers and tunnels to fall to anarchy. despite their promises that the scum that teem in these sewers like rats would be ousted, they still thrive and make our work more dangerous. the elders of my tribe once shared that aside from the slaves, even the lowliest of people once existed with some meager dignity. they mentioned a small village of tents where the slums sit now, where all one had to do was merely provide for themselves. those times are long behind the city of the mountain now. the taxes are unpredictable and one cannot predict what strange fines may arrive at one's doorstep. those who decide such things have learned from the tindremenes well. regardless of the past, we must work. one of the few organizations accepting people of all levels of skill is the urland that maintains the sewers below, the ugiyan urland. it is an urland full of those with no where else to go. criminals, misfits, outcasts—all banished below for hours every day to maintain the sewers. as one with skills in reading and writing, i do not belong here. they see little worth in my skills beyond my ability to read aloud the notes left by the overseers. location: cave camp east keep - northeast against the mountains title: aegos aegos, when i first tried to trade for a kallardian helm, imagine my surprise when i got something quite unlike what you described. a conical metal helmet with a half-mask descending to over the nose and chainmail hanging from all sides, and a long plume coming off the top had been placed before me. i immediately rejected their offer, telling them that this is no kallardian helm. they assured me it was, and that it was made in the great forest of nordveld. when i described what you had actually wished for to them, they laughed at me and told me that i spoke of the kallards of the far north of nordveld that live among the tundras and fjords. conveniently, those particular ice-eyes are said to have far less contact with the outside world. an authentic helm of such a style would be much more expensive. naturally. i offer this to you with a much lighter coinpurse than i had wished for. i trust that this is enough to convince you to protect me during my stay in gaul'kor. location: east of tindrem; tribe rat den; inside mine title: n/a why did it have to be the bloodthirsty kind of tribe rat? why not the tribe mice i've heard about? even a steintroll would've been better. at least you can try to figure out a steintroll and get on its good side. i've heard stories of people being brought right in, treated like a king or a queen by the little shits. but how do you even begin to try to understand a rat on two legs that bludgeoned someone to death with a big rock? someone else was hiding up here with me, he slid down and tried to talk to them and they just-well, they just killed him. i think i may just need to run for the exit. location: sylvan sanctum, outer rooms on a table. title: n/a text: i have found a most unusual gemstone. it is unlike any i have yet studied, of a pale red and much heavier than it looks. its surface is smoother than one would expect, however most intriguing of all, it is, well, singing. i didn't notice it at first when i pulled it out of that drawer, but when i hold it close to my head i can hear a most pleasant and pure tone. i can't explain why, but it calms me effortlessly, and i have been carrying it with me everywhere. the shape of it is also rather odd, it's as if it has been cut to fit perfectly in the palm of my hand. location: sylvan sanctum title: n/a text: we has just expanded into a new region of the structure, taking note of our surroundings and listing our findings and usual. nyra, ever the inquisitive one, had only just reached out her hand to examine what appeared to be a simple stone outcropping. the instant she touched it, the seemingly inert rock sprang to life, breaking away from the wall and began lumbering after us! i've not run so fast in quite some time. what a luxury it would be to study them with my own eyes, what a rare opportunity to encounter a stable entity such as that. all i could make out when i looked back was the glint of something metallic that appeared to be stuck in its chest. after we made some distance and could no longer hear the thumping behind us, we stopped and caught our breath. it's almost as if it was protecting something, but what? location: fab west bank title: cavete text: as all know, the cliffside village outside of our fair city has fallen into disrepair over the decades. it would seem that as of late dangerous outlaws, such as exiled eeta, have taken up residence in the ruins. with the loss of the settlement, the few who tended the ruined altar above have gone silent. these individuals are well-trained and dangerous, and approaching them in an attempt to negotiate is not encouraged. inexperienced fighters are encouraged to let other, better trained individuals handle these matters. location: library in the necro dungeon title: the imperial campaigns: a time of dragons author: kaia chloros the imperial campaigns are remembered by the descendents of the empire as a time of many things. it was a time of grand battles, conquests, and conquering. it was also a time of abundnance and glory, where goods both domestic and foreign flooded the markets of tindrem allowing her people to partake in nave's many bounties and curioisities. it was also a time of architectural and infrastructural ingenuity; to the eastern settlement of gabaria; to the southerly settlements of canteri, chloros, and amodia; to even the western continents of sarducaa and nordveld. the success and refined cultures of the settlements of beth jedda and varborg clearly owe their successes to the empire's guidance. from a more poetric perspective, the imperial campaigns are also known as a time of dragons and heroes. as a scholar of magical history, you may find it surprising that i would cover a topic such as dragons. or perhaps, if you are more informed, you are surprised i didn't write about the topic sooner. do not be misinformed dear reader: there is much magic to be found in dragons. as magnifacent, gargantuan creatures of fable and legend, it is little wonder that precious little can actually be confirmed about them. those who may know hide themselves away in the specula summa, and as such we must draw from the wealth of information uttered from all sources, including the khurs who despise t he dragons so. the dragons are tied heavily in many legends to the mountains, particularly the talus mountains in tindremic folklore and history. some say that they are intelligent beings who could fully communicate with mankind if they so chose, while others claim they are nothing but simple beasts, circling the skies and burning cattle. others still haveb speculated that they may have something to do with the lizard-men found in the stairs of echidna, which would indeed make them the largest, most powerful, and most influential of the cold broods. as for what they have left behind, there is a rumor that some isolated communities in the talus mountains revere them as gods, gathering the bones of dragons and treating them as sacred objects, praying that one day the dragons will return to them. the khurites gather their bones for different reasons entirely, as evidence of the "defeat of the dragon" by their legendary bird-man "geeredh". it is said that a statue of this creature can even be found in the city of morin khur, curiously permitted to stand even after the city was taken by emperor livi avitus. it is said that these bones, as well as the other parts of a dragon, hold unique magical properties unseen elsewhere. there are also tales of mages and shamans who can harness the lingering power of these magnificent creatures, though evidence of what said magic or ritual would look like is quite lacking. instead, we must look to legend and myth to perhaps slightly understand what this could be. the tindremic provinces claim that the empire used dragons during the imperial campaigns, a fact rather well attested to by the skeletons said to be found in the south and the khurites' tales of defeating a dragon that is synonymous with the empire. how then were these dragons used? were they allies, as some would have us believe? or trained animals as others would have us believe? is the power found throughout their remains merely a coincidence? or were they themselves capable of casting great magics? is it true that they still exist in the caves beneath the talus mountains? or are they long-dead beings, driven to extinction by exploitation and war? there is much to wonder about dragons, and a great wealth of information to sort through.  location: first necromancer room in the necro dungeon title: n/a author: n/a unlike velius, who would rather prattle about predictions and that failed ruin rightfully designated lavra impios, my attention is on what is before us: a structure that stretches deep into the earth. based on the opening that yawns out to the irminian sea, i believe it's possible part of the original structure may have been lost to the water, though perhaps it was built around it? even so, i sense something is amiss. the twists, turns, and tunnels would indicate that the architects followed a pre-designated path. a cave system. i cannot deny the silent presence of the oghmir emanating from these walls either. i see the evidence of their craftsmanship. why, then, was this place abandoned? it would seem that time and time again others have tried to settle this place throughout history, and it always ends in failure. location: morin khur sewers, rat king part. on a barrel title: morijoksa, text: you are not from here, i know that you must blindly trust me when i say that the city of the rats is no legend. it is not some small nest that you can scatter the vermin from. they have lived in this space for centuries. imagine it! hundreds of years of stolen things piled up... and what we might find in such a place.  location: morin khur sewers, rat king part (i think...) title: n/a text: i am lost and tired. i feel as if i am going insane, so i must write. this places has so many damned twists and turns, it is like a nightmare induced by the strongest concoction imaginable. i had thought i escaped and yet here i am once again. back in the same place. the city of the rats is real, and i am lost in it. it is true what the rumors say about the place, the rats make little of their own. it would seem that every structure has been haphazardly mashed together with things they have pilfered to make some twisted interpretation of a settlement. at times i hear something particularly large lumber through the place, testing the supports of the rickety structures. it seems to mostly stay across some bridge above. i can only hope it stays there. location: top of the necro dungeon title: n/a text: the other's can't understand the concern of the khurites, if most here even understand their tongue at all. they neglect the skill's usefulness, but i have studied their language ever since i was assigned to the east. it was my immediately apparent fluency that surely earned me the attention of the procurator. i listen to the khurite laborers from time to time. sometimes they share their nightmares. one said he dreamt of a great, terrible sea bird circling above him in the sea, and he claimed that any time he attempted to reach shore it would dive down and begin to drown him. everyone was silent after that.  location: top of necro dungeon on the center table title: n/a text: maros, i trust we need not remind you how important this restoration is to the provinces. the setbacks you have experienced are unfortunate, but this venture is still exceedingly valuable to us. the eastern seaboard continues to elude our grasp, but according to our surveyors there may be access to a suitable sea cave that a small harbor could be carved out of. haste and secrecy are of the utmost import. burn after reading. location: the 3rd 3x rooms in mino dungeon in front of the entrances. title: n/a text: "the stride of the murnahas." that is what i believe he told me he wanted, and so it was on me to provide the body of such a thing. all reported sightings i had ever heard of centered around the talus mountains, and it is there that i learned of my quarry: a rumor of a horned monster lurking in a tunnel carved many centuries ago by the hands of the stone folk. when i arrived, the locals were delighted to hear that a man of magical talent had arrived to rid them of their problem. i waited until i was alone at night to cast my spells and confront the beast. i had to worry little about decomposition, the biting air left no room for it. instead, my new followers and i began a slow march back towards the east with the body of the creature quite literally in tow. the villagers likely did not even notice the empty graves until the morning. credit: @sigvald location: next to the third set of enemies in the tower of descensus. title: the trbe-forming rats by rastius amateu text: a visual archive of readable world lore, organized by location and title so discovered texts can be found again quickly. the aggressive sort which dwells just out of sight and attacks when approached is but one of many species scattered throughout the known world, but they are the most well-known due to their aforementioned aggression and proximity to civilization. they are an extremely territorial species that typically avoid direct contact when left alone. however, they are not unintelligent. like many other tribe rats, they have been observed rearing the pups of nightsnatchers, and they unanimously form semi-structured societies that intermingle two species of tribe rat. they prove themselves to be cunning time and time again and will present an even greater danger to any who might think these bipedal rodents have the minds of simple beasts incapable of planning or forethought. the next sort are rather difficult to encounter to those who do not know their locations, and i dare not reveal the ones most familiar to me, lest others who wish them ill will find their way to them. the rodents i speak of are rather shy of human society and live in mountains and forests. their fur is typically gray or brown in color, resembling common mice much more than their rat-like counterparts. they build their simple, tiny homes out of grass, clay, and branches—some crafting huts while others seem content with small burrows. several groups i've found are even open to trade, though they typically value practical goods they can make use of over curiousities and trinkets. the third sort i have only encountered second-hand; told to me by a sarducaan friend of mine. he described desert tribe rats with large ears and long legs that raise bats in the mountain caves, an element i have also seen in the tribe rats i'm familiar with. just like the tribe rats of forests that can be found in myrland, these tribe rats are said to only be found far away from human civilization. when i asked my good friend his theory on why that often seems the case for more peaceful creatures, he simply suggested looking no further than the swords, spells, and bows of man. a grim but likely theory. a fourth kind of tribe rat, which i have only managed to find evidence of in writings, are the small-eyed and large-toothed ones with uncharacteristically small ears found exclusively underground that walk on all fours, though little else is written of them beyond their peculiar, highly specialized forms. location: haven, small messed up hut in the hills above opening training area title:n/a text i moved here to get away from it all. hopefully, they'll never find me now, and i can live my life in peace, away from those bandits... if they find me, they will not spare my life. so if you read this, i'm most likely dead, but i want you to know that i've hidden my valuables in teh busehs north of my cabin. good thing these bandits can't read... location: a farm poi ne of the keep in tindremic midlands title: n/a text: i love my husband with all of my heart, but this venture of his was nothing short of foolish. he wished for us to reclaim a small village abandoned by his great grandfather, yet none of us have an upbringing or education in farming. he claimed it would be easy, that “if the uneducated provincials can make their living farming, then surely we can too.” but i am not so confident, we were both born to stone walls and paved streets, as were the slaves we brought with us. we know the trials and challenges of navigating a city and its many characters, not the wilderness that becomes as still as death in the pitch black night. after raising my concerns that the slaves quarters look much like our own, he assured me that the collapsed building on the other side of the garden is what we will be living in once it’s remade into a beautiful villa. i must admit it would be quite the remarkable home after living in an insula our entire marriage. the children have even dragged a chest there and started to pretend as if the structure is already complete and we’re already living inside. but i fear that they will be disappointed. such an endeavor may take months or years. and where will the money come from? one of the slaves returned to us out of breath, exclaiming that the fortress to the north has a group of outlaws living inside. i refuse to stay here any longer. if my husband wishes to risk his safety and our very livelihood on his stubbornness, fine. but i will not risk the childrens’ lives, or my own, on his confidence. i am taking them with me and heading to the city in the morning. it became an argument, he promised he would be able to send for the guards before the outlaws even realize we’re here. but what if they already know? after my last entry, i have decided to leave my journal here. i know you will be reading this and trying to understand why i have chosen to leave. read my own words, when i thought no one else would see them. i have not abandoned you, only this place. when you wish to return to us, we will be in the city. your wife, larisa

blocks.html:
Relic Wars

Track meteor events, beam colors, reward types, capture pressure, essence orbs, and the risks around valuable relics.

Overview

Relic Wars are a conflict driving mechanic in which meteors with unique and powerful rewards drop over the map. These events are visible from any part of the map, and great fanfare in the form of a sonic boom is heard as they descend. After landing, pillars of light emit upwards to invite all daring adventurers.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uV7WxE8q31o

blocks.html:
Meteor Types

Meteors that fall take 15 minutes to crack open and reveal the rewards. In the mean time, muster your forces and compete to take control of the area. Meteors are displayed on the map for all to see. There are five different types of meteors:

  • Reliquary Relics - These are pickable relics which must be transported to a reliquary. Once placed in the reliquary, they bestow a global bonus to everyone in the guild. Guilds with large numbers of players see diminishing returns to these effects. This is marked by a gold beam.
  • Divinium Equipment - Exceptionally powerful gear from the gods. Players cannot bank, log out, stash, or otherwise hide this equipment! Once you have these, you use it until you die or drop it. All divinium gear glows brightly to put onlookers in awe. This is marked by a red beam.
  • Ore - Mineable meteors that gives rare extraction yields directly. This is marked by a purple beam.
  • Wave - Waves of enemies will be attracted to the enemy, with a boss at the end that yields great rewards. This is marked by a white beam.
  • Hoard - These spawn treasures around the meteor. There are rather rare items obtainable from this event. This is marked by a blue beam.

blocks.html:
Reliquary Relics:

Reliquaries are TC structures which must be built to house a relic. They cannot be placed inside of keep walls. The following relics and their effects are listed here:

Relic of Abundance - Generates supply over time

Relic of Acuity - Increases weakspot chance

Relic of Amplification - Increases spell damage and healing

Relic of Eminence - Increases glory gained

Relic of Empowerment - Increases melee damage bonus

Relic of Endurance - Damage reduction

Relic of Fortification - Increases guild defence on all guild structures

Relic of Fortune - Increasese Loot Luck

Relic of Honing - Increase Pet XP

Relic of Prospecting - Increases mining yields

Relics will have a shield on them that protects them temporarily. Guilds may purchase a “Relic Siphon” from the quartermaster NPC from the TC barracks to weaken and eventually break the shield to steal the relic. Siphoning takes 50 minutes.

blocks.html:
Essence Orbs

Essence Orbs are powerful items which are used to augment a player’s power via the mastery tree. Gathering 100 radiant fragments from meteor drops/waves allows you to trade them to an Essence Artificer for an unidentified Essence Orb. Identifying this orb unlocks its bonuses, and allows it to be equipped in the mastery menu by right clicking it from your inventory. You can have a maximum of 2 essence orbs. The first essence orb slot unlocks at clade 20, and the second at mastery level 20. To remove an essence orb from your mastery, you must siphon it out with a “blank” essence orb, which is very costly.

Essence orbs ARE tradeable.

guides.title: Reputation & Wayshrines
guides.summary: Manage faction standing and travel with task sources, reputation limits, city access, penalties, and wayshrine behavior.

blocks.html:
Reputation is a mechanic which grants or denies access to certain parts of the map. Your standings with each faction in the game are found on the statistics menu of your character sheet. Having a negative reputation means that guards of a specific faction will attack you on sight, regardless of your murdercounts. Players can be flagged as a murderer and enter guarded cities assuming you have the reputation for it, but players will be able to attack you on sight.

Your character's race directly impacts the maximum and minimum amount of reputation you can have for each faction. Humans have a clade gift which increases the minimum standing that you can have with each faction. Thursars also have a "Risar Known" gift which is supposed to let them become friendly with Risars (but it is currently non-functional).

blocks.html:
Note the caps on standing are -1000 to 1000 now.

Different reputation standing levels have different descriptors. From worst standing to best is: Bad -> Detested -> Disliked -> Tolerated -> Liked -> Admired. These tiers do not currently have any impacts. Anything higher than 0 is currently maximum effect, although having a higher standing does create a cushion which allows you to lose reputation penalty free.

Gaining/Losing Reputation

Reputation is gained through doing tasks. There are four taskmasters:

  • Bounty Hunter - Killing targeted red players
  • Courier - Running supply parcels
  • Hunter - Killing wildlife
  • Soldier - Killing monsters

The most efficient method of gaining reputation is by grinding out hunter/soldier tasks simultaneously while doing courier tasks when they are convenient. Bounty hunting can be an efficient way of gaining reputation, but it is somewhat luck based and there is a decent possibility of dying and losing the bounty contract. Hunting and soldier tasks do not lose on death, so they may actually be completed and deposited anywhere in the world.

Here is a map of courier task pathing and which cities taskmasters give what reputation. Note that cave camp taskmasters are Tindremic, although Hyllspeia parcels can be turned in here.

blocks.html:
Reputation is lost in three ways: being seen by a guard when you are attackable (gray/detested/flagged as a war target), killing NPCs of a faction, or by being reported as a murderer.

Fastest way to restore negative Khurite Reputation: Run parcels from Cave Camp to Kranesh or Hyllspeia to Kranesh. Do tasks from the Kranesh taskmasters. Do jungle camp tasks.

How to restore negative Tindremic Reputation: Do tasks in Cave Camp. Run parcels from Kranesh to Cave camp. Do tasks in Gual Kor.

How to restore negative Kallardian reputation: Run parcels from Kranesh to Cave camp.

It is not currently in the ruleset to interact with reputation for the Anam Sith, Bet Huergar, Sarduccaan Empire, nor Shinar Kipouri.

guides.title: Territory Control
guides.summary: A working reference for claims, prominence, structures, supply lines, taxes, upkeep, guild territory, and sieging preparation.

blocks.html:
Territory Control

Introduction

A working reference for claims, prominence, structures, supply lines, taxes, upkeep, guild territory, and sieging preparation.

The official manual for TC is found here: https://www.mortalonline2.com/help-center/gameplay-help/getting-started-with-territory-control-and-sieging-manual/

An alternative guide authored by maemayu is found here:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1an0yeS1IcacikfkrWfiTlzL-iblGSOoS7M_k0RFleSA/edit?tab=t.0

Mortalitas also published a spreadsheet which is found here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZeXhejJxaEmGyXPjiuz2HAWdjOTQtoOsu4H0TfWsoJY/

Getting Started

Quick guide for how to participate in TC:

Create a guild at the guild stone in town for 200g

Gather 1000 prominence from tasks or killing AI and enough gold to build a house.

Build your house or stronghold. Strongholds give significantly more territory.

Find the “Land Registrar” NPC in town and buy a claiming stone for 10g and 1000 prominence

Add the claiming stone to your base.

Buy a “Chancery” from the Town Architect NPC in most towns and construct it next to your house.

You may now acquire and build as many TC structures as your heart desires. Pay your upkeep through your chancery.

Run supply shipments from town to and from your chancery to stock your vendors.

The official manual for TC is found here: https://www.mortalonline2.com/help-center/gameplay-help/getting-started-with-territory-control-and-sieging-manual/ An alternative guide authored by maemayu is found here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1an0yeS1IcacikfkrWfiTlzL-iblGSOoS7M_k0RFleSA/edit?tab=t.0 Mortalitas also published a spreadsheet which is found here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZeXhejJxaEmGyXPjiuz2HAWdjOTQtoOsu4H0TfWsoJY/ Getting Started Quick guide for how to participate in TC: Create a guild at the guild stone in town for 200g Gather 1000 prominence from tasks or killing AI and enough gold to build a house. Build your house or stronghold. Strongholds give significantly more territory. Find the “Land Registrar” NPC in town and buy a claiming stone for 10g and 1000 prominence Add the claiming stone to your base. Buy a “Chancery” from the Town Architect NPC in most towns and construct it next to your house. You may now acquire and build as many TC structures as your heart desires. Pay your upkeep through your chancery. Run supply shipments from town to and from your chancery to stock your vendors.

blocks.html:
Prominence

Prominence is a form of currency that is used for TC expenditures. It is not a physical currency like gold coins, but rather accrued in the guild tab. Spendable prominence is only acquirable when guild tagged. Prominence does not stockpile when a player is unguilded. There are three types of prominence:

  • Glory - Gained from killing most AI, as well as tasks.
  • Might - Gained from killing war targets (orange) as well as destroying their TC structures. Might is drained from the enemy guild and added to your own. The guild rank of the target player determines how much might is awarded, i.e. 10 might for a rank 10 kill.
  • Prosperity (previously called surplus) - Gained from running parcel tasks, and from supply runs from your town to your chancery

For the purpose of TC there is no functional difference between the types of prominence other than how they are acquired. 1 glory = 1 might = 1 prosperity. The main difference between these types of prominence are the ease of acquiring them, and the associated Steam achievements plus titles. To see prominence related achievements visit #titles-achievements.

In most situations, most guilds will have a large surplus of prominence. Only new guilds which are trying to build many TC structures will struggle to have enough prominence.

Prominence can be stolen with the guild war function. When killed by a war target, prominence is drained from the guild treasury equal to the guild rank of the player. Killing a rank 8 war target will yield 8 might, and cost that guild 8 prominence. It is theoretically possible to totally drain an enemy guilds prominence via war combat.

blocks.html:
Guild Tiers

Guilds are able to upgrade their guild “tier” via holding a certain number of supply towers and spending a certain amount of prominence per level. The requirements for each successive tier increase per level, culminating in rank 8 Raising your guild tier gives a distinct advantage of increasing the supply cap of the guild. The max guild tier is rank 8, which has a cap of 10,000 supply. Guild tiers do NOT increase the territory size of houses nor strongholds. Guild tier 2 also allows guilds to contest outposts when they also have at least 20 members.

blocks.html:
Guild Member Ranks

There are 10 ranks within a guild, each with different capabilities. Each rank possesses unique authority within the guild. Every rank has the ability to do everything a lower rank member can. Kicking and promoting within a guild is limited by that person's rank, i.e. a rank 5 cannot kick a rank 6.

Rank 1 - Add money to guild treasury

Rank 2 - Claim territory (housing)

Operate keep gate levers

Rank 3 - Upgrade guild structures

Claim production goods

Rank 4 - Kick members

Invite members

Spend prominence

Claim production goods

Rank 5 - Manage alliances

Rank 6 - Manage wars

Toggle guild guards

Declare and accept sieges

Rank 7 - Manage guild territory

Manage decorations in guild buildings

Manage guild structures

Promote and demote members

Rank 8 - Take from guild treasury

Buy/change guild tabard

Change guild profile (U menu)

Rank 9 - Manage keep password

Expand guild territory

Demolish guild keep

Rename guild keep

Rank 10 - Everything

In most situations, rank 4 is sufficient for most officers in a guild. Any rank above that requires big trust as there is huge griefing potential. Someone rank 7 can clear out all guild tagged buildings of decorations, for example. The general rule of thumb is give people only the permissions that are needed, and no more than that.

blocks.html:
Siege Weaponry

Sieging is a core feature of territory control. Siege weapons are purchased at the Quartermaster found in TC barracks structures. A T2 barracks is needed for a T2 quartermaster to buy the advanced siege weapons. There are two types of siege weapons: Manganons and Ballistas. Both have a wheeled and stationary version. The wheeled versions offer the ability to reposition the weapon at the downside of increased cost at the vendor. Both manganons and ballistas need a supply tent to place them down. A stone cutting (or firepot) tent is required before placing manganons and a bolt tent is needed for ballistas.

Manganons are the bread and butter of sieging. They can be used both as anti-personnel, as well anti-materiel. Here are some sieging data points:

Each manganon can shoot 100 times

Each manganon boulder deals a max of 52,000 vs. a single target

Each manganon has a total potential of 5,200,000 damage vs. a single target

Manganons do splash damage, and can target multiple structures

Wooden structures have a base defense of 50% when fully built

Stone structures have a base defense of 80% when fully built

Storehouses and relics can boost this defense further, so they must be focused first

Each manganon boulder costs 500 stone

The calculation for how many manganons are needed is to take the total damage a manganon can do, and subtract the defense values from its target. So for a example, a manganon does 5,200,000 damage total, but versus a stone structure which reduces damage by 80%, so do (5.2m x 0.2) to come to a total of 1,040,000 damage per mang. If a structure has 100% defense, it cannot be hurt by manganons.

Based on this chart, a stone structure with 25,000,000 HP and 80% defense would thus need 25,000,000/1,040,000 = 24.04 manganons rounded up to 25, not counting for any repairing. That comes out to (25 x 100) boulders, or 2,500.

blocks.html:
Keeps

Keeps are the pinnacle of territory control. These are the strongest structures with the most utility. The interactable gates combined with the supply line defense bonus make these a natural bastion for guilds to base out of.

Owning a keep gives a small control radius which is increased over time based on the guilds level. Keeps will continue to expand until they hit the radius of another keep. House radius do NOT interact with the keep radius.

Here you can see the Gaul Kor keep coming into contact with the TOP keep circle, which prevents the TOP keep radius from expanding further. The owning guild can freely build TC anywhere in this circle, assuming there are no other limiting factors such as a no-build zone.

blocks.html:
Keeps come from tier 1 to tier 3. Each tier increases the size of the keep, and its HP. Read more about these values in #housing.

A big advantage of owning a keep is that all structures within the keep radius have a portion of their upkeep converted into tax which is paid into the keep owning guild’s treasury. This is not an extra tax, but rather diverts upkeep to the owning guild instead.

blocks.html:
Outposts

The Reckoning expansion brought the addition of Territory Control Outposts. These static structures are placed in 35 unique zones around the map. Capturing one gives ownership of the territory, and many associated perks. This guide will go over the entire system regarding outposts.

Purpose

Why take outposts?

Territory owners receive many unique benefits for controlling a zone.

Tax yield from all houses in that territory. Depending on the houses in the zone, this can be between 24g and 350g per day for holding the territory.

Zone specific buffs when in the zone; Each zone has 5% loot luck, 10% loot amount, and 2 zone-specific boosts such as profession (butchery, fishing, etc) boost, or a crafting boost.

Supply generation. Each zone generates between 30 and 40 supply per hour that can be collected from the outpost chest.

Resource generation. Each zone generates stone and wood which can be collected from the outpost chest. This adds up

Access to the outpost priest and banker. The bank holds 20 slots.

Ego. Controlling a territory means you’re the big guy in town. Others will envy you and want to steal your gains.

Overall these rewards are enticing, as most big guilds are participating in this system. The passive gold gain alone is incentive enough for many, as this goes straight into the guild treasury and can fund territory control buildings. The rewards make these objectives worthwhile.

Capturing

So how exactly do you capture outposts?

Phase 0 - Preparation.

Your guild must be a minimum of rank 2. Guild levels can be raised by capturing supply towers and upgrading it in the social menu (default hotkey o) by spending prominence. You must also have a minimum of 20 characters on the guild roster.

blocks.html:
The next step is gather enough gold and prominence to contest the zone. It requires 100g and 10,000 prominence to contest zones each and every time. Most large or established guilds have millions of prominence stashed. Gold must be deposited into a chancery structure, which requires building a house and putting a guild stone in it.

Once the prerequisites of guild rank/gold/prominence is met, press the map key (default M) to open the map. Right click on a zone you wish to contest. A popup will ask if you are sure, and you select “ok” to initiate a siege. There will be a 1 hour preparation time for defenders to rally before you can start the siege. Once the siege has started, you have 1 hour to prepare before the siege officially starts.

A popup will ask if you are sure, and you select “ok” to initiate a siege. There will be a 1 hour preparation time for defenders to rally before you can start the siege. Once the siege has started, you have 1 hour to prepare before the siege officially starts.

blocks.html:
Phase 1 - Outer Gate

Once the siege has started, 3 “Outpost Urn Tents” will spawn outside of the outpost. These periodically spawn urns (about one every 20 seconds).
blocks.text: Phase 1 - Outer Gate Once the siege has started, 3 “Outpost Urn Tents” will spawn outside of the outpost. These periodically spawn urns (about one every 20 seconds).

blocks.html:
Attackers are required to pick these up and run them to the gate. After 21 urns are deposited successfully at the gate, a fuse is lit and they detonate. This detonation will kill anyone near it, including defenders. Once the gate is detonated, phase 2 begins.

Phase 2 - Inner Gates

When the outer gate is breached, the inner gates automatically close. Defenders at this point should have already retreated, or they will need to reopen the gates to retreat to the final zone.

At this point the attackers have to breach the interior gates. To do this, they must activate the levers next to the two interior gates. The standard best practice is to activate both levers. This will start a 10 minute countdown timer for the gates to lower. Once the inner gates are open, the final phase of the attack beings.

Defenders can sally forth and jump over the walls to contest the levers. Should the levers be disengaged, they will start to rise at the same rate they lowered. For example, if attackers have the gates lowering for 5 minutes, it will take 5 minutes to fully raise them again.

Phase 3 - Capture the Flag

The final phase is a simple capture the flag. 1 member of the attacker must remain within the predefined white circle around the flag to contest it. The flag lowering takes 5 minutes, and the raising of the attacker flag takes another 5 minutes. A single defender in the circle prevents flag progress. Attackers must wipe out all defenders to progress. Conversely, defenders must purge all attackers from the circle to fully end the siege.

A single attacker/defender in the flag zone will cause overtime. Overtime does not end until either the attackers are removed from the flag zone, or the flag is raised after defenders are pushed out.

Once the outpost siege has ended, there is a 2 hour cooldown period in which there can be no siege declared on the outpost again.

blocks.html:
Attacker Tips

The reality is, “offlining” outposts is rather easy. Attack an outpost at 3am during the off hours of the enemy guild and you can steal it rather easily.

Repeatedly conquering territories tests the willpower of opponents who want the zone. Several zones can be conquered solo and the people who challenged it gave up.

Gravity snare is a huge spell to get defenders off of the walls.

If you REALLY REALLY want to take an outpost, the bulwark tagmanton or manganons are good at clearing out defenders.

Defender Tips

It is often prudent to “sally”, or charge out, when the enemy has their hands full of urns in the first phase.

There are 3 really good hiding spots on the flag zone that many guilds will overlook, allowing there to be indefinite overtime until attackers give up or find you.

Obscure Mechanics

Pressing combat mode (default X) will automatically drop any outpost urns you are carrying.

Defenders can sally out and pick up urns to drop them.

ANY guild can complete phase 1 and 2 of the outpost siege

If an outpost siege goes into overtime, where time has run out but attackers are still on the final flag, if they step off the flag for even a millisecond the siege will end in favor of the defenders.

There is a “no build zone” around outposts to prevent cheesing.

If you want to open the inner gates as a defender, you must select the center of the gate to interact with it and NOT the lever. Pictured:

manganons and ballistas. both have a wheeled and stationary version. the wheeled versions offer the ability to reposition the weapon at the downside of increased cost at the vendor. both manganons and ballistas need a supply tent to place them down. a stone cutting (or firepot) tent is required before placing manganons and a bolt tent is needed for ballistas. manganons are the bread and butter of sieging. they can be used both as anti-personnel, as well anti-materiel. here are some sieging data points: each manganon can shoot 100 times each manganon boulder deals a max of 52,000 vs. a single target each manganon has a total potential of 5,200,000 damage vs. a single target manganons do splash damage, and can target multiple structures wooden structures have a base defense of 50% when fully built stone structures have a base defense of 80% when fully built storehouses and relics can boost this defense further, so they must be focused first each manganon boulder costs 500 stone the calculation for how many manganons are needed is to take the total damage a manganon can do, and subtract the defense values from its target. so for a example, a manganon does 5,200,000 damage total, but versus a stone structure which reduces damage by 80%, so do (5.2m x 0.2) to come to a total of 1,040,000 damage per mang. if a structure has 100% defense, it cannot be hurt by manganons. here is a quick chart that shows the conversion for mangs to damage against various defenses:  based on this chart, a stone structure with 25,000,000 hp and 80% defense would thus need 25,000,000/1,040,000 = 24.04 manganons rounded up to 25, not counting for any repairing. that comes out to (25 x 100) boulders, or 2,500. constructing siege weapons is made faster via the engineering skills. oghmirs have a “siegemaster” clade gift that has a similar effect. the system also includes an essence orb effect which allows siege weapons to be operated more quickly. keeps keeps are the pinnacle of territory control. these are the strongest structures with the most utility. the interactable gates combined with the supply line defense bonus make these a natural bastion for guilds to base out of. owning a keep gives a small control radius which is increased over time based on the guilds level. keeps will continue to expand until they hit the radius of another keep. house radius do not interact with the keep radius. here you can see the gaul kor keep coming into contact with the top keep circle, which prevents the top keep radius from expanding further. the owning guild can freely build tc anywhere in this circle, assuming there are no other limiting factors such as a no-build zone.  keeps come from tier 1 to tier 3. each tier increases the size of the keep, and its hp. read more about these values in #housing. a big advantage of owning a keep is that all structures within the keep radius have a portion of their upkeep converted into tax which is paid into the keep owning guild’s treasury. this is not an extra tax, but rather diverts upkeep to the owning guild instead. territory control datasheet this is the mostly* complete list of all tc structures. the missing fields will be filled in clusters over time. the defense (wood vs. stone) might be inaccurate too, so please take that column with a grain of salt. outposts the reckoning expansion brought the addition of territory control outposts. these static structures are placed in 35 unique zones around the map. capturing one gives ownership of the territory, and many associated perks. this guide will go over the entire system regarding outposts. purpose why take outposts? territory owners receive many unique benefits for controlling a zone. tax yield from all houses in that territory. depending on the houses in the zone, this can be between 24g and 350g per day for holding the territory. zone specific buffs when in the zone; each zone has 5% loot luck, 10% loot amount, and 2 zone-specific boosts such as profession (butchery, fishing, etc) boost, or a crafting boost. supply generation. each zone generates between 30 and 40 supply per hour that can be collected from the outpost chest. resource generation. each zone generates stone and wood which can be collected from the outpost chest. this adds up access to the outpost priest and banker. the bank holds 20 slots. ego. controlling a territory means you’re the big guy in town. others will envy you and want to steal your gains. overall these rewards are enticing, as most big guilds are participating in this system. the passive gold gain alone is incentive enough for many, as this goes straight into the guild treasury and can fund territory control buildings. the rewards make these objectives worthwhile. capturing so how exactly do you capture outposts? phase 0 - preparation. your guild must be a minimum of rank 2. guild levels can be raised by capturing supply towers and upgrading it in the social menu (default hotkey o) by spending prominence. you must also have a minimum of 20 characters on the guild roster. the next step is gather enough gold and prominence to contest the zone. it requires 100g and 10,000 prominence to contest zones each and every time. most large or established guilds have millions of prominence stashed. gold must be deposited into a chancery structure, which requires building a house and putting a guild stone in it. once the prerequisites of guild rank/gold/prominence is met, press the map key (default m) to open the map. right click on a zone you wish to contest. a popup will ask if you are sure, and you select “ok” to initiate a siege. there will be a 1 hour preparation time for defenders to rally before you can start the siege. once the siege has started, you have 1 hour to prepare before the siege officially starts. phase 1 - outer gate once the siege has started, 3 “outpost urn tents” will spawn outside of the outpost. these periodically spawn urns (about one every 20 seconds). attackers are required to pick these up and run them to the gate. after 21 urns are deposited successfully at the gate, a fuse is lit and they detonate. this detonation will kill anyone near it, including defenders. once the gate is detonated, phase 2 begins. phase 2 - inner gates when the outer gate is breached, the inner gates automatically close. defenders at this point should have already retreated, or they will need to reopen the gates to retreat to the final zone. at this point the attackers have to breach the interior gates. to do this, they must activate the levers next to the two interior gates. the standard best practice is to activate both levers. this will start a 10 minute countdown timer for the gates to lower. once the inner gates are open, the final phase of the attack beings. defenders can sally forth and jump over the walls to contest the levers. should the levers be disengaged, they will start to rise at the same rate they lowered. for example, if attackers have the gates lowering for 5 minutes, it will take 5 minutes to fully raise them again. phase 3 - capture the flag the final phase is a simple capture the flag. 1 member of the attacker must remain within the predefined white circle around the flag to contest it. the flag lowering takes 5 minutes, and the raising of the attacker flag takes another 5 minutes. a single defender in the circle prevents flag progress. attackers must wipe out all defenders to progress. conversely, defenders must purge all attackers from the circle to fully end the siege. a single attacker/defender in the flag zone will cause overtime. overtime does not end until either the attackers are removed from the flag zone, or the flag is raised after defenders are pushed out. once the outpost siege has ended, there is a 2 hour cooldown period in which there can be no siege declared on the outpost again. attacker tips the reality is, “offlining” outposts is rather easy. attack an outpost at 3am during the off hours of the enemy guild and you can steal it rather easily. repeatedly conquering territories tests the willpower of opponents who want the zone. several zones can be conquered solo and the people who challenged it gave up. gravity snare is a huge spell to get defenders off of the walls. if you really really want to take an outpost, the bulwark tagmanton or manganons are good at clearing out defenders. defender tips it is often prudent to “sally”, or charge out, when the enemy has their hands full of urns in the first phase. there are 3 really good hiding spots on the flag zone that many guilds will overlook, allowing there to be indefinite overtime until attackers give up or find you. obscure mechanics pressing combat mode (default x) will automatically drop any outpost urns you are carrying. defenders can sally out and pick up urns to drop them. any guild can complete phase 1 and 2 of the outpost siege if an outpost siege goes into overtime, where time has run out but attackers are still on the final flag, if they step off the flag for even a millisecond the siege will end in favor of the defenders. there is a “no build zone” around outposts to prevent cheesing. if you want to open the inner gates as a defender, you must select the center of the gate to interact with it and not the lever. pictured:  if an outpost changes hands, the previous guild loses access to the priest and banker. however, when they recapture it, everything placed in the banker will still be there. outpost map of myrland. the markers are not pixel perfectly accurate, but you should easily be able to find the outposts if you go to the marker. guild tier list. prominence cost + supply tower requirement are the cost to reach that level, and supply is the max supply cap for being on that tier. updated tc cost and upkeep data: outpost map of sarducaa. please note that the zone borders are inherently accurate. if you go to the marker you will find the outpost. this will be updated when starvault fixes the in-game map.

guides.title: Weather
guides.summary: Understand regional climate, heat, humidity, wind, body temperature, equipment effects, and player-driven weather changes.

blocks.html:
Weather

Understand regional climate, heat, humidity, wind, body temperature, equipment effects, and player-driven weather changes.

Regions

The world is broken up into hidden localized zones, each roughly 1km². These each have specific properties that influence the general climate of each area.. The north is generally colder, the central portion of the map moderate and more dry, and the southern part is warmer and wetter. Use good judgment and the World Heat stat in the statistics menu to get a general idea of the climate of each zone.

Atmospheric Conditions

There are three variables which determine the state of weather:

  • Heat - The temperature outside.
  • Humidity - How wet the air is.
  • Wind - How strong the wind is blowing.

From these variables arise several weather conditions. Different combinations of heat/humidity/wind will result in different weather conditions. This chart demonstrates the differences:

blocks.html:
World heat is visible in the statistics page of the character menu. Humidity and wind are not numerically measurable right now, but there may be visual and audio cues to pick up on. Knowing the climate of a specific location also helps greatly with determining the conditions.

Body Temperature

Your character has a specific stat called Body Heat visible on the statistics page of the character doll. This stat directly influences your character's stamina regen- if heat is too high or too low, you will have regeneration penalties proportional to the body heat level. If your body heat is at an extreme, you will take damage over time proportional to how high or low that temperature is.

Myrland is mostly temperate, meaning that body heat isn’t critical to monitor except in extreme situations. The other continents such as Sarducaa and Nordveld will have zones that are devastating to be in without proper clothing. You will die in parts of these continents without proper clothing, healing, clade gifts and/or weather alteration.

blocks.html:
Modifying Body Heat

Armor directly impacts the body heat stat. This mechanic is not fully implemented, however. Armor generally lowers body heat currently. The rule of thumb is lighter armor is better against heat, while heavier armor is better against cold. The backing material is expected to play a significant role in heat regulation.

Some elementalism spells modify your body heat. Ice spells may add chilled. Fire spells can add “warmed”. The expected utility of these spells is that you want to hit enemies with warming spells in hot environments, and hit them with chilling spells in cold locations. Using a heat spell on an enemy in a cold environment could actually benefit them a small amount!

blocks.html: Certain clade gifts alter how impacted one is to certain temperatures, too. The human gifts “Southerner” and “Northerner” impact resistance to hot and cold temperatures respectively. Thursars have a more general purpose clade gift called “Thermoregulation” which protects against both heat and cold.

blocks.html:
Polarization

Weather is alterable by players using the Elementalism subschool known as Polarization. This series of spells influences the specific atmospheric conditions - heat, humidity, and wind. Each Polarization spell impacts the local weather in different ways.

Flowing Nimbic Spirits are the primary reagent used for weather altering effects. These are purchasable from Tindrem, Toxai, and Jungle Camp for 10c in elementalist-specific currency each. There is no known way to synthesize these yet, although it is theorized that alchemy would be the source.

blocks.html:
In conjunction with the weather chart and knowledge of the local climate, make a determination of what the current weather conditions are. Compare that to your desired condition and cast the appropriate Polarization spell until the desired effect is achieved.

Examples:

You are in the jungle and you want snow. You know the jungle is high heat, high humidity. Because humidity is required for snow, your own roadblock is high heat, which needs to be lowered. Thus cast Frigidity a bunch until it starts snowing.

You need fog/rain to cast lightning ball. You are in Meduli which is dry and warm. You thus need cold and humidity. Cast frigidity and condensation until it starts to rain. Note: players might be unable to make foggy-only weather right now, and rain is always the result.

blocks.html:
Uses for Weather

Why is weather important? It can have many gameplay impacts. Certain powerful Elementalism require atmospheric conditions to successfully cast:

  • Lightning Ball - Requires cloudy weather.
  • Firestorm - Requires very windy weather.
  • Hailstorm - Requires snowing weather.
  • Tar Pit - Requires foggy weather.

Offensive and Defensive Usage - If an enemy is known to use certain elementalism spells such as hailstorm, the main counter to that would be making the weather too warm. If they use firestorm, calm the wind. If they use tar pit, decrease the humidity. This is a big brain application of polarization, so you must know your enemy and appropriate counter. Players can also mess with the body heat of friendly/enemy groups, although this will only be realistically viable on new continents.

Disruption/cover - One of the most disruptive things that can happen is a severe storm or a blizzard. This interferes with player visibility as well as audio cues. If, for instance, a siege is underway, inducing a blizzard right before attacking will throw the attackers off balance and give an advantage to the defenders.
